members.osint_investigator: Senior OSINT investigator - pivots, cross-referencing, Brazilian sources, breadth
members.redteam_lead: Red team / pentest lead - attack surface value, rules of engagement for light/active modules
members.legal_dpo: Legal counsel & DPO (VETO) - LGPD, provider terms, licences, retention

A1.option: c (with the corporate default of a)
A1.decision: V3LUM ships licence_profile=corporate as the default and the only profile usable without a recorded legal basis. Every source carries per-source terms evidence in the single provider registry. Under corporate only 'open' sources, and 'key-terms' sources whose plan is recorded as business-compatible, run; 'noncommercial' and 'license' sources run only through a legal-maintained licence_allow entry (or a recorded licence); 'unknown' sources stay disabled until reviewed. The research profile exists only with a recorded legal basis and stamps a licence banner. Coverage lost to the profile is always visible (one terminal line, a report appendix, doctor --licences) and backed by manual pivot links, never by automatic LIGHT/ACTIVE substitutes.
A1.rationale: Five members chose (c) and the architect (a+c); nobody supported (b). legal_dpo's floor is adopted in full: an internal corporate CSIRT is a commercial user for almost every free tier, a banner documents a breach but does not cure it, so 'research' needs a recorded legal basis, key-terms count only with a business-compatible plan, unknown fails closed, abuse.ch is split per its 2026-10-21 terms and shodan_internetdb is relabelled noncommercial. The architect's floor makes it data plus one gate: per-source terms in one registry, enforcement only in core/policy.py on every path, Module.terms defaulting to 'unknown', a CI test per feed. cti_lead, osint_investigator, redteam_lead and analyst_ux insisted that the loss of coverage (ipv4 keyless 31 -> 19, sha256 9 -> 5) be visible and quickly recoverable: the allow-list, the ranked review queue, the coverage table and the manual-pivot fallback do that, and redteam_lead's 'no automatic fallback to active scanning' is binding.
binding_rules: Module.terms takes exactly one of: 'open' | 'key-terms' | 'noncommercial' | 'license' | 'unknown'. The base-class default changes from 'open' to 'unknown', and @register refuses any module (plugins and P331 specs included) whose class body does not declare terms explicitly.

Per-source terms live in the provider registry v3lum/data/providers.json (AR11) at providers.<provider_id>.sources.<source_id>.terms = {class, evidence_url, quote, checked_at (ISO date), reviewer, free_plan_business_use: true|false|null}. Member conditions that say data/source_terms.json mean this registry. CI fails when a module, or any feed of an aggregator module, has no entry.

Module.terms must equal the most restrictive class among the module's registry sources, in the order open < key-terms < license < noncommercial < unknown (CI-checked). In chair files, 'terms' is that class. For aggregators, final_conditions must list the class of each feed and say which feeds are noncommercial/license.

Setting licence_profile = 'corporate' (default) | 'research'. Under corporate: 'open' runs; 'key-terms' runs only when the provider's free_plan_business_use is true or setting key_plans.<key_name> == 'business' (recorded by `v3lum keys set <name> --plan business` or the wizard); 'noncommercial' and 'license' run only with an active licence_allow entry; 'unknown' never runs.

Research profile: selectable (config or per run with --licence-profile research) only when licence_allow.json holds a research_basis {legal_ref, approver, date, scope} recording a provider grant or written permission. Otherwise the CLI refuses with 'licence_profile=research needs a recorded legal basis (docs/LEGAL.md)'. Research covers noncommercial/license sources within that scope only; unknown-terms sources stay disabled in every profile.

Research cases record the profile in case metadata. Every report and export of such a case carries a licence banner listing only the noncommercial/license sources actually used in that run, and research cases are never pushed to MISP/OpenCTI (P303).

licence_allow is a legal-maintained file (setting licence_allow_path, default ~/.v3lum/licence_allow.json, 0600; may point to a team-shared read-only path). Each entry is {source_id, basis: licence|provider_grant|terms_clause, scope (e.g. 'own-network defence only, no resale'), legal_ref, approver, decided_at, review_by (at most 12 months after decided_at), evidence_url, quote}.
A licence_allow entry past its review_by date is inactive (fail closed) and doctor warns 30 days ahead. Active entries are shown in `v3lum info <module>` and in the report coverage section.

Enforcement happens only in core/policy.py (P327) and covers scan, run, shell, extract --scan, batch, watch and doctor health checks. A licence-blocked source gets Status.SKIPPED with reason_code 'licence' and a readable reason ('skipped: noncommercial terms (licence profile corporate)').

A licence-blocked passive source is never replaced automatically by a LIGHT/ACTIVE alternative (e.g. no port scan instead of InternetDB). Where the provider's web UI allows manual use, the engine emits its manual pivot link (P311) with 'automation skipped: licence'.

Aggregators filter per source: decide() hands the module ctx.allowed_sources; the module queries and uses only those feeds and reports the others in coverage with reason_code 'licence'. A module whose sources are all blocked is skipped before it runs.

Visibility: the terminal prints one aggregated line ('N sources skipped: licence profile corporate - v3lum doctor --licences'). The HTML/MD coverage appendix 'Coverage lost under licence profile' lists each source per entity type. `v3lum doctor --licences` (offline, from metadata) prints per-entity-type coverage before/after, the unknown-terms review queue ranked by coverage impact, and the licences to budget.

`v3lum doctor --licences --refresh` re-fetches every evidence_url last checked more than 30 days ago (meant to run monthly; doctor reminds when a check is overdue). It stores the page hash and date and flags changed pages 'terms changed - review', and never enables or disables a source by itself.

Initial classes (binding; a chair may only make one stricter): abuse.ch MalwareBazaar, URLhaus and ThreatFox = 'license' (terms 2026-10-21 s.4.1) until a Spamhaus/abuse.ch subscription or written decision is recorded; abuse.ch YARAify, Feodo Tracker and SSLBL = 'open' (CC0, s.3.4); Shodan InternetDB, Shodan CVEDB, VirusTotal public API and Censys free = 'noncommercial'.

More initial classes: SANS ISC = 'noncommercial' (allow-list candidate under its 'protect your own network' clause, no resale); Google Safe Browsing v4/v5 = 'noncommercial' (Google Web Risk = 'license'); ransomware.live keyless v2 = 'noncommercial' (PRO key = 'key-terms'); XposedOrNot keyless = 'noncommercial' (xonAPI+ = 'key-terms', business plan).

More initial classes: Team Cymru MHR, Robtex, Malpedia, blocklist.de, CINS, ET, GreenSnow, DataPlane and Phishing Army = 'noncommercial'; OpenSanctions = 'noncommercial' (business licence = 'license'); Hudson Rock free tools, LeakCheck public, Filescan, MalwareIntel, SecurityContext, VirusShare lists, ViriBack and binlist/data = 'unknown'.

Day-1 legal review queue (doctor --licences prints it ranked by coverage impact): abuse.ch MalwareBazaar/URLhaus/ThreatFox (or a Spamhaus subscription), Shodan InternetDB (or a Shodan licence), SANS ISC, Team Cymru MHR, the FireHOL/blocklist.de/CINS family, ransomware.live PRO terms, and the OpenSanctions business licence. No unknown-terms source may be default-enabled at release.

Reference module fix in phase 0: shodan_internetdb declares terms='noncommercial' (it currently inherits 'open'), its tests are updated, and App.doctor stops calling internetdb.shodan.io under the corporate profile.

Terms classes (definitions for every chair file and registry entry): 'open' = free use, internal business use included (public domain, CC0, CC BY, open government data, and permissive or copyleft licences whose obligations V3LUM meets by runtime download and attribution, A6); 'key-terms' = use is through a key whose plan's terms decide business use (key_plans, BR4); 'license' = business use needs a separate paid subscription, contract or written permission (examples in BR14-BR16); 'noncommercial' = the terms exclude commercial or business use; 'unknown' = terms not published or not yet reviewed.

Offline modules with no registry source (disclosure 'none' and no dataset, e.g. validators and extraction) declare terms='open'. A dataset is a registry source like any other: a module that uses datasets takes the most restrictive class among its sources (BR3).

A2.decision: Scans default to TLP:AMBER (setting tlp, on every execution path). The FIRST TLP 2.0 labels are supported, AMBER+STRICT included. TLP is attached to each seed and inherited by pivots and extracted entities. The single policy gate enforces it: AMBER excludes unknown-tier and query-reusing providers; AMBER+STRICT allows trusted providers only and no external push; RED allows offline and internal platforms only. Providers that publish lookups never receive values at any TLP (rule 7). Renderers generate the marking on every report page, section, file name and export. At AMBER and above, manual pivot links become non-clickable text with a disclosure warning.
A2.rationale: Unanimous (a). legal_dpo's floor is adopted: amber default for scan/run/watch, lowering recorded, pivots inherit the TLP, manual links non-clickable with a warning at AMBER+, AMBER excludes unknown tier and providers that redistribute/publish queries, RED = shares_input False plus internal platforms, LGPD applies at every TLP. The architect's floor is adopted: TLP per seed with propagation, one choke point, renderer-generated markings, table-driven tests. osint_investigator's point (log retention alone would exclude almost everything) matches legal_dpo's redistribution/publication line. cti_lead supplied the STIX/MISP markings and the AMBER+STRICT export block, redteam_lead the AMBER minimum for LIGHT/ACTIVE cases and the RED limits on target contact, analyst_ux the shell and prompt changes. The chair is stricter on one point: publishing providers are blocked at every TLP because team rule 7 is not TLP-dependent. RED follows legal_dpo's 'offline plus the company's own platforms': LIGHT/ACTIVE contact at RED is allowed only with verified company-operated assets, and then also under the architect's non-corporate-egress-or-recorded-override condition. redteam_lead's wider 'own assets or authorized scope' is not adopted at RED.
binding_rules: TLP values (FIRST TLP 2.0): 'clear' | 'green' | 'amber' | 'amber+strict' | 'red'. Setting tlp defaults to 'amber'. --tlp exists on scan, run, extract --scan, batch input (-i) and watch. The shell has `set tlp <level>` and its prompt shows mode and TLP (e.g. v3lum[passive|AMBER]).

TLP is stored per seed. Pivots and entities extracted from text/files inherit their parent's TLP, and case TLP = the highest of its seeds. Choosing a TLP lower than the configured default is recorded in the case audit (OS user, time, from, to). LIGHT/ACTIVE cases are at least AMBER: a lower --tlp is raised to amber with a notice.

Gate in core/policy.py (Status.SKIPPED, reason_code 'tlp'). CLEAR/GREEN: every disclosure class, with unknown-tier providers only under the per-run --allow-unknown flag (A8). AMBER: excludes unknown-tier providers and providers flagged reuses_queries (their terms allow redistributing, selling or reusing submitted values or content, 'improve the service' and model training included).

AMBER+STRICT: trusted-tier providers only, and no REST push to any platform outside the organisation. RED: only modules with disclosure 'none' or 'internal'. Target contact counts as internal only for verified own assets (txt_verified/attested, not third_party_hosted). At RED, LIGHT/ACTIVE runs only on such assets, through a non-corporate egress profile or with a recorded --egress-override, and every other target is refused.

Providers flagged publishes_queries (public recent-lookups pages, public scan feeds) never receive an investigated value at any TLP (team rule 7; Status.SKIPPED reason_code 'policy'). Log retention alone is not an exclusion criterion.

Under RED, ctx.http and ctx.dns of 'none'/'internal' modules raise PolicyError for any public host, public DoH included. DNS then works only through a configured internal resolver (disclosure 'internal'); otherwise the answer is 'could not verify'.

Markings are generated by the renderers from the case TLP, never typed by hand: terminal report header; HTML header, footer, top of every section and print CSS (label plus TLP 2.0 colour); Markdown first line; JSON top-level 'tlp' field; report file names carry the label (e.g. <case_id>.TLP-AMBER.html).

Exports: STIX 2.1 marking-definition with object_marking_refs on every object (TLP 2.0 definitions, AMBER+STRICT supported); MISP tlp:* tag, with distribution 0 (your organisation only) for AMBER, AMBER+STRICT and RED (P303).

Manual pivot links: at AMBER and above they render as non-clickable text with 'opening sends <value> to <host>'. At RED, third-party links are hidden from reports and shown only by `v3lum links` with the warning. Links are never auto-opened, and `links --open` at AMBER+ needs an interactive confirmation naming the host (non-TTY refuses).

Cross-case data never travels down: a case shows sightings only from cases with TLP <= its own. Higher AMBER/AMBER+STRICT cases appear as 'seen in N restricted cases' with no ids, dates or verdicts. RED cases and LIGHT/ACTIVE engagement cases never surface in a lower-TLP case. CLEAR/GREEN exports and shareable reports omit cross-case references.
TLP is not a privacy classification: the LGPD controls of A4, A8 and A10 apply at every TLP, CLEAR included.

TLP-skipped modules are summarised in one terminal line with the reason and listed in the HTML/MD coverage appendix. core/policy.py ships table-driven tests over TLP x disclosure x tier x publishes/reuses flags x opsec x own-asset/scope.

A3.decision: The default set is computed by core/policy.py from metadata: a module runs in a plain `v3lum scan x` only if its Module.default_enabled is True and it passes every gate (licence, TLP, tier, privacy, keys, opsec, egress, quota). Module.default_enabled can only lower the computed set. It must be False for LIGHT/ACTIVE, unknown-tier or unknown-terms sources, unbounded or slow sources, bulk downloads and person-profiling sweeps. Official Brazilian open data, offline data, case-DB/internal sightings, DoH DNS and manual links are explicitly default-on. A measured time budget, named presets, demotion rules and one canonical list of skip reasons make the default set observable.
A3.rationale: Unanimous (a). The architect's floor makes the default set computed, not hand-set: the author may only opt out, max_requests > 10 is opt-in unless a curated pack has its own cap and deadline, p50 > 10 s is opt-in, and datasets > 50 MB never download inside a scan. legal_dpo's floor makes unknown tier/terms, LIGHT/ACTIVE, person_name, third-party breach checks and sensitive site categories never default, and requires licence clearance: here the gate enforces that for noncommercial/license sources, so they may stay default candidates and show up as 'coverage lost under licence profile' (A1) instead of disappearing silently. osint_investigator supplied seeds-versus-pivots (run_on) and the list of default-on official Brazilian sources. analyst_ux supplied the measurable time budget, the presets and auto-demotion, cti_lead the minimum answer set per type, redteam_lead the fetches_target rule.
binding_rules: Effective default set = modules with Module.default_enabled=True that pass every gate of core/policy.decide at run time (licence, TLP, tier, privacy, keys, opsec, egress, quota, demotion). The set is computed from metadata, and Module.default_enabled can only lower it: an author can opt a module out, never force it in.

default_enabled (Module attribute and chair-file field) MUST be False when any of these holds: opsec LIGHT or ACTIVE; terms 'unknown'; provider tier 'unknown'; declared max_requests > 10 per entity (except curated packs with their own cap and deadline, A5); expected_latency (p50) > 10 s; a known high false-positive rate; needs a dataset > 50 MB that `v3lum data update` cannot pre-fetch; category person_name (source modules that search or enrich people by name; offline correlation packs over facts already collected, such as P258, follow their own purpose-gated conditions).

default_enabled MUST also be False for: username sweeps beyond the A5 default subset; fresh assessments by fetches_target providers (modes that use cached results with no publication may be True); sensitive site categories (NSFW, dating, religion, health, politics).

default_enabled MAY be True for 'noncommercial'/'license' sources that meet every other criterion. Under the shipped corporate profile the gate skips them with reason_code 'licence' (that is how 'coverage lost under licence profile' is reported) until a licence_allow entry or recorded licence clears them. legal_dpo's requirement that a default source be allowed by the licence profile is thus enforced on the effective default set, and Module.default_enabled is only the candidate flag. Their final_conditions must say 'off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared'.
Key-required sources MAY be default_enabled=True: they run by default once the key is configured, and report NEEDS_KEY otherwise.

New contract fields: Module.max_requests (int, HTTP requests per entity per run). ScopedHttp enforces it: further requests raise RequestCapReached, the run keeps its data with partial=True and stop reason 'request_cap'. Module.expected_latency (float seconds, declared p50). doctor and the feedback loop measure the real p50 and precision.

Demotion: a default module whose measured p50 > 10 s over >= 20 runs, whose findings are marked wrong in > 30% after >= 10 votes, that fails its health check on 3 consecutive `doctor --sources` runs, or that is BLOCKED on 5 consecutive runs leaves the default set (state in ~/.v3lum/health.json) with a doctor notice. Explicit -M still runs it, and it returns once it passes again.

Privacy defaults: per-person breach/infostealer modules use run_on='own_assets' (A4); username packs use run_on='seeds' (A5); person_name modules are never default. A provider receiving PERSONAL_TYPES (A8) enters the default set only when the registry records personal_data_review {basis, reviewer, date}; until then it runs only when explicitly selected in a case with a recorded purpose (reason_code 'privacy').

Default-on by decision (still subject to every gate): the BR CNPJ/QSA official open-data chain (BrasilAPI with Minha Receita fallback, QSA; CPF never looked up); CGU sanctions bulk lists matched locally once fetched by `v3lum data update`; TCU certidoes; BCB authorised institutions and DominiosVerificados; registro.br RDAP for .br names. Geo-blocked gov.br endpoints are on only when egress_country='BR' (A9).

Also default-on: offline/local modules (warninglists, validators, extraction); case-DB sightings (P375); internal TIP lookups when configured (A12); DoH-based DNS modules; manual pivot links (no network).

Time budget (acceptance tests AR21): default scans of a domain, IPv4, URL, SHA-256, e-mail and CNPJ show the first-screen summary within 20 s and complete at p90 within 60 s with recorded latencies on a cold cache. Setting scan_deadline (default 90 s; 0 = unlimited; --timeout overrides) ends a scan with partial results, a header banner, and pending sources marked SKIPPED reason_code 'deadline'.
Presets: --preset quick (the default set) | deep (every ready module that passes the gates; --all-modules becomes an alias). -M/-x/-c keep working, and no preset or -M bypasses a gate.

Reporting: the terminal prints one line 'N opt-in sources not run (use --preset deep)'. `v3lum modules` and `v3lum info` show, per module, whether it is in the effective default set and the reason_code when it is not.

Minimum answer set: docs list the default sources for ipv4, domain, url, sha256, email and cve. A test asserts that at least 2 reputation-capable sources per type are default-ready under corporate (keyless, or with the recommended free keys of A15), and doctor warns when fewer are ready.

Canonical reason codes, used by policy, engine, coverage, docs and every chair file. SKIPPED: not_default, demoted, licence, tlp, tier, privacy, own_asset, opsec, authorization, scope, egress_country, deadline, policy, config, not_applicable. NEEDS_KEY: needs_key. UNAVAILABLE: package, dataset, offline. QUOTA: quota. RATE_LIMITED: rate_limited.

More canonical reason codes. BLOCKED: hostile_host, circuit, challenge, geo_block, login_wall. ERROR: timeout, sanitizer, error. ModuleResult.reason_code carries the code, and the human text stays in the reason/error field. Partial runs keep status ok/empty with partial=True and stop_reason in {request_cap, deadline, quota, rate_limited, cancelled}.

A4.option: a+b+c (the third-party opt-in limited to analyst-typed seeds)
A4.decision: Breach and infostealer data is scrubbed at ingestion at one engine choke point, and the HTTP cache is covered too. Values are pseudonymised with a keyed HMAC in evidence file names and in the case-DB/sightings search indexes. By default, per-person breach and stealer checks run only for addresses on verified org-profile domains. They run for other addresses only when the analyst typed them as seeds and passed --breach-scope all with a recorded purpose, never for pivots or for addresses found in text. Generic, role and test addresses are flagged and never scored. Credentials are never tested.
A4.rationale: legal_dpo (a+b+c) sets the floor, and cti_lead and the architect hold the same position. redteam_lead (b) accepts legal's tightening. osint_investigator (a+b with c relaxed to seeds) is folded in as a stricter limit on the opt-in: analyst-typed seeds only, never pivots or WHOIS/text-discovered addresses. analyst_ux (a+c) worried that pseudonymising the case DB would break 'search previous cases by IOC'. A keyed HMAC keeps exact-value search working (the query is hashed the same way), so legal_dpo's floor costs only substring search on personal types. All members agreed the HTTP cache must be covered, which today stores raw breach bodies for the whole TTL.
binding_rules: Breach, infostealer and people-data providers are flagged sensitive=true in the provider registry. Module.sensitive is derived (category breach_leak, or any source of a sensitive provider) and requires a per-source sanitizer schema registered in core/sanitize.py; otherwise @register fails.

The P145 sanitizer is a mandatory engine stage right after Module.run returns. It runs before the graph, evidence, case DB, events/live feed, reports, STIX/MISP and --debug output, and modules cannot opt out. It fails closed: on an exception the raw payload is dropped and the run ends Status.ERROR with reason_code 'sanitizer'.

HTTP cache: raw bodies of sensitive providers never reach http_cache.db. HttpClient applies the source's sanitizer schema to the body before caching or returning it, and falls back to no-store when no schema exists. Their TTL is at most min(7 days, cache_max_age_days, retention_days).
Kept: breach names, breach dates, data classes, counts, stealer family, log/compromise dates, corporate/user service counts, and the password FORM (plaintext, or hashed: <algorithm>).

Dropped, never masked: passwords, password hashes, salts, masked passwords/hints, top_passwords, top_logins, logins, cookies, session tokens, autofill, computer names, infected-host IPs, malware paths, leaked file contents and combo lines (email:password, user:pass@host).

Generic, role and test addresses are flagged, capped at POSSIBLE and never scored as exposure. The bundled list is v3lum/data/generic_addresses.json: role local parts such as test, info, contato, contact, sac, admin, noreply/no-reply, suporte, support, vendas, financeiro, rh, webmaster, postmaster, abuse; IANA example and test domains; plus LeakCheck found >= 100 or Hudson Rock >= 5 computers.

Evidence filenames are <module>__<type>__<hmac12>__<sha10>.json for every entity type. hmac12 = the first 12 hex of HMAC-SHA256(installation secret, '<type>:<normalized value>'). The installation secret is ~/.v3lum/secret.key (32 random bytes, 0600, created on first run). No raw value ever appears in a path.

For PERSONAL_TYPES (A8), the case-DB search columns and the sightings index store the same keyed HMAC, never the value. Exact-value search hashes the query. Plain values stay only inside the 0600 case JSON and the report.

Breach scope: per-person breach/infostealer modules declare run_on='own_assets' and by default run only for addresses on verified org_profile domains (txt_verified or attested, A11 BR4). With `--breach-scope all` plus `--purpose "<text>"` (recorded in the case and audit) they also run on analyst-typed seed addresses. Addresses found as pivots, in WHOIS, in pasted text or in pages outside org domains are never checked.

Without the flag, a non-org address produces one line 'breach check skipped: not an org domain' (Status.SKIPPED, reason_code 'privacy'). Third-party addresses that are checked produce context only (first_seen_breach, data classes), severity at most MEDIUM, with no exposure score.

Breach/stealer sources with 'unknown' or 'noncommercial' terms stay disabled under corporate until reviewed or allow-listed (A1); Hudson Rock free tools and LeakCheck public are 'unknown' today. Own-domain bulk endpoints (HIBP domain search, XON domain breaches, stealer domain searches) use run_on='own_assets_only' (A11).
Leaked credentials are never tested, validated or used, in any mode or engagement (no login attempts, spraying or validation).

Tests run trimmed Hudson Rock, LeakCheck, XposedOrNot and HIBP fixtures end to end. A grep over http_cache.db, evidence, case DB, every report and export format, events and --debug output finds no masked password/login, computer name, victim IP or malware path.

A5.option: a (amended for the archived WhatsMyName dataset)
A5.decision: One username checker engine. WhatsMyName (CC BY-SA, runtime-only, pinned, attributed) is the default engine, with a small reliability-ranked default subset run only on analyst-typed handles. The Maigret DB is the opt-in extended pack. WhatsMyName was archived on 2026-11-09; Maigret entries with explicit two-sided markers may back-fill default slots left by failing WMN sites only after legal_dpo approves it in writing, and then only through a V3LUM selection list, never through a merged dataset. Every result is tri-state, polite and labelled as a weak signal, and the politeness limits are hard.
A5.rationale: Five members chose (a). osint_investigator chose Maigret-primary on new evidence: WMN was archived on 2026-11-09, about 26 WMN entries are sign-up/availability oracles, and the curated Maigret profile scored 24/40 with 0 false positives against WMN's 16/40 with 0 false positives. The chair keeps the majority choice and addresses the evidence: the dataset is pinned, an oracle lint covers rule 2 and precision is measured from the team's own egress. legal_dpo's floor is kept: WMN stays runtime-only and unmerged, the default is a small curated subset, sensitive categories are off, the homonym label is mandatory and pasted-text usernames are never swept. Because A8 forbids sending usernames to unknown-tier operators, every site needs a recorded tier. The architect's floor is kept: one engine, FOUND/ABSENT only on explicit markers, concurrency <= 8, deadline 120 s, caps 150/600. analyst_ux's 100-site/30-s target sets the default size. Auditor correction: legal_dpo's floor (its A5 position and its P113 vote) keeps the Maigret DB as the opt-in extended pack and the default WMN-based (plus the Ceos calibrated sites), so back-filling default slots with Maigret entries would be looser than the floor. The back-fill is therefore held until legal_dpo approves it in writing (docs/LEGAL.md); WMN content is never copied or merged in any case. legal_dpo's 'at most 1 request per handle per site' is adopted, which removes the single retry other members proposed.
binding_rules: One checker engine (P113 username_check) serves every pack. Site definitions come from WhatsMyName and the Maigret DB. WhatsMyName (CC BY-SA 4.0, archived 2026-11-09) is downloaded at runtime into ~/.v3lum/datasets, pinned by SHA-256, attributed, and never bundled or merged. The Maigret DB (MIT) is pinned; updates are verified with db_meta SHA-256 and never applied mid-run.

V3LUM corrections, exclusions and per-site tiers live in a separate V3LUM-authored overlay (v3lum/data/username_overlay.json) that never copies WMN text. Sherlock data is used only for username-syntax regexes and its exclusions list.

Default pack: module username_check (P113), run_on='seeds', default_enabled=True. It holds at most `username_default_sites` sites (default 100, hard max 150), selected by measured precision: the official claimed account must be FOUND and a random 20-char control ABSENT, from the team's egress. Every selected site has explicit presence AND absence markers.

The default pack takes WhatsMyName entries plus the Ceos calibrated sites (P113). Maigret entries with two-sided markers may fill the slots of failing WMN sites only after legal_dpo records approval in docs/LEGAL.md (legal floor: until then Maigret stays the opt-in extended pack). Any selection ships as a V3LUM selection list (site ids plus dataset hash), never as merged data.

Extended pack: module username_check_extended (same engine), default_enabled=False, run only by -M or --preset deep. It covers the Maigret curated profile (no protection, activation or engine entries) plus the remaining WMN sites, with a cap of 600 requests per username.

Rule 2 lint (P327) over the datasets: entries whose probe is a sign-up, register, availability, check_username, validate, password-reset or login endpoint are excluded (about 26 in WMN, plus Maigret and Sherlock ones). Only public profile URLs are fetched: no logged-in scraping, cookies, or WAF/challenge bypass.

Limits: exactly one request per handle per site, with no retries (a connection error or timeout = UNKNOWN); global concurrency <= 8; one request at a time per host; min_interval >= 1 s per host; per-site timeout 10 s; redirects not followed (the redirect response is evaluated against the markers); after a 403, 429 or challenge on a host its remaining sites are stopped; cap 150 requests per username in the default pack; pack deadline 120 s (target p50 <= 30 s). A FOUND site may get one control request with a random handle (P113, legal_dpo's '+1 control re-check'), counted in the cap; it is not a retry.

Tri-state per site: FOUND only on the presence marker with no absence marker; ABSENT only on the absence marker; blocked, challenge, login redirect, timeout or 429 = UNKNOWN (rule 5). Each result keeps site, state, matched marker, URL and checked_at as evidence.

Presentation: the terminal lists FOUND rows only, with counts per state. Every hit is labelled 'same handle does not prove identity' with confidence POSSIBLE; PROBABLE needs a P258 linkage signal (non-default avatar match, extracted ids, bio link to a known entity). Handles of <= 4 chars or dictionary words are flagged high-collision. Found profiles become pivots with expand=False.

Privacy: packs run only on analyst-typed seeds, never on pivots or on usernames found in pasted text. A single token detected as a username with confidence < 0.75 runs a pack only after a TTY confirmation or with an explicit 'username:' prefix. Never infer sensitive traits from hits.

Sensitive and closed sites: nsfw_sites=false and sensitive_sites=false (dating, religion, health, politics) are the defaults. Sites whose profiles are visible only after login are excluded, and Tor/I2P sites are excluded unless opted in.

Each site is a provider that receives a username (A8). Only sites recorded in the overlay as trusted or community are ever queried, with a rationale such as 'major platform' or 'Tranco top-50k on <date>'. Unknown-tier sites never receive a username at any TLP; at AMBER+STRICT only trusted sites are queried.

Health: `doctor --sources` re-measures a rotating sample of <= 25 sites per run, at most once a day. Sites failing their claimed/unclaimed self-test are auto-disabled until they pass again, with a doctor notice.

A6.decision: V3LUM never copies or vendors GPL/AGPL/LGPL code: behaviour is reimplemented from documentation and specs. LGPL libraries may be used only as unmodified optional extras, and GPL/AGPL tools only as separately installed external processes. GPL, CC BY-SA and non-commercial data are downloaded at runtime only. Only permissive data is bundled, and every notice is generated from one registry and checked in CI. V3LUM's own licence is proprietary-internal (company-owned, internal use), written to stay Apache-2.0-compatible.
A6.rationale: Unanimous (a), and all six members recommend proprietary-internal now. legal_dpo's floor: no GPL/AGPL code copied, LGPL only as unmodified optional pip dependencies, GPL/AGPL tools only as external processes, share-alike data runtime-only by CI check, notices generated from the registry. The architect's floor: generated attribution, a dependency licence check, everything beyond rich + requests optional, adapted MIT code carrying a header. redteam_lead added pinned active-mode content and external scanners on PATH. analyst_ux added that downloads happen out of band and never stall a scan. cti_lead and osint_investigator confirmed that ioc-finder is not needed.
binding_rules: No GPL, AGPL or LGPL code is copied, pasted or vendored into V3LUM. Behaviour from such projects (e.g. InQuest iocextract, AGPL scanners) is reimplemented from documentation and specs, and those projects serve as study material only.
LGPL libraries may be used only as unmodified optional pip dependencies inside an extra, never in core and never vendored. ioc-finder (LGPLv3+) is not adopted (P172).

GPL/AGPL tools (nmap, nuclei, masscan...) run only as separately installed external processes found on PATH and version-checked by doctor. They are never imported, bundled, auto-downloaded or auto-updated.

Data licences: GPL, CC BY-SA and non-commercial datasets (e.g. webappanalyzer technologies GPL-3.0, WhatsMyName CC BY-SA 4.0, PHPIDS LGPL-3.0, Malpedia/OpenSanctions NC) are downloaded at runtime into ~/.v3lum/datasets and never bundled. Only MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, CC0, CC BY 4.0, IANA public data and the unmodified PSL (MPL-2.0) may be bundled.

One registry (P330: bundled files, register_dataset licence/terms/attribution fields, adapted code) generates THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and data/NOTICE, each entry with name, source URL, version/commit or etag, SHA-256, licence, attribution text and bundled-or-runtime. CI fails on a bundled file without an entry, or on a copyleft/NC dataset that is bundled.

Code adapted from MIT/BSD/Apache projects (SpiderFoot, Maigret, Sherlock, ioc-extractor, ioc-fanger, lemmeknow, Machinae, mihari...) carries a header with source URL, commit and licence, plus a THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md entry.
Dependency licence check in CI: runtime dependencies must be permissive, or LGPL used unmodified as optional extras. Everything beyond rich + requests is an optional extra with wheels.

Datasets that drive LIGHT/ACTIVE behaviour (wordlists, nuclei templates, takeover fingerprints) are pinned by commit/SHA-256 in a lock file (data/active.lock) and refreshed only by `v3lum data update` with a diff summary, never mid-engagement.

Runtime datasets larger than 5 MB are fetched by `v3lum data update` (with a first-run hint), never in the middle of a scan. Reports surface the attributions of the sources and datasets actually used (P336).

V3LUM's own licence is proprietary-internal (all rights reserved, company-owned, internal use only), written to stay Apache-2.0-compatible. Apache-2.0 is decided only if an external release is approved.

A7.decision: LIGHT stays opt-in (--mode light) and runs only on analyst-typed seeds, after the passive results for that entity. ACTIVE needs a real authorization reference and a scope file on every execution path. The core checks scope at connection time, after DNS resolution and on every redirect hop. Pivots never inherit scope. Hard rate and size ceilings, a list of forbidden actions enforced in code, safe pinned nuclei templates, a kill switch, an audit record with a hash-chained request ledger, and an engagement banner on every report page complete the envelope. No LIGHT or ACTIVE module merges before the safety suite passes.
A7.rationale: Unanimous (a). legal_dpo's floor is adopted (Codigo Penal art. 154-A as broadened by Lei 14.155/2021, provider AUPs): a mandatory non-empty REF plus scope, ACTIVE only on scope matches, CDN/SaaS IPs excluded unless listed, one gate for run/shell/watch, no -y/non-TTY bypass, <= 10 req/s, top-1000 ports, wordlists <= 5k, the forbidden-action list, safe nuclei tags, and LIGHT never on pivots or hostile hosts. The architect's floor is adopted: scope parsed once and enforced after resolution and per redirect, central limits, an ACTIVE budget per case, external binaries pinned and never auto-installed, a per-request audit log, `run` defaulting to passive. Where members gave different numbers, the chair took the stricter one: redteam_lead's 2 connections per host over legal_dpo's 4, his LIGHT limits, method allow-list, no OAST, kill switch and ledger. osint_investigator and cti_lead supplied archive-first ordering and the victim-token rule, analyst_ux the readable refusals.
binding_rules: ACTIVE needs --mode active, --authorized REF and --scope FILE on every path (scan, run, shell, watch, batch; TTY or not; -y included). REF must match ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:/#-]{2,63}$ and must not be a placeholder (confirmed, yes, ok, none, n/a, test). The bare `--authorized` form (const 'confirmed') is removed. A refusal lists exactly what is missing.

Scope file (TOML via tomllib, or JSON; schema in docs/ROE.md): authorization_ref (must equal --authorized), owner, contacts, ticket, window_start/window_end (UTC), targets {domains (exact or explicit '*.' wildcard), cidrs, url_prefixes}, exclusions, optional lower limits (max_rps, max_concurrency, max_pps <= 1000, max_requests <= 50000) and an optional ROE user_agent/header. Outside the window the run is refused, and the file's SHA-256 is stored in the case.

Scope is checked by the core at connection time, after DNS resolution through the egress profile and again on every redirect hop. The target must match by domain/URL prefix or CIDR, and the resolved IP must not be private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT, ULA or cloud metadata unless the scope lists it.

CDN/shared-hosting/SaaS IPs (noise and warninglist ranges) are excluded from every ACTIVE probe unless the scope lists them explicitly. For an in-scope domain resolving to such an IP, HTTP probes to that host name need it listed under shared_infra_hosts, and network probes (ports, TLS sweeps) need the IP/CIDR itself.

Pivots never inherit scope. ACTIVE modules run only on entities matching the scope, and LIGHT modules only on analyst-typed seeds. LIGHT never runs on pivots. light_for_own_assets=true (default false) only lets LIGHT run without --mode light on typed seeds that are verified own assets. Every other entity gets passive modules only (Status.SKIPPED, reason_code 'scope').

Hard ceilings, enforced in HttpClient and the socket connector (modules and host profiles cannot raise them). Every ACTIVE probe type: <= 10 requests/probes per second and <= 2 concurrent connections per target host. Port scans: <= 1000 TCP ports (top-1000 by default or an explicit list), no UDP sweeps, <= 100 packets/s in total unless the scope raises the total (maximum 1000).

More hard ceilings: wordlists <= 5000 entries from any source, --wordlist included; ACTIVE budget 10000 requests/probes per case unless the scope sets max_requests (<= 50000); LIGHT <= 1 req/s and <= 25 requests per target host per scan.

Forbidden in code and in the P327 lint, in every mode and engagement: exploitation or payload-based confirmation; credential brute force, spraying, default-login checks or any login attempt; use of leaked or found credentials and keys; JWT/hash cracking; DoS, stress or load tests; uploads, writes or deletes.

Also forbidden: state-changing methods toward targets (ACTIVE uses GET/HEAD/OPTIONS unless core policy allow-lists a module for a documented read-only reason; LIGHT uses GET/HEAD); claiming dangling resources or takeovers; downloading object contents from exposed buckets beyond the listing/metadata needed to prove exposure; OAST/interactsh callbacks.

nuclei is an optional external binary: found on PATH, version-checked by doctor, never auto-installed or updated. It runs with -duc -ni, rate limit <= 10, and a pinned template set (data/active.lock).

nuclei templates allowed: only those whose tags are all in {tech, panel, exposure, misconfig, ssl, dns, detect, discovery} and none in {intrusive, dos, fuzz, fuzzing, brute-force, bruteforce, default-login, exploit, rce, sqli, xss, lfi, ssrf, oast, injection, file-upload}; protocols http, ssl and dns only (no code, headless, file, javascript or network).

Kill switch: Ctrl+C, the end of the scope window or the scan deadline sets the runtime cancel flag. HttpClient and the socket connector then refuse new target requests, and all target traffic stops within 2 s.

Audit (P324): every LIGHT/ACTIVE run (scan, run, shell) writes a case with an audit record (OS user, REF, scope SHA-256, window, mode, egress profile, targets, modules, time) and a per-case JSONL request ledger (UTC time, module, method, host, resolved IP, port, redacted path, status, bytes, egress profile, opsec). The ledger is hash-chained and written even with --no-evidence.

Every page and section of a LIGHT/ACTIVE case report carries a banner: mode, authorization reference, scope SHA-256, window, egress profile/IP, targets touched and request counts. Out-of-scope refusals list each target and the reason.

Sequencing: passive results for an entity (TI and archive lookups included) are absorbed before any LIGHT/ACTIVE module runs on it (P376). URLs that probably carry a per-recipient token (an org_profile e-mail in plain, URL-encoded or base64 form, or opaque tokens of >= 16 chars in path/query) are never fetched automatically and need a per-URL confirmation.

`v3lum run` uses the configured mode (passive by default) and honours an explicit --mode. It refuses with a hint ('needs --mode light: contacts the target') instead of escalating with max(mode, opsec). In the shell, `set authorized <ref>` binds to a scope file (`set scope <file>`) and expires after 8 h.

LIGHT requests use the egress-profile UA (setting ua_light, a common browser UA by default) and never the V3LUM or contact UA. ACTIVE may use the scope file's ROE UA/header: an engagement token agreed with the scope owner, never the organisation's name, team, mailbox or analyst (P326 veto_lift: LIGHT/ACTIVE requests never carry the organisation's identity).
Merge gate: no LIGHT module (G03 light) and no G13 ACTIVE module is merged or enabled before the AR20 safety suite passes.

A8.decision: Every provider has a trust tier (trusted, community or unknown) with a recorded rationale in the provider registry, and every module declares its disclosure class. Unknown-tier providers are never default, are excluded at AMBER and above, need a per-run flag at CLEAR/GREEN and never receive personal identifiers. Undeclared hosts are refused at runtime. Every report lists the hosts that were actually contacted, with tier, terms class and counts, and shows per entity who received its value.
A8.rationale: cti_lead and legal_dpo chose (a+b); the other four chose (a) and asked for the host list anyway (analyst_ux, architect, redteam_lead), so (a+b) is the council's position. legal_dpo's floor is adopted: tier with rationale per source, unknown never default or at AMBER+, never sent personal identifiers at any TLP, a privacy/terms review (international transfer basis, LGPD art. 33) before providers that receive personal identifiers become default, a host ledger in every report. The architect's floor is adopted: one registry keyed by provider and host, a CI test per declared host, ScopedHttp refusing undeclared hosts, the host list taken from the HTTP event log. osint_investigator supplied the --allow-unknown opt-in, the badges and promotion records, redteam_lead the per-entity disclosure ledger, analyst_ux the header line. The chair adds the 'target' disclosure class so the RED rules for LIGHT/ACTIVE (A2) are expressible.
binding_rules: Tier is recorded per provider in v3lum/data/providers.json (AR11): 'trusted' | 'community' | 'unknown', with tier_rationale (operator, terms, data handling), reviewer and date. All hosts of a provider share its tier. Module.trust_tier is derived from Module.provider (modules never declare a tier). Modules with disclosure none, internal or target have tier 'n/a'.

Tier definitions. trusted: government bodies, national CERTs/CSIRTs, internet registries and RIRs (IANA, NIC.br/registro.br, RIPE NCC...), established security non-profits and academic institutions with published terms (e.g. abuse.ch, Spamhaus, SANS ISC, Shadowserver, CIRCL, MITRE, CISA/NVD), and established companies with published terms, a privacy policy and a business offering.

community: well-known community projects or small companies with an identifiable operator, public documentation/terms and >= 2 years of public track record. unknown: anonymous or individual operators, no terms or privacy policy, < 2 years or unverifiable track record. A promotion from unknown to community is recorded with reviewer and date.

unknown tier: default_enabled=False always; excluded at AMBER, AMBER+STRICT and RED; at CLEAR/GREEN only with the per-run --allow-unknown flag (recorded in the case). It may receive only IOC_TYPES values, never a PERSONAL_TYPES value or a CNPJ, at any TLP. Manual pivot links to unknown-tier sites carry an 'unknown operator' badge, and the same limit holds for links: the P311 lint rejects unknown-tier hosts for PERSONAL_TYPES and CNPJ templates.

Canonical type sets in core/entities.py: PERSONAL_TYPES = {email, phone, username, person_name, cpf, pix_key, plate_br, imei, coordinates, social_account, telegram_handle, telegram_invite, discord_invite, fediverse_handle, bsky_handle, steam_profile, vin, email_headers}.

IOC_TYPES = {domain, url, ipv4, ipv6, cidr, asn, md5, sha1, sha256, sha512, ssdeep, cve, mitre_technique, onion, btc_address, eth_address, xmr_address, other_crypto_address, favicon_hash, cert_fingerprint, analytics_id, plus the P333 structural hashes}. SECRET_TYPES = {jwt, telegram_bot_token, cloud/API keys, private keys, full card numbers} are never sent anywhere or exported.

Module.disclosure is declared explicitly and CI-checked: 'none' (the value never leaves the machine), 'internal' (company-operated or contracted platforms, A12), 'third_party' (an external provider receives the value), 'target' (LIGHT/ACTIVE contact with the investigated host itself). Module.shares_input becomes a derived alias (disclosure in {third_party, target}).

Required registry provider flags (CI-checked): publishes_queries (rule 7: never receives values), reuses_queries (excluded at AMBER and above), fetches_target (the provider fetches the target live: only cached/no-publish modes may be default), sensitive (A4), and personal_data_review {basis, reviewer, date}. personal_data_review must be recorded before a provider that receives PERSONAL_TYPES enters the default set.

Runtime host enforcement: ScopedHttp refuses hosts not declared in Module.hosts (exact or '*.' wildcard) for PASSIVE modules, including on every redirect hop. Disclosure 'none' modules get no network at all, and 'internal' modules only their configured hosts. A violation gives Status.SKIPPED with reason_code 'policy', is written to the case audit and is shown by doctor. The core DoH resolver is the only implicit host and is not charged to modules.

Disclosure ledger: every report lists, from the runtime HTTP event log rather than declarations, the hosts contacted with provider tier, terms class and request counts, and per entity the providers that received its value. The header carries the line 'value disclosed to N third-party providers', with the host list in the appendix.
`v3lum modules` and `v3lum info` show tier, disclosure, terms class and the publishes/reuses/fetches_target/sensitive flags.

Chair files: provider_tier is the registry tier of the proposal's provider. For multi-provider proposals it is the lowest tier among the providers that receive values, and final_conditions state the tier of each provider. Use 'n/a' only for offline, internal or target-contact modules.

A9.option: other: b for geo-restricted official sources reached from the team's real Brazilian egress; a (manual links only) for anti-bot/CAPTCHA walls
A9.decision: Geo-restricted Brazilian official endpoints are automated with honest 'blocked' handling, but only when the team declares that its real passive egress is in Brazil. Otherwise they are skipped with a reason and a manual pivot link. Sources behind interactive anti-bot challenges are shipped as manual pivot links only. A challenge seen at runtime is detected and reported, never bypassed, and the host is short-circuited for the rest of the run.
A9.rationale: All six members separated the two problems the same way. legal_dpo's floor: calling a gov.br endpoint from the team's own Brazilian network is ordinary access, defeating a geo-block through a VPN exit chosen to evade it is circumvention, and anti-bot walls are a refusal of automation under rule 1, so those sources are links only. The architect's floor: requires_egress metadata plus a declared egress_country, a per-run in-memory short-circuit (never cached across runs), no header/UA retries, recorded challenge fixtures. redteam_lead added no IP rotation, cti_lead and osint_investigator doctor verification and the link fallback on every BLOCKED result. analyst_ux's daily circuit breaker becomes A3 demotion after 5 consecutive blocked runs, which respects the architect's 'not cached across runs'.
binding_rules: Module.requires_egress is a frozenset of ISO country codes (e.g. {'BR'}). Setting egress_country holds the ISO code of the default/passive egress (default '' = unknown) and is declared by the team. A module whose requirement is not met gets Status.SKIPPED with reason_code 'egress_country' ('needs BR egress') and its manual pivot link is emitted.

egress_country='BR' only when the team's real Brazilian network is the passive route. It is never satisfied by a proxy, VPN or Tor exit chosen to defeat a geo-block, and IPs are never rotated. requires_egress modules always use the default passive route, never proxy_light/proxy_active.
`v3lum doctor --egress` verifies the declaration on request against a known geo-blocked gov.br endpoint and warns on a mismatch. It never changes the setting automatically.

Sources known to sit behind interactive anti-bot challenges (Cloudflare managed challenge/Turnstile, Akamai bot manager, Vercel checkpoint, DDoS-Guard, CAPTCHA) ship as manual pivot links only, with no automated module.

Runtime challenge, CAPTCHA, geo-block and login-wall pages give Status.BLOCKED (reason_code challenge, geo_block or login_wall, via P321) with a readable reason, never EMPTY or ABSENT. They are never retried with another UA, headers, cookies, proxy/IP, solver or headless browser. FlareSolverr, cloudscraper and undetected-browser packages are forbidden dependencies (P327 lint).

A host that returned a challenge or geo-block is short-circuited for the rest of the run (in memory, reason_code 'circuit') and never cached across runs. Every BLOCKED result emits the source's manual pivot link with the reason.
A source BLOCKED on 5 consecutive runs leaves the default set (A3 demotion) with a doctor notice; explicit selection still runs it.
Portal terms that forbid robots are respected. Official open-data APIs and dumps (LAI, Decreto 8.777/2016) are preferred over portal scraping.
Tests use recorded challenge, geo-block and login-wall fixtures.

A10.option: other: a + legal hold, complete purge, 30-day cache cap and a minimal engagement audit retention; app-level encryption at rest deferred
A10.decision: Case data is kept for retention_days (default 180) and then purged by one routine that removes every copy: DB rows, feedback, evidence, reports including -o paths, sightings and the case's cache rows. Only a value-free tombstone remains, and cases under legal hold are exempt. The HTTP cache is capped at 30 days. A minimal LIGHT/ACTIVE engagement audit (no bodies, paths redacted) follows a separate audit retention. Files are 0600 in a 0700 home. Application-level encryption is deferred, and OS full-disk encryption is the documented baseline.
A10.rationale: legal_dpo's floor (LGPD arts. 15-16 and 18 IV) is adopted in full: 180 days, a purge command and reminder, legal hold with reason and requester, a complete purge with secure_delete + VACUUM and a tombstone, a 30-day cache cap, 0700/0600, redacted evidence. The architect's floor: retention covers every place data lands, datasets and quota counters are excluded, migrations, an end-to-end purge test. The architect also judged app-level encryption to be key management the team does not need yet, and legal_dpo made it optional, so it goes to the backlog. cti_lead's 730-day IOC split retention is not adopted because legal_dpo's floor removes sightings with the case; long-lived IOC memory belongs in the team's MISP. redteam_lead's separate retention for the minimal engagement audit exists only as a setting that defaults to retention_days. Keeping it longer (he proposed 5 years, as the team's legal defence under LGPD art. 7 VI / 16 I) needs legal_dpo's written decision, so the default never goes beyond legal_dpo's tombstone-only floor. analyst_ux supplied the shell-history rules, osint_investigator the per-case hold.
binding_rules: Setting retention_days (default 180) covers case rows, evidence, reports in case directories, report paths recorded in the case (-o), feedback rows, sightings index rows, watch alerts and first_seen state, and the HTTP-cache rows fetched during the case. Datasets and quota counters are excluded.

Setting cache_max_age_days (default 30): HTTP-cache rows older than this are deleted automatically at start-up or maintenance, and `cache stats` shows the oldest entry. No cache TTL may exceed min(cache_max_age_days, retention_days).

Setting audit_retention_days (default = retention_days, i.e. 180) applies only to the minimal LIGHT/ACTIVE engagement audit: authorization reference, scope SHA-256, window, analyst, and the request ledger without bodies, paths redacted. A longer value (e.g. 5 years under LGPD art. 7 VI / 16 I) may be set only with a written legal decision recorded in docs/LEGAL.md. Everything else of the case follows retention_days.

`v3lum cases purge [--older-than DAYS] [--dry-run]` and `v3lum cases delete <id>` share one routine. It removes DB rows, feedback, the case directory (evidence, reports), recorded report paths, sightings index rows and the cache rows fetched during the case (cache keys are recorded per case), then runs PRAGMA secure_delete=ON + VACUUM, keeping only a value-free tombstone (case id, created, purged_at, purged_by, counts).

Legal hold: `v3lum cases hold <id> --reason "<text>" --requester "<name>"` and `v3lum cases unhold <id>`. Held cases are exempt from purge and marked in `cases list`, and every hold change is written to the audit.
Startup reminder: at most once per day, one non-blocking line listing cases past retention (e.g. '3 cases older than 180 days: v3lum cases purge').

Permissions: os.umask(0o077) at CLI start; ~/.v3lum and every subdirectory 0700 (chmod when they already exist); the DB, cache, quota, evidence, report, config, org_profile, licence_allow, secret.key and shell-history files 0600, written with os.open(..., 0o600). doctor warns on looser modes.

Privacy-sensitive modules store only sanitized/redacted evidence (P145). Feedback notes and per-finding votes are case data, purged with the case; only aggregated per-source/per-rule counters without entity values survive.
Shell history: 0600, follows retention_days, `history clear` exists, and lines typed in TLP:RED sessions are not written.
Application-level encryption at rest is not in this build (BACKLOG.md, P3). docs/LEGAL.md requires OS full-disk encryption on analyst machines as the baseline.

Schema migrations (AR04) add the needed columns (tlp, legal_hold, purpose, cache keys per case...). Purge is tested end to end on a temporary home: every listed artefact is gone and the tombstone is present.
Long-lived IOC memory belongs in the team's MISP/OpenCTI (via the P303 export), not in V3LUM beyond retention_days. A split IOC retention is not adopted.

A11.decision: This build ships an organisation profile: own domains, brands, CNPJ roots, ASNs/CIDRs, app ids, suppliers and opt-in executives, each with verification state and criticality. It is a local, schema-validated, 0600 TOML/JSON file that is never exported. Own-asset-only endpoints require verified entries. Membership is computed with the PSL and ipaddress. Seeding is passive and confirmed by an analyst. Ownership tags drive severity and report ordering, and the profile informs the active scope but never becomes it.
A11.rationale: Unanimous (a). legal_dpo's floor: a sensitive inventory that is 0600 and never exported; own-asset-only modules need DNS TXT or a recorded attestation; executives only by opt-in with notice; seeds confirmed by an analyst; changes audited. The architect's floor: JSON/TOML (no YAML in core), schema validation, PSL/ipaddress membership with tests, the profile hash in case metadata. redteam_lead's point that owning a domain does not authorize scanning the CDN behind it makes the scope a separate, confirmed file (stricter than the synthesizer draft and consistent with legal's mandatory --scope). osint_investigator and cti_lead supplied brand variants and criticality, analyst_ux the team-shared path and the single hint line.
binding_rules: The file org_profile.toml (TOML via tomllib, or .json) lives at setting org_profile_path (default ~/.v3lum/org_profile.toml; may point to a team-maintained read-only file). It is 0600, schema-validated with clear errors. There is no YAML in core: PyYAML is an optional extra used with safe_load only.

Entries: domains (verification: seeded | confirmed | txt_verified | attested {by, date}); brands (keywords with accent-folded and IDN/homoglyph variants); cnpj_roots (8 digits); card_bins (the organisation's own card BIN prefixes, used by P357 watch rules); asns; cidrs; app_ids (e.g. M365 tenant ids); favicon hashes; suppliers (used by watch); executives (explicit opt-in only, informed under the VIP-protection programme); criticality per entry (critical|high|medium|low); a third_party_hosted flag.
Membership uses the PSL registrable domain plus a subdomain match, and ipaddress containment for IPs; never string suffix matching. Tests cover subdomains, IDN and IPv6.

Own-asset-only modules (run_on='own_assets_only', e.g. HIBP/XON domain search, stealer domain searches, IntelX phonebook, Hunter domain search) require a txt_verified entry (DNS TXT 'v3lum-verify=<token>') or an attested entry (analyst name and date). Anything else gets Status.SKIPPED with reason_code 'own_asset'. Without a profile they print one hint line, not one error per module. Per-person breach/infostealer modules (run_on='own_assets', A4) likewise treat an address as own only when its domain entry is txt_verified or attested; any other address is third-party under A4 BR9-BR10.
Never exported or sent out: reports, STIX/MISP and case JSON carry only own_asset/third_party tags and the profile SHA-256 (case metadata). Watch and typosquat matching are local.

`v3lum org show|check|seed|verify`. `seed` proposes entries from passive sources (registro.br RDAP publicIds CNPJ, NIC.br ASN list, RIPEstat announced prefixes, M365 tenant domains, CT SAN affiliates, BCB/gov.br lists) as a normal passive scan through the policy gate, never LIGHT/ACTIVE. Every proposal needs analyst confirmation, nothing is auto-trusted, and profile changes are written to the audit trail.

The ACTIVE scope never defaults from the profile. `v3lum scope draft --from-org` writes a draft scope file that the analyst confirms and binds to the authorization reference (A7). Own assets tagged third_party_hosted (CDN, cloud front doors, SaaS, detected by ASN/warninglists) are excluded from ACTIVE network probes unless the scope lists them explicitly.

Findings are tagged own_asset or third_party, and reports list 'your assets' findings first in their own section. Ownership drives the severity rules of P027, P028, P084, P146 and P291, and criticality feeds P302.
LinkedIn 'X-ray' and similar people lookups exist only as manual links or through an official API, never as automated search-engine scraping.

A12.decision: This build ships read-only lookups against V3LUM's own case DB (P375) and the team's own MISP and OpenCTI (P1), with TheHive and the team's primary SIEM via approved saved searches (P2). They are plain HTTP adapters, disabled unless configured, using least-privilege keys from `v3lum keys`. TLS verification is always on. They carry disclosure 'internal' (allowed at TLP:RED) only for company-operated or contracted instances. Queries are bounded and results respect the platform's own markings.
A12.rationale: Unanimous (a). legal_dpo's floor: 'internal' means operated by the company or a contracted processor (community MISP instances and sharing groups are third parties); no write-back; SIEM searches on people only within a case with a purpose and the monitoring policy. The architect's floor: requests-based adapters without PyMISP/pycti, disabled unless URL + key, read endpoints only, a ca_bundle setting instead of verify=False, synthetic fixtures per platform version or the adapter waits. cti_lead set MISP/OpenCTI as P1, redteam_lead the bounded queries and the no-write rule, analyst_ux the timeout and the 'known internally' first line, osint_investigator the query order.
binding_rules: Scope of this build: V3LUM case-DB sightings (P375); MISP restSearch and OpenCTI GraphQL read-only adapters (P1); a TheHive read-only lookup and the team's primary SIEM through SOC-approved templated saved searches (P2). Other SIEMs come later.

Adapters are plain requests-based clients (no PyMISP/pycti runtime dependency), disabled unless URL and key are configured. Keys come through `v3lum keys` and belong to read-only least-privilege service accounts. Adapters call only documented read/search endpoints (GET, or the platform's read-only search POST) and never write back or share; export happens only through the explicit P303 command.

disclosure='internal' (allowed at TLP:RED) applies only to instances operated by the company or a contracted processor. Community or shared instances and sharing groups are 'third_party' providers with tier and terms like any other.
TLS verification is always on. Setting ca_bundle points to internal CAs. No verify=False option exists anywhere in V3LUM.

Bounded queries: TIP lookups time out after 5 s; SIEM searches cover <= 30 days by default, return <= 1000 results and time out after 30 s; each platform has a rate limit. A failure means could not verify (rule 5).
Results carry the platform's TLP/marking, and the higher of platform and case TLP applies. They never appear in a lower-TLP report.
SIEM queries for PERSONAL_TYPES run only within a case with a recorded purpose and follow the company's monitoring policy. Results follow the case retention.
Internal sightings are shown first ('known internally: MISP event #N, TheHive case #M'). Query order: case DB, then MISP/OpenCTI, then TheHive, then SIEM.
Each adapter ships synthetic fixtures for the documented platform version. An adapter without them waits for the next build.

A13.decision: The core chooses egress per request: third-party APIs and DoH use the default route, LIGHT/ACTIVE target contact uses separate proxy_light/proxy_active profiles. These profiles fail closed and leak nothing around the proxy (no environment proxies, no local DNS, no raw sockets outside the core connector). A hostile-host guard, on by default and evaluated after the entity's passive results, refuses LIGHT/ACTIVE contact with flagged or hostile-shaped hosts from the corporate egress unless a non-corporate profile or a recorded override exists. Refusals turn into manual pivots.
A13.rationale: Unanimous (a); redteam_lead calls it the most important opsec control in the build. legal_dpo's floor: separate egress only for LIGHT/ACTIVE, third-party APIs on the default route, a contracted VPN, socks5h, egress never used to multiply quotas, guard on by default, overrides recorded with a reason. The architect's floor: profiles chosen by HttpClient and a core socket connector (the lint fails direct socket use), guard driven by case tags after the passive results, no Tor for ACTIVE, public IPs only on request. redteam_lead added fail-closed sessions with trust_env=False and the ECS fix, osint_investigator and cti_lead the hostile-shaped heuristics and the manual-pivot fallback, analyst_ux the explanatory refusal and the override flag name.
binding_rules: Settings: proxy (the default route, for third-party APIs and DoH), proxy_light and proxy_active (a contracted research VPN/proxy or socks5h). HttpClient and a core socket connector pick the session per request from module opsec and case tags. Modules never choose proxies.
Third-party API traffic always uses the default route, never proxy_light/proxy_active: anonymizers must not breach provider terms or multiply quotas, and P334 budgets are global whatever the egress.

Non-default profiles get their own requests.Session with trust_env=False (no environment proxies, NO_PROXY bypass or ~/.netrc credentials) and explicit proxies. Names are resolved through the profile (socks5h via optional PySocks, or DoH through that proxy), and a test asserts no local getaddrinfo for target hosts.

Fail closed: when a configured profile's proxy is unreachable, its requests are refused and never sent via the default route. Tor is allowed for LIGHT reads only, never as proxy_active. Raw-socket work (TLS handshake, JARM, port scan, AXFR, websocket) obtains sockets only from the core connector, and the lint fails direct socket use in modules.

Hostile-host guard: on by default, on every path including `v3lum run`. It refuses LIGHT/ACTIVE contact, redirect targets included, with an entity tagged malicious/phishing/c2/suspicious in the case or in case-DB sightings, or listed by a consensus source.
The guard also refuses hostile-shaped entities: lookalikes of an org_profile brand, domains registered <= 30 days ago, lure-word domains, and URLs/domains extracted from text or e-mail inputs.

A refusal gives Status.BLOCKED with reason_code 'hostile_host' ('needs non-corporate egress'). The guard yields only when proxy_light/proxy_active is configured, or when --egress-override "<reason>" is passed; the override is recorded in the case audit and the report banner.
The guard decides only after the entity's passive results are absorbed: two-phase scheduling per entity, passive first, then LIGHT/ACTIVE (P376).

The refusal message says why and offers passive alternatives (urlscan search results, archived copies, sandbox reports), the config command for proxy_light and the override syntax. The refused contact becomes a manual pivot. `links --open` on a flagged host shows the contact warning first.

Evidence files and ledger entries record the egress profile. `v3lum doctor --egress` shows each profile's public IP, on request only, via a benign echo service. The report header shows the egress used.
Every Google DoH JSON query carries edns_client_subnet=0.0.0.0/0 (P029). DoH travels on the default route.

A14.decision: This build ships `v3lum watch` as a separate, foreground, bounded command (plus --once for external schedulers) with no daemon. Its rules come only from the org profile. Phase 1 polls approved CT and NRD sources with first_seen diffing; a CertStream consumer is an optional extra and direct CT-log polling is deferred. Alerts are deduplicated JSONL/terminal lines, and hits trigger only capped passive enrichment. People are never watched. Telegram public-channel watch exists only as the council approved it in P357: inside watch, over public t.me/s previews, text only, with no account, session or bot token.
A14.rationale: Unanimous (a). legal_dpo's floor: rules only over org_profile brands/domains and IOC types, never natural persons; ransomware feeds only via terms-compatible access with victim metadata only; no automatic LIGHT/ACTIVE; foreground with max runtime; retention and TLP apply. The architect's floor: reuse the normal pipeline, add --once, keep CertStream as an optional extra with strict bounds, defer direct RFC 6962 polling, offline replay tests with a fake clock. cti_lead and osint_investigator wanted Telegram channel watch to wait for legal review, and legal_dpo allows public previews only. Auditor correction: the council approved P357 telegram_channel_watch 5-1 (cti_lead and legal_dpo in favour, legal_dpo with its A14 conditions), and an approved proposal stays approved unless a team rule or a floor requires otherwise; legal_dpo's floor permits public previews, so A14 adopts P357's conditions instead of excluding it. redteam_lead and osint_investigator noted that local filtering of the whole stream reveals nothing about what is watched. analyst_ux supplied the polling MVP, the one-line digest, mutes and per-rule precision.
binding_rules: `v3lum watch` is a separate command, never part of scan. It runs in the foreground only, with --once for cron/systemd timers, --max-runtime (default 8 h) and --max-alerts, and has no daemon or service management.

Rules come only from org_profile brands, domains, CNPJ roots, card BINs and the supplier list, plus IOC types. No rule may target a natural person (names, personal e-mails, usernames, phones), except own-domain addresses for infostealer exposure. Matching is local, after IDNA->Unicode, accent folding and the typosquat permutation set, and keywords never leave the machine.

Phase 1 (this build): saved hunts re-run on an interval over approved polling sources (crt.sh/Cert Spotter deltas for org domains, NRD feeds), with first_seen diffing persisted in SQLite via a migration.

The CertStream-compatible WebSocket consumer exists only as the optional extra v3lum[watch], with a configurable URL. A self-hosted certstream-server-go is preferred; certstream.calidog.io is a community-tier best-effort source. Direct RFC 6962/static-ct-api log polling is deferred to BACKLOG.md.

Alerts fire only for NEW registrable domains, deduplicated by registrable domain plus certificate serial: one terminal line each, JSONL (timestamp, rule id, matched name, registrable domain, reason, cert sha256, issuer, not_before) and the case DB. Certificate metadata only. Above 200 alerts per hour a summary line replaces the rest. Mutes exist per rule and per domain, and per-rule precision comes from feedback.
Hits only enqueue capped passive enrichment through the policy gate (<= 30 per hour; the rest is listed). Watch never makes automatic LIGHT/ACTIVE contact.

Ransomware victim feeds are used only through terms-compatible access (the ransomware.live PRO key) and only as victim metadata; leaked files are never downloaded or opened (rule 3). Telegram public-channel watch runs only as approved in P357: inside `v3lum watch`, t.me/s public previews only, text only (media and files never fetched, links never visited automatically), no account, session, joining or bot token (rule 1), a curated channel list with a justification per channel reviewed by the CTI lead and legal, and P145 scrubbing before alerts or cache (PAN to BIN + last 4, CPF masked, credentials and leaked records dropped).
Alerts and first_seen state follow retention_days and the TLP (default AMBER).

Bounds: queues are bounded (drop and count), dedupe uses an LRU, reconnects use backoff with jitter and a maximum reconnect rate, and memory is capped. Offline tests replay recorded messages through an injectable transport with a fake clock.

A15.decision: This build ships `v3lum keys setup`, a skippable wizard generated from module metadata and the provider registry. It ranks keys by coverage gained under the active licence profile and shows each provider's licence class and tier in plain words. Keys of noncommercial or license providers are labelled as needing a licence or legal decision. The wizard records each key's plan, tests every key with one benign call and stores keys 0600 behind central redaction. The docs carry a recommended minimal budget. Accounts are created by hand under the corporate identity.
A15.rationale: Unanimous (a). legal_dpo's floor: the terms decide what is offered rather than adding a warning; NC/license keys leave their modules disabled under corporate even when set; abuse.ch is presented per its 2026-10-21 terms; accounts are opened manually by an employee authorised to accept terms; there is one account per provider; keys never appear in logs, URLs or evidence. The architect's floor: content generated from REGISTRY and the provider registry, getpass plus 0600 plus masked display, the test call through health_check, central redaction first. redteam_lead added a licensed passive attack-surface source to the budget and the no-multiple-accounts rule. osint_investigator added the Portal da Transparencia key, analyst_ux `keys test` and the first-scan hint, cti_lead the ranking under the licence profile.
binding_rules: `v3lum keys setup` content is generated from REGISTRY (requires_keys, optional_keys, coverage gained per entity type) and the provider registry (licence class, tier, free_plan_business_use), never from a hand-maintained list.

Keys are ranked by coverage gained under the active licence profile. Each step says what the key unlocks and the provider's licence class and tier in plain words. Under corporate, keys of noncommercial/license providers are shown as 'requires licence/legal decision' and their modules stay disabled even when a key is set. VirusTotal public and Censys free are not offered under corporate.
The wizard records the key's plan ('business' or 'free') in key_plans (A1). Every step can be skipped (Enter) and the wizard can be resumed.

Accounts are created manually under the corporate identity by an employee authorised to accept the provider's terms. No automated sign-up; one account per provider unless its terms allow more; never multiple free accounts, shared personal accounts or other people's keys.

Keys are entered with hidden input (getpass), stored 0600 and displayed masked, and are never logged. Key values are registered with the central redactor (AR01), so they never appear in URLs stored in the cache, in events, errors, evidence or reports.
One benign test call per key runs through the module's health_check (P337), counted in quotas, and reports ok / invalid / quota. `v3lum keys test` re-checks all keys non-interactively.
The first scan with no keys configured prints one hint line pointing to `v3lum keys setup`.

docs/KEYS.md recommended free keys with checked terms: abuse.ch Auth-Key (YARAify/Feodo/SSLBL usable now; MalwareBazaar/URLhaus/ThreatFox pending a licence decision), OTX, GreyNoise community, AbuseIPDB, urlscan (search only), ransomware.live PRO, GitHub token, Portal da Transparencia API key.

docs/KEYS.md paid budget: HIBP Core (from US$4.39/month, own domains), xonAPI+ (from US$9/month), Google Web Risk, a Spamhaus/abuse.ch commercial subscription (or written permission), a licensed passive attack-surface source (commercial Shodan/Censys/Netlas tier, also covering InternetDB) and the OpenSanctions business licence. A DPA/terms review is required wherever personal identifiers are sent.

A16.option: other: a, sequenced (phase-0 contract freeze before the parallel groups)
A16.decision: This build implements every approved P1 and P2 proposal, P3 items only when cheap, and every approved correlation pack and pivot-link pack. It is sequenced. Phase 0 lands the safety core and module contract v2 and then freezes docs/MODULE_GUIDE.md. Phase 1 delivers the group P1 modules with the correlation and pivot packs; phase 2 delivers P2. Source modules become default only after the legal gates exist, LIGHT/ACTIVE modules only after the safety suite passes, and every merge passes the contract, fixture and acceptance gates. Everything else goes to BACKLOG.md with its reason and the condition that would unblock it.
A16.rationale: Five members chose (a). The architect's (a, sequenced) is the technical floor: about 300 modules cannot be written against a contract that is still changing (confidence label and criterion, QUOTA status, metadata schema, provider registry, sanitizer, policy gate, error markers), so those land first and freeze. legal_dpo's sequencing floor: P145, P327 and P377 before any source module is default-enabled, vetoed items only in their veto_lift form, a backlog with legal preconditions. redteam_lead's gate: safety tests before any LIGHT/ACTIVE module. analyst_ux's golden-path acceptance tests gate each group. osint_investigator wanted pivot packs complete even if automation slips, and cti_lead the verified core-defect fixes in phase 0. The must-have list is the union of the members' lists.
binding_rules: Scope: implement every approved P1 and P2 proposal now. Implement a P3 proposal only when it is effort S, adds no new runtime dependency and its group's P1/P2 items are done. Every approved correlation pack (P027, P028, P084, P146, P171, P258, P291) and every approved pivot-link pack ships, the packs complete even if the related automated modules slip.
BACKLOG.md records every rejected, deferred, P3 or unimplemented item with its reason and the condition that would unblock it, legal preconditions included.

Phase 0, before any G01-G14 work: P327, P328, P321, P322, P326, P332, P334, P145, P377, P378, P376, P029, the P311 pack schema and AR01-AR07, AR09-AR11, AR13, AR15-AR17, AR19 and AR24. Phase 0 ends by publishing and freezing docs/MODULE_GUIDE.md as module contract v2, with the four reference modules updated as templates. No breaking contract change is allowed during phases 1-2 without an architect-approved migration.

Phase 1: the remaining core P1 items (P172 with P217 and the P333 first-wave types it consumes, P302, P303, P311 page generator, P324, P325, P336, AR14, AR20, AR21) and the group P1 modules, with all correlation and pivot-link packs. Phase 2: P2 items. P3 items follow the scope rule above.
No source module is default-enabled before P145, P327 and P377 (with the policy gate) are merged (legal sequencing).
No LIGHT module (G03 light) and no G13 ACTIVE module is merged or enabled before the AR20 safety suite passes.
