Merge gate per module: the registry contract test, trimmed real fixtures without personal data, offline tests with FakeHttp (unmatched requests fail, the network guard is active), a provider-registry entry for every host and feed, and the P327 lint. Per group: the AR21 golden-path acceptance tests (time budget, <= 25 non-info findings on benign fixtures, coverage and TLP shown, no secrets in any output).
Dependencies: core stays rich + requests on Python >= 3.11. Every other runtime dependency is an optional extra with wheels, under a permissive licence or LGPL used unmodified (A6).
Vetoed proposals ship only in their veto_lift form (P326, P332). P341 is rejected.

Release blockers (must-haves): P145, P327, P377, P378, P328, P321, P322, P326, P332, P334, P376, P029, P302, P311, P172, P171, P303 (markings and personal-data stripping), P336, P324, P325, P375, P379, the A10 purge and permissions, ACTIVE scope binding (A7) and URL/key redaction (AR01).

architecture_actions.action: Central secret redaction (phase 0). Add redact_url() and redact_text() to core/http.py. They mask every configured key value (Config.keys()), key-like params (key, apikey, api_key, token, access_token, auth, sig) and path-embedded keys such as abuse.ch v2 export URLs. Apply them before anything is cached, emitted, logged, raised or persisted: the HttpCache url column (keep the cache key), EventBus http events and LiveFeed.on_http, HttpError/NetworkError text via _short(), ModuleResult.error and coverage reasons, case DB, evidence and reports. For keyed requests, disable automatic redirects, or strip every credential header (X-Api-Key, Auth-Key, Authorization...) when the host changes, and refuse https->http downgrades. Test: scan with a fake key in a query string and a path, then grep cache, feed, coverage, case DB, evidence and reports for zero hits. Used by P379 and P326.

SSRF and redirect guard (phase 0). HttpClient follows redirects in its own loop (at most 5 hops) and keeps the chain in Response.history. Every hop re-applies the destination checks. PASSIVE modules may reach only declared hosts (P327). ACTIVE targets must pass the scope check after resolution (A7). LIGHT/ACTIVE contact re-runs the P376 hostile-host guard. Private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT, ULA and cloud-metadata (169.254.169.254) addresses, single-label names and internal suffixes are refused unless the analyst's seed itself is internal or the scope lists them. The resolved IP is pinned for the connection. Unit tests use FakeHttp redirect chains and fake DNS answers pointing at internal addresses.

File permissions (phase 0, A10). Call os.umask(0o077) in cli.main. paths.home()/sub() create ~/.v3lum and every subdirectory 0700 and chmod existing ones. v3lum.db, http_cache.db, quota.db, evidence, reports (write_reports), config.json (written through os.open(..., 0o600) instead of chmod after writing), org_profile, licence_allow, secret.key and the shell history are written 0600. doctor warns on looser modes. Tested on a temporary home.

Schema migrations and one purge routine (phase 0, A10). Add PRAGMA user_version migrations: one ordered list in core/store.py, also used by the cache and quota DBs. They add the tables and columns this build needs: sightings (P375), evidence versions, audit and ledger (P324), per-source/per-rule Beta feedback (P325), quota windows (P334), watch first_seen (P030), tlp, legal_hold, purpose and cache keys per case. Replace Store.delete_case with one delete/purge routine: DB rows, feedback, the case directory, recorded -o report paths, sightings rows, the case's cache rows, then secure_delete + VACUUM, keeping a value-free tombstone. Add `cases purge --older-than/--dry-run`, `cases hold/unhold`, the daily startup reminder and automatic deletion of cache rows older than cache_max_age_days. Test migrations from an empty DB and from a v1 fixture DB, and purge end to end.

Per-run deadlines and kill switch (phase 0). Context gets a deadline (start + cls.timeout) that ScopedHttp enforces: request timeout = min(remaining, default), retries and Retry-After waits are capped by the remaining time, and HttpClient._read checks the deadline between chunks to stop slow-drip servers. HttpClient and the core socket connector raise Cancelled for new requests once Runtime.cancel_event is set (Ctrl+C, end of the scope window, scan deadline), so target traffic stops within 2 s. The engine marks overdue runs ERROR reason_code 'timeout' and drops results and evidence writes that arrive after _finish(). New setting scan_deadline (default 90 s; 0 = unlimited; --timeout overrides) renders partial results with a header banner and lists pending sources as SKIPPED 'deadline'. Tests use a fake slow transport and a fake clock. P339 builds on this.

Noise semantics (phase 0). Evaluate noise for every node when it is added (Graph.add_node/_absorb), not only inside _should_expand after the depth/expand checks. seeds_linked and shared_infrastructure skip noise nodes and weak relations (mx_host, nameserver, cert_san, expand=False hosted_domain). Noise applies only to infrastructure entities (domain, IP) and bare-host URLs: URLs with a path or query on big platforms (docs.google.com/forms, sites.google.com, drive.google.com, onedrive.live.com...) are expanded with URL-level modules and tagged hosted_on_legit_platform. Add vocab tags sinkhole, parked, benign_scanner and attributes is_sinkhole, is_parked. Ship data/noise.json built from the P169 warninglists, or remove the references. Regression tests: two unrelated Google Workspace domains are not 'linked' via aspmx.l.google.com, and a Google Forms phishing URL is investigated.

Pivot expansion rules (phase 0). Graph keeps Node.path_confidence = the maximum over paths from a seed of the product of edge confidences, with edges labelled by the P322 model. Auto-expansion is skipped below min_expand_confidence (default 0.5) and for identity pivots from POSSIBLE links. From TEXT/FILE parents only IOC_TYPES auto-expand; PERSONAL_TYPES become expand=False pivots for analyst selection (interactive pick, or --expand-personal with a recorded purpose), replacing INPUT_LIST_CAP for them. Engine.select enforces Module.run_on (any | seeds | own_assets | own_assets_only). Context exposes ctx.is_seed, ctx.depth, ctx.provenance (parent path and relations) and ctx.allowed_sources. P302 uses path_confidence for scoring.

Homonym-safe high_signal_tags (correlations/generic.py). A single module's 'ransomware' or 'sanctions' tag no longer yields a fixed 0.8 CRITICAL. CRITICAL needs an exact identifier match (CNPJ, LEI, wallet, domain, URL) or >= 2 independent upstream families. Name-only matches become MEDIUM/POSSIBLE 'possible match - verify identifiers', and the finding states the match type and propagates the underlying confidence. Tested with a homonym fixture. The other legacy rules are replaced or capped by P171 (multi_source_malicious), P146 (breach_and_infostealer) and P291 (exploitable_exposure).

Result model v2 (phase 0, with P322/P328/P332). Finding and Correlation get deterministic ids = sha256(module|entity.key|title or rule|stable data key)[:16] instead of uuid4, so feedback, sightings, STIX ids and grouping link the same finding across runs. Add Finding.source (registry source id), Finding.observed_first and observed_last (provider timestamps), Finding.criterion and confidence_label, ModuleResult.reason_code and partial. Response gains fetched_at (the cache row time) and from_cache, which propagate to evidence. Keep ModuleResult.finding() backward compatible and stored cases renderable.

Dataset manager v2 (phase 0). Extend register_dataset(name, url, ttl, licence, terms_class, attribution, validate=, min_bytes=, expect=json|lines|csv, pinned_sha256=, max_bytes=, large=). Downloads stream to a unique temp file with an atomic rename and conditional GET (ETag/If-Modified-Since). The P321 classifier and the validator run before the previous copy is replaced, and the previous copy is kept on failure. Names with path separators are rejected. safe_extract() handles gz/bz2/zip with limits (total bytes, ratio, members; no absolute or '..' paths, no symlinks). datasets/MANIFEST.json records url, fetched_at, sha256, bytes, etag and licence. Above ~1M entries a SQLite or sorted-file index replaces the in-memory frozenset. A dataset larger than 5 MB (A6 BR9) is never downloaded during a scan: the module returns UNAVAILABLE reason_code 'dataset' ('run v3lum data update <name>'). Stale copies are served at once while refresh is deferred to `v3lum data update`. Datasets that drive LIGHT/ACTIVE behaviour are pinned (data/active.lock) and refreshed only by `v3lum data update` with a diff summary. Findings and evidence cite the dataset name, sha256 and fetched_at, and coverage/doctor show dataset age. A first-run hint suggests `v3lum data update --essential`. P330, P149, P071 and P159 build on this manager.

Single provider registry (phase 0). v3lum/data/providers.json, loaded by core/providers.py. Per provider: hosts, tier with tier_rationale/reviewer/date (A8), flags publishes_queries, reuses_queries, fetches_target, sensitive, personal_data_review, an HTTP profile (P326), a quota block (P334), error_markers (P321), reliability (Admiralty A-F with justification) and sources. Each source has terms {class, evidence_url, quote, checked_at, reviewer, free_plan_business_use} (A1/P377) and its upstream family (P171). The registry is consumed by HttpClient, QuotaBook, core/policy.py, scoring, the keys wizard and doctor. A CI test requires an entry for every host a module declares and for every feed of an aggregator module.

Plugin hardening (core/module.py load_modules). ~/.v3lum/plugins/*.py load only when setting plugins_enabled=true (default false) and never with --no-plugins. The directory and files must be owned by the user and not group/world-writable. Plugins pass the P327 registration lint, are labelled 'unreviewed' in modules, info and the coverage table, and are listed by doctor. LIGHT/ACTIVE plugins are refused unless their SHA-256 is allow-listed in setting plugin_allow. The same ownership checks apply to ~/.v3lum/specs (P331) and ~/.v3lum/rules (P301).

Safe rendering of untrusted data (phase 0). ui.safe_text(value) = rich.markup.escape plus removal of C0/C1 control characters except newline and tab. Apply it to every module-derived value in ui/render.py, ui/live.py, App.show_single and Markdown table cells; today '[/bold]' in a page title aborts the report and ESC/OSC sequences reach the terminal. One safe_href() (http/https only) is used for every anchor in HTML and Markdown, and ModuleResult.link() rejects other schemes. Entities tagged malicious/phishing/c2/suspicious are defanged and non-clickable (hxxps://evil[.]com) in terminal, Markdown and HTML by default (--no-defang disables it; JSON/STIX stay raw).

First-screen honesty in terminal, HTML and MD. Add a 3-line 'bottom line' block at the top: what the input is (type plus 2-3 key facts), why the score (top-3 contributors with confidence labels, P302), what to do next (highest recommendation). The header carries TLP, mode, egress, partial-result notes (deadline, entity budget) and 'N of M applicable sources answered; K could not verify' (P328), instead of printing case.notes last. The lowest level reads 'no findings'; 'inconclusive' replaces 'clean' below the coverage threshold; skip reasons are aggregated into one line per reason_code. Unit tests cover the header text and the merge order.

Policy and rules-of-engagement wiring in CLI/app/shell (phase 0, with P327 and A7). Every execution path calls core/policy.decide: scan, run (App.run_single), shell, extract --scan, batch -i, watch and doctor health checks. `run` defaults to the configured mode (passive), honours an explicit --mode, and refuses with a hint instead of escalating with max(mode, cls.opsec). --authorized REF is mandatory and non-empty (the const='confirmed' form is removed) and --scope FILE is required for ACTIVE, interactive or not, -y included. LIGHT/ACTIVE `run` writes a case and audit record. Shell `set authorized` binds to `set scope` and expires after 8 h. extract --scan accepts --tlp/--mode/--purpose. Table-driven tests: run_single refuses under TLP:RED, with an exhausted quota and without authorization.

Case purpose, ticket and legal basis (phase 0, LGPD arts. 6 I and X, 10 par. 2, 37). ScanOptions/ScanRequest gain purpose, ticket and legal_basis (codes defined in docs/LEGAL.md). Add --purpose and --ticket flags, with config defaults allowed for IOC-only scans. They are required (interactive prompt; non-TTY refuses) when any seed is a PERSONAL_TYPES entity, or when --breach-scope all or --expand-personal is used. They are stored in the case, the report header and the P324 audit trail.

TLP plumbing (phase 0, A2). Add setting tlp (default 'amber') to config.DEFAULT_SETTINGS, replacing the hard-coded --tlp default 'clear'. --tlp takes TLP 2.0 values including amber+strict on scan, run, extract --scan, batch and watch. TLP is stored per seed and inherited by pivots, and case TLP = max of the seeds. Lowering it below the default is recorded (who, when). The shell gets `set tlp` and the prompt shows the level. Renderers generate the marking: render_case header, HTML header, footer, every section and print CSS, Markdown first line, JSON 'tlp' field, file names. STIX/MISP markings come through P303 and HTML integrity through P336. Tests cover each path.

Interactive console safety. Add a `paste` command: read until a blank line or EOF, build one text_blob, show the extraction preview and confirm before scanning. Bracketed-paste bursts are routed through it instead of starting one scan per line. Below 0.75 detection confidence, always print 'read as <type> (<confidence>); force with TYPE:value', and in a TTY confirm before running noisy packs (username, people). Ship the actor/malware alias index (P295) so malware names are not read as usernames. Document it in the console help.

Test infrastructure (phase 0). An autouse fixture patches socket.socket.connect, socket.create_connection and socket.getaddrinfo to fail unless the test is marked @pytest.mark.live. Key env names are derived from config.KNOWN_KEYS (all aliases cleared; 11 leak today). FakeHttp gains header matching, redirect/history support and host recording (assert requested hosts are a subset of declared hosts plus DoH). A registry-wide contract test checks metadata enums, explicit declarations, registry entries for hosts and feeds, vocab-only names, and a fixture-backed test file per module. It gates every merge.

Safety suite gating every LIGHT and G13 ACTIVE merge (A7, A16). (a) Scope fuzz: an ACTIVE scan over FakeHttp/fake DNS with out-of-scope, CDN and private pivots sends them zero requests. (b) A PASSIVE test module calling an undeclared host ends SKIPPED 'policy'. (c) Egress fails closed when proxy_light is down. (d) Cancel stops a 100-request loop after at most one more request. (e) A fake key never appears in cache, evidence, feed, reports or case DB. (f) ACTIVE issues only GET/HEAD/OPTIONS unless allow-listed. (g) The P145 grep over breach fixtures passes. (h) TLP-leak tests for sightings and exports pass. (i) Every LIGHT/ACTIVE run writes the audit record and the hash-chained request ledger, even with --no-evidence (A7 BR13, P324).

Golden-path acceptance tests (A3 time budget, A16 group merge gate). One test per common input (domain, IPv4, URL, SHA-256, e-mail, CNPJ), using FakeHttp with recorded fixtures and simulated latencies. They assert: first-screen summary within 20 s and completion at p90 within 60 s simulated, <= 25 non-info findings on benign fixtures, could-not-verify sources listed, TLP marked, and no secret strings in any output. The harness lands in phase 1, and each group adds the fixtures of its default modules.

Docs consolidation. docs/RULES.md is generated from the core/policy.py rule table (rule id, text, enforcing test) and linked from README, MODULE_GUIDE and `v3lum info`; today there are three diverging copies with 6 or 7 rules. docs/ROE.md holds the scope-file schema with an example, forbidden actions, ceilings, kill switch, ledger and deconfliction. docs/OPSEC.md covers egress profiles, the hostile-host guard, DNS/ECS and manual links. docs/LEGAL.md holds ROPA and LIA templates, DPIA triggers, the retention schedule, a processor list generated from the registry, the disclosure workflow and the allow-list procedure. docs/KEYS.md holds the A15 budget. README, ARCHITECTURE and MODULE_GUIDE are updated (rules 1-7, LGPD, licence profile, TLP defaults, terms default 'unknown'). A docs test checks that referenced files exist (noise.json, pivot_links, core.feedback).

Platform floor. pyproject requires-python >= 3.11 (3.10 reached end of life in October 2026). tomllib (or JSON) is used for org_profile, scope and spec files, with no PyYAML in core. Every non-core dependency (dnspython, phonenumbers, Pillow, PySocks, websocket client...) is an optional extra with wheels. CI runs on 3.11-3.13 with a dependency licence check (permissive, or LGPL unmodified and optional, A6).

Personal-data masking in every output (phase 0). entities.display_value() and every renderer and export mask CPF with the government pattern (***.456.789-**). Card numbers are truncated to BIN6 + last 4 at detection, and IBAN and other national ids are masked. The full CPF exists only in the 0600 case store and never in file names, links or exports. --show-personal unmasks a single view and is recorded in the case audit. detect.extract_iocs keeps CPFs found in text masked and never expands them.

summaries.A: Chunk A covers the infrastructure sources of V3LUM: domain/DNS (G01), IP/network (G02), URL/web (G03) and e-mail/breach (G04). Of its 114 proposals, 98 are approved, 12 rejected and 4 deferred. The 93 mechanically approved items all stay approved. The five vetoed items are approved only in their veto_lift form: IPQualityScore without its e-mail/phone validators, the posture graders without Observatory scans or new SSL Labs assessments in passive mode, third-party URL scanners as search-only, Hudson Rock behind an allowlist scrub before the HTTP cache, and page capture as a sandboxed, explicit-only extra. Both contested items (MxToolbox API, keyed anonymizer tie-breakers) and the two mechanically deferred ones go to BACKLOG.md with their unblock conditions, and the 12 rejections are kept as a deny-list (dead or challenge-walled sources, Save Page Now, borrowed Google keys, account-enumeration oracles, SMTP probing, plaintext leak services). The binding agenda rules shape every spec. Per-source terms follow A1, so noncommercial and licensed feeds (InternetDB, ctl.shodan.io, Robtex, urlscan free tier, GreyNoise community, SANS ISC, XposedOrNot keyless, OpenPhish, the FireHOL/ET/CINS family) stay default candidates that are skipped under the corporate profile until licence-cleared, while unknown-terms sources (Hudson Rock, LeakCheck public, Lunar, EmailRep, HoneyLabs, the keyless anonymizer and reputation APIs) ship disabled. Where one proposal mixed trusted and unknown-tier or unknown-terms operators (crt.name, MerkleMap, small subdomain sources, azmap.dev, AdGuard/OpenDNS/CleanBrowsing, smet.cz, DomainsDB, dnstwister, unshorten.me, public who-dat), the chair split them into opt-in modules so the default set stays trusted, reviewable and A3-compliant. LIGHT behaviour (favicon fetch, well-known files, web fingerprint, JS extraction, contact harvesting, TLS inspection, redirect tracing) is opt-in and gated on the AR20 safety suite, and passive archive-based paths provide the default answers. Breach and infostealer modules follow A4 (own verified assets by default, metadata only, P145 scrubbing before the cache, generic-address rule, cross-source merging through one HIBP catalogue helper), and own-asset bulk endpoints follow A11 BR4. Recurring safeguards: no submission code paths (rule 7), no account-existence oracles (rule 2), explicit could-not-verify statuses for 403/429/timeouts and error-in-200 bodies (rule 5), shared core helpers (hostname sink, IP-range index, permutation engine, safe-fetch, mmh3, ctx.tls, breach catalogue) and real trimmed fixtures before any keyed module merges. Legal and budget decisions for the human team are listed in the chair's needs_human output.
summaries.B: Chunk B holds 104 source proposals: usernames and social platforms, phones, threat-intel reputation and hashes, vulnerabilities, ransomware and dark-web trackers, crypto assets and the team's internal platforms. The chair keeps all 85 mechanically approved items, defers the three contested ones (P117 Reddit API, P161 isMalicious and P200 RansomPosts, each waiting for a licence decision, a provenance-bearing fixture or a clean chain of title), rejects P201 Tor search because neither veto is lifted, and leaves the 13 rejected and 2 deferred items unchanged: 85 approved, 14 rejected, 5 deferred. Every approved spec applies the chunk-D policy. Licence classes are per source under the corporate profile: abuse.ch MalwareBazaar/URLhaus/ThreatFox, VirusTotal public, ransomware.live, Chainabuse, Team Cymru MHR and StopForumSpam are default candidates that stay off until licence-cleared (Shodan CVEDB and TikTok are licence-gated and opt-in), while memory.lol, Arctic Shift, X oEmbed, SecurityContext, Filescan, scraped community pages and unreviewed IOC feeds stay disabled until their terms are recorded. unavatar.io and the threat-actor-usernames API are left out of the build because A8 bars sending usernames and e-mails to unknown-tier operators, HackerOne's undocumented GraphQL waits for recorded terms and a fixture, and BotScout is dropped for its precision. The username engine follows A5 (a WhatsMyName-based default of at most 100 sites, Maigret as the extended pack, one request per handle per site). legal_dpo's floor removes the paths that breach provider terms (the YouTube handle-page scrape, the X syndication endpoint, Duolingo, and TikTok without TikTok's written permission). The architect's floor reshapes several items: per-platform adapters, API-only Docker Hub and git metadata, endoflife as a dataset plus a rule, crypto graph expansion as an engine policy, and offline-first KEV/EPSS/CVE data with one CVE card and a shared fan-out budget. Read-only behaviour is enforced in code wherever a provider also accepts submissions. Leaked personal data from Telegram and the leak trackers is scrubbed at ingestion. Internal MISP, OpenCTI, TheHive and SIEM lookups stay read-only, injection-safe and TLP-bound. Priorities follow the medians except P128 (a pivot pack that A16 ships in phase 1), P153 OTX and P175 YARAify (needed for the corporate minimum answer set while abuse.ch and VirusTotal are licence-gated) and P207 TRON (a 3-3 tie; the dominant Brazilian fraud rail), which are raised to P1. After audit: the A1 class citations point to the current BR14-BR16 and BR20; the username packs exclude the platforms whose own module checks presence and the YouTube, X and LinkedIn pages that other items' floors bar, and run only sites whose terms are recorded 'open'; mixed offline/online designs (EPSS, VulnCheck, the self-hosted Esplora) are separate module classes with one disclosure class each; shared abuse.ch datasets are downloaded once; the P311 privacy-link, P087 Gravatar and VirusTotal export wording are aligned.
summaries.C: Chunk C covers 119 proposals: Brazilian company and public data, CTI frameworks, file, geo and media analysis, the gated pentest modules and the manual pivot-link packs. The result is 100 approved, 13 rejected and 6 deferred. Every mechanical outcome is kept: the 98 approved items stay approved with no override, and the 10 rejected and 3 deferred items stay as they are. Two vetoes are lifted by adopting legal_dpo's veto_lift conditions. P025 becomes a LIGHT HTML-similarity check of lookalikes, with MX-spy removed and no headless browser. P307 keeps only first-party search APIs (Brave preferred, no SerpApi, no autonomous payments). Two vetoes stand: P058 (torrent history per IP) and P245 (TSE/PEP data). Of the four contested items, P226 (OpenCorporates), P247 (Escavador) and P297 (MalwareIntel) are deferred for budget, licence or unknown terms. Active WAF probing (P280) is rejected, because P072 already carries the passive wafw00f signatures. Chunk D's binding rules shape the specs. Rule 4: a CPF is never a lookup or join key, RFB-masked fragments included; ICIJ and WikiLeaks are searched for entities only; person searches are purpose-bound. A1: DataJud becomes noncommercial; ORKL, the CTI news feeds, DJEN and Tavily/Exa stay unknown until legal reviews them; YARA Forge's NC rules, Malpedia and OpenSanctions are gated by licence. A7: one gate and one ceiling block apply to every ACTIVE module. nuclei is held to the A7 tag set, so cve, kev and takeover templates are excluded until A7 is amended, and JARM and origin checks never touch hostile infrastructure. A9: the DOU scrape is replaced by official open-data dumps because robots.txt forbids it, and PNCP, Compras.gov.br and DJEN wait for fixtures captured from the team's Brazilian egress. The Brazilian chain is P1 and default-on, as A3 decided: CNPJ resolver, CGU and TCU sanctions, BCB authorised institutions, boleto/PIX parsers and validators. File analysis runs in one shared sandbox with FILE-only inputs, and a shared LIGHT fetcher downloads analyst-typed URLs. The 19 pivot packs follow the P311 schema, but phase 0 must freeze it with two additions: an optional per-link max_tlp field, and verified values of curl, browser or false. One priority is raised: P252 to P1, because the P1 modules P219 and P240 need its homonym score. Audit corrections: unknown-tier link hosts take IOC values only (A8), the P233 payment URL is a domain pivot only (legal floor), P269 owns the sandbox and a LIGHT fetcher bound by A7, the IBGE lookup stays inside its module, JWTs are never exported, ETDA waits for a legal class, and the effort-M P3 items are BACKLOG under A16.
summaries.D: Council #1 sets V3LUM's direction as a breadth-first multikit that is lawful by construction. What the council approved is enforced by one policy gate (core/policy.decide) fed by one provider registry (data/providers.json), not by module discipline. The shipped defaults are conservative: the corporate licence profile (noncommercial, license and unknown-terms sources stay off until legal clears them through a recorded allow-list), TLP:AMBER with FIRST TLP 2.0 markings on every page and export, passive mode, unknown-tier providers excluded and never sent personal identifiers, and a computed default set with a measured 20 s/60 s time budget. Every lost source is shown with its reason and a manual pivot link instead of a silent gap. The team rules become code: breach data is scrubbed at one choke point before the HTTP cache, evidence and reports; 403/429/challenge/error-in-200 responses always mean 'could not verify' (a new QUOTA status, tri-state results, nothing cached); personal identifiers are pseudonymised in paths and indexes and never auto-expanded from pasted text; LIGHT is opt-in and seeds-only; ACTIVE needs a real reference and a scope file checked after resolution, with hard rate ceilings, forbidden actions, a kill switch, a hash-chained request ledger and a hostile-host egress guard. The build is sequenced: a phase-0 freeze of module contract v2 and the safety core (policy, statuses, confidence labels, sanitizer, licence and org profiles, HTTP profiles, quotas, egress, redaction, deadlines, SSRF guard, permissions, migrations, dataset manager, test guards) comes before the 14 groups start in parallel. P1 modules follow with every correlation and pivot-link pack, then P2; P3, rejected and deferred items go to BACKLOG.md. In chunk D, 41 of the 42 core proposals are approved, P326 and P332 through their legal_dpo veto_lift conditions, and P341 (DeepL Free report translation) is rejected. After audit, the agenda rules keep every mechanically approved proposal (Telegram public-channel watch follows P357's conditions) and hold the Maigret back-fill of the default username pack until legal_dpo decides in writing.

Written legal decision if the minimal LIGHT/ACTIVE engagement audit must outlive retention_days (e.g. 5 years under LGPD art. 7 VI / 16 I; A10 BR3); until then audit_retention_days = retention_days = 180.

Team declarations and policies: whether the passive egress really is in Brazil (egress_country='BR', A9 BR2); the company monitoring policy and the SOC-approved SIEM saved searches (A12 BR1/BR7); the VIP-protection notice for executives listed in org_profile (A11 BR2); OS full-disk encryption on analyst machines (A10 BR10).
CTI lead and legal review of the curated Telegram channel list (data/telegram_watch.json, one justification per channel) before P357 runs (A14 BR7, legal_dpo's P357 condition).

final_conditions: Two modules. ct_logs (default) queries crt.sh, Cert Spotter and ctl.shodan.io. ct_logs_extra (default_enabled=False) holds crt.name and MerkleMap, whose operators are unknown tier (A8) until a promotion is recorded: excluded at AMBER and above, --allow-unknown at CLEAR/GREEN.

Per-source terms in the registry: crt.sh open (Sectigo, trusted); Cert Spotter keyed = key-terms, keyless = noncommercial (SSLMate: 'personal or evaluation'); ctl.shodan.io = noncommercial, same licence decision as Shodan InternetDB; crt.name unknown; MerkleMap key-terms on a company account.

ctl.shodan.io and keyless Cert Spotter are off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared (licence_allow entry or Shodan licence); Cert Spotter runs with the team's own key once key_plans.certspotter is recorded (A1). crt.sh alone keeps the module useful. Keys certspotter, crtname, merklemap go in config.KNOWN_KEYS, Bearer header only.

crt.sh: GET https://crt.sh/?q=%25.{domain}&output=json&exclude=expired. Sources run concurrently inside one module budget (default 30 s, setting max 90 s; retries on 502/503/timeout bounded by it, AR05). A crt.sh timeout/5xx with no other answer = could not verify, never 'no certificates'. Per-source status is kept.

A body truncated at the core 15 MB cap is never parsed as complete: mark partial=True and use Cert Spotter (after=<last id> pagination, at most 5 pages). Declared max_requests <= 10 per entity, expected_latency <= 10 s.

One shared core hostname-sink helper (also used by P007/P016): split name_value on newlines, lowercase, strip '*.', Entity.try_make + PSL/IANA TLD check, keep names ending in .{apex}, dedupe, provenance list per name. Wildcard entries become a wildcard_cert attribute of the parent, not names.

Run once per registrable domain: subdomain entities reuse the apex result and trigger no CT request. Subdomain pivots are bounded by max_pivots/EXPAND_CAP; cert sha256 becomes cert_fingerprint pivots with expand=False. CT-only names that get NXDOMAIN through DoH are labelled historical and get passive modules only; a DoH error or timeout leaves them unresolved (could not verify, rule 5).

Out-of-apex SAN names become cert_san affiliate pivots (expand=False). Shared certificates (> 20 SANs over > 5 registrable domains, or CDN/hosting shared-cert issuer/subject patterns, P034 ranges) give only a shared_cert attribute: no affiliate pivots, excluded from CR31 and seeds_linked.

Earliest not_before is reported as first_cert_seen (a lower bound of age), never as a registration date. The report shows counts (certs, unique names, earliest not_before, issuers) and the top 20 names; the full list goes to the JSON/HTML appendix.

Brand mode is opt-in (setting ct_brand_search, default false), because the keyword query discloses the brand to crt.sh (as for DomainsDB, P005). When on and the seed is an org_profile domain: one crt.sh identity search q=%25{brand}%25 per scan for org_profile brands of >= 4 chars; out-of-profile names become lookalike pivots (expand=False) for P028.

Tests with trimmed fixtures (crt.sh JSON, Cert Spotter page, crt.name text, ctl.shodan.io JSON): multi-line name_value split, '*.' stripping, out-of-apex names dropped, truncated body, crt.sh timeout still yields Cert Spotter names with partial status, a subdomain triggers no CT request, a multi-tenant certificate links nothing.
P001.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. All six members asked to keep the small operators out of the default set (crt.name, MerkleMap: cti_lead, osint_investigator, redteam_lead, legal_dpo). The chair puts them in a separate opt-in module so the default module holds only trusted providers (A3 BR2, A8 BR12). The chair file's tier, terms and default describe ct_logs: terms is noncommercial for the ctl.shodan.io and keyless Cert Spotter parts, which legal_dpo's floor keeps off under corporate. legal_dpo listed ctl.shodan.io as unknown, but its own conditions let a licence_allow entry clear it, which is the noncommercial treatment; A1 BR14 classes the Shodan free services the same way. The architect's floor: truncation handling, the shared hostname sink, keys in KNOWN_KEYS. analyst_ux: concurrent sources in a 30 s budget, one query per registrable domain, the summary. cti_lead and redteam_lead: shared-certificate rules and first_cert_seen wording. osint_investigator: brand mode, limited to org_profile brands and opt-in because a keyword query discloses the brand, following legal_dpo's rule for keyword-disclosing adapters (P005 DomainsDB).
P001.title: Certificate Transparency search (crt.sh, Cert Spotter, crt.name, ctl.shodan.io, MerkleMap)

final_conditions: DNS only through ctx.dns (core DoH): SPF, DMARC (p, pct, sp, rua, ruf), DKIM over a bundled common-selector list capped at 30, MTA-STS TXT, TLS-RPT, BIMI, CAA and the DNSSEC AD flag. No SMTP/STARTTLS connection to MX hosts (checkdmarc's SMTP checks are not ported). The MTA-STS policy file fetch belongs to wellknown_files (P065, LIGHT), which owns the single MTA-STS parser.

SPF evaluator bounded by RFC 7208: 10 DNS-mechanism lookups, 2 void lookups, loop detection on include/redirect, recursion depth <= 10 and a hard cap of 40 DoH queries per run. It outputs spf_lookups and spf_void_lookups for P027 CR02.

DMARC discovery: for a subdomain query _dmarc.<name>, then the organisational domain (PSL) and apply its sp= tag. Check the external-report authorization record (<domain>._report._dmarc.<dest>) for at most 5 rua/ruf destinations and output dmarc_rua_external.

Rule 5: a DoH error, SERVFAIL, REFUSED or timeout on TXT, _dmarc or MX means could not verify. No 'missing SPF/DMARC' finding is raised on missing data; a dead-DoH unit test proves it (email_basics has this defect today).

SPF mining: CIDRs reached through include:/a:/mx: of SaaS/ESP providers (Google, Microsoft, SendGrid, Mailchimp, Amazon SES... per the noise list) are tagged third_party_mail, expand=False, never treated as the organisation's netblocks, never fed to reputation/attack-surface rules and never eligible for an ACTIVE scope.
Only direct ip4/ip6 mechanisms of the domain's own record become candidate CIDR pivots (expand=False) until RDAP/NIC.br confirms ownership.

Severity by ownership: for org_profile own domains, missing DMARC or p=none -> MEDIUM, SPF +all -> HIGH, SPF permerror (> 10 lookups) -> MEDIUM. Any other domain gets ONE info 'posture summary' finding (SPF/DMARC/DKIM/MTA-STS/BIMI table); P027 CR01 raises it when the case warrants. Absent BIMI/MTA-STS/TLS-RPT is never above info.
DKIM: no key under the common selectors is worded 'not determined (N common selectors checked)', never 'DKIM missing'. Runs on registrable domains and e-mail domains only, once per scan.

checkdmarc logic is re-implemented (Apache-2.0, attribution in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) without importing dnspython; recon-ng (GPL) is idea only. New attribute names (spf_lookups, spf_void_lookups, dmarc_pct, dmarc_sp, dmarc_rua_external, dkim_selectors, mta_sts, tls_rpt, bimi) are added to core/vocab.py in the same change.

Tests with trimmed DoH fixtures: an include loop, a > 10-lookup SPF tree, a dead DoH answer that must not yield a 'missing' finding, a third-party domain without DMARC giving one info finding, an own domain giving the MEDIUM finding.
P002.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. The architect's floor moves the MTA-STS HTTPS fetch out of this passive module into P065 and bounds the SPF evaluator (40 queries, 30 selectors; redteam_lead's 60-selector cap is looser). cti_lead and redteam_lead require the third-party tag on SaaS netblocks so Microsoft/Google ranges never reach scans or scopes. cti_lead and analyst_ux require ownership-based severity, with ownership taken from org_profile as in P027. legal_dpo asked only for the checkdmarc attribution. Data travels through the core DoH resolvers (Google/Cloudflare): tier trusted, terms open (P029).
P002.title: E-mail security posture (SPF tree, DMARC, DKIM selectors, MTA-STS, TLS-RPT, BIMI, CAA, DNSSEC)

final_conditions: IANA bootstrap files (dns, ipv4, ipv6, asn) are registered datasets (24 h TTL, stale copy kept on failure) behind a shared bootstrap helper that whois_fallback (P343) reuses. Query the authoritative RDAP server directly; rdap.org (community tier, volunteer-run) is only a fallback, following its 302.

.br names, and BR IP/ASN space after the LACNIC answer says country BR, always go to rdap.registro.br with the P326 profile: a non-browser user_agent and Accept application/rdap+json. 403/429/timeouts give BLOCKED/RATE_LIMITED 'could not verify' (never cached, so the next scan retries) and emit the registro.br web whois as manual_link.
404 means 'not registered' only from the authoritative registry server, never from rdap.org or after an error. Per-query lookups only, no bulk harvesting (NIC.br and ARIN RDAP terms).
Minimise at ingestion, before res.raw and evidence: keep registrant organisation, CNPJ publicIds, roles, registrar with IANA id and abuse contact, events, status and nameservers.

Drop natural-person names, personal e-mails and phones of registrant/admin/tech contacts (legalRepresentative included) unless the entry is a role/abuse contact. ARIN POCs reduce to role/org; Whois-RWS POC lookups are off by default.

CPF: never unmasked or stored. A publicId of type cpf is discarded and never pivoted. A publicId of type cnpj becomes a cnpj pivot (relation registrant) and its 8-digit root is recorded so branch registrations link to one company.
Emit registrant_kind = org | individual | redacted. An individual-held .br name whose label matches an org_profile brand feeds P028 typosquat scoring.

Privacy/proxy values ('REDACTED FOR PRIVACY', Domains By Proxy, Withheld for Privacy, WhoisGuard, Contact Privacy, registrar-generic addresses) are recorded as privacy_proxy and never used for pivots or registrant clustering (CR32). The list ships as data with tests. Reports show 'redacted (privacy)' neutrally.

Events map to created/expires/updated and domain_age_days (shown in days). Nameservers become nameserver pivots (expand=False). The registrar abuse contact and IANA registrar id stay as attributes for the takedown packet (P345).

Fixtures scrubbed of natural-person data: registro.br domain with CNPJ (bb.com.br -> 00.000.000/0001-91), registro.br 403, rdap.org 302 to the registry, ARIN IP, ASN, a TLD absent from the bootstrap. whois_fallback runs only when RDAP fails and never replaces the CNPJ pivot.
P003.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. legal_dpo's floor minimises registry contacts at ingestion (natural persons dropped, CPF never stored or pivoted, no bulk harvesting); osint_investigator's wish to keep legalRepresentative names as case attributes is therefore not adopted. The architect's floor: bootstrap datasets with a shared helper, 403 as blocked/could-not-verify, scrub before res.raw, scrubbed fixtures. cti_lead: privacy-proxy exclusion and registrar abuse attributes. osint_investigator: CNPJ root and registrant_kind. registro.br RDAP is default-on by decision (A3 BR9). Tier community because rdap.org, a volunteer redirector, receives values on fallback; registries are trusted. Terms open (public registry data).
P003.title: RDAP registration data (IANA bootstrap + rdap.org + registro.br + ARIN)

final_conditions: Requires key 'hostio', registered once in config.KNOWN_KEYS (env V3LUM_KEY_HOSTIO; V3LUM_HOSTIO_TOKEN/V3LUM_HOSTIO_KEY only as aliases). Without it: NEEDS_KEY. The token goes in a header if the API supports it; otherwise as a query parameter registered with the central redactor (AR01).

Key-terms: the key belongs to a company/team account, never an analyst's personal free account, on a plan whose terms permit internal business use. The plan (key_plans.hostio) and terms URL are recorded in the registry before it runs under the corporate profile (A1).

Endpoints: /api/web/{domain}, /api/related/{domain} and /api/domains/{field}/{value} for googleanalytics, adsense, redirects, backlinks and ipinfo. run_on='seeds'; pivots only on explicit -M. Monthly budget via the P334 quota block (<= 80% of the plan); at most 5 requests per entity (max_requests 5). cache_ttl 7 days.

Reverse analytics/AdSense results follow the P061 rules: an id seen on > 50 domains is a shared agency/platform id (no same_analytics link); an id shared with an org_profile own site on a non-own site is a clone indicator, not a same-owner link; same_analytics confidence is at most PROBABLE (<= 0.7).
Redirect relations are recorded with their dates. Backlinks become links_to pivots with expand=False. Results are ownership candidates for the analyst, never scope.
Errors in 200 bodies are mapped through P321 markers: invalid key -> NEEDS_KEY, quota -> QUOTA, throttling -> RATE_LIMITED, never EMPTY.
Merge only with a trimmed real success fixture captured with the team key, plus an error fixture (architect floor). The web view https://host.io/{domain} is the manual_link.
P004.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (architect and analyst_ux voted P3). legal_dpo's floor is the key-terms rule (company account, recorded plan). The architect's floor: one key name with aliases, header token or redaction, the core monthly budget, seeds-only through run_on (AR07 now provides it), and a real fixture before merge. cti_lead and osint_investigator: the P061 shared-id rule and the confidence cap. Key-required sources may be default-enabled (A3 BR5). host.io is a commercial API with published terms and paid plans: tier trusted.
P004.title: host.io domain relations (keyed)

final_conditions: Module nrd_feeds matches locally (disclosure 'none', shares_input=False) against registered datasets: the WhoisDS daily free NRD zip (terms open: 'may be reused, including for commercial purposes', verified 2026-11-26) and the registro.br release list lista-processo-liberacao.txt (open; NIC.br, trusted). Lists are never redistributed.

smet.cz today.txt has unclear licence terms (unknown): it ships as a separate dataset source nrd_smet, default_enabled=False and disabled in every profile until legal records its terms. ICANN CZDS is deferred to BACKLOG.md (needs streaming download-to-disk and per-TLD caps; later only with the company's own account, legal-accepted per-TLD terms, no redistribution, superseded zones deleted).
DomainsDB keyword search discloses the brand: a separate module domainsdb_search, key-terms, default_enabled=False, keywords only from org_profile brands.

domainsdb_search's provider is unknown tier until reviewed, and A8 BR4 lets unknown-tier providers receive only IOC_TYPES values (a brand keyword is not one): it runs only after a recorded promotion to community tier, and its source is then flagged reuses_queries (fail closed) so it stays excluded at AMBER and above.

Lists are fetched by `v3lum data update` or a background refresh into ~/.v3lum/datasets, never blocking a scan for more than 10 s. A missing or > 48 h old list gives UNAVAILABLE reason_code 'dataset' ('NRD lists not downloaded/stale'), never EMPTY. A challenge page or empty file never replaces the last good copy (P321, AR10).

Zip via the core safe_extract helper: in memory, at most 3 members, <= 50 MB uncompressed, ratio cap 100x, member names never used as paths. The registro.br file is decoded as ISO-8859-1 and '#' lines are comments.

Keep a rolling 30-day local window of daily lists, first_seen = list date, so a scan answers 'registered/released in the last 30 days'. first_seen diffing is persisted in the case DB so watch (P030) alerts only on new matches.

Brand matching uses only org_profile brands and domains (P378) and the shared P012 permutation helper (one implementation), including pt-BR combo-squats with lure words and accent homoglyphs. No brand or keyword leaves the machine.

Tag newly_registered (and typosquat when matched) only after DoH confirms an A or MX answer, capped at 100 confirmations per run. registro.br release-list hits are tagged in_release (re-registration risk), not newly_registered. An NRD hit alone is LOW; severity rises only with a brand match plus MX or a fresh certificate (P028).
Wording on a miss: 'not in the last N days of WhoisDS lists (gTLD coverage only)', never 'not newly registered'. For .br: 'no NRD feed for .br: CT + permutations + DoH only'.

Tests with trimmed fixtures (WhoisDS zip, registro.br release list): local match, DoH-confirmed tagging, stale-list UNAVAILABLE, oversized/zip-bomb rejection, challenge page not replacing the last good copy.
P005.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (osint_investigator voted P1). legal_dpo's floor sets per-feed terms: WhoisDS and the registro.br list are open, smet.cz is unknown (so it is split out and stays off until reviewed, which keeps the default module's terms open, A3 BR2), DomainsDB discloses the keyword and is opt-in, CZDS needs an institutional account. The architect's floor defers CZDS for lack of streaming support and requires the safe-archive helper and one permutation implementation. cti_lead: the 30-day window and the severity ladder. osint_investigator: pt-BR combo-squats, dataset validation, the in_release tag. analyst_ux: no scan waits on downloads, honest miss wording. Tier community for the WhoisDS list operator; no value is sent. Auditor: while DomainsDB is unknown tier it cannot receive brand keywords (A8 BR4), so it runs only after a recorded promotion and keeps the AMBER+ exclusion through a reuses_queries flag.
P005.title: Newly registered / released domain feeds (WhoisDS, smet.cz, registro.br release list, DomainsDB)

final_conditions: Requires key 'securitytrails' (already in config.KNOWN_KEYS), sent in the APIKEY header. Without it: NEEDS_KEY.

Key-terms: a company/team account, never an analyst's personal free account. The free plan targets individuals, so under the corporate profile it runs only when legal records that the plan permits internal business use (registry free_plan_business_use=true) or key_plans.securitytrails='business' (A1).

Endpoints: /v1/domain/{domain}, /v1/domain/{domain}/subdomains and /v1/history/{domain}/dns/a. Subdomain labels come back without the apex: append it and validate through the shared hostname sink (P001).
run_on='seeds' (depth 0; pivots only with explicit -M). Monthly window through the P334 quota block (<= 80% of the plan's published limit). cache_ttl 7 days.

Every historical record keeps first_seen/last_seen. Old A records are never current infrastructure. Origin-IP hypotheses (cdn_origin_hypothesis) stay INFO/LOW until passive evidence confirms them currently (the IP presents the site's certificate or serves the site per a scan engine). Confirming by sending Host headers to the IP is ACTIVE and not part of this module.
429 and quota-exceeded bodies give RATE_LIMITED/QUOTA; 401/403 give NEEDS_KEY ('invalid key'); never EMPTY.
The web UI is behind Cloudflare: manual pivot link only (A9).
Merge only with trimmed real /domain and /history/{domain}/dns/a fixtures captured with the team key, plus the existing 401 fixture (architect floor).
P006.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. legal_dpo's floor: a company account and a recorded business-compatible plan before it runs under corporate. The architect's floor: the monthly window, seeds-only through run_on (AR07), real fixtures before merge. cti_lead and redteam_lead: historical data stays a hypothesis, and confirmation by Host-header requests is ACTIVE. Key-required sources may be default-enabled (A3 BR5). SecurityTrails (Recorded Future) is an established company: tier trusted.
P006.title: SecurityTrails API (domain, subdomains, DNS history)

final_conditions: One adapter per provider, each with its own key, terms label, min_interval, P334 budget and per-source status. Module subdomains_keyed: Chaos (ProjectDiscovery, trusted), DNSDumpster, FullHunt and BeVigil (community). Module subdomains_keyed_minor (default_enabled=False): BufferOver and jsmon, unknown tier (excluded at AMBER and above, --allow-unknown at CLEAR/GREEN).

Each adapter runs only when its own key is configured (optional_keys) and reports NEEDS_KEY, never EMPTY, without it. Keys are registered in config.KNOWN_KEYS (V3LUM_KEY_<NAME>; V3LUM_CHAOS_KEY, V3LUM_DNSDUMPSTER_KEY, V3LUM_FULLHUNT_KEY, V3LUM_BEVIGIL_KEY, V3LUM_BUFFEROVER_KEY, V3LUM_JSMON_KEY as aliases) and sent in headers only (DNSDumpster: X-API-Key on api.dnsdumpster.com).

Key-terms per adapter: a company/team account, never an analyst's personal free account, on a plan whose terms permit internal business use; legal records plan and terms URL in the registry before the adapter runs under the corporate profile (A1).

Parsing: Chaos labels come back without the apex (append '.{domain}'); BufferOver returns comma-separated records (split the IP from the hostname); DNSDumpster keeps ~1 request per 2 s (min_interval 2 s). Every name goes through the shared hostname sink of P001 (validation, provenance per name, dedupe).
Per-source cap of 5000 names and a per-provider budget so one huge domain cannot drain a quota. Runs once per registrable domain, on seeds and own assets first.
401/403 bodies map to NEEDS_KEY ('invalid key'), credit/quota exhaustion to QUOTA, throttling to RATE_LIMITED; never EMPTY.
Each adapter merges only with a trimmed real success fixture captured with the team key (only 401 fixtures exist for DNSDumpster and FullHunt, which serve the NEEDS_KEY tests).
P007.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3 (redteam_lead voted P2). legal_dpo's floor: key-terms per adapter, and jsmon/BufferOver are unknown tier, never default and excluded at AMBER and above; the chair puts them in a separate opt-in module so the default module keeps a community tier (A3 BR2, A8 BR12). The architect's floor: one adapter per provider with its own key, status and budget, header auth, the shared hostname sink, real success fixtures before merge. Key-required sources may be default-enabled (A3 BR5).
P007.title: Keyed subdomain sources (Chaos, DNSDumpster, FullHunt, BeVigil, BufferOver, jsmon)

final_conditions: Keyless GET https://digitalassetlinks.googleapis.com/v1/statements:list?source.web.site=https://{domain}&relation=delegate_permission/common.handle_all_urls on registrable domains, cache_ttl 24 h.

Record the linked Android package names and SHA-256 signing-certificate fingerprints as attributes (official_android_apps, added to core/vocab.py). No pivot expansion. The same signing certificate across apps or domains is recorded as an organisation-asset link (info).
One client: mobile_app_impersonation (P346) reuses this module's client and attributes instead of re-implementing it.
An empty statements list reads 'no Digital Asset Links statements published', never 'no official apps'. 429 gives RATE_LIMITED and 403/5xx give could-not-verify statuses (rule 5).
Tests with the trimmed google_digital_asset_links.json fixture plus an empty-list and an error case.
P008.rationale: Approved 6-0. The tally median is P3 (cti_lead, osint_investigator and legal_dpo voted P2); the chair raises it to P2 because P346 (P2) depends on this client, as the architect noted, and the effort is S. legal_dpo found no personal data (organisation package names and certificates). Google public API: tier trusted, terms open (Google APIs terms, no commercial-use bar recorded in the research).
P008.title: Google Digital Asset Links (domain -> Android apps)

final_conditions: Register dominios_gov_br.csv (dominiosgovbr.sisp.gov.br) as a dataset: daily TTL, list date in provenance, stale copy kept on failure. Parse with the csv module and a field-size limit; validate the header and a minimum row count before replacing the cached copy; normalise names via Entity.try_make.
Matching is local (disclosure 'none', shares_input=False, allowed at TLP:RED). An exact listed domain is marked official_gov_br with the agency CNPJ as a cnpj pivot (relation registrant).

Official status is a known_good dampener for domain-level reputation of the exact listed domain only. It never suppresses URL-level findings: compromised municipal/agency gov.br hosts serve phishing and must still be reported.

gov.br lookalike detection: the list is exposed through one shared protected-domains helper (gov.br list + BCB DominiosVerificados, P360) consumed by typosquat (P012), which applies its severity ladder (e.g. receita-federal-gov.*). This official-domain set is separate from org_profile brands and does not change P028's org_profile-only rules.
Dataset missing or failed: UNAVAILABLE reason_code 'dataset' ('could not verify'), never 'not an official gov.br domain'.
Capture a trimmed real CSV fixture before merge (none exists) and test exact match, URL-level non-suppression and the unavailable path.
P009.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (analyst_ux voted P1). cti_lead and osint_investigator: the known_good dampener never hides URL-level phishing on compromised gov.br hosts. The architect's floor: dataset with stale fallback, csv field limits, unavailable status, a shared protected-domains helper and a real fixture. legal_dpo: open government data (Decreto 8.777/2016) matched locally. Government data source: tier trusted, terms open.
P009.title: gov.br official domain list (official vs lookalike)

final_conditions: Local list only (architect floor): the Tranco daily top-1M zip is a dataset fetched by `v3lum data update` (> 5 MB, never mid-scan, A6), extracted with the core safe_extract helper and indexed on disk at refresh time (SQLite table or sorted file + bisect). Lookups never load 1M entries into a Python dict.
No API fallback: a missing list gives UNAVAILABLE reason_code 'dataset'. The module keeps disclosure 'none' (shares_input=False) and runs under TLP:RED. List id and date are recorded in provenance.
Rank is a score dampener only, never known_good or an allow-list, and only for the exact registrable domain. It never lowers URL-level or consensus (P171) verdicts.

Ship data/shared_platforms.json (sharepoint.com, onedrive.live.com, 1drv.ms, sites.google.com, docs.google.com, drive.google.com, forms.gle, storage.googleapis.com, s3.amazonaws.com, blob.core.windows.net, dropbox.com, notion.site, forms.office.com, free hosting, dynamic DNS, URL shorteners...). Hosts on it show their rank but are never dampened.
PSL private suffixes (github.io, pages.dev, web.app, workers.dev, netlify.app, vercel.app, firebaseapp.com...) are ranked per registrable domain under the suffix, never by the platform's rank.
Display as context: 'Tranco #1,234 - popular' or 'not in top 1M' with the list date. 'Not in top 1M' is info only, never a finding by itself; 'young and unpopular' contributes at most LOW.
The Le Pochat et al. (NDSS 2019) citation goes into THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and the report footer when Tranco data is used.
Tests with a trimmed CSV slice: exact-domain lookup, a phishing URL on a top-1k shared platform (sites.google.com) keeps its full score, a PSL private-suffix host is ranked per registrable domain.
P010.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (cti_lead and analyst_ux voted P1). The architect's floor removes the API fallback (cti_lead allowed it at CLEAR/GREEN) so the module never discloses, and requires an on-disk index. cti_lead and analyst_ux supplied the shared-platform list and the rule that rank never dampens URL-level or consensus verdicts. legal_dpo: the citation. Tranco is an academic project: tier trusted, terms open.
P010.title: Tranco popularity rank

final_conditions: Module m365_tenant uses Microsoft first-party domain-level endpoints only: login.microsoftonline.com/{domain}/.well-known/openid-configuration (tenant GUID, tenant_region_scope), GetUserRealm with one hard-coded, documented non-existent local-part constant, and the ODC federationprovider endpoint (tenant id).
E-mail inputs are reduced to their domain before any request. Unit tests assert that no request URL ever contains the input's local part and that the only local part sent is the constant.
Rule 2: GetCredentialType, Autodiscover user checks and OneDrive/Teams/login oracles must not exist in code; a test asserts such URLs cannot be built.

One openid-configuration call per registrable seed domain; GetUserRealm/ODC only when a tenant exists. NameSpaceType 'Unknown' means no Entra ID tenant (EMPTY). An unexpected ODC schema gives ERROR 'schema changed', never EMPTY.
Federation AuthURL/IdP hostnames (ADFS, Okta, Ping) become identity_provider attributes and pivots that get passive modules only. This module never contacts them.

azmap.dev (no published terms, unknown operator) is a separate adapter module m365_tenant_azmap: default_enabled=False, terms 'unknown' and tier unknown, so it stays disabled until legal records its terms and a promotion; even then it is excluded at AMBER and above, one call per domain, cache 24 h.

Related tenant domains (azmap): the full list as an attribute with a count. A related domain pivots only after DNS confirmation (MX *.mail.protection.outlook.com or TXT MS=), at most 50 confirmations within 100 DoH queries and 10 pivots per tenant, relation same_m365_tenant (added to core/vocab.py), confidence at most PROBABLE.

The same tenant id across domains feeds the company correlation as PROBABLE same organisation. A tenant shared by a suspicious domain and others is an attacker-infrastructure cluster candidate (PROBABLE), never proof of ownership. Wording: 'N domains share Microsoft 365 tenant <name>'.

Tenant-related domains are candidate own assets for `org seed` (analyst confirms) and never join an ACTIVE scope automatically. bbot (AGPL) code is not copied; the technique is re-implemented. Tests use the six recorded fixtures.
P011.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (redteam_lead voted P1). legal_dpo's floor: domain-level endpoints only, a fixed constant local part, no user-level oracles in code (rule 2), azmap.dev a separate adapter with unknown terms (so the chair keeps it out of the default module, A3 BR2). The architect's floor makes enumeration structurally impossible through URL assertions and caps the DNS confirmation. redteam_lead: IdP hosts are never contacted and tenant domains never join a scope. analyst_ux: one call per seed and the 10-pivot cap. cti_lead and osint_investigator: PROBABLE clustering. Microsoft public identity endpoints: tier trusted, terms open.
P011.title: Microsoft 365 / Entra tenant discovery (domain-level)

final_conditions: Permutation engine as one shared core helper (also used by nrd_feeds P005 and watch P030), re-implementing the dnstwist fuzzers with the Apache-2.0 NOTICE: addition, bitsquatting, homoglyph, hyphenation, insertion, omission, repetition, replacement, subdomain, transposition, vowel-swap, dictionary and TLD swap. IDN candidates are validated with IDNA/UTS-46 before any query.

BR set: the pt-BR lure dictionary (>= 60 words: pix, boleto, fatura, 2via, atualizar, cadastro, seguranca, desbloqueio, token, resgate, pontos, beneficio, fgts, inss, cnh, detran, ipva, receita, cpf, gov, app, online...) lives in data/brand_lures_pt.json (shared with P028), own work or permissively licensed, never GPL/CC BY-SA.

Combo-squats {brand}-{word}, {word}-{brand}, {brand}{word}; accent homoglyphs (a/á/â/ã, e/é/ê, i/í, o/ó/ô/õ, u/ú, c/ç) plus rn/m, vv/w, l/1, o/0; TLD swaps incl. com.br, net.br, app.br, online, site, top, xyz, shop, vip. Unit test: brand 'itau' yields itau-seguranca.com.br and the punycode of itaú.com.br.

Reverse mode (default, offline, < 1 s): is the INPUT a lookalike of a protected domain (org_profile brands/domains, BCB DominiosVerificados P360, gov.br list P009)? If so: a lookalike pivot and a finding. Forward scans run only on analyst-typed org_profile domains/brands or with explicit -M typosquat, never on pivots, subdomains or arbitrary hostile domains (run_on='seeds').

Forward caps: 150 top-ranked candidates in a default scan (500 with --preset deep or watch); staged checks, NS/A first and MX/AAAA only for registered names; DoH budget 300 queries per run (configurable), <= 10 q/s, 45 s module budget, ctx.cancelled() checks; a hit cap is reported in coverage.

Registration is checked only through the core DoH resolver with ECS disabled (P029), never the system/corporate resolver, and never by registro.br availability calls (P021). RDAP for registered candidates goes through the P003 helper, at most 10 lookups per run (20 with deep), and lookalike registrant data follows the P003 minimisation.
Rule 5: a DoH SERVFAIL, REFUSED or timeout on a candidate means 'could not verify' (counted in coverage), never 'not registered'; only an NXDOMAIN answer for the queried types counts as unregistered.

Severity ladder (unit-tested): registered only = INFO, counted in one info table; one activity signal (MX, CT certificate <= 30 d, NRD <= 30 d, non-parking A record) = MEDIUM; HIGH needs >= 2 weaponisation signals (also phishing-list hit, LIGHT page similarity) AND evidence it is not brand-owned. This applies to BCB/gov.br protected domains too.

Not brand-owned means: not an org_profile domain, RDAP registrant/CNPJ root differs from org_profile (or from the institution's CNPJ in the BCB list), NS/MX not the brand's, registrar not a brand-protection registrar (MarkMonitor, CSC, Com Laude...). Own defensive registrations are listed in the own-asset section, never as typosquat findings. Parking-NS/sinkhole lists cap lookalikes at LOW.

No LIGHT contact in this module: candidates are hostile by default, and HTTP, page-similarity and MX checks live in typosquat_live_checks behind the P376 guard. Lookalike pivots are expand=False. The terminal shows the top 10 by score; the rest goes to HTML/JSON. Lookalikes of org_profile brands feed watch mode (P030).
dnstwister.report (discloses the brand) is a separate opt-in adapter module typosquat_dnstwister: default_enabled=False, community tier, excluded at AMBER and above, one fuzz call per brand.
Tests: reverse match, defensive registration, the 'itau' combo set, parked cap, cap hit, ECS present on every DoH query.
P012.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. cti_lead, osint_investigator and analyst_ux supplied the severity ladder and own-asset suppression, reconciled with P028 (cti_lead's two-signal HIGH, osint_investigator's MEDIUM for one signal, BCB banks not HIGH by themselves). redteam_lead: DoH without ECS only and no LIGHT contact. legal_dpo's floor: Apache NOTICE, no copyleft word lists, dnstwister opt-in and excluded at AMBER+, P003 minimisation, no registro.br availability calls. The architect's floor: one shared helper, IDNA validation, staged checks with a hard DoH budget, seeds only, expand=False pivots. analyst_ux: the reverse mode and the 150-candidate interactive cap. The BCB and gov.br lists stay protected domains as the approved proposal says. Tier community because RDAP fallback goes through rdap.org; terms open (own code over DoH/RDAP).
P012.title: Typosquat / brand-impersonation engine (dnstwist algorithms + DoH registration check)

final_conditions: A correlation rule in v3lum/correlations/ownership.py (architect floor), not a module with clients. It reads facts already in the graph from rdap (registrant CNPJ/org), ct_logs (certificate O=), dns_records/email_security_posture (MX/SPF tenancy), m365_tenant (tenant id) and web_fingerprint or the archived homepage snapshot (P059). No network calls.

CONFIRMED only from authoritative data: the RDAP registrant CNPJ root (registro.br publicIds) matches org_profile cnpj_roots or the queried company, or the domain is an org_profile own domain. Only CONFIRMED marks an asset own/known_good.

PROBABLE at most: an OV/EV certificate O= match, especially with a DNS tenancy signal (MX/SPF/M365 tenant). A CNPJ printed on the site never confirms ownership: at most POSSIBLE (fake stores copy real companies' CNPJs). POSSIBLE is worded 'unconfirmed link'.

A site CNPJ that differs from the RDAP registrant CNPJ, or a site CNPJ on a domain <= 90 days old without a registry match, raises MEDIUM 'CNPJ displayed does not match registrant' (tags fraud, clone indicator). Site CNPJs are validated offline by check digits (P232); an invalid CNPJ on a commercial site is suspicious.

The verdict lists its evidence bullets with evidence ids ('RDAP CNPJ = org CNPJ root', 'CT O= matches', 'MX in the same M365 tenant'). In passive mode the rule uses RDAP/CT/DNS facts only, and the report says when no homepage evidence was available.

Person ownership only for a person the analyst typed as a seed, inside a case with a recorded purpose, from public registrant data already returned by RDAP/CT. CPF is never unmasked. Natural-person matches are POSSIBLE/PROBABLE with evidence, tagged privacy, never auto-pivoted (expand=False), and follow the case retention (A10).

Homepage facts come only from web_fingerprint (LIGHT, analyst-typed seeds, P376 guard) or archived snapshots. Candidates from typosquat/NRD/CT are never fetched live. CONFIRMED/PROBABLE results feed the report and `org seed` proposals (analyst-confirmed), never an ACTIVE scope.
Unit tests on synthetic graphs, one per verdict level, including the copied-footer case and an RDAP-contradicted footer CNPJ.
P013.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (osint_investigator voted P1). The architect's floor turns the Céos verifier into a rule over existing facts, which also removes the module's own LIGHT homepage fetch. cti_lead and osint_investigator: only registry data confirms, a displayed CNPJ is at most POSSIBLE and a mismatch is a fraud signal (the Céos 'published CNPJ confirms' rule is not ported). legal_dpo's floor: person ownership only for analyst-supplied persons with a purpose, never auto-pivoted. redteam_lead: no live visits to candidates and no scope effect. analyst_ux: evidence bullets and wording. A correlation rule: tier and terms n/a.
P013.title: Domain ownership verifier (company + person) via RDAP, homepage and CT (Céos port)

final_conditions: Passive endpoints only, held in a code allow-list: hostsearch, reverseiplookup, aslookup, dnslookup, analyticslookup. A test asserts that nmap, zonetransfer, mtr, httpheaders and pagelinks URLs cannot be built (they make HackerTarget probe the target).

Plain-text errors in HTTP 200 are matched before parsing (P321 markers): 'API count exceeded' -> QUOTA with the provider marked exhausted for the day; 'error check your search parameter' -> ERROR; 'no records found' -> EMPTY.

Quota through the provider-keyed P334 block: 50/day per egress IP (budget <= 80%), shared by every module calling api.hackertarget.com. Keyless use runs only on seeds (run_on='seeds'); pivots use it only with a key.

Optional key 'hackertarget' in config.KNOWN_KEYS (V3LUM_HACKERTARGET_KEY as alias), sent in the URL only through the central redactor (AR01). Key-terms: a company/team account on a plan recorded by legal (key_plans.hackertarget). Keyless use under corporate needs legal to record free_plan_business_use=true from HackerTarget's free-tier terms (A1).
analyticslookup results go through the P061 shared-id rule.
Reverse-IP answers with > 50 domains, or on CDN/shared-hosting IPs (P034), become a count attribute only: no pivots, no co-hosting correlation.
An exhausted quota gives ONE report line per scan ('HackerTarget free quota used for this egress IP: add a key'), not one per entity.
Tests with the six recorded fixtures, including quota_exceeded, and the forbidden-endpoint assertion.
P014.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (cti_lead voted P3). legal_dpo's floor: never wire the active endpoints (scanning by proxy), key-terms for the key and the documented free quota keyless. The architect's floor: a code allow-list with a test, error strings before parsing, a provider-keyed daily budget, the key only behind redaction. osint_investigator and cti_lead: seeds first and the P061 rule. analyst_ux: one quota line and the shared-hosting cap. HackerTarget is a small company with a long public record: tier community.
P014.title: HackerTarget free API (hostsearch, reverse IP, ASN, analytics lookup)

final_conditions: Per-source status, terms label and budget for mnemonic, Robtex and CIRCL, so legal can disable one without losing the others. Registry: Robtex free API = noncommercial ('non-commercial, low volume'), tier community; CIRCL pDNS = license (CSIRT access granted on request), tier trusted.

mnemonic pDNS v3 keyless (public TLP:CLEAR records, tier trusted) is classed open only once legal records its terms with evidence (legal_dpo: recorded before the corporate default); until then it is skipped under the corporate profile with reason_code 'licence'.

Robtex is off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared (licence_allow entry or a Robtex pro plan); while skipped it emits its web page (robtex.com/dns-lookup/{domain}, /ip-lookup/{ip}) as manual link. CIRCL runs only with the team's own vetted account and a licence_allow entry recording the CIRCL grant.

mnemonic: limit 25 per page, offset pagination capped at 4 pages; epoch-millisecond timestamps; optional key 'mnemonic' raises the quota. Robtex: NDJSON parsed line by line, skipping malformed or truncated lines; min_interval >= 2 s and its published 10 requests/hour per egress IP as a P334 budget.

CIRCL: credentials registered as two keys (circl_pdns_user, circl_pdns_pass) and sent only in the Authorization header (basic auth), never in URLs. CIRCL TLP/handling rules apply: CIRCL-sourced records are not exported outside the team (STIX/MISP) unless CIRCL allows. One COF/NDJSON parser for all providers.

Every record keeps first_seen/last_seen and the source. Records are ordered by last_seen; records last seen more than 12 months ago are marked historical, never current infrastructure, and do not pivot by default.

IP -> domains on CDN/shared-hosting IPs (P034 labels or > 50 co-hosted names) are stored as counts, not pivots, and are excluded from shared-infrastructure correlations. On dedicated IPs (<= 50 names) co-hosted domains become hosted_domain pivots (phishing kits commonly share one VPS).
Resolutions to known sinkhole IPs tag the domain sinkholed. Cap 200 records per entity; the report shows 'resolved to N IPs since <date>' and a table capped at 20 rows.
Tests with the recorded mnemonic and Robtex fixtures (pagination, NDJSON with a truncated line, CDN count-only, sinkhole tag) and a synthetic CIRCL fixture for the auth header.
P015.rationale: Approved 6-0. The tally median is P2 on a 3-3 split (cti_lead, osint_investigator and analyst_ux voted P1); the chair keeps P2. legal_dpo's floor: per-adapter terms (Robtex non-commercial with its 10/hour limit, mnemonic terms recorded, CIRCL only with the team's own vetted account and its sharing limits). The architect's floor: per-source status, capped pagination, NDJSON robustness, basic auth in headers only. cti_lead, osint_investigator and analyst_ux: timestamps, the 12-month historical line, shared-hosting counts, sinkholes and the caps. Terms is noncommercial for the Robtex part, which stays off under corporate until licence-cleared. Auditor: mnemonic's corporate default waits for legal's recorded terms (legal floor).
P015.title: Passive DNS (mnemonic, Robtex, CIRCL pDNS)

final_conditions: One adapter per source with its own token bucket and per-source status; a blocked source is recorded as BLOCKED, never as zero names, and coverage shows 'k/N sources answered'. Adapters run concurrently inside one 30 s module budget. Runs once per registrable domain.

Default module subdomains_passive: THC ip.thc.org (community tier; terms open, reviewed by legal_dpo: free service, no contractual bar). Its POST lookup returns {domains:[{domain,last_seen_on}], next_page_state}: loop while next_page_state is set (at most 10 pages, max_requests 10), honour x-ratelimit-remaining, 429 = RATE_LIMITED, last_seen_on flags stale hosts.

Opt-in module subdomains_passive_extra (default_enabled=False, unknown tier until a promotion is recorded, excluded at AMBER and above): AnubisDB (anubisdb.com), Subdomain Center, subdomain.app and ScanMalware. myssl.com (CN operator, terms not reviewed) and RapidDNS (HTML scraping) are separate toggles with terms 'unknown' until legal records them; RapidDNS needs a recorded ToS/robots review.

Registry terms per feed (A1 BR3): THC, AnubisDB and Subdomain Center are 'open' (legal_dpo: free services with no published terms, no contractual bar); subdomain.app and ScanMalware get entries recorded by legal with evidence before they run; myssl.com and RapidDNS stay 'unknown' until legal records them (RapidDNS after the ToS/robots review).

Every name goes through the shared hostname sink of P001 and is merged with ct_logs into ONE deduped subdomain attribute with per-name provenance. Per-source cap 5000 names; partial flags honoured (ScanMalware degraded/partial/stale/subdomains_truncated, subdomain.app total > count, myssl code != 0).

Wildcard detection through ctx.dns.wildcard (P029): resolve two random 16-char labels and compare answers (Cloudflare NOERROR/NODATA quirk); names resolving only to wildcard answers are dropped. DoH resolution is capped at 300 names per run; the rest stay unresolved with expand=False.

Names seen only in one unknown-tier or noisy source (AnubisDB, Subdomain Center) are 'unconfirmed' unless they resolve (non-wildcard) or a second source agrees, and are never shown as assets otherwise. Names with an NXDOMAIN answer are labelled historical; DoH errors or timeouts leave them unresolved (could not verify, rule 5).

Only resolving, non-CDN-only names pivot (engine cap 12), prioritising telling labels (vpn, sso, mail, admin, dev, api). Discovered names get passive modules only. Names resolving to private, loopback or link-local addresses give a LOW 'internal address in public DNS' finding and are never contacted or pivoted.

Challenge pages (AnubisDB Cloudflare 'Attention Required', RapidDNS challenges) give BLOCKED reason_code 'challenge', are never retried with another UA or identity (A9), and lead to A3 demotion after 5 consecutive blocked runs. RapidDNS keeps min_interval >= 2 s and stops on Response.blocked.
Each adapter ships its own trimmed fixture (THC lookup, AnubisDB JSON and 403 page, Subdomain Center, subdomain.app...).
P016.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (redteam_lead voted P1). Tiers differ between members: legal_dpo rated AnubisDB and Subdomain Center community and ScanMalware unknown, osint_investigator the reverse. The A8 definitions require published terms for community tier, so the chair takes the stricter reading: only THC is community and default; the rest is opt-in and unknown until promoted. At the default TLP:AMBER unknown-tier sources are excluded anyway, so the outcome matches every member's intent. legal_dpo's floor: no CAPTCHA bypass, RapidDNS only after a ToS/robots review, myssl kept out. The architect's floor: per-source status and buckets, the shared sink, wildcard detection, caps, own fixtures. redteam_lead: internal-address findings and passive-only pivots. analyst_ux: one merged attribute, the budget and the label priority.
P016.title: Keyless passive subdomain aggregator (THC, AnubisDB, Subdomain Center, subdomain.app, myssl, ScanMalware, RapidDNS)

final_conditions: Implement only if a live keyed response can be captured from the team's corporate egress during implementation (recorded by doctor) to build trimmed real fixtures. Otherwise the module is not merged and goes to BACKLOG.md with reason 'unreachable from the research egress (connection reset)' (architect floor: merge gate).

Requires key 'validin' in config.KNOWN_KEYS (V3LUM_VALIDIN_KEY as alias), sent in a header; NEEDS_KEY without it. Key-terms: a company/team account; legal confirms that the Community tier permits internal business use (registry free_plan_business_use) or records a paid plan before it runs under corporate.
Connection resets, 403 and timeouts give could-not-verify statuses (BLOCKED/ERROR with reason), never EMPTY (rule 5). Daily/monthly Community caps go into the P334 quota block.

Domain/IP DNS history keeps first_seen/last_seen. Host-response features (title, body and banner hashes) and certificates become pivots with expand=False and feed phishing-kit clustering as hypotheses.
default_enabled=False until doctor --sources shows it reachable from the team network; explicit -M or --preset deep runs it.
P017.rationale: Approved 5-0 with one defer (architect) at median P3. The architect's defer rests on the module contract: no response was captured, so no real fixture exists. The chair makes that a hard merge condition, as cti_lead and osint_investigator proposed (backlog with reason 'unreachable' otherwise). legal_dpo's floor: key-terms with a recorded business-compatible plan. Kept opt-in while reachability is unproven (analyst_ux: otherwise only 'could not verify' lines). Validin is a small commercial provider with published terms: tier community.
P017.title: Validin passive DNS / host responses / certificates (community key)

final_conditions: cl0q is a small operator: tier unknown (A8) until a promotion is recorded. default_enabled=False; excluded at AMBER, AMBER+STRICT and RED; at CLEAR/GREEN only with --allow-unknown. It receives only IOC_TYPES values (favicon hashes, domains, ASNs), never personal identifiers.

Requires key 'cl0q' in config.KNOWN_KEYS (V3LUM_CL0Q_KEY as alias), sent only in the X-API-Key header, never as ?key= (the cache stores URLs). Without it: NEEDS_KEY. Key-terms: a company/team account on a plan recorded by legal before it runs under corporate.
Main use: reverse favicon-hash lookups. The mmh3 favicon hash is computed locally by the shared core helper of favicon_hash (P062); only the hash leaves the machine.
Results are hypotheses: relation related, expand=False, confidence at most POSSIBLE (<= 0.5).
Free tier limits (30 req/min, 1,000/day) go into the P334 quota block; 401 'missing API key' gives NEEDS_KEY, throttling RATE_LIMITED, daily exhaustion QUOTA.
Merge only with a trimmed real success fixture captured with the team key (only the 401 fixture exists).
P018.rationale: Approved 4-0 with two defers (cti_lead, analyst_ux: the Shodan/FOFA/Netlas favicon pivots already cover the need) at median P3. legal_dpo and osint_investigator classify cl0q as unknown tier, so it is never default and excluded at AMBER and above (A3 BR2, A8). The architect's floor: header-only key, real fixture before merge, the shared mmh3 helper and a confidence cap.
P018.title: cl0q domain search (favicon-hash / tech / ASN reverse lookups)

P019.rationale: Contested 3-2-1 (yes: redteam_lead, legal_dpo, architect; reject: cti_lead, analyst_ux; defer: osint_investigator). The chair defers it.
