Every yes vote describes a low-value opt-in second opinion. legal_dpo's own condition classes the anonymous tier as unknown terms, so under A1 it could not run at all until reviewed. cti_lead and analyst_ux show it duplicates dnsbl (P045) and email_security_posture (P002), with long-tail lists that list whole allocations and a risk of double-counting listings in the score. osint_investigator's middle path is adopted: a MxToolbox SuperTool manual pivot link belongs in the G14 link pack now, and BACKLOG.md records the unblock condition: legal records the MxToolbox API terms, the team holds a company key, and a coverage gap over P045 is shown. If built later: command allow-list (blacklist, mx, spf, dmarc, dns) with a test that smtp/http/https/ping/tcp can never be requested.
P019.title: MxToolbox REST API (blacklist/MX/SPF lookups)

final_conditions: Module protective_dns queries Cloudflare security.cloudflare-dns.com (1.1.1.2) and family.cloudflare-dns.com (1.1.1.3) through the JSON DoH layer, and Quad9 dns.quad9.net (RFC 8484 wire format). Registry: Cloudflare and Quad9 = open, tier trusted.

Opt-in module protective_dns_extra (default_enabled=False) holds AdGuard (dns.adguard-dns.com, family.adguard-dns.com), OpenDNS (doh.opendns.com) and CleanBrowsing. AdGuard and OpenDNS stay terms 'unknown' until legal records their terms; CleanBrowsing's free filters are 'for parents, not organizations' (noncommercial) and run only with a paid team account recorded as a licence.

Wire-format resolvers go only through dnspython (optional extra); without it those adapters report UNAVAILABLE reason_code 'package'. No hand-rolled DNS wire parser. ECS is never sent (P029). One query per resolver per name; cache only for the record TTL.

Each resolver endpoint declares a category: security (Quad9, Cloudflare 1.1.1.2, CleanBrowsing security, OpenDNS standard), family/adult (Cloudflare 1.1.1.3, AdGuard family, CleanBrowsing family, OpenDNS FamilyShield) or ads (AdGuard default). Only security-category blocks are maliciousness signals.

Blocked = the filtered answer matches the bundled per-resolver block-signature table (sinkhole/block-page IPs, 0.0.0.0, NXDOMAIN) AND the unfiltered core DoH reference resolves the name. The signature table ships as data with tests.

A block only by family/ads resolvers while the security sibling resolves gives an info tag 'content filter (adult/ads)' with zero risk; test: 1.1.1.3 blocks while 1.1.1.2 resolves gives no malicious finding.

Severity: one security resolver blocking = LOW 'blocked by <resolver>'; >= 2 = MEDIUM naming them. All protective-DNS votes count as ONE upstream family in P171 consensus (their feeds overlap), so HIGH comes only with another independent family.
Rule 5: no answer, REFUSED or timeout = 'could not verify <resolver>'. A full pass reads 'not blocked by N security resolvers at <time>', never 'clean'.
Tests with the recorded Cloudflare security/family and AdGuard family fixtures plus synthetic block-page, NXDOMAIN-with-reference and timeout cases.
P020.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (cti_lead P1, architect P3). legal_dpo's floor sets per-resolver terms: CleanBrowsing excludes organisations, OpenDNS and AdGuard need recorded terms, Cloudflare and Quad9 may run by default. The chair puts the not-yet-cleared resolvers in an opt-in module so the default module stays open and trusted (A3 BR2). The architect's floor: wire format only via dnspython, a bundled block-signature table, block only when the reference resolves. cti_lead and analyst_ux: only security-category blocks count, family/ads blocks are content context. Severity takes the lower of the members' ladders (cti_lead, osint_investigator) because P171 treats these resolvers as one family.
P020.title: Protective-DNS block check (Cloudflare Security/Families, AdGuard, Quad9, OpenDNS, CleanBrowsing)

final_conditions: applies() only to individual .br names in a case: own .br domains and .br lookalikes found by P012, at most 20 names per run. Never the bulk registration checker for typosquat permutations (DoH/RDAP do that), per registro.br anti-abuse terms.

Primary: the registro.br avail/raw endpoint; fallback: BrasilAPI registrobr (community tier, MIT), which discloses the name to a third party (shares_input=True) and keeps its own status. The BrasilAPI body is validated for error-in-200.

Adds only availability and release-process status (registered / available / in release process) and an expiry fallback when rdap.registro.br is blocked. Registration dates and the CNPJ pivot stay with rdap (P003); this module is never a CNPJ source.
min_interval >= 5 s on registro.br, cache 24 h. 403/429/timeouts give BLOCKED/RATE_LIMITED (could not verify). 'available' or 'in release' is claimed only from a normal API answer.
Tests with the recorded registro.br avail and BrasilAPI fixtures plus a 403 case.
P021.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. legal_dpo's floor: individual names only, a per-run cap and no bulk availability probing. The architect's floor: .br only, availability/release status only (no overlap with rdap), could-not-verify mapping. Kept opt-in as drafted (analyst_ux). Tier community because BrasilAPI receives the name on fallback; registro.br is trusted. Terms open (public registry service, MIT community API).
P021.title: registro.br domain availability/status (registro.br API + BrasilAPI)

final_conditions: One adapter per provider (WhoisXML API, Whoxy, WhoisFreaks), each with its own key in config.KNOWN_KEYS, status and credit budget (P334 monthly window). Company-paid keys only; legal records the licence/purchase in licence_allow before an adapter runs under corporate. WhoisXML and Whoxy take keys in the URL: only through the central redactor (AR01).
default_enabled=False. Never runs on auto-pivoted entities: run_on='seeds' or explicit -M selection. Results are candidates, never scope.

Reverse WHOIS by registrant e-mail or name only when that registrant value came from a WHOIS/RDAP record already in the case (no free-text person search), the analyst selected it, and the case has a recorded purpose (fraud/actor infrastructure). Never people-search (rule 4).

Privacy/proxy and redacted registrant values (the P003 privacy_proxy list, placeholder e-mails with privacy, proxy, redacted, whoisguard or contact-form patterns) are never used as reverse-WHOIS selectors or for CR32 clustering.

Minimise at ingestion: keep domain, registrar, dates and the matching field; drop other personal fields. Natural-person values are kept only as the link between hostile assets, tagged privacy and kept under case retention (A10).
Historical records carry their record date; pre-2018 (pre-GDPR) data is labelled historical. CR32 confidence follows the match field: e-mail > organisation > name.

cache_ttl 30 days (within cache_max_age_days); person-name/e-mail queries are removable with the cache purge. Error bodies map to NEEDS_KEY (Whoxy {status:0,'Invalid API Key'}, WhoisFreaks 400 'Please provide apikey') or QUOTA (credits exhausted).
Each adapter merges with a trimmed real success fixture captured with the team key, plus its error fixture.
P022.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3 (osint_investigator voted P2). legal_dpo's floor: company-paid keys with recorded licence terms, off by default, reverse WHOIS on persons only inside a case with a purpose, minimisation, privacy tag and retention. osint_investigator tightened the selector rule (only registrant values already found in the case). The architect's floor: one adapter per provider with budgets, seeds only, redaction for URL keys, real fixtures. cti_lead: privacy-proxy exclusion and historical labels. Tier community (Whoxy and WhoisFreaks are small companies; WhoisXML is trusted); terms license (paid credits).
P022.title: WHOIS history / reverse WHOIS (WhoisXML, Whoxy, WhoisFreaks)

final_conditions: Keyless OONI measurements API (api.ooni.io measurements and aggregation, ?domain=&probe_cc=&limit=), probe_cc=BR by default plus the case country; pagination via metadata.next_url, capped at 2 pages.
Context only: anomalies or confirmed blocking per country (court- or ANATEL-ordered blocks, DNS tampering) are shown as info and never contribute to the risk score.

OONI data is reused with attribution (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and the report footer when used). The research did not confirm the exact Creative Commons variant: legal records it with evidence before merge, and if it carries a NonCommercial clause the source is classed noncommercial and is off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared.
Opt-in: default_enabled=False; runs with -M ooni or --preset deep. Errors and timeouts = could not verify.
Tests with the recorded measurements and aggregation fixtures.
P023.rationale: Approved 4-0 with two defers (cti_lead, analyst_ux: low signal for a CTI cell) at median P3. osint_investigator: context only, BR probes by default. legal_dpo: attribution under the OONI data licence. The architect found it bounded and fixture-backed. Opt-in as drafted. OONI is an established non-profit measurement project: tier trusted, terms open (CC data with attribution, queried at runtime).
P023.title: OONI censorship measurements per domain

P024.rationale: Rejected 0-6, as the synthesizer proposed. sub.md and recon.cloud are dead, certificatedetails.com sits behind an anti-bot challenge (rule 1) and the openSquat NRD feed would require impersonating its client (legal_dpo, architect). crt.sh, Cert Spotter and WhoisDS (P001, P005) cover the need. Recorded in BACKLOG.md as a rejection so the sources are not re-added (analyst_ux).
P024.title: Dead or blocked domain sources (sub.md, certificatedetails.com, recon.cloud, openSquat NRD)

final_conditions: veto_lift (1): MX-spy is removed entirely: no SMTP dialogue (EHLO/MAIL FROM/RCPT TO) with any server in any mode. Mail capability is inferred passively from DNS facts already in the graph (MX, null MX, SPF, DMARC) and shown as 'can receive mail (reply/BEC risk)'. A unit test asserts no connection to ports 25, 465 or 587.

veto_lift (2): the module declares opsec LIGHT (not ACTIVE), disclosure 'target', default_enabled=False, and runs only with --mode light. Per candidate it makes one GET of the homepage (plus the favicon for its mmh3), with no form submission, credential entry or download; non-HTML bodies are not parsed and are discarded.

Targets (A7 BR5): analyst-typed seed domains only. A seed that is itself a suspected lookalike is checked directly; for an org_profile brand seed the registered lookalikes P012 found in the same case are listed, and only those the analyst confirms (TTY; non-TTY only when supplied as seeds) become seeds, recorded in the case audit; at most 20 per run.

Passive first (P376): it runs after the candidate's passive results. Unregistered names, parked names (parking NS/IP), defensive registrations (registrant/NS in org_profile, or archived/urlscan evidence of a redirect to the brand) and candidates without A/AAAA records are classified without contact and never fetched.

veto_lift (2) / A13: lookalikes of an org brand are hostile-shaped, so the hostile-host guard refuses contact from the corporate egress unless proxy_light is configured or --egress-override "<reason>" is recorded; a refusal is BLOCKED reason_code 'hostile_host' and becomes a manual pivot.

Fetch through the core client only: SSRF/address guard (no private, loopback, link-local or metadata targets, AR02), manual redirects <= 5 hops re-checked by scope and guard, 2 MB cap, ua_light UA, A7 LIGHT ceilings (<= 1 req/s, <= 25 requests per host per scan), P334 LIGHT budget and the P324 hash-chained request ledger.

veto_lift (3): similarity comes only from ppdeep (pure-Python ssdeep, optional extra) over normalised HTML, plus title, form-action hosts and favicon mmh3 (shared helper), against the brand reference page; JavaScript is never executed. Reference: the brand seed's homepage fetched once in the same LIGHT run, or its archived copy already in the case (no third-party request here).

veto_lift (3): no headless browser, screenshot or pHash in this module (the architect does not approve a renderer for it); screenshots only through a separately approved capture module (P347) run by the analyst.

Output states per candidate: parked, defensive (never flagged), live clone (score >= threshold, a named constant), unrelated, could not verify. Wording is plain: 'page 87% similar to <brand homepage> -> likely live clone' with the matched features and compared hashes; 'lookalike / phishing-capable indicator', never 'malicious' alone.
veto_lift (4): the dnstwist.it web app is never used (it would learn the brand). The dnstwist-derived algorithm carries the Apache-2.0 header and a THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES entry (A6).

Merge gate: G13 LIGHT, so not merged or enabled before the AR20 safety suite passes (A16). Offline tests use recorded lookalike and brand pages (FakeHttp), a parked page, a defensive redirect and a hostile-guard refusal.
P025.rationale: Vetoed by legal_dpo (MX-spy is SMTP mailbox probing, rule 2); veto_lift adopted, so the item is approved and every legal_dpo lift condition is in final_conditions. All six members want page similarity and all drop MX-spy. The architect's floor shapes the build: a LIGHT module (opsec changed from active), HTML fuzzy hashing with ppdeep, no headless browser or pHash (so legal_dpo's renderer clause leaves screenshots out), a 2 MB cap and the egress guard. redteam_lead and cti_lead asked for passive classification first and a fail-closed guard, analyst_ux for the plain wording. The candidate cap is the architect's 20 (stricter than redteam_lead's 50), and the analyst confirms the list so every contacted host is an analyst-selected target (A7 BR5). Median priority P2.
P025.title: Typosquat live checks (MX-spy, page similarity LSH/pHash)

final_conditions: Ship data/pivot_links/domain_dns.json in the frozen P311 pack schema (label, template, entity_types, category, host, verified, checked_at, privacy, publishes=false, touches_target, login_required, antibot). The pack is offline data (disclosure 'none'): V3LUM never requests these URLs or any API behind them.

Rendering follows A2/P311: at TLP:AMBER and above every link is non-clickable text with 'opening sends <value> to <host>'; at RED third-party links are hidden from reports and listed only by `v3lum links` with the warning; links are never auto-opened and `links --open` at AMBER+ needs an interactive confirmation naming the host.

CI renders every template with a sample value per declared entity type and with hostile values (quotes, spaces, unicode, newlines): each result must be an https URL on the declared host, built only from whitelisted placeholders through the declared encoder (never str.format, never {raw} in URL position).

Every link host has a provider-registry entry with tier and rationale (A8); unknown-tier hosts get the 'unknown operator' badge and their templates take IOC_TYPES values only (A8 BR4): never PERSONAL_TYPES, CNPJ, company names, keywords, malware or actor names, or other free text (P311 lint).

Initial host tiers for the registry reviewer to confirm: trusted - crt.sh (Sectigo), DNSViz (Sandia/Verisign Labs), Verisign DNSSEC Debugger, MXToolbox, dmarcian, DomainTools, whois.com; community - CompleteDNS, host.io, Whoxy, intoDNS, who.is.

Order: P311 groups links by analyst question with verified links first; inside a group the pack's file order is the curated analyst-value order (crt.sh, DNSViz, Whoxy and host.io history, MXToolbox and dmarcian first, then CompleteDNS, DomainTools, intoDNS, Verisign, who.is, whois.com); the terminal shows at most 8 links per seed, the rest go to HTML and `v3lum links`.

Verified links carry checked_at; `v3lum doctor --links` (offline) lists unverified links and links not re-checked for more than 180 days. The pack ships in phase 1 with the other pivot packs (A16), whatever the state of the related automated modules.

Entries (domain): CompleteDNS NS history page (never its /dns-history/ajax/ endpoint), crt.sh HTML search, DNSViz, host.io, Whoxy WHOIS/history, dmarcian DMARC Inspector, DomainTools reverse IP and WHOIS, intoDNS, MXToolbox SPF (dmarc: and mx: actions too), Verisign DNSSEC Debugger, who.is, whois.com.
cert_fingerprint: the crt.sh certificate lookup by SHA-256 renders only for 64-hex SHA-256 fingerprints; no template for other fingerprint forms unless verified.

Flags: pages that make the provider query the target's DNS live (intoDNS, MXToolbox, dmarcian, Verisign debugger) are touches_target=true and follow P311 (defanged, non-clickable warning, hidden for hostile entities unless expanded). The DNSViz label warns that its 'Analyze' button runs and publishes a fresh analysis.

whois.domaintools.com served a CAPTCHA to automated clients: antibot=true, verified by browser only, ranked last in its group. No template points to a page that lists recent lookups publicly (publishes must be false).
P026.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (osint_investigator and analyst_ux voted P1). It is pure data for the P311 engine, so it follows that schema; the architect's CI rendering test with hostile values and cti_lead's stale-link check are kept. cti_lead's scan-trigger concern maps to P311's touches_target and publishes flags; analyst_ux's curated order is the pack's file order inside P311's verified-first grouping. Host tiers are stated per A8; the pack itself sends nothing (tier n/a, terms open, default-on per A3 as manual links).
P026.title: Pivot links: domain & DNS tools (verified templates)

final_conditions: Rules in v3lum/correlations/email_spoofing.py. CR01 spoofable_email_domain: no DMARC, p=none or pct<100 (p=quarantine with pct=100 counts as enforcing) AND SPF missing, ~all, ?all, +all or permerror.

CR02 spf_lookup_limit: MEDIUM when SPF evaluation needs > 10 DNS-mechanism lookups or > 2 void lookups (RFC 7208 permerror), LOW at exactly 10. CR03 dmarc_reports_external_unauthorized: LOW in HTML/MD, INFO in the terminal, when a rua/ruf destination outside the policy domain lacks its authorization record (<domain>._report._dmarc.<dest>, checked by P002); a failed lookup = could not verify.

Inputs are only vocab attributes produced by email_security_posture/dns_records: spf, dmarc, dmarc_policy plus the new keys spf_lookups, spf_void_lookups, dmarc_pct, dmarc_sp and dmarc_rua_external, added to core/vocab.py in the same change. Rules make no network calls.

DMARC discovery for subdomains: when a subdomain has no _dmarc record, use the organisational domain's record (PSL) and its sp= tag before raising CR01. An org with p=reject and a subdomain without a record is not spoofable.

SPF evaluation in the producing module is bounded: <= 10 DNS-mechanism lookups and 2 void lookups, a recursion cap and include-loop detection. All lookups go through the core DoH resolver on the passive egress, never directly to the target's authoritative NS.

Rule 5: rules consume only DNS answers with status NOERROR/NXDOMAIN. SERVFAIL, REFUSED, timeouts or an unevaluated SPF chain mean 'could not verify' and the rule must not fire; never report 'SPF/DMARC missing' on missing data.

Ownership scoping: CR01 is HIGH only for analyst-typed seeds, verified org_profile domains, or the sending domain of the phishing case under triage. Pivot/third-party domains get LOW, omitted at depth >= 2. No spoofing-posture findings on entities tagged malicious/phishing, because attacker domains are not the subject.

Non-sending domains (null MX '0 .', no MX, or no A record) get CR01 at MEDIUM instead of HIGH (pivot/third-party domains stay LOW) with the specific advice 'no mail service: publish v=spf1 -all, a null MX and DMARC p=reject' instead of the generic text.

Every finding shows the record observed, the record to publish and a P322 criterion. It carries the ATT&CK ids T1566 and T1684.001, validated against the bundled ATT&CK data. Thresholds are named constants in one place.

Tests: positive and negative graph fixtures per rule, including a DoH SERVFAIL/timeout case that must not fire, p=none + ~all (HIGH on a seed, LOW on a pivot), a missing record, sp=none on the org domain, > 10 lookups, null MX and quarantine with pct=100.
P027.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. All conditions are consolidated. cti_lead and analyst_ux asked for ownership-scoped severity. osint_investigator and redteam_lead asked for DMARC sp= inheritance via the PSL, the parked-domain variant and no findings on attacker domains. redteam_lead asked for a bounded SPF evaluation through DoH. The architect's floor requires vocab-only inputs and a SERVFAIL fixture that must not fire (rule 5, the same trap email_basics falls into today). legal_dpo raised no concern.
P027.title: Correlation pack: e-mail spoofing posture (CR01-CR03)

final_conditions: Rules CR04 and CR05. CR04 typosquat_phishing_capable: HIGH when registered + MX + RDAP registration <= 90 days + registrant/NS/MX not the brand's. CR05 typosquat_with_fresh_certificate: HIGH when the FIRST certificate ever logged for the name (earliest not_before) is <= 30 days old, never on the latest auto-renewal.

Rules CR06 and CR35. CR06 typosquat_on_malicious_infra is CRITICAL under the consensus condition below. CR35 new_brand_keyword_domain: MEDIUM when the domain is <= 30 days old and combines a brand keyword with a lure word.

Rules make no network calls. They read only existing graph facts and vocab attributes: lookalike relations to an org_profile domain or brand (P012 permutations, CT and NRD hits), RDAP registration date and registrant, MX/A/NS answers, the CT first certificate and TI verdicts. New attribute keys go to core/vocab.py in the same change.

Protected brands, domains and NS come only from org_profile (P378), including its suppliers list: never hard-coded and never from ad-hoc flags. Without a profile the rules do not fire (no typosquat-of-google noise).

Own-asset suppression: domains in org_profile, domains whose RDAP registrant/NS/MX match the profile (registro.br publicIds CNPJ root in cnpj_roots) and BCB DominiosVerificados domains (P360) are never flagged and are tagged own_asset / verified_fi. CR04 stays POSSIBLE when RDAP is redacted or unavailable.

CR06 is CRITICAL only when >= 2 independent upstream families (P171 definition, after warninglist suppression) flag the IP AND the IP is neither a CDN/shared-hosting edge (is_cdn and is_hosting false, < 50 co-hosted names) nor a sinkhole. Otherwise it is HIGH. Shared-hosting hits never count unless the domain itself is flagged.
Parked domains (parking NS/IPs) are capped at MEDIUM with a 'parked' label until their MX, A record or certificate changes.

Lure words live in data/brand_lures_pt.json (editable, tested), PT and EN: conta, pix, boleto, sac, segunda-via/2via, fatura, cartao, credito, emprestimo, fgts, inss, gov, receita, regularizar, desbloqueio, premio, cashback, pontos, login, seguranca, atualizacao, token. They match after IDNA->Unicode, accent and homoglyph folding.

Wording is 'lookalike / phishing-capable indicator', never 'malicious' unless CR06 consensus applies, to avoid labelling registrants (possibly natural persons) without evidence. No automated takedown or abuse report: notification is a manual, separately approved action.
A registrant CNPJ exposed by registro.br RDAP becomes a cnpj pivot (company due diligence). CPF registrants and legalRepresentative names are never pivoted and are masked in every output.

The pack only correlates existing results. It never triggers LIGHT contact with candidate domains: page similarity stays in LIGHT modules behind the P376 egress guard. Values are shown defanged, and each alert prints its evidence chain on one line (registered N days ago, MX yes/no, first cert date, TI sources).

Tests: positive and negative graph fixtures per rule from real typosquat samples. A parked lookalike stays <= MEDIUM, a fresh MX-enabled lookalike is HIGH, and both an own defensive registration and a legitimate brand subsidiary are suppressed.
P028.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1 (redteam_lead voted P2). The suppression of own defensive registrations, asked for by osint_investigator, redteam_lead, the architect and analyst_ux, is the core of the spec. Brand data comes only from org_profile, a legal_dpo and architect floor. CR06 counts independent upstreams and excludes CDN/sinkhole/shared hosting (cti_lead, analyst_ux). CR05 uses the first certificate (analyst_ux). The wording avoids defaming registrants and no takedown is automated (legal_dpo). The pack never contacts candidates (redteam_lead). analyst_ux's ad-hoc --brand flag is not adopted, because legal_dpo's floor limits brand keywords to org_profile; partner brands go into the profile's suppliers list instead.
P028.title: Correlation pack: typosquat & brand abuse (CR04-CR06, CR35)

final_conditions: core/dns.py keeps the Google/Cloudflare JSON resolvers with automatic failover as the default. Failover happens only on transport errors, 5xx and 429, never on NXDOMAIN. Failover time per query is <= 5 s across resolvers, and a per-run circuit breaker skips a resolver after 3 consecutive failures.

Every Google DoH JSON query sends edns_client_subnet=0.0.0.0/0 (verified live 2026-11-26), and a unit test asserts it on every request. Cloudflare stays ECS-free and is preferred for names tagged hostile. RFC 8484 providers are used only through no-ECS endpoints (e.g. dns.quad9.net, not dns11).

NXDOMAIN only comes from an answer with Status 3. SERVFAIL, REFUSED, timeouts and transport errors stay distinct and reach modules as could-not-verify, never empty/NXDOMAIN. Fix Resolver._system: only EAI_NONAME maps to NXDOMAIN; EAI_AGAIN, timeouts and other OSError map to SERVFAIL with the error text.

DoH is the default. dns_mode=system (dnspython, UDP/53) runs only when configured explicitly, never as a silent fallback, because the corporate resolver's IP would reach the target's NS; doctor warns when dns_mode=system. RFC 8484 wire format comes only through dnspython as an optional extra, with no hand-rolled DNS message parser.

The resolver list is configurable (setting doh_providers, https only, validated) and may include the company's internal DoH, listed first when set. The docs present it as the opsec option for typosquat permutation lists, since a public resolver operator sees every permutation.

Default resolvers are limited to providers whose terms allow business use, recorded with evidence in the provider registry (Google Public DNS, Cloudflare 1.1.1.1, Quad9; tier trusted). OpenDNS and CleanBrowsing free resolvers keep terms 'unknown' (off under corporate) until reviewed.

TLP: the chain never moves a query from the system/internal resolver to a public DoH provider when the case is TLP:AMBER or above, or when the caller has disclosure 'none'/'internal'; it answers SERVFAIL / could-not-verify instead. Under RED only an internal resolver may be used (A2).
The AD flag is reported as 'validated by resolver', never as proof. TXT quoting and multi-string answers are normalised. Each DnsAnswer records the resolver used, and evidence files carry it.
DNSBL lookups (Spamhaus etc.) never go through public resolvers. Refusal codes (127.255.255.x) map to BLOCKED/RATE_LIMITED, never to 'not listed'.

Helper ctx.dns.wildcard(zone) runs a random-label A/AAAA probe, cached per run, so modules can tell wildcard and Cloudflare NOERROR/NODATA zones from real records. An NXDOMAIN used for takeover/typosquat decisions is confirmed by a second resolver.

DoH gets its own HTTP scope on the default passive egress: no module UA or min_interval, not counted in module quotas or max_requests. Parser tests run over the 18 recorded DoH fixtures (AD flag, multi-string TXT, CAA/HTTPS/DS), plus one test per status mapping.
P029.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1 (architect and analyst_ux voted P2); the chair keeps P1 and phase 0 because every DNS module depends on these semantics. cti_lead and redteam_lead documented the ECS leak of the egress subnet to attacker-run NS (verified live). osint_investigator, redteam_lead and analyst_ux documented the getaddrinfo-to-NXDOMAIN rule-5 bug. legal_dpo's floor limits default resolvers to business-compatible terms and stops public fallback for AMBER/RED and offline modules. The architect's floor: keep the JSON failover, wire format only via dnspython, its own HTTP scope, fixture tests. The resolvers are a data source: tier trusted, terms open per the registry evidence.
P029.title: DoH resolver layer hardening (multi-provider, wire format, AD flag, TXT normalisation)

final_conditions: `v3lum watch` is a separate command, never part of scan. It runs in the foreground only, with --once for cron/systemd timers, --max-runtime (default 8 h) and --max-alerts, and has no daemon or service management.

Rules come only from org_profile brands, domains, CNPJ roots, card BINs (P357) and the supplier list, plus IOC types. No rule may target a natural person (names, personal e-mails, usernames, phones), except own-domain addresses for infostealer exposure. Matching is local after IDNA->Unicode, accent folding and the P012 permutation set, and keywords are never sent to any third party.

Phase 1: saved hunts re-run on an interval over approved polling sources (crt.sh/Cert Spotter deltas for org domains, NRD feeds), with first_seen diffing persisted in SQLite through a schema migration (AR04).

CertStream: a WebSocket consumer only in the optional extra v3lum[watch] (pure-Python client) with a configurable URL. A configured self-hosted certstream-server-go is used first, and certstream.calidog.io is a community-tier best-effort source. Direct RFC 6962/static-ct-api log polling is deferred to BACKLOG.md.

Registry: certstream.calidog.io is tier community, terms open (public CT data, MIT server; evidence recorded per A1); a self-hosted certstream-server-go is disclosure 'internal'. The consumer sends no investigated value because all filtering is local, and the polling sources keep their own modules' registry tier and terms.

Bounds: a keyword/permutation prefilter runs before queueing; the queue is bounded (drop and count); dedupe uses an LRU; reconnects use backoff with jitter and a maximum reconnect rate; memory is capped.

Alerts fire only for NEW registrable domains, deduplicated by registrable domain plus certificate serial. Each is one terminal line with the reason it matched, a JSONL record (timestamp, rule id, matched name, registrable domain, reason, cert sha256, issuer, not_before) and a case-DB entry. Certificate metadata only. Above 200 alerts per hour a summary line replaces the rest.

Hits only enqueue a normal passive scan through the policy gate, capped at 30 auto-enrichments per hour, with the rest listed for the analyst. Watch never makes automatic LIGHT/ACTIVE contact with hits (A13).

Ransomware victim watch runs only with the ransomware.live PRO key (terms-compatible) and only on victim metadata; leaked files are never downloaded or opened (rule 3). Telegram public-channel watch is delivered only by P357, under its own conditions (A14 BR7).
Mutes exist per rule and per domain, and per-rule precision comes from P325 feedback. Alerts and first_seen state follow retention_days and the case TLP (default AMBER).
doctor shows source health (CertStream reachability, polling source status). Offline tests replay recorded certstream messages through an injectable transport with a fake clock.
P030.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. Brand CT monitoring is early warning for BR phishing waves (cti_lead, osint_investigator), and local filtering of the whole stream reveals nothing about what is watched (redteam_lead). legal_dpo's floor: org_profile-only rules, no natural persons, local keywords, terms-compatible victim feeds, retention and TLP. The architect's floor: a foreground --once command, polling phase 1 with first_seen diffing, CertStream only as an optional bounded extra, direct log polling deferred, replay tests. analyst_ux asked for the polling MVP and the one-line digest. It is opt-in by nature (a separate command), hence default_enabled false. Auditor: provider_tier/terms set to community/open because the CertStream consumer is itself a data source, and the Telegram exclusion was replaced by the approved P357 conditions (A14).
P030.title: Watch mode: CertStream real-time CT + rule-based hunting with first_seen diffing (mihari-style)

final_conditions: Keyless RIPEstat Data API (stat.ripe.net/data/<call>/data.json), sourceapp=v3lum on every call, attribution to RIPE NCC per its terms. cache_ttl 24 h.

IPs: network-info, prefix-overview, rir-geo, whois, abuse-contact-finder and reverse-dns-ip. ASNs: as-overview, announced-prefixes and asn-neighbours. Company names: searchcomplete (ASN/prefix candidates, low confidence, expand=False). PTR chains: dns-chain.
Check the JSON envelope inside HTTP 200 (status, status_code, messages of type error) and map it to ERROR or RATE_LIMITED through P321 markers, never EMPTY.
announced-prefixes for big ASNs (~680 KB) is streamed and capped: at most 100 cidr pivots, while the attribute keeps the total counts.
Drop RIPE person objects at ingestion; keep role, organisation and abuse-c contacts (LGPD minimisation).
Expose the abuse-contact lookup as a shared helper reused by takedown_packet (P345). rir-geo is shown as geolocation context only (MaxMind-derived).
Tests with the recorded fixtures (network-info, prefix-overview, whois, abuse-contact), an error envelope and a capped announced-prefixes answer.
P031.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. legal_dpo's floor: person objects dropped at ingestion, sourceapp and RIPE NCC attribution. The architect's floor: error checks inside the 200 envelope, capped announced-prefixes, low-confidence searchcomplete, the shared abuse-contact helper. RIPE NCC is a regional internet registry: tier trusted; free for corporate use: terms open.
P031.title: RIPEstat Data API (network-info, prefix-overview, whois, abuse contact, geoloc, AS pivots, searchcomplete, reverse DNS)

final_conditions: TXT queries through ctx.dns (core DoH): {reversed_ipv4}.origin.asn.cymru.com, origin6.asn.cymru.com with full 32-nibble IPv6 expansion, AS{n}.asn.cymru.com for AS names and peer.asn.cymru.com. whois.cymru.com:43 is not used (raw TCP through HTTPS-only proxies).

Parse 'ASN | prefix | CC | registry | allocated' after the core TXT normalisation (P029: Google unquoted, Cloudflare quoted or multi-string). Output asn, as_org (from the AS name), country and a cidr pivot (relation belongs_to_asn).
An NXDOMAIN origin answer means 'no announcing ASN' (documented meaningful absence, P328). SERVFAIL, REFUSED or timeouts = could not verify. Private and bogon IPs are skipped.
Cache by DNS TTL (DoH profile). Tests with the seven recorded fixtures (Google and Cloudflare forms, origin6, AS name).
P032.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1; no member set conditions beyond the synthesizer's. legal_dpo verified that Team Cymru offers IP-to-ASN as a no-cost community service suited to automation, which is not the Malware Hash Registry classed noncommercial in A1. Tier trusted, terms open; data flows through the core DoH resolvers.
P032.title: Team Cymru IP-to-ASN via DNS (DoH)

final_conditions: Per-source status for PeeringDB, CIRCL BGP Ranking and Shadowserver, so one throttled API does not hide the others. Registry (A1 BR3, A8 BR12): PeeringDB (free under its AUP), CIRCL BGP Ranking (free CIRCL service) and the Shadowserver public API (free public-benefit service) are 'open', tier trusted, each with evidence recorded.

PeeringDB: GET peeringdb.com/api/net?asn={n}&depth=2 (org name as ASN operator, network type NSP/Content/Enterprise/Hosting, IXPs, policy). Responses capped; anonymous throttling handled by min_interval and an optional key 'peeringdb' in config.KNOWN_KEYS (Authorization header).
PeeringDB AUP: poc/contact objects are dropped at ingestion and never stored or reused (no harvesting or marketing); only role information needed for context is kept.

CIRCL BGP Ranking per ASN (position/total as a percentile) and ipasn_history are context only, shown as 'rank X (higher = more malicious activity observed)' with an explanation. They never raise an IP or domain above INFO and never count as a consensus vote (P171): large clouds and hosters always rank high.
Shadowserver keyless net/asn API (origin and prefix lookups), terms recorded in the registry; a key, if used, goes in a header. Failures = could not verify.

Registering the company's own ASNs/netblocks with Shadowserver for free reports is an institutional DPO/IT decision documented in docs/LEGAL.md, not something the tool does; ingesting those reports is out of scope for this module.
Tests with the recorded PeeringDB, BGP Ranking and Shadowserver fixtures.

final_conditions: One shared core IP-range index (sorted integer intervals + bisect, IPv4 and IPv6), used by cloud_ranges, ip_context_lists, nicbr_asn, ip_offline_db, ip_blocklists and tor_relays. No per-module radix trees. The noise layer reads it through a core noise-provider hook with no network on the noise path (AR06).

Each provider file is a registered dataset with its own TTL (daily; Azure Service Tags weekly) and parser test: AWS ip-ranges.json, Google cloud.json, Cloudflare ips-v4/v6, Fastly public-ip-list, Oracle OCI public_ip_ranges.json, GitHub meta. Azure Service Tags only from a stable URL or via cloudcheck data, never by scraping the download page.

cloudcheck signatures (AGPL-3.0 repository): runtime-downloaded data only into ~/.v3lum/datasets, never bundled, committed or code-copied, with a THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES entry (A6). The official provider files alone must pass the same tests (a test runs without cloudcheck).

Downloads are validated (content type, minimum size and entry count, parse success) before replacing the cached copy; a failed download keeps the last good copy with its date. Dataset age is shown; a missing dataset gives UNAVAILABLE, never 'not cloud'.

Accept IP/CIDR only (domains are covered through their resolves_to pivots), so the module keeps disclosure 'none' (shares_input=False). Labels: is_cloud, is_cdn, is_hosting plus provider/region/service.

Shared edges (CDN/WAF/anycast fronts: Cloudflare, Akamai, Fastly, CloudFront, Azure Front Door, Google front ends) are noise: no pivots and no IP-reputation expansion to co-tenants. IaaS compute (EC2, GCE, Azure VMs, OCI, DigitalOcean...) is NOT noise: reputation still applies, with a verdict lifetime <= 14 days because addresses are reassigned.
CDN/shared-hosting labels make IP-reputation and co-hosting pivots expand=False but never suppress findings about the domain or URL itself.

Scope guard (A7): ACTIVE network probes against IPs labelled CDN or shared hosting are refused unless the scope file lists that IP or range. Own domains on these ranges are tagged third_party_hosted (P378). If the dataset is missing or older than 7 days, ACTIVE network modules refuse to run (fail closed) and doctor warns.

The provider/service label (e.g. 'Cloudflare CDN edge', 'AWS us-east-1 EC2') appears next to the IP in the terminal entity map and HTML, and the pivot note says 'not pivoted: shared CDN/cloud IP'. Unit tests for an edge IP and an IaaS IP.

The architect's floor: one shared core range index, a dataset per provider file, IP/CIDR input only, a local noise hook. legal_dpo's floor (A6): cloudcheck data runtime-only and attributed, official files preferred. cti_lead separated CDN edges from IaaS compute so real C2 on rented VPSs is not hidden. redteam_lead made it a fail-closed safety dataset for the ACTIVE scope guard. osint_investigator: labels never hide domain/URL findings. analyst_ux: visible labels and dataset age. Tier community is the lowest dataset provider (cloudcheck); the cloud providers are trusted. Terms open (public provider data; AGPL data met by runtime download, A1 BR19).
P034.title: Cloud/CDN provider ranges (AWS, GCP, Azure, Cloudflare, Fastly, Oracle...) + cloudcheck signatures

final_conditions: Split (architect floor). tor_exit_local: check.torproject.org/torbulkexitlist as a 1 h dataset matched through the shared IP index (P034), disclosure 'none', allowed at TLP:RED. tor_onionoo: Onionoo details?search=, disclosure third_party.

Onionoo contact fields (operator e-mails/names) are dropped at ingestion.

Historical check, only when the IOC carries a date: CollecTor exit-lists (and the mthcht Tor history, MIT) as monthly archives through the core safe_extract helper (in-memory tar/xz, member and size caps, no extraction to disk), indexed locally ip -> timestamps from the tordnsel format (ExitNode / Published / LastStatus / ExitAddress).

CollecTor/mthcht archives larger than 5 MB are fetched by `v3lum data update` (with a first-run hint), never in the middle of a scan (A6 BR9); a month that is not downloaded reads 'history not downloaded (run v3lum data update)', never 'not an exit'.
The historical answer prints the date checked and the source ('was an exit on 2026-11-20, CollecTor'). dan.me.uk is not used.

Severity: is_tor_exit alone = LOW context with tag anonymizer and the note 'Tor exit: traffic from many users, no attribution possible', never malicious and never higher without other evidence (CR28). Non-exit relays = info. ATT&CK T1090.003 is mapped when an IOC IP is a Tor exit.

The bulk exit list's age is shown; older than 6 h it is refreshed, otherwise the result is could-not-verify. Onionoo uses If-Modified-Since. ExoneraTor is a manual pivot link. Tor Metrics attribution (CC0/CC BY) in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
Tests with the recorded bulk-list and Onionoo fixtures, a CollecTor archive slice, a stale-list case and an exact-IP filter case.

Tor Project public data: tier trusted, terms open.

Tests with the recorded abusix_contacts_doh.json fixture and an IPv6 nibble case.

final_conditions: Phase 0 fix of the existing reference module (A1 BR18): declare terms='noncommercial' (it inherits 'open' today) and update its notice and tests.

Tags (cdn, cloud, self-signed, eol...) map to attributes. Hostnames returned for a CDN/shared-hosting IP (P034) are attributes or expand=False pivots: co-tenants, not the target.

final_conditions: Per-list terms registry; a list is wired only once its entry is recorded. SpamCop and DroneBL are 'open' within their free-use terms. Spamhaus ZEN/DBL only through a DQS key on the plan legal decides (key-terms; commercial DQS for business use; key_plans.spamhaus_dqs); public Spamhaus mirrors are noncommercial and never used. Project Honey Pot http:BL is key-terms (company account).
URIBL, SURBL, UCEPROTECT and Barracuda are noncommercial/fair-use lists: off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared (their free-use terms recorded and allowed by legal).

Keyed zones (Spamhaus DQS, Project Honey Pot http:BL) embed the key in the query name: never through public DoH. They use only the system resolver through dnspython (optional extra; otherwise UNAVAILABLE reason_code 'package'), with the qname redacted in logs, cache and evidence (AR01).

Lists that refuse public resolvers (Spamhaus without DQS, URIBL, SURBL, unregistered Barracuda) are not queried through DoH and appear as ONE coverage line ('needs DQS key/registration'). Unkeyed lists that answer public resolvers (SpamCop, DroneBL) go through the core DoH layer.

Bundled per-list return-code tables with tests. Refusal answers (Spamhaus 127.255.255.252/254/255, URIBL/SURBL 'query refused', NXDOMAIN via public resolvers for Spamhaus) give BLOCKED ('could not verify', P321), never 'listed' or 'not listed'.
A per-run 127.0.0.2 test-point check per list: if it fails, that list is could-not-verify for the run, never 'not listed'. IPv6 nibble format tested.
UCEPROTECT Level 1 only counts. Level 2/3 (whole allocations/ASNs) and similar network-wide listings are never evidence against a single IP: at most info 'neighbourhood listing', zero risk.

One aggregated finding: 'listed on k of n queried lists (names, return codes)'. A single SpamCop/DroneBL listing = LOW. Listings tag spam, not malicious, and all DNSBLs count as ONE 'spam' family vote in P171 consensus.
Domain zones (DBL/SURBL/URIBL) for domains, IP zones for IPs. Lookups are capped per run (<= 10 lists per entity). http:BL scores are log-scaled; NXDOMAIN there means not listed.
Tests with the recorded DoH fixtures (SpamCop test point, Spamhaus via public resolver, Barracuda test) plus refused-answer and Level 2/3 cases.
P045.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. legal_dpo's floor: per-list terms (Spamhaus public mirrors non-commercial and refused via public resolvers, DQS on the plan legal decides, the others only within recorded terms) and the http:BL key never through a third-party resolver. The architect's floor extends that to every key-in-qname zone: system resolver only, qname redacted, bundled return-code tables. cti_lead and analyst_ux: refusal codes, UCEPROTECT L1 only, one spam family vote, one aggregated finding. Terms is noncommercial for the NC lists, which stay off under corporate until licence-cleared. Tier community is the lowest list operator.
P045.title: DNSBL / RBL lookups via DoH (SpamCop, Spamhaus ZEN/DBL via DQS, DroneBL, UCEPROTECT, Barracuda, SURBL, URIBL, Project Honey Pot)

final_conditions: Every provider (VPNDetection, IPQuery, IPLocate, InternetData, ipapi.is, proxycheck.io) is terms 'unknown' and tier unknown until legal reviews it: disabled in every profile until legal records its terms (A1); then default_enabled=False, excluded at AMBER and above, --allow-unknown at CLEAR/GREEN until promoted (proxycheck.io and ipapi.is may be promoted with keys and terms).
IPLogs is excluded: it advertises active probing of queried IPs (response field 'probed') and documents no lookup mode that never triggers it.

Runs only on analyst-typed seed IPs (run_on='seeds'): never on pivots, never on IPs extracted from text, log or e-mail inputs, never for bogon, CDN or cloud-range IPs (P034). IPs of customers or employees (personal data) are enriched only with the offline datasets (P047, P035, P040, P034).

Offline lists answer first; online votes are asked only when they are silent. At most 4 providers are wired, each with its own fixture, status and min_interval (1 req/s); cache 24 h; optional keys (iplocate, ipapiis, proxycheck) in config.KNOWN_KEYS.

One shared vote helper with ip_geolocation (P051). Providers are asked one at a time and asking stops once 3 agree or 3 agreeing answers become impossible. VPNDetection and InternetData share a backend and count once.

A verdict needs >= 3 answered, agreeing, independent providers. Fewer answers give the attribute anonymizer_votes, status ok, and the wording 'inconclusive (insufficient votes)', never 'not a VPN' or 'clean'. Failed providers are listed as could not verify.
Output is ONE line with the votes, e.g. 'VPN: 3 of 4 providers (VPNDetection, IPQuery, IPLocate); hosting: 4/4'. Verdicts are context tags (vpn, proxy, hosting) feeding CR28, never malicious.
Use the P331 declarative collector for these adapters where it fits.
P046.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (cti_lead and legal_dpo voted P3). legal_dpo's floor decides the shape: all providers are unknown terms and tier until reviewed, IPLogs is out, and IPs that are personal data never reach these operators. That resolves the conflict between osint_investigator (IPLogs only for hostile IPs) and redteam_lead (never for hostile IPs). It also overrides analyst_ux's wish to run on IPs from pasted logs. The architect's floor: a shared vote helper, at most 4 providers with fixtures, the >= 3 vote rule. cti_lead's 'at most 3 per lookup' is met in the common case by asking providers one at a time. Unknown tier and terms: default_enabled false (A3 BR2).
P046.title: Keyless VPN/proxy/hosting consensus (VPNDetection, IPLogs, IPQuery, IPLocate, InternetData, ipapi.is, proxycheck.io)

final_conditions: Datasets only via `v3lum data update` (setup wizard pre-fetch): DB-IP Lite country + ASN mmdb (monthly; not the 86 MB city file), IPtoASN TSV (at most daily), bgp.tools asns.csv (at most daily), and optionally MaxMind GeoLite2 (weekly). gzip/tar go through the core safe_extract helper with size caps, streamed to disk above 50 MB.

Interactive scans never block > 10 s on a first download. A missing dataset gives UNAVAILABLE reason_code 'dataset' ('run v3lum data update'), never EMPTY. Coverage shows the dataset name and age ('DB-IP Lite 2026-11, 12 days').

Lookups are local (disclosure 'none', shares_input=False, allowed at TLP:RED). Offline answers come first and are the only geo/ASN source under TLP:RED and for bulk pastes; online geo/ASN modules (P051, P036) run only when the offline answer is missing or for depth-0 seeds.
mmdb files are read through the optional pure-Python 'maxminddb' package (requires_packages, Apache-2.0). IPtoASN loads into the shared core IP-range index (P034).

bgp.tools: asns.csv only, with a descriptive UA carrying the team role contact (setting contact_email, P326), never an analyst's personal e-mail; without the setting the source is SKIPPED reason_code 'config'. It labels hosting versus eyeball networks.

MaxMind GeoLite2 is optional and terms 'license': the company's MaxMind account with the EULA accepted by legal and recorded in licence_allow (off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared). Account id and licence key are two registered keys sent with HTTP Basic auth on the permalink URLs, never ?license_key=. The 30-day update/deletion obligation is automated.

Registry terms: DB-IP Lite CC BY 4.0 (open), IPtoASN PDDL (open), bgp.tools free use with descriptive UA (open), GeoLite2 EULA (license). Attribution strings go in the report footer and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
Geodata is country/city/ASN context only and is never used to locate a specific individual or household (EULA, LGPD).
Tests with trimmed fixtures (bgp.tools CSV slice, a small test mmdb, an IPtoASN slice): offline lookup, missing dataset, size caps.
P047.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. legal_dpo's floor: DB-IP attribution, IPtoASN PDDL, bgp.tools only with a role contact, GeoLite2 only with a company account and a legal-accepted EULA, never locating individuals. The architect's floor: country+ASN only, safe archives, the optional maxminddb reader, the shared index, Basic auth for MaxMind. osint_investigator and analyst_ux: offline-first ordering, visible freshness, no blocking downloads. Terms is license for the optional GeoLite2 part only; the rest is open. Tier community is the lowest dataset operator (IPtoASN, bgp.tools); no value leaves the machine.
P047.title: Offline IP datasets (DB-IP Lite, IPtoASN, MaxMind GeoLite2, bgp.tools asns.csv)

final_conditions: Endpoint allow-list in code: IP and domain report lookups of existing data only. The domain/URL 'scan' endpoints are never wired in any mode (they make Criminal IP crawl the target outside our ledger); a test asserts they cannot be called.

Requires key 'criminalip' in config.KNOWN_KEYS (V3LUM_CRIMINALIP_KEY as alias), sent in the x-api-key header. Key-terms: a company/team account on a plan recorded by legal before it runs under corporate.

Risk scores are one vote, never 'malicious' alone; port/vulnerability data is version-inferred and follows P291 caps. The report page search.criminalip.io/asset/report/{ip} is the manual link.
Merge only with a trimmed real success fixture captured with the team key, plus the recorded no-key fixture.

Kept opt-in as drafted. Criminal IP is an established commercial CTI vendor: tier trusted.

Keys fofa_email and fofa_key in config.KNOWN_KEYS; FOFA takes the key in the URL, so merge only after the central redaction (AR01).

A later promotion needs legal_dpo's written decision and keeps the AMBER+ exclusion.
default_enabled=False. Own-asset or engagement targets are never sent without a per-scan opt-in flag recorded in the case.
base64-encoded queries (domain=, icon_hash=, cert=). Results are pivots with expand=False.

P049.rationale: Approved 4-0 with two defers (cti_lead, architect: paid, unverified, no fixture) at median P3. legal_dpo's floor: a company licence after a transfer review, infrastructure selectors only, never at AMBER and above, off by default; the chair implements the AMBER+ exclusion through the unknown tier, which also limits FOFA to IOC types. redteam_lead: no own-asset or engagement targets without a per-scan opt-in. The architect's defer becomes merge conditions (redaction for the URL key, a real fixture). Terms license (paid).

P050.rationale: Contested 3-0-3 (yes: osint_investigator, redteam_lead, legal_dpo; defer: cti_lead, architect, analyst_ux). The chair defers it. All yes votes are P3 tie-breakers for the keyless consensus (P046). P046 itself stays disabled until legal reviews its providers, and no fixture exists for IPHub, FraudGuard or Focsec.
