P050.title: Keyed VPN/proxy detection (IPHub, FraudGuard, Focsec)

final_conditions: Offline first: ip_offline_db (P047) answers first. This online chain runs only when the offline answer is missing or on explicit request (-M ip_geolocation or --preset deep), only on analyst-typed seed IPs (run_on='seeds'), never on pivot IPs, at most 2 providers per IP.
Bogon, RFC 1918, CGNAT, loopback and link-local addresses are filtered before any call. IPs from internal logs, e-mails, customers or employees (personal data) use the offline data only.

Wired now (commercial use allowed): ipwho.is (success:false + message in a 200 body = ERROR/QUOTA; connection.domain becomes an org-domain pivot with expand=False) and FreeIPAPI (free.freeipapi.com/api/v1/json/{ip}, 60 req/min; isProxy is a weak signal). Both community tier.

IP2Location.io keyless, GeoJS and ip.guide are added only after legal records their terms and tier (ip.guide serves JSON as text/plain: parse regardless of the header). KeyCDN is not wired: its mandatory UA 'keycdn-tools:https://<site>' would disclose the company's website on every lookup.
One shared vote helper with P046. Output: country and ASN/ISP with the agreeing sources ('BR - 2/2 providers'), labelled approximate; city only as 'approximate (<provider>)' with disagreements shown.
Geolocation is context only: never a risk factor by itself, never presented as a person's location, never a located_at/coordinates pivot.
1 req/s per provider, cache 24 h, per-provider fixture and status. Tests with the recorded ipwho.is and FreeIPAPI fixtures and a success:false body.
P051.rationale: Approved 6-0. The tally median is P3 on a 3-3 split (osint_investigator, redteam_lead and legal_dpo voted P2); the chair keeps P3 because offline data answers the question first. cti_lead, osint_investigator, the architect and analyst_ux require offline-first and no default fan-out to six providers, so it is opt-in. legal_dpo's floor: per-provider terms (only ipwho.is and FreeIPAPI state commercial use), offline only for personal IPs, never a person's location. redteam_lead's removal of KeyCDN is adopted because its UA identifies the company (stricter than legal_dpo's off-by-default). The architect: shared vote helper, bogon filter, error-in-200 handling.
P051.title: Keyless IP geolocation chain (ipwho.is, FreeIPAPI, ip.guide, IP2Location.io, GeoJS, KeyCDN)

final_conditions: veto_lift: accepts = {ipv4, url} only; e-mail and phone are removed from accepts and produces. The e-mail and phone validation endpoints are never wired: a unit test asserts no request to /api/json/email or /api/json/phone can be built (provider-side mailbox/carrier probing = rule 2 by proxy).

veto_lift: URL reputation runs only for URLs tagged hostile (malicious/phishing/suspicious), never for internal, confidential or org_profile URLs, and is skipped at TLP:AMBER and above: the URL source carries a source-level reuses_queries flag in the registry, so core/policy.py excludes it at AMBER+ (Status.SKIPPED reason_code 'tlp'). It is also flagged fetches_target.
veto_lift: a company-owned key with IPQS terms recorded by legal (key-terms, key_plans.ipqs) before it runs under corporate. Key 'ipqs' in config.KNOWN_KEYS.
veto_lift: success:false in a 200 body ('Invalid or unauthorized key', quota messages) maps through a P321 marker to NEEDS_KEY, QUOTA or ERROR, never EMPTY.

IPQS puts the key in the URL path (/api/json/ip/{key}/{ip}): merge only after the central redaction (AR01) masks configured key values anywhere in URLs, path included, in the cache, events/live feed, logs and evidence.

Monthly budget (1,000 free lookups) through the P334 block. default_enabled=False. The fraud score is one vote, never 'malicious' alone. The registry and core/policy.py (P327) support this source-level flag overriding the provider's, with a policy-table test.
Merge only with a trimmed real success fixture captured with the company key, plus the recorded invalid-key fixture.
P052.rationale: Vetoed by legal_dpo (5-1 otherwise): as drafted it accepted e-mail and phone, and IPQS validation of those probes mailboxes and carriers (rule 2). veto_lift adopted: legal_dpo's lift conditions match what every other member asked (cti_lead, osint_investigator, redteam_lead and analyst_ux all excluded the e-mail/phone endpoints; redteam_lead flagged the URL endpoint fetches_target). The chair implements the lift's AMBER+ exclusion of URL checks through a source-level reuses_queries flag, so the gate in core/policy.py enforces it. The architect's floor: path-key redaction and a real fixture. Approved at median P3, opt-in. IPQS is an established company: tier trusted.
P052.title: IPQualityScore (IP/URL/email/phone reputation, keyed)

final_conditions: Registry tier unknown (Chinese operator; queries reveal targets; the LGPD art. 33 transfer is not reviewed): excluded at AMBER, AMBER+STRICT and RED, CLEAR/GREEN only with --allow-unknown, and only IOC_TYPES selectors (infrastructure), never personal data (A8 BR4). Legal/procurement records the data-transfer decision; a promotion needs legal_dpo's written decision and keeps the AMBER+ exclusion.

Requires key 'zoomeye' in config.KNOWN_KEYS (V3LUM_ZOOMEYE_KEY as alias) in the API-KEY header. Key-terms: a company/team account on a plan recorded by legal before it runs under corporate. default_enabled=False.
POST https://api.zoomeye.ai/v2/search with a base64-encoded query. JSON code/error bodies (401 'login_required') map to NEEDS_KEY or ERROR, never EMPTY.
Results follow the CDN/shared-hosting noise rules (P034); pivots are capped and expand=False.
The web deep link (zoomeye.ai/searchResult?q=<base64>) is a manual link only. Merge only with a trimmed real success fixture, plus the recorded 401 fixture.
P053.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. legal_dpo's floor, shared by cti_lead and osint_investigator: infrastructure selectors only, excluded at AMBER and above, off by default, with a recorded data-transfer decision; the unknown tier enforces it through the gate, as for FOFA (P049). The architect's floor: header key, base64 POST, error mapping, a real fixture, capped pivots. Terms key-terms with a company account.
P053.title: ZoomEye API v2 (keyed)

P054.rationale: Deferred 2-0-4, as the tally decided (cti_lead, redteam_lead, architect and analyst_ux deferred). hunter.how and Driftnet add little over Shodan, Censys, Netlas and ONYPHE; Driftnet is unverified and only a 'token expired' fixture exists for hunter.how. BACKLOG.md records the unblock condition: a demonstrated coverage gap in the licensed scan engines, verified endpoints with real fixtures, and legal_dpo's terms and tier review (hunter.how is Chinese-operated).
P054.title: Minor scan engines (hunter.how, Driftnet)

P055.rationale: Rejected 0-6, as the synthesizer proposed. BGPView and BinaryEdge are discontinued and ipapi.co serves an anti-bot challenge that rule 1 forbids bypassing (legal_dpo, architect). RIPEstat, Team Cymru, PeeringDB and the offline datasets (P031-P033, P047) cover the need; bgp.he.net and bgp.tools web pages belong in the IP pivot-link pack (osint_investigator). Recorded in BACKLOG.md so these sources are not re-added.
P055.title: Dead/blocked IP sources (BGPView, BinaryEdge, ipapi.co)

P056.rationale: Rejected 0-6, as the synthesizer proposed. The ip-api.com free tier is non-commercial and plain HTTP, which exposes every queried IP in clear text (redteam_lead) and conflicts with the LGPD art. 46 security duty (legal_dpo). Commercial-friendly alternatives exist: ipwho.is, FreeIPAPI (P051) and the offline DB-IP data (P047). Recorded in BACKLOG.md as a rejection.
P056.title: ip-api.com free tier

final_conditions: Ship data/pivot_links/ip_network.json in the frozen P311 pack schema (label, template, entity_types, category, host, verified, checked_at, privacy, publishes=false, touches_target, login_required, antibot), plus the optional per-link max_tlp field that the phase-0 schema must include. The pack is offline data (disclosure 'none'): V3LUM never requests these URLs or any API behind them.

Rendering follows A2/P311: at TLP:AMBER and above every link is non-clickable text with 'opening sends <value> to <host>'; at RED third-party links are hidden from reports and listed only by `v3lum links` with the warning; links are never auto-opened and `links --open` at AMBER+ needs an interactive confirmation naming the host.

CI renders every template with a sample value per declared entity type and with hostile values (quotes, spaces, unicode, newlines): each result must be an https URL on the declared host, built only from whitelisted placeholders through the declared encoder (never str.format, never {raw} in URL position).

Every link host has a provider-registry entry with tier and rationale (A8); unknown-tier hosts get the 'unknown operator' badge and their templates take IOC_TYPES values only (A8 BR4): never PERSONAL_TYPES, CNPJ, company names, keywords, malware or actor names, or other free text (P311 lint).

Initial host tiers for the registry reviewer to confirm: trusted - bgp.he.net (Hurricane Electric), IPinfo, Tor Project ExoneraTor, CIDR Report (APNIC/Geoff Huston); community - FOFA (CN), Criminal IP (KR), Scamalytics; unknown - Myip.ms.

Order: P311 groups links by analyst question with verified links first; inside a group the pack's file order is the curated analyst-value order (bgp.he.net, IPinfo, ExoneraTor and Scamalytics first, then Criminal IP, FOFA, CIDR Report, Myip.ms last); the terminal shows at most 8 links per seed, the rest go to HTML and `v3lum links`.

Verified links carry checked_at; `v3lum doctor --links` (offline) lists unverified links and links not re-checked for more than 180 days. The pack ships in phase 1 with the other pivot packs (A16), whatever the state of the related automated modules.

Entries: bgp.he.net IP, prefix and AS pages (manual only, never scraped: automation uses RIPEstat/Team Cymru), IPinfo IP and ASN pages, Scamalytics IP page, Tor ExoneraTor, CIDR Report AS page, Criminal IP asset report, FOFA queries, Myip.ms (antibot=true: CAPTCHA after a few lookups).
No link is rendered for private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT, ULA or reserved addresses, nor for single-label or internal host names (redteam_lead); a unit test covers each range.

FOFA and Criminal IP carry a 'foreign provider: queries are logged abroad - never paste internal host names' badge (legal_dpo, osint_investigator) and max_tlp=green: at TLP:AMBER and above they are hidden from reports and listed only by `v3lum links` with the warning (redteam_lead).

FOFA templates use a vetted {b64q} placeholder: the P311 base64 encoder applied to a fixed query expression declared in the entry (ip="{q}", icon_hash="{q}", cert="{q}"), unit-tested; if {b64q} is not available FOFA is dropped (architect). favicon_hash and cert_fingerprint templates render only for those entity types.
P057.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (osint_investigator and analyst_ux voted P1). The common P311 pack conditions apply. The architect's floor requires the vetted base64 query placeholder for FOFA or no FOFA. legal_dpo, osint_investigator, cti_lead and analyst_ux asked for the foreign-provider warning; redteam_lead's stricter hiding of foreign-jurisdiction links at AMBER+ and his no-links-for-private-addresses rule are adopted. Myip.ms is unknown tier (badge, IP values only) and ranked last.
P057.title: Pivot links: IP & ASN tools (verified templates)

final_conditions: BACKLOG unblock (veto_lift form only): the link renders only for IPs that P169 warninglists or cloud ranges tag as hosting/datacenter, VPN, Tor or open proxy, never for residential, mobile or CGNAT space, org_profile ranges or IPs of employees, customers or victims.

BACKLOG unblock (continued): hidden unless the analyst enables a per-case 'sensitive pivots' setting with a recorded purpose; V3LUM never fetches or stores the page and records only the analyst's conclusion, never titles; the link warns that titles can reveal sensitive data and is non-clickable at TLP:AMBER+.
P058.rationale: Rejected: vetoed by legal_dpo (torrent histories of residential, CGNAT and rented residential-proxy IPs profile uninvolved people, LGPD art. 11) and rejected on substance by cti_lead (false attribution, value 2) and analyst_ux (CGNAT mixes thousands of users). The veto_lift is not adopted: limiting the link to hosting/VPN/Tor/proxy IPs removes the attacker-home use case that gave the link its value, while VPN and Tor exits still expose other users' titles. osint_investigator, redteam_lead and the architect supported only a gated P3 link. BACKLOG keeps the veto_lift form as the unblock condition.
P058.title: Pivot link: I Know What You Download (torrent activity per IP)

final_conditions: Default scan: the Wayback availability API (archive.org/wayback/available) plus one CDX summary query per registrable seed domain/URL inside a 15 s budget. CDX uses collapse=urlkey, fl=original,timestamp,statuscode,mimetype, limit/page parameters and a total row cap of 20,000; a body truncated at the core cap is partial, never complete. Gentle use (~15 req/min).
Arquivo.pt CDX (NDJSON) is queried for .br/.pt and Portuguese-language sites even when Wayback answers, and as the fallback when web.archive.org is unreachable.

Common Crawl (latest 1-2 indexes only, backoff; records via Range from data.commoncrawl.org) and CarbonDate run only with --preset deep or -M. CarbonDate may read the live URI: its source is flagged fetches_target and never receives URLs carrying tokens or recipient identifiers. UKWA stays disabled until it answers.
Per-source status. Connection resets, 504 and timeouts give could-not-verify ('archive unreachable'), never 'never archived' or 'no captures'.

Before pivots, attributes, res.raw, evidence and reports, the core URL-redaction helper masks userinfo (user:pass@), tokens, session ids, query-string secrets (P312 detectors) and e-mail addresses in archived URLs; unit test with the user:pass@ sample.

Archived bodies are fetched only from archive hosts (id_ raw snapshots), never via the live site, handled as untrusted data (never executed or rendered), and kept only as extracted indicators plus SHA-256, not stored in full.

Archived URLs are never requested from the live target in any mode, except by the ACTIVE path module within an authorized scope (replaying archived tokens is credential use). Save Page Now and any 'save'/'archive now' endpoint are never called (rule 7, P080).

Outputs: archive_first (a lower bound of web presence, never a registration date; no captures never means a new domain), archive_last, archive_count and the closest snapshot link; archived_url pivots expand=False and capped; URL lists go to JSON/appendix (P060). first_seen = min(RDAP created, first CT not_before, first capture).

Archive-first: web_archives exposes the closest archived homepage snapshot (id_ body from the archive host, 1 MB cap, within the 15 s budget) so modules needing homepage-derived data (title, CNPJ text, analytics ids, favicon, contacts, P072 matchers) use it in passive mode.

Registry terms (A1 BR3): the Internet Archive (Wayback CDX and availability), Arquivo.pt (FCT public service), Common Crawl (free terms of use) and CarbonDate (ODU academic service) are 'open', each recorded by legal with evidence; the Internet Archive grants access for research, so legal records internal CTI research as the purpose. UKWA stays disabled. Volume stays low (rule 6).
Tests with the recorded availability, Arquivo.pt CDX, CarbonDate and UKWA 403 fixtures plus a truncated CDX body and a connection reset.
P059.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1 (cti_lead voted P2). legal_dpo's floor: the research-purpose record for the Internet Archive, masking of credentials and victims' e-mails before evidence, bodies kept only as indicators, no 'save' endpoint. The architect's floor: CDX caps, per-source status, the core redaction helper, capped expand=False pivots. redteam_lead: no replay of archived URLs against the target and CarbonDate flagged fetches_target. osint_investigator: Arquivo.pt for Portuguese sites and archive-first homepage data. analyst_ux: the 15 s default budget, deep-only slow sources and the combined first_seen. All archives are established non-profits or public bodies: tier trusted, terms open.
P059.title: Web archives (Wayback CDX + availability, Arquivo.pt, Common Crawl, CarbonDate, UKWA)

final_conditions: A library on top of web_archives (P059): same client, same per-source status, archive hosts only. OTX, urlscan and ghostarchive are dropped from this module's hosts; their URL lists reach it through the graph from their own approved modules. IntelX via waymore stays off (P139 rules).
At most 20 archived bodies per run via id_ raw URLs, 1 MB each, fetched only from archive hosts and treated as untrusted data (never executed or rendered).

waymore filter/keyword lists (MIT) are bundled with attribution to keep interesting URLs (configs, backups, admin, API paths). Query-string secrets in harvested URLs are masked by P312 before storage.
Robofinder technique: robots.txt versions via CDX collapse=digest, parsed with a size cap; Disallow/Allow/Sitemap lines are unioned and disallowed paths become url entities with expand=False.

chronos technique: archived favicons are hashed with the shared pure-Python mmh3 helper (Shodan form: mmh3 over base64.encodebytes with the trailing newline, Shodan test vectors) and become favicon_hash pivots with expand=False.
Historical analytics ids and favicon hashes carry the snapshot date and are historical; the P061/P062 noise rules apply, and ids are never linked across eras without overlapping dates.
Harvested URLs, disallowed paths and endpoints are never requested from the live target outside the ACTIVE path module within scope.

Output: one grouped attribute 'interesting archived URLs' by category (config, backup, admin, API, robots Disallow), capped at 50 in the report; no per-URL findings except masked secrets from secret_scanner. default_enabled=False (opt-in).
Fixtures: CDX slices from web_archives plus one archived robots.txt and one archived favicon.
P060.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (cti_lead and analyst_ux voted P3). The architect's floor: a library over the archive client, archive hosts only, capped bodies, the shared mmh3 helper. legal_dpo's floor: P059 masking, no submissions anywhere, IntelX off, bodies kept as indicators. redteam_lead: harvested paths are never browsed. osint_investigator and cti_lead: dated historical ids. analyst_ux: grouped, capped output and opt-in. Archive hosts only: tier trusted, terms open.
P060.title: Archive mining techniques (waymore URL harvesting, historical robots.txt, historical favicons)

final_conditions: Split (architect floor). analytics_ids extracts ids locally from bodies already in hand (web_fingerprint, archived snapshots, urlscan DOM, text/file inputs): disclosure 'none', runs under TLP:RED, makes no request to the target. gtm_expand fetches https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtm.js?id=GTM-... from Google: disclosure third_party.

Regexes, bounded, case-sensitive and tested against a 1 MB adversarial body within a time budget: UA-\d{4,10}-\d{1,4}, G-[A-Z0-9]{6,12} (the bellingcat digits-only regex is fixed), GTM-[A-Z0-9]{4,9}, pub-\d{16} and ca-pub-; in GTM expansion also quoted AW- and DC- ids.

GTM expansion: at most 5 containers per run, 1 MB cap, cache 7 days. Unknown containers return HTTP 200 with a generic ~242 KB runtime and no macros: 'not found' is decided from content, never from status.

Reverse lookups happen by pivoting analytics_id entities to the modules that accept that type (host.io P004, HackerTarget P014, urlscan P066), each under its own licence and key decisions; no reverse client is re-implemented here. SpyOnWeb is left out until a real fixture exists.

Shared-id rule: an id whose reverse lookup returns > 50 domains, or a known agency/CMS/site-builder template id, is labelled 'shared ID': info, no pivots, no same-owner correlation, confidence <= 0.3. Reverse-lookup pivots are capped at 10 per id.
Clone rule: a non-own site carrying an id used by an org_profile own site gives 'possible clone of <brand> (copied tracking ID)' as a phishing indicator, never a same-owner link.

same_analytics pivots are expand=False, confidence at most PROBABLE (<= 0.7), never sufficient alone for CONFIRMED ownership (P013). Ids from archived snapshots carry the snapshot date; a same_analytics link needs overlapping dates.
Each same_analytics link shows the id and where it was seen (live page, archive date, GTM container). Tests with the recorded GTM container fixture, a high fan-out id and the clone case.
P061.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (osint_investigator voted P1). The architect's floor splits the offline extractor from the Google fetch (legal_dpo asked the same so TLP:RED keeps local extraction) and moves reverse lookups to the modules that own those clients. cti_lead supplied the clone rule; cti_lead, osint_investigator and analyst_ux the > 50-domain shared-id rule. redteam_lead's 10-domain threshold is not adopted, but his expand=False pivots and analyst_ux's 10-pivot cap bound the agency fan-out he feared. Google is trusted; terms open (public JavaScript).
P061.title: Analytics / tag-manager / AdSense ID extraction and reverse lookup

final_conditions: Two modules over one pure-Python mmh3 core helper (Shodan test vector: Google favicon -> 708578229; mmh3 over base64.encodebytes with the trailing newline), reused by archive_mining, cl0q and the engine pivot links. Also MD5 and SHA-256 of the bytes.

favicon_hash (PASSIVE, default): hashes favicon bytes from archived snapshots (Wayback id_ via the P059 client) or existing urlscan results, and hashes typed favicon_hash values into engine pivot links. No contact with the target.

favicon_fetch (LIGHT, default_enabled=False): one GET of the icon on analyst-typed seeds only (never pivots), after the entity's passive lane, through the P376 egress guard (hostile hosts only via a non-corporate egress, fail closed), counted in the P334 LIGHT budget. Not merged or enabled before the AR20 safety suite passes.

The icon URL comes from <link rel=icon> on the shared homepage fetch or /favicon.ico, and is fetched only through the core safe-fetch helper: http/https, public IPs on every hop, same registrable domain or its CDN, 1 MB cap, image content type (hostile pages control that href).
A bundled list of default/blank favicon hashes (web servers, CMS, hosting panels, parking pages, routers), plus hashes reported on > 1,000 hosts, marks noise: recorded, never pivoted.

Engine pivot links (Shodan, FOFA, Criminal IP, Netlas, ZoomEye) by default; automatic reverse queries only through enabled keyed engine modules. Reverse matches are hypotheses: relation similar_favicon, expand=False, never eligible for an ACTIVE scope.
Tests with the recorded design_pivots_and_js fixture, the Shodan test vector, a default-favicon suppression and a hostile href to a private IP that the safe-fetch helper refuses.
P062.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. cti_lead, osint_investigator and redteam_lead require passive bytes first and the live fetch only as LIGHT behind the egress guard; A3 BR2 makes LIGHT opt-in, so the chair splits the passive hashing (default) from the live fetch (opt-in). The architect's floor: one mmh3 helper with the test vector and the SSRF-safe fetch. redteam_lead: similar_favicon hypotheses, never scope. legal_dpo: own code, links only. The passive module reads from the Internet Archive: tier trusted, terms open.
P062.title: Favicon hash (Shodan-compatible mmh3 + MD5/SHA-256)

final_conditions: The module issues no request of its own: it consumes the cached homepage response of web_fingerprint (P072) through the shared homepage fetch helper and is SKIPPED (reason_code 'not_applicable') when there is none. A FakeHttp test asserts zero requests. It declares opsec PASSIVE and disclosure 'none' (offline analysis).

Core change first (architect floor): Response preserves multi-valued headers, keeping the Set-Cookie list (urllib3 getlist) also in the HTTP cache, because requests joins duplicate Set-Cookie headers with commas and Expires dates contain commas.

Scoring like Mozilla Observatory: start at 100 and subtract per missing/weak header; HSTS checks only over HTTPS; CSP-Report-Only counts as monitoring only; cookie heuristics for session-like names (sess|sid|auth|token|jwt|remember) without Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite.
Bundle OWASP Secure Headers ci/headers_add.json and headers_remove.json from the GitHub repository (the owasp.org URL 404s) with the Apache-2.0 NOTICE.
Non-2xx/3xx, blocked, proxy or WAF pages are inconclusive.
ONE aggregated finding per site: the grade plus the list of missing/weak headers, no per-header findings.

Severity: LOW only for org_profile own assets and authorized in-scope targets; INFO for every other site; attributes only, no finding, for sites tagged phishing/malicious. CR18/CR19 (P084) may raise it to MEDIUM only on own assets. Never more than LOW in the risk score.
Tests with fixtures carrying several Set-Cookie headers; a third-party site missing 6 headers yields exactly one info finding; zero-request assertion.
P063.rationale: Approved 6-0. The tally median is P3 on a 3-3 split (redteam_lead, legal_dpo and the architect voted P2); the chair keeps P3 because it is own-asset hygiene rather than threat intelligence (cti_lead, osint_investigator). redteam_lead and the architect made it request-free, consuming the web_fingerprint response, so it is offline analysis that may stay default-enabled. The architect's floor: multi-valued headers in the core first. cti_lead, redteam_lead and analyst_ux: ownership-scoped severity and one aggregated finding. Offline: tier n/a; bundled Apache-2.0 data: terms open.
P063.title: HTTP security headers & cookie-flag audit (OWASP Secure Headers lists)

final_conditions: Strictly offline (disclosure 'none', shares_input=False): unwrap Microsoft SafeLinks (url=), Proofpoint v2/v3 (u= and __...__ forms), Google /url?q=, Mimecast and LinkedIn/Facebook redirectors, nested wrappers included (bounded at 5 levels), and decode Unfurl-style parameters (timestamps, base64, snowflake ids) without following any redirect.
No automated call to dfir.blog or any Unfurl service (manual link only). Unfurl code is ported only after re-checking its Apache-2.0 LICENSE, with attribution.
It is the single unwrapping helper, also used by email_header_analyzer (P085) and the P172 text extraction.
Keep wrapped -> unwrapped as a relation. Wrapper hosts (safelinks.protection.outlook.com, urldefense.com, *.proofpoint.com, Mimecast, Google /url) are noise: never IOCs, never reputation-checked.

Recipient identifiers embedded in wrapper parameters (SafeLinks data=/sdata= recipient e-mail and tenant id, Proofpoint recipient fields, base64-encoded e-mails) are redacted before evidence and report.

wa.me/<digits> and api.whatsapp.com/send?phone= decode to phone entities (E.164, BR default region); t.me/<name> to telegram_handle (P333). They are PERSONAL_TYPES from text: expand=False pivots for analyst selection (AR07), never followed.
Unwrapped URLs inherit the case TLP and are passive-only pivots; URLs carrying recipient tokens are flagged 'recipient token' and never fetched automatically (A7).
Tests with the recorded SafeLinks fixture, a SafeLinks-in-Proofpoint nesting, recipient redaction and a wa.me decode.
P064.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. legal_dpo's floor: strictly offline and recipient identifiers redacted. cti_lead: nested wrappers and wrapper hosts as noise. osint_investigator: WhatsApp/Telegram hand-offs decoded, kept as non-expanding personal pivots per AR07. The architect: the single bounded unwrapping helper. Offline module: tier n/a, terms open (own code).
P064.title: URL rewrite unwrapping & decoding (SafeLinks, Proofpoint, Google redirects, Unfurl-style)

final_conditions: LIGHT module (default_enabled=False; not merged or enabled before the AR20 safety suite passes). It runs only on analyst-typed seeds, never on pivots, after the entity's passive lane, through the P376 egress guard (hostile-tagged hosts only via a non-corporate egress, fail closed), counted in the P334 per-target-host LIGHT budget.

Fixed request set: /.well-known/security.txt (and the legacy /security.txt), robots.txt, at most 5 sitemap files, and the MTA-STS policy https://mta-sts.{domain}/.well-known/mta-sts.txt. This module owns the single MTA-STS policy fetch and parser; email_security_posture (P002) stays DNS-only.
All fetches through the core safe-fetch helper: public IPs on every hop; caps security.txt 64 KB, robots.txt 512 KB, sitemap 5 MB.

Sitemaps: no DTD/entity processing (defusedxml optional extra or a bounded <loc> extractor); .xml.gz through the safe-archive helper (10 MB decompressed cap); sitemap-index recursion at most 1 level and 5 files; same-site URLs only, deduplicated, at most 200 url pivots with expand=False.
Soft-404 is decided from content (security.txt must be text/plain with a Contact: line), with no random-path probe. 404 means absent only when the server answered normally.

security.txt (RFC 9116): validate Expires (expired = info), Contact, Encryption and PGP signature presence (no verification dependency). Contacts are role contacts: contact_email pivots with expand=False, no mailbox checks; they feed the takedown packet (P345) for compromised legitimate sites hosting phishing.

Disallow paths and sitemap URLs are url entities with expand=False and are never requested in LIGHT (fetching them is forced browsing: the ACTIVE path module within scope only). In passive mode, archived robots.txt comes from P060.
Tests with the recorded security.txt and robots fixtures plus an XML-bomb sitemap, a gzip bomb and a soft-404 page.
P065.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (cti_lead voted P3). LIGHT, so opt-in (A3 BR2) and gated on the safety suite (A16). redteam_lead: seeds only, after the passive lane, behind the egress guard, with a fixed request set and no forced browsing. The architect's floor: the safe-fetch caps, XML/gzip bomb protection, content-based soft-404, the single MTA-STS parser. osint_investigator: security.txt contacts for takedowns and archived robots in passive mode. legal_dpo found it benign. Target contact: tier n/a; own code: terms open.
P065.title: security.txt, MTA-STS policy, robots.txt and sitemap.xml

final_conditions: Search API only. No scan-submission code path exists in V3LUM (public, unlisted or private) unless a later proposal is separately approved: a test asserts no POST to /api/v1/scan/ is ever issued (rule 7). Only the submission endpoint publishes, so the search source is not flagged publishes_queries.

Terms: the urlscan.io ToS (verified 2026-11-26) provide the free service 'only for your own personal use' and bar commercial endeavours not approved by urlscan, so free/keyless use is noncommercial. Off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared: a company key under urlscan's commercial terms or urlscan's written approval recorded in licence_allow (A1 day-1 queue).

API-Key header (key 'urlscan' in config.KNOWN_KEYS). Honour X-Rate-Limit-* headers; 429 = RATE_LIMITED. size <= 100 and at most 2 search_after pages. Result details (/api/v1/result/{uuid}) only with a key (403 fixture otherwise).

Two labelled queries per domain: page.domain:{d} (the site itself) and domain:{d} AND NOT page.domain:{d} (third-party pages that loaded its resources; for org_profile domains these are brand-abuse candidates). hash: searches for favicon/JS hashes give expand=False pivots and skip common library/CDN files (noise list).
E-mails, recipient identifiers and token-like values in result URLs are redacted by the core URL-redaction helper before attributes, res.raw and evidence (fixture test).
Every hit shows its scan date; results older than 30 days are historical, not current state. urlscan verdicts count as one vote in consensus.
Screenshots and DOM of existing public scans come only from urlscan.io, never from the target, and may be stored as evidence and embedded as data URIs in reports (P336).
Report links urlscan.io/domain/{domain} and urlscan.io/ip/{ip} are the manual links. Tests with the recorded search, no-key and result-403 fixtures.
P066.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1 (legal_dpo voted P2). cti_lead and legal_dpo both verified the personal-use clause; legal_dpo's floor makes free use noncommercial, so it stays a default candidate that is off under corporate until a commercial plan or written approval is recorded (stricter than the A15 BR8 key list, which assumed checked terms). The architect's floor and legal_dpo: no submission code path at all, header key, capped pagination, redaction before storage. osint_investigator: the brand-abuse query and hash pivots. redteam_lead and cti_lead: dated, historical hits and urlscan-only screenshots. urlscan is an established company: tier trusted.
P066.title: urlscan.io search (search only, never submit)

final_conditions: Google Web Risk (uris.search; class license, A1 BR15) is the corporate path, off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared: a company billing account recorded in licence_allow and key 'webrisk' in config.KNOWN_KEYS. The key is a URL parameter: merge only after the central redaction (AR01).
Safe Browsing v4/v5 (noncommercial; v4 deprecated; Google sends commercial users to Web Risk) runs only through licence_allow or the research profile.

The unofficial Transparency Report status endpoint is not automated (undocumented internal API): it becomes a manual pivot link (transparencyreport.google.com/safe-browsing/search) in the URL link pack.

Disclosure minimisation: before uris.search, recipient identifiers and token-like query values are removed (A7 BR15 heuristics); the URL is reduced to scheme://host/path when they match. The Update API with local hash prefixes is deferred to BACKLOG.md (architect floor: a large protocol to build later against Google's canonicalisation test vectors).

Wording: a hit names the threat type and check time ('Google Web Risk: SOCIAL_ENGINEERING at 03:12 UTC'); a miss reads 'not on Google's lists at <time>', never 'safe'. Google verdicts count as one vote in consensus.

Without a Web Risk key under corporate: one coverage line ('needs Web Risk key'). Keyless or unregistered calls (403 PERMISSION_DENIED, 400 'API key not valid') map to NEEDS_KEY. An empty {} answer means no match.
Tests with the recorded Safe Browsing 403 fixture and synthetic Web Risk hit/miss answers.
P067.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (architect voted P3). legal_dpo's floor, shared by cti_lead and osint_investigator: Web Risk is the corporate path, Safe Browsing stays research-only, and the Transparency Report endpoint is not automated (stricter than analyst_ux's opt-in, so it becomes a manual link). The architect's floor defers the hash-prefix Update API, so the chair adds query stripping to honour legal_dpo's minimisation preference. analyst_ux: the wording and the single coverage line. Terms is noncommercial for the Safe Browsing part; Web Risk is license, off until the contract is recorded. Google: tier trusted.
P067.title: Google Safe Browsing v4 + Transparency Report status

final_conditions: Two modules over one analysis library, both default_enabled=False. js_endpoints_archive (PASSIVE): JS bodies from Wayback id_ snapshots (P059 client) and urlscan bodies already retrieved into the case by urlscan_search (P066, under its licence gate; no urlscan request from this module), at most 10 files per entity.
js_endpoints_live (LIGHT): same-origin <script src> files of analyst-typed seeds only; not merged or enabled before the AR20 safety suite passes.

js_endpoints_live runs after the entity's passive lane, through the P376 egress guard (hostile-tagged hosts: archived/urlscan copies first, live only via a non-corporate egress), counted in the P334 LIGHT budget; files beyond the budget are listed 'not fetched: budget'. Fetches go through the core safe-fetch helper: same registrable domain, <= 20 files x 2 MB, referenced source maps <= 5 MB.

Regex safety (architect floor): linear patterns or a tokenizer, at most 2 MB scanned per file, and a test that every pattern finishes on a 2 MB adversarial minified fixture within 2 s. LinkFinder and jsluice matchers (MIT) and gitleaks rules (217 of 222 compile in Python re; RE2-only ones translated or skipped) are ported with attribution.

Secrets go through the shared secret_scanner (P312): masked (first4...last4 + SHA-256) in findings, res.raw, evidence, HTTP cache and logs. Evidence keeps the JS URL, its SHA-256 and a redacted excerpt, never the raw body holding the secret.
A found secret is never validated or used: no getMe, webhook call or provider API (Lei 12.737/2012). Third-party secrets produce a responsible-disclosure note, not pivots.

Phishing-kit exfiltration indicators (Telegram Bot API URLs and chat ids, Discord webhooks, form-action/drop endpoints) are masked findings; pivots go to the endpoint host, never to the token (telegram_bot_token is a SECRET_TYPE).

Extracted endpoints and paths are url entities with expand=False and are never requested (API probing is ACTIVE within scope); third-party domains are links_to with expand=False. Pivots are deduplicated and capped at 200; the report shows an attribute list grouped by host, capped at 100.

Findings only for secrets matched by provider-specific rules; generic entropy-only matches are an info count. Tests: positive controls (aws-access-token, github-pat), jquery 3.7.1 with zero hits, the adversarial fixture.
P068.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (analyst_ux voted P3). cti_lead, osint_investigator and redteam_lead want archived JS first and the live fetch only as LIGHT on seeds behind the guard; the chair ships both as opt-in modules (LIGHT is never default, A3, and the passive path needs more than 10 archive requests per entity). legal_dpo's floor: secrets masked everywhere, evidence without raw bodies, never validated. The architect's floor: backtracking-safe patterns with a time test, safe-fetch caps, capped pivots. cti_lead and osint_investigator: phishing-kit exfiltration channels as masked findings. analyst_ux: grouped endpoints. Archive path tier trusted; terms open.
P068.title: JavaScript endpoint & secret extraction (LinkFinder regex, jsluice ideas)

final_conditions: This build (architect floor): Postman public workspace/collection search metadata only (workspace/collection name, publisher, URL, request hosts matching the target domain) plus the APIs.guru list.json (CC0) as a daily dataset matched locally. No collection/environment downloads: deep mode is deferred to BACKLOG.md.

Postman's search is an undocumented website API: terms 'unknown', so the Postman source stays disabled in every profile until legal records its terms (A1); meanwhile the Postman public search page is a manual pivot link. APIs.guru matching runs normally.
Queries are limited to org_profile domains and brands: no searches about third-party organisations. Hits not tied to the target by publisher or request host are discarded.

Report existence and location only (workspace/collection URL, publisher, matched domain, secret type when visible in metadata), never request bodies; secrets are masked by P312 and never used or replayed.

Undocumented endpoint: 403 or a challenge = BLOCKED with no bypass; an unexpected shape = ERROR 'schema changed', never EMPTY; queries capped per scan; pagination (body.from += 25) bounded to 2 pages.
default_enabled=False. bbot code (AGPL) is not copied; the technique is re-implemented.
Tests with the recorded postman_public_search.json and apisguru_metrics.json fixtures and a schema-change case.
P069.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3 (cti_lead and redteam_lead voted P2). legal_dpo's floor: the undocumented endpoint has unknown terms (so it stays disabled until reviewed, A1) and raw collections must never be stored; the architect's floor defers deep mode altogether. cti_lead's own-asset-only scope is adopted (stricter than osint_investigator's 'or the case company'). redteam_lead: no replay and the publisher/host filter. Tier community for APIs.guru (Postman is trusted); terms unknown for the Postman part; opt-in.
P069.title: Public API exposure (Postman public workspaces, APIs.guru directory)

final_conditions: Split by opsec (architect floor). unshorten_preview (PASSIVE, default): documented no-click preview pages (TinyURL preview, Bitly '+' info page), only for shortener providers that offer one and whose registry tier is trusted or community with recorded terms; other shorteners on the bundled list are left to unshorten_trace. A challenge or login page gives BLOCKED and the manual link (A9).

unshorten_me (default_enabled=False): the unshorten.me JSON API is unknown tier (excluded at AMBER and above) with its 10 new lookups/hour per IP as a P334 quota; its service fetches the short link, so its source is flagged fetches_target.

unshorten_trace (LIGHT, default_enabled=False; not merged or enabled before the AR20 safety suite passes): analyst-typed seeds only, never confidential client URLs. A direct HEAD/GET of a short link counts as a click visible to the link creator's analytics.

The tracer uses the core safe-fetch helper: allow_redirects=False loop, <= 10 hops, http/https only, ports 80/443 unless explicit, every hop's host resolved and refused when private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT or metadata (169.254.169.254), 256 KB body cap, no cookies, no JS, HEAD then GET. Every hop is recorded (redirects_to) and written to the request ledger.

By default the tracer contacts only hosts on the bundled shortener/redirector list and reads the Location header; the first non-shortener destination is recorded uncontacted unless the analyst passes --follow-final, which goes through the P376 egress guard (hostile hosts only via a non-corporate egress, fail closed).

URLs carrying a probable per-recipient token (an org_profile e-mail in plain, URL-encoded or base64 form, or opaque tokens of >= 16 chars) are never contacted automatically and need a per-URL confirmation (A7 BR15).

Bundled shortener list covering services common in BR smishing (encurtador.com.br, cutt.ly, rb.gy, is.gd, shorturl.at, t.co, bit.ly, tinyurl...), with fixture tests. Hop URLs are masked for e-mails and tokens before evidence.

The final URL becomes a url pivot for the passive reputation modules. Tests: redirects to 127.0.0.1 and to an RFC 1918 address are refused; a token URL is not contacted; the unshorten.me fixture parses.
P070.rationale: Approved 6-0. The tally median is P2 on a 3-3 split (cti_lead, osint_investigator and analyst_ux voted P1 for BR smishing triage); the chair keeps P2 because the passive previews deliver most of the value at low effort. The architect's floor splits passive previews from the LIGHT tracer and makes every hop SSRF-checked. cti_lead and osint_investigator: unshorten.me is unknown tier, and self-following is a visible click, hence LIGHT. redteam_lead: contact only shorteners and stop before the landing page unless asked, never contact token URLs. legal_dpo: masked hops and the quota. Default module tier trusted (Bitly, TinyURL), terms open. Auditor: the default preview module contacts only trusted or community shortener providers with documented no-click previews (A3 BR2, A8).
P070.title: Short-link expansion & redirect-chain tracer

final_conditions: One on-disk index (SQLite: host / registrable domain / normalised URL -> feed bitmask, fetched_at) built at `v3lum data update` or background refresh time; lookups never load the ~2-3M entries into Python sets. Per-feed TTL (1-12 h), conditional GET, provenance per hit, per-feed terms label and enable flag. Large feeds use their txt variants and are > 5 MB: never fetched mid-scan (A6).

Per-feed terms: CERT.PL Hole (any use incl. commercial; trusted), Phishing.Database (MIT), StevenBlack (MIT), MetaMask eth-phishing-detect (permissive), spmedia (MIT), Botvrij, CyberCrime-Tracker and Procon-SP run with attribution. HaGeZi TIF and ScamSniffer are GPL-3.0 data: runtime download only, never bundled or used as fixtures (A6). Test fixtures are synthetic or from permissive lists.

OpenPhish community feed: 'non-commercial use only', and its terms forbid use for an organisation's security operations, detection or enrichment without written consent (verified 2026-11-26): off under every profile unless legal records OpenPhish's written consent or a paid feed in licence_allow.
Phishing Army (CC BY-NC, with OpenPhish upstream): off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared.

PhishTank dump (commercial use allowed per its FAQ) only with the team's own app key if downloads are reachable; disabled until then. Procon-SP 'Evite estes sites' (BR fake stores) is optional with retry; when its backend errors, the source emits its manual pivot link.

Verdict scope: URL-list entries match the exact normalised URL, and the host only when it is not a shared platform. A URL listing never propagates to the registrable domain of shared hosting, file sharing, PSL private suffixes (data/shared_platforms.json, P010) or Tranco top-10k domains. Domain lists match the FQDN and its parents, except shared platforms.

Category and fidelity per list: phishing (CERT.PL, Phishing.Database, OpenPhish) = MEDIUM for one list, HIGH with >= 2 independent families (P171) or CERT.PL; c2 (CyberCrime-Tracker) = HIGH; crypto_scam (ScamSniffer, MetaMask, spmedia) = MEDIUM; ads/tracking/aggregate (StevenBlack, HaGeZi TIF) = LOW tag only, never 'phishing'.

Hits carry the list name and listing date; listings older than 30 days are historical. CERT.PL InsertDate/DeleteDate (JSON) give listing and removal history. Missing or stale lists give UNAVAILABLE ('not checked'), never 'not listed'.

Feed specifics: MetaMask fuzzylist Levenshtein matching against crypto brands (re-implemented); ScamSniffer domains.json only (address.json and combined.json are frozen since Feb 2024 and never used for address reputation; the public list has a 7-day delay); CyberCrime-Tracker entries have no scheme: host/IP pivots and path patterns (/panel/, /gate.php) as family hints.

Matching is local (disclosure 'none', allowed at TLP:RED). Tests with the recorded feed slices: a sharepoint.com/docs.google.com phishing URL flags only the URL, a stale list reads 'not checked', an OpenPhish entry is skipped under corporate.
P071.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. legal_dpo's floor, confirmed by cti_lead and osint_investigator: OpenPhish's community terms exclude corporate security use (written consent needed), Phishing Army is non-commercial, GPL feeds are runtime-only. The architect's floor: one on-disk index with per-feed TTL, provenance and enable flags. cti_lead, osint_investigator and analyst_ux: URL-level scope on shared platforms, per-list fidelity, listing dates and honest 'not checked'. Terms is noncommercial for OpenPhish and Phishing Army only. Tier community is the lowest list maintainer; CERT.PL and Procon-SP are trusted.
P071.title: Downloadable phishing/malicious domain & URL lists matched locally (OpenPhish, CERT.PL, Phishing.Database, HaGeZi TIF, Phishing Army, StevenBlack, Botvrij, PhishTank dump, CyberCrime-Tracker, ScamSniffer, MetaMask, spmedia, Procon-SP)

final_conditions: Two modules over one matcher library. web_fingerprint_archive (PASSIVE, default): runs the matchers over the closest archived homepage snapshot provided by web_archives (P059); no target contact. web_fingerprint (LIGHT, default_enabled=False; not merged or enabled before the AR20 safety suite passes): one homepage GET.

The LIGHT GET uses the core safe-fetch helper, shared with security_headers, analytics_ids, js_endpoints and favicon_fetch (cache hit): analyst-typed seeds only, after the passive lane, through the P376 guard, within the P334 LIGHT budget. Redirects are followed manually (<= 5 hops), each hop re-checked; private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT and metadata addresses are refused.

The LIGHT request uses the egress-profile browser-like UA (setting ua_light, P326), never the API UA. A challenge or block page gives BLOCKED and is never retried with other UAs or a headless browser (rule 1).

Technology data: enthec/webappanalyzer JSON (GPL-3.0 data) downloaded at runtime into ~/.v3lum/datasets, never vendored or committed, attributed in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md (A6). Test fixtures use a small hand-written fingerprint file in the same format. An own MIT rule set for phishing-kit and panel signatures (titles, asset paths) stays separate from the GPL data.

Matchers: headers, cookies, meta, html, scriptSrc, url, dns (via ctx.dns) and certIssuer from tls_inspect/CT data (no new socket). No JS engine and no probe rules. JS-flavoured regexes are compiled by a converter that skips and logs failing patterns, scan at most the first 500 KB of HTML and pass a per-pattern time-budget test.
Passive WAF/CDN detection: the header/cookie-only subset of wafw00f signatures (BSD-3 NOTICE) plus CNAME/IP-range attribution (P034). wafw00f's attack-payload probes are never ported.

Corporate secure-web-gateway block/warning pages (Zscaler, Netskope, Fortinet, Palo Alto... configurable signatures) read 'blocked by corporate proxy' and are never fingerprinted as the target. 4xx/5xx and proxy error bodies are inconclusive.

Output: one compact technology list (name, version, category). Version-inferred CVEs collapse into one finding per technology ('jQuery 1.12.4: 4 CVEs, max CVSS 6.1'), POSSIBLE (<= 0.5), at most MEDIUM unless KEV (then capped HIGH, P291 label). Hostile-tagged hosts get technologies as attributes, not vulnerability findings.
Capture 3-5 trimmed real homepage fixtures (none exists) plus a challenge page and a corporate-proxy block page.
P072.rationale: Approved 6-0. The tally median is P2 (redteam_lead and the architect voted P1). LIGHT is never default (A3 BR2), so the chair adds the passive path osint_investigator asked for (fingerprint the archived snapshot) as the default module; the live GET is opt-in. The architect's floor: one shared safe homepage fetch, GPL data runtime-only with hand-written test data, the regex converter with time budgets, no probes, real fixtures. legal_dpo: GPL hygiene and no evasion of block pages. cti_lead: corporate proxy pages. redteam_lead: seeds only, per-hop checks, the LIGHT UA. analyst_ux and redteam_lead: collapsed, capped CVEs. Passive path tier trusted (Internet Archive); terms open.
P072.title: Light web fingerprint (status, title, server, technologies via Wappalyzer-format DB, passive WAF/CDN signatures)

final_conditions: Requires key 'builtwith' (already in config.KNOWN_KEYS). BuiltWith takes KEY= in the URL: merge only after the central redaction (AR01).

Key-terms: a company/team account on a plan whose terms permit internal business use, recorded by legal before it runs under corporate. The free key returns technology groups only; the Domain API uses paid credits under a P334 budget, ~1 req/s.
Every call carries NOPII=yes and HIDETEXT=yes so no personal data comes back.
Errors[] arrays in 200 bodies ('You need to login or create an account', credit messages) map to NEEDS_KEY, RATE_LIMITED or ERROR, never EMPTY.
Relationship data (shared analytics/AdSense ids) follows the P061 shared-id and clone rules; the relationships web page is a manual pivot link.
Merge only with a trimmed real success fixture captured with the team key (none exists).
P073.rationale: Approved 5-0 with one defer (cti_lead: the valuable relationship data is paid) at median P3. legal_dpo's floor: key-terms, NOPII and HIDETEXT on every call. The architect's floor: URL-key redaction first, error mapping, a real fixture. Opt-in as drafted. BuiltWith is an established company: tier trusted.
P073.title: BuiltWith APIs (keyed)

final_conditions: Use api.phishstats.info only (the phishstats.info:2096 host is unusable behind HTTPS-only proxies). _where filter values are built with proper encoding, never by concatenating raw input; exact host/ip filters first (LIKE queries are slow). Brand monitoring uses org_profile brands and domains.

Terms: PhishStats licenses use 'for lawful security research, threat intelligence, and related purposes' (verified 2026-11-26): open, recorded in the registry. URLs are never submitted (submissions are redistributed to the community, rule 7).

Victims' e-mails and token-like query/fragment values in result URLs are redacted by the shared URL-redaction helper before pivots, attributes, res.raw, cache, evidence and report; a test asserts no e-mail from the fixture ('#test@example.com') reaches the evidence.
Limits: <= 20 req/min from the RateLimit headers and the anonymous 50/day per egress IP as a P334 budget; cache 1 h; result cap 100. Timeouts/5xx = could not verify.
Scores below the provider's phishing threshold are suspicious at most. Verdict scope follows P071 (URL level, no propagation to shared platforms).
Tests with the recorded PhishStats fixtures, including the victim-e-mail redaction.
P074.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. legal_dpo's floor: licensed for threat intelligence, no submissions, victims' e-mails redacted at ingestion, the anonymous quota. The architect's floor: the shared redaction helper with a test, encoded filters, caps. cti_lead: score threshold and P071 verdict scope. osint_investigator: exact filters for brand monitoring. PhishStats is a small identifiable operator with public terms: tier community.
P074.title: PhishStats API

final_conditions: POST checkurl.phishtank.com/checkurl/ with format=json and the full URL base64-encoded then form-encoded. The User-Agent is PhishTank's documented format 'phishtank/<the team's own registered username or app name>' from a setting, never another user's username or app key (rule 1); the optional app key 'phishtank_app' goes in config.KNOWN_KEYS.
default_enabled=False until a live check from the team network shows it answers reliably (< 10% blocked), recorded by doctor.
403 or a Cloudflare challenge gives BLOCKED (one coverage line), never bypassed. After 5 consecutive blocked runs the source is demoted to link-only (A3/A9) and doctor says so.

A finding only when verified=true AND valid=true; in_database alone is not a verdict (example.com shows in_database=true). Hits older than 30 days are historical; PhishTank counts as one vote in consensus.

Only suspected-phishing URLs under triage (analyst-typed seeds or URLs tagged phishing/suspicious), never org_profile or confidential client URLs. Per-IP limits from X-Request-Limit headers go into the P334 budget.
Tests with the recorded checkurl JSON and 403 HTML fixtures, including the in_database quirk.
P075.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. legal_dpo and redteam_lead confirm the 'phishtank/<app>' UA is the provider's documented requirement, not a bypass, and the FAQ allows commercial use. The architect's and analyst_ux's condition keeps it opt-in until reachability from the team network is proven. analyst_ux and osint_investigator: verified/valid only, demotion after repeated blocks. PhishTank (Cisco Talos): tier trusted, terms open.
P075.title: PhishTank checkurl (single-URL verdict)

final_conditions: veto_lift: Mozilla Observatory scan triggering is removed: no POST to the Observatory API. Only a documented read-only lookup of existing results that never triggers a scan may be used; if none exists, Observatory is not implemented and only a non-triggering manual link remains.

veto_lift: SSL Labs never starts a new assessment in passive mode. Passive lookups use getEndpointData per resolved IP, which per Qualys's v3 docs 'does not initiate new assessments, even when a cached report is not found' (analyze with fromCache=on still starts one on a cache miss, so it is not used passively). 'blacklisted'/error bodies give ERROR.

veto_lift: new SSL Labs assessments live in a separate module ssllabs_assess with opsec=ACTIVE (--mode active --authorized REF --scope FILE, A7), only for org_profile-owned assets or scope-file targets, with publish=off, no maxAge, startNew never repeated. Not merged or enabled before the AR20 safety suite passes.

veto_lift: SSL Labs terms are non-commercial: legal records them, and the source is skipped under the corporate profile (reason_code 'licence') unless a licence_allow entry exists. The v4 registration e-mail, if used, is a role mailbox (P326).
veto_lift: HSTS preload uses /status only, never /preloadable (which makes hstspreload.org fetch the site).

The passive module runs only on org_profile own assets and in-scope targets (run_on='own_assets'); default_enabled=False. Grades are second opinions next to security_headers (P063) and tls_inspect (P275).
Tests with the recorded SSL Labs cached/info, Observatory and HSTS fixtures, and a test that no Observatory POST, analyze-on-miss or /preloadable request can be built in the passive module.
P076.rationale: Vetoed by legal_dpo (5-1 otherwise): Observatory scans join MDN's public history (rule 7) and SSL Labs' free terms are non-commercial. veto_lift adopted, in a stricter form: redteam_lead showed from Qualys's own docs that analyze with fromCache=on starts a new assessment on a cache miss, so the passive path uses getEndpointData only. The architect's floor puts any new assessment in a separate ACTIVE module behind the authorization gate. cti_lead and analyst_ux limited the module to own assets. Approved at median P3, opt-in. Qualys, Mozilla and Chromium: tier trusted; terms noncommercial (SSL Labs).
P076.title: Third-party posture graders (Mozilla Observatory, SSL Labs, HSTS preload)

final_conditions: Two modules over one extractor, both default_enabled=False. site_contacts_archive (PASSIVE): contact/about/footer pages from archived snapshots (P059 client, <= 5 pages) and pages already fetched by web_fingerprint. site_contacts (LIGHT): live pages; not merged or enabled before the AR20 safety suite passes.
site_contacts: analyst-typed seeds only, never pivots, after the entity's passive lane, through the P376 guard, counted in the P334 LIGHT budget.

Crawl bounds: at most 10 pages of the same registrable domain (home, contact, about, footer links) via the core safe-fetch helper, GET only, no forms, no login/admin/search pages, no query-string crawling, robots.txt honoured (urllib.robotparser), 1 MB per page, stdlib html.parser.

Extract: role/corporate e-mails (contato, sac, atendimento, security, abuse, dpo, ouvidoria...), official social profile URLs (Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, Telegram, YouTube), wa.me/api.whatsapp.com and tel: phones (E.164), BR phone formats, PIX key patterns (CPF/CNPJ keys validated offline and masked) and CNPJ text (check digits).

Organisational/role contacts and official social profiles become attributes and expand=False pivots. Personal e-mails/phones of natural persons on legitimate third-party sites are counted only, not stored or pivoted.

On org_profile own sites, personal contacts are kept only as privacy-tagged mentions. On sites tagged phishing/fraud/fake store, contacts become privacy-tagged expand=False pivots for analyst selection when the case has a recorded purpose. CPF is never expanded and is masked.
No mailbox verification, and no automatic Proton/Gravatar/breach sweeps of harvested personal addresses: they run only when the analyst selects them (purpose recorded).
theHarvester (GPL-2.0) is idea-only. Tests with synthetic HTML fixtures (role vs personal contacts, wa.me and PIX patterns, robots.txt refusal, page cap).
P077.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3 (osint_investigator voted P2). legal_dpo's floor: robots.txt, role contacts kept, natural persons tagged privacy and never auto-pivoted or swept. cti_lead's stricter rule for legitimate sites (personal contacts counted, not stored) is adopted, while osint_investigator's scam pivots (WhatsApp, PIX, CNPJ on fake stores) are kept under legal_dpo's case-purpose clause. redteam_lead: seeds only, hard crawl caps, no mailbox checks. The architect: bounded same-site crawl with the stdlib. osint_investigator: archive-first, hence the passive variant. LIGHT is opt-in (A3). Archive path tier trusted; terms open.
P077.title: Target-website contact harvesting (corporate e-mails, phones, social links)

final_conditions: veto_lift: search/cached-result endpoints only: urlDNA search, urlquery report search and Lookyloo (CIRCL) lookups of existing captures. No submission or scan code path exists in this module; a test asserts no request to any submit/scan endpoint (urlDNA scan, urlquery submit, Lookyloo /submit) can be built.

Sucuri SiteCheck, Web-Check and CheckPhish are not implemented: Sucuri's only endpoint starts a scan when no recent result exists, CheckPhish only scans, and Web-Check checks make its server fetch or port-scan the target (api/ports.js connects to 32 ports). They are third-party touches of the target.

veto_lift: any future submission module may send URLs only to providers whose result is documented as non-public (private, unlisted and not shared with other customers), otherwise never; only for URLs tagged hostile, with an explicit per-URL flag; never confidential client URLs or URLs embedding personal data; skipped at TLP:AMBER and above. Recorded in BACKLOG.md; not built now.

veto_lift: company-owned keys (urldna, urlquery in config.KNOWN_KEYS) with terms recorded by legal (key-terms). Missing keys give NEEDS_KEY (urlDNA 422 'authorization header field required', urlquery 401 empty body). Each adapter has its own status and budget.

Registry terms per source (A1 BR3): urlDNA and urlquery are key-terms (company keys, plans recorded by legal). The keyless Lookyloo lookups of CIRCL's public instance (trusted) run once legal records CIRCL's terms for that instance with evidence (legal_dpo's lift lists Lookyloo capture lookup as allowed).

Results are third-party verdicts shown as attributes with scan dates (> 30 days = historical), one vote in consensus, never ground truth. E-mails and tokens in result URLs are redacted by the core helper before evidence.
default_enabled=False. Each adapter merges with a trimmed real success fixture, plus the recorded no-key fixtures.
P078.rationale: Vetoed by legal_dpo (5-1 otherwise): as drafted it allowed submissions to services whose captures may be public (rule 7). veto_lift adopted, in a stricter form: the architect's floor ships only the search/cached-result part in this build, and redteam_lead showed that Sucuri's 'cached result' starts a scan when no recent one exists and that Web-Check port-scans the target, so those adapters are dropped. cti_lead and osint_investigator: rule 7 without exception for hostile URLs. analyst_ux: explicit gates for any submission. legal_dpo's submission conditions become the BACKLOG unblock rule. Approved at median P3 (redteam_lead voted P2), opt-in. Tier community (urlDNA, urlquery are small companies; CIRCL is trusted).
P078.title: Third-party URL scanners (Sucuri SiteCheck, Web-Check, CheckPhish, urlDNA, urlquery, Lookyloo)

P079.rationale: Deferred 2-0-4, as the tally decided (cti_lead, redteam_lead, architect and analyst_ux deferred). CrawlGraph backlink data is low value for phishing/C2 work, keyed from a small operator, and only a missing-key fixture exists; urlscan, host.io relations and web_archives cover most of the need. BACKLOG.md records the unblock condition: a recurring need (SEO poisoning or fake-store cases, cti_lead), a company key whose plan legal records, and a real fixture.
P079.title: CrawlGraph backlinks (keyed)

P080.rationale: Rejected 0-6, as the synthesizer proposed. Save Page Now publishes a public capture and makes the Internet Archive fetch the target (rule 7), which can tip off the adversary (redteam_lead). V3LUM's own SHA-256 evidence store covers preservation (legal_dpo, architect). web_archives (P059) also forbids every 'save'/'archive now' endpoint. Recorded in BACKLOG.md as a rejection.
P080.title: Wayback Save Page Now (automatic archiving)

P081.rationale: Rejected 0-6, as the synthesizer proposed. xeuledoc relies on an API key lifted from Google's web client and a spoofed origin (rule 1: borrowed credentials) and exposes document owners' personal data (legal_dpo); the AGPL code is study-only. Google Docs/Forms phishing URLs are still investigated through the URL-level modules (osint_investigator). Recorded in BACKLOG.md as a rejection.

WOT crowd reputation is low-value and gameable, its past browsing-data scandal makes it a poor dependency for a corporate DPO (legal_dpo), and protective DNS, blocklists and urlscan answer the same question better (P020, P071, P066). Recorded in BACKLOG.md as a rejection.
P082.title: WOT (Web of Trust) scorecard API

final_conditions: Ship data/pivot_links/url_web.json in the frozen P311 pack schema (label, template, entity_types, category, host, verified, checked_at, privacy, publishes=false, touches_target, login_required, antibot). The pack is offline data (disclosure 'none'): V3LUM never requests these URLs or any API behind them.

Rendering follows A2/P311: at TLP:AMBER and above every link is non-clickable text with 'opening sends <value> to <host>'; at RED third-party links are hidden from reports and listed only by `v3lum links` with the warning; links are never auto-opened and `links --open` at AMBER+ needs an interactive confirmation naming the host.

CI renders every template with a sample value per declared entity type and with hostile values (quotes, spaces, unicode, newlines): each result must be an https URL on the declared host, built only from whitelisted placeholders through the declared encoder (never str.format, never {raw} in URL position).

Every link host has a provider-registry entry with tier and rationale (A8); unknown-tier hosts get the 'unknown operator' badge and their templates take IOC_TYPES values only (A8 BR4): never PERSONAL_TYPES, CNPJ, company names, keywords, malware or actor names, or other free text (P311 lint).

Initial host tiers for the registry reviewer to confirm: trusted - BuiltWith, urlscan.io, Netcraft, securityheaders.com (Snyk), Google Play; community - aa419, ScamAdviser, W3Techs, Website Informer; unknown - CrawlGraph, Ghostarchive, WebTechSurvey.

Order: P311 groups links by analyst question with verified links first; inside a group the pack's file order is the curated analyst-value order (urlscan.io, BuiltWith, Netcraft site report, ScamAdviser and aa419 first, then W3Techs, WebTechSurvey, Website Informer, CrawlGraph, Ghostarchive, securityheaders.com); the terminal shows at most 8 links per seed, the rest go to HTML and `v3lum links`.

Verified links carry checked_at; `v3lum doctor --links` (offline) lists unverified links and links not re-checked for more than 180 days. The pack ships in phase 1 with the other pivot packs (A16), whatever the state of the related automated modules.

Entries: BuiltWith profile and relationships (analytics_id relationship template stays verified=false until checked), urlscan.io domain/IP search page only (never a scan submission, rule 7), aa419 fake-sites search, CrawlGraph backlinks, Netcraft site report (searchdns omitted: JS/cookie bot gate), Ghostarchive search, ScamAdviser, W3Techs, Website Informer, WebTechSurvey.

Legal floor (rule 7): no MDN Observatory link, because opening it starts a scan whose result joins MDN's public per-host history. securityheaders.com is included only with &hide=on (otherwise it is listed on the public recent-scans page), and the CI test asserts hide=on.

Each template is reviewed before release: a page whose first view creates a public page or listing is publishes=true and removed by the P311 lint; a page that makes the provider fetch the target live (securityheaders.com and ScamAdviser at least) is touches_target=true.

touches_target links in this pack render only for values the analyst typed (legal_dpo), are hidden at TLP:AMBER and above and for hostile entities unless the analyst expands them (links_for receives the case TLP; tested), and are otherwise defanged and non-clickable with the warning.

Google Play search and app-details links only for brand/app keywords and for package names found by other modules (APK triage, Digital Asset Links); the pages are never fetched or parsed (Google Play terms, no scraping). aa419 and ScamAdviser stay for Brazilian fake-store cases (osint_investigator).
P083.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (osint_investigator and analyst_ux voted P1). legal_dpo's floor on rule 7 removes MDN Observatory (its scans join a public per-host history; other members only wanted it hidden) and forces hide=on for securityheaders.com. The architect's floor makes scan-trigger hiding code-enforced from the case TLP. redteam_lead's review of every template for live crawling or public first-view pages, osint_investigator's urlscan search-only rule and the Google Play scope are kept.
P083.title: Pivot links: URL & website tools (verified templates)

final_conditions: Rules: CR17 weak_or_expired_tls, CR18 login_page_without_hsts, CR19 insecure_session_cookie, CR20 cors_credentialed_reflection, CR21 secret_in_public_asset, CR22 jwt_weak_configuration, CR23 sensitive_file_exposed and CR24 public_cloud_bucket, each with a P322 criterion and positive/negative graph fixtures.
Rules only consume facts from LIGHT/ACTIVE modules that already ran under the policy gate. A rule never triggers new contact or further probing.

Ownership scoping: CR17-CR20 and CR22 keep their severity only for verified org_profile own assets, in-scope targets or an explicit web-assessment run (an analyst-typed seed scanned with --mode light or active). On other third-party hosts they are INFO context.
On hostile hosts (tagged malicious/phishing/c2), every rule CR17-CR24 yields INFO context only. INFO context never raises the case score and is hidden from the terminal top list.
CR17-CR19 become inconclusive when TLS interception was detected for the run (shared core/tls.py helper, P329).
CR20 is produced only from the ACTIVE cors_probe on in-scope authorized targets, because a crafted Origin header is not visitor traffic. LIGHT data may only report observed ACAO headers.

CR21 reports type, asset URL and line, SHA-256 and a masked preview (first 4/last 4 chars), entropy-gated. The secret is never validated, tested, used or turned into a pivot. Key types that are public by design (Google Maps/Firebase web keys, Stripe pk_, Sentry DSN) are excluded or capped at LOW.
CR22 is static analysis only (alg none, HS* on public tokens, missing or very long exp, kid/jku/x5u anomalies): no offline secret cracking.
CR23 requires a content-signature match kept in evidence, never the HTTP status alone. Evidence keeps SHA-256, size, the signature and a redacted excerpt, never the full body (rule 3).

CR24: 403 = LOW 'bucket exists, private; ownership not verified'. It fires only for buckets attributed to the target by evidence (referenced in its pages, DNS or CNAME). Permutation-only hits are 'unattributed' (INFO, existence only, no listing). Nothing is ever written to a bucket.
Findings on assets outside org_profile are labelled third_party. Recommendations for them stop at 'notify the owner through a manual, approved disclosure process'.
Test: a phishing-kit fixture yields no MEDIUM-or-higher hygiene finding.
P084.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. cti_lead, osint_investigator and analyst_ux scoped severity to own assets, so hygiene noise on phishing kits never competes with the verdict. redteam_lead tied each rule to its opsec level and authorization, ruled out credential attacks and limited CR24 to attributed buckets. legal_dpo's floor: secrets reported masked and never used, sensitive files kept as hash plus redacted excerpt, third-party findings never trigger probing. The architect's floor: rules never trigger contact, TLS-interception awareness, content signatures.
P084.title: Correlation pack: web hygiene (CR17-CR24)

final_conditions: Static, offline parsing (disclosure 'none', allowed at TLP:RED): stdlib email parser on bytes with caps of 25 MB per file, 2,000 headers and 64 KB per header. Malformed input gives ERROR with the reason, never a crash (MHA's fallback Received regex as an idea).

A reported e-mail is attacker-controlled: never fetch remote images, tracking pixels, CSS, fonts or links, never resolve UNC/file paths, never open, render, execute, upload or write attachments to disk.

Received chain: reversed to chronological order, each split on its LAST ';' for the date, hop delays via total_seconds() (day-aware, negatives flagged), 'IPv6:' tags blanked before scanning addresses. Tokenization ported from mail-parser (Apache-2.0, NOTICE; the trailing '::' branch of REGXIP6 last).

Trust boundary: only Received headers added by the organisation's own MTAs/gateways (hostnames and authserv-id configured in org_profile/settings) are trusted; the first external hop they record is the originating IP. Lower hops are attacker-controllable and labelled unverified; private/internal hops are skipped.
Authentication-Results are trusted only from the configured authserv-id; others read 'claimed by <host>', never verified. SPF/DKIM/DMARC results are parsed, with Received-SPF as fallback.
Findings: From vs Return-Path/Reply-To mismatch, display-name brand spoofing (an org_profile brand in the display name with an unrelated domain), X-Mailer and similar sender-tool hints.

Bodies are decoded (quoted-printable/base64); URLs are unwrapped through the url_unwrap helper (P064, no second implementation), defanged and never followed. URLs carrying the recipient's address (plain, URL-encoded or base64) are flagged 'recipient token'. Extracted IPs, domains and URLs are passive-only pivots.
Attachments: name, size, declared type and locally computed SHA-256/MD5 only, as hash pivots with expand=False; never sent to sandboxes or services that publish.
.msg files via the optional olefile package (requires_packages, size cap), reading __substg1.0_007D001F (UTF-16LE transport headers). extract-msg, EmailAnalyzer and MHA (GPL) are ideas only.

Privacy: recipient and reporter addresses are redacted in shared reports (HTML/MD) and STIX/MISP exports and kept only in the local case; recipients are never pivoted; bodies and attachments are not stored beyond the case evidence, under case retention (A10).

The report opens with a verdict block: From vs Return-Path/Reply-To, SPF/DKIM/DMARC and who asserted them, originating IP, sending infrastructure (ASN/provider), total delay, unwrapped URLs. Input via the email_headers type (P333, phase 1). Fixtures: a trimmed real .eml with a Received chain, a SafeLinks URL and a malformed header.
P085.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. cti_lead's trust boundary keeps forged lower hops from blaming innocent IPs. redteam_lead: static parsing only, so planted beacons never fire. legal_dpo's floor: recipients redacted in shared outputs, bodies under case retention, GPL tools ideas only. The architect's floor: byte caps, no attachment handling, olefile as an optional extra, the single unwrapping helper, authserv-id trust. osint_investigator: Reply-To and display-name tricks. analyst_ux: the verdict block. Offline: tier n/a, terms open.
P085.title: E-mail header / .eml / .msg analyzer

final_conditions: Endpoints: search/commits?q=author-email:{email} (sorted by date) for logins and repositories, and search/users?q={email} in:email for public profile e-mails.

Team-owned token only (rule 1): key 'github' (already in config.KNOWN_KEYS) in the Authorization header; legal records the token's plan as business-compatible (A1). Search limits (10/min unauthenticated, 30/min with token) via min_interval; 403/429 secondary limits give RATE_LIMITED ('could not verify'), with the token hint once.

Runs on analyst-typed seed addresses for third parties and on org_profile domain addresses; never on addresses found as pivots or in pasted text unless the analyst selects them. As a provider receiving PERSONAL_TYPES it enters the default set only after personal_data_review is recorded (A3 BR8); a case purpose is recorded (AR16).
A login is reported only after an exact e-mail match in commit metadata or the public profile; fuzzy user-search hits are discarded (13 hits for test@example.com).

Confidence: commit author e-mails are self-asserted, so commit-only matches are POSSIBLE (<= 0.4); a signature-verified commit or an address public on the profile gives PROBABLE (<= 0.6); never CONFIRMED.

Placeholder and role addresses (noreply, test, admin, octocat@github.com) are ignored or down-weighted and deduplicated by author.login. noreply addresses (<id>+<login>@users.noreply.github.com) are decoded to the user id.

Minimisation: keep login, profile URL and the matching repository/commit references only (no bio, location or follower harvesting). Username pivots are expand=False and never auto-expand into further people lookups.

Purpose limitation (GitHub AUP s.7, LGPD): security investigations inside a case only, never profiling, HR/performance use, marketing or resale; employees' addresses only under the company security policy and privacy notice; the processing is listed in the ROPA (docs/LEGAL.md).
Fixtures are re-captured from the team network (api.github.com was blocked in the research sandbox); the recorded search fixtures cover parsing and the fuzzy-match discard.
P086.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. legal_dpo's floor: a team token, exact matches, minimal fields, no auto-expansion, the AUP purpose limit and the ROPA entry. cti_lead: commit e-mails are self-asserted (POSSIBLE unless verified). osint_investigator and cti_lead: seeds and own-domain addresses only, placeholders ignored. The architect and analyst_ux: header token, rate-limit mapping, exact-match confirmation, expand=False usernames. GitHub: tier trusted; key-terms via the team token.
P086.title: E-mail -> GitHub (commit author search, user search in:email)

final_conditions: Hash locally and never send the plaintext address: SHA-256 of the trimmed lowercase e-mail for GET api.gravatar.com/v3/profiles/{hash}; MD5 only for legacy avatar URLs. Hash lookups are still a disclosure (e-mail hashes are dictionary-reversible personal data), so the TLP and privacy gates apply.
Runs on analyst-typed seed addresses for third parties and on org_profile domain addresses; it enters the default set only after personal_data_review is recorded for Gravatar (A3 BR8).

Unauthenticated limit 100/h from X-RateLimit headers (optional key 'gravatar' raises it); 429 gives RATE_LIMITED. A 404 {'error':'Profile not found'} is a declared absence ('no public Gravatar profile'). Avatar existence via d=404.
Keep only the display name, verified-account URLs and the avatar hash. verified_accounts become username/url pivots as PROBABLE identity links (expand=False); free-text profile links are POSSIBLE.

Avatar images are never loaded into reports (self-contained reports, P336); they stay links. Avatar correlation uses file or perceptual hashes only, never face recognition or face embeddings (no biometrics, LGPD art. 11).
Tests with the recorded v3 404 and schema fixtures.
P087.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (architect voted P1). legal_dpo's floor: local hashing, only display name, verified accounts and avatar hash kept (osint_investigator's location and about text are not adopted), no biometric processing. cti_lead and osint_investigator: seeds and own-domain addresses only and the PROBABLE/POSSIBLE split. The architect: 429 mapping and avatars as links only. Gravatar (Automattic): tier trusted, terms open.
