P087.title: Gravatar profile (REST v3 by e-mail hash) + avatar existence

final_conditions: Extend the existing email_basics in place: its hard-coded FREE_PROVIDERS/ROLE_ACCOUNTS sets move to data files. The offline classification (disposable, free provider, role account, relay/alias service) runs with disclosure 'none' and works under TLP:RED.

Lists: disposable-email-domains (CC0) and AfterShip email-verifier free-provider and role-account lists (MIT), bundled and also registered as refreshable datasets with the bundled copy as fallback; matching is PSL-aware. Role local parts are shared with the A4 file v3lum/data/generic_addresses.json (one list).

A local supplement adds missing temp-mail domains (pee.place, tempmail.net, omail.io) and Brazilian webmail domains as free providers (uol.com.br, bol.com.br, terra.com.br, ig.com.br, globo.com, globomail.com, zipmail.com.br, r7.com, yahoo.com.br, hotmail.com.br, outlook.com.br), with a unit test.
Forwarding/alias services (simplelogin.io, anonaddy.com/addy.io, burnermail.io) are tagged relay (privacy tools), not disposable, and never scored as malicious.

Online second opinions (Kickbox Open disposable API, MailCheck.ai /domain) live in a separate opt-in module email_hygiene_online (default_enabled=False): domain only, never the full address; terms recorded per provider before use. Disify is not used (needs the full address, flagged example.com).
No SMTP checks of any kind (P096). Outputs map to the vocab attributes disposable and free_provider plus role_account and relay.
Tests with the recorded Kickbox and MailCheck.ai fixtures for the online module and list-based unit tests for the offline part.
P088.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. The architect's floor: one set of data files in email_basics, datasets with bundled fallback, the offline part TLP:RED-safe and the online checks in a separate opt-in module. osint_investigator: Brazilian webmail domains. legal_dpo: CC0/MIT lists and domain-only online checks. No member wanted SMTP. Offline default module: tier n/a, terms open.
P088.title: E-mail hygiene (disposable lists, free/role providers, Kickbox, MailCheck.ai) - extends email_basics

final_conditions: Terms: EmailRep (Sublime Security, US) terms were not reachable on 2026-11-26, so the source is 'unknown' and stays disabled in every profile until legal records them (A1); afterwards it is key-terms with a company account and a recorded plan. default_enabled=False.

It receives the full address: runs only on analyst-typed seed addresses (sender addresses in phishing triage, own-domain addresses), never pivots. Its registry source carries reuses_queries=true (fail closed), so it is skipped at TLP:AMBER and above; the recipient is recorded in the ROPA.

Key header 'Key' (key 'emailrep' in config.KNOWN_KEYS) plus Accept: application/json; without it the endpoint serves HTML (test). Invalid key 401 JSON gives NEEDS_KEY; anonymous or throttled 429 gives RATE_LIMITED.

Dropped at ingestion, never stored, pivoted or scored: 'deliverable', 'accept_all' (provider-side SMTP verification) and 'profiles' (server-side account checks), which would be rule 2 by proxy (consistent with P095).

Kept as attributes: reputation, suspicious, blacklisted, malicious_activity, credentials_leaked/data_breach flags (metadata only, A4), first/last seen, spoofable, spf_strict, dmarc_enforced and domain age.
Merge only with a trimmed real success fixture captured with the team key (only error/HTML samples exist).
P089.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3 on a 3-3 split (cti_lead, redteam_lead and analyst_ux voted P2). legal_dpo's floor decides the gating: unknown terms until recorded, full-address disclosure only for seeds and never at AMBER and above, ROPA entry. cti_lead's removal of the deliverability and profiles fields is adopted (stricter than osint_investigator's 'unverified hints'), because they come from mailbox and account checks the team rules forbid. The architect's floor: headers, error mapping, a real fixture. Unknown terms: default_enabled false (A3 BR2). Sublime Security: tier trusted.
P089.title: EmailRep.io reputation (keyed)

final_conditions: Endpoint allow-list in code: domain-search, email-count and email-finder only. The verifier is never wired (Hunter's SMTP probing on our behalf, rule 2); a test asserts its URL cannot be built.

domain-search returns employees' addresses and is own-asset-only (A11 BR4): run_on='own_assets_only', requiring a txt_verified or attested org_profile entry, otherwise SKIPPED reason_code 'own_asset'. Third-party domains get email-count only (counts, no addresses), inside a case with a recorded purpose.

email-finder only for a person the analyst typed inside a case with a recorded purpose; person_name modules are never default (A3). Generated or guessed addresses pivot with expand=False so account-revealing modules never run on them.

Minimisation: reports show counts and the address pattern; individual addresses only when necessary (own domains), tagged privacy, under case retention, never bulk-exported. The own-domain pattern feeds an offline 'is this sender address plausible for our company' check against BEC lookalikes.

Hunter takes api_key in the URL: merge only after the central redaction (AR01); key 'hunter' already registered. Key-terms: a company/team account on a plan recorded by legal before it runs under corporate. Monthly credits (free plan 25 searches/month) via the P334 block.
401 authentication_failed gives NEEDS_KEY. Merge only with a trimmed real success fixture captured with the team key. default_enabled=False.
P090.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3 (osint_investigator and redteam_lead voted P2). A11 BR4 (binding) makes Hunter domain search own-asset-only with verified entries, which is stricter than legal_dpo's 'or a supplier/actor domain in a case'; those domains keep the count-only endpoint, and osint_investigator's third-party pattern request is therefore not adopted. legal_dpo's floor: never the verifier, email-finder only for named persons, minimisation and no bulk export. The architect's floor: endpoint allow-list, URL-key redaction, expand=False guessed addresses, a real fixture. Hunter is an established company: tier trusted.
P090.title: Hunter.io domain search / e-mail pattern (keyed)

final_conditions: Sources: keys.openpgp.org VKS by-email (only e-mail-verified UIDs) for investigated addresses, and the keyserver.ubuntu.com HKP machine-readable index (op=index&options=mr; info:/pub:/uid: lines, uid %-escaped). pgp.mit.edu (timed out) and keyserver.pgp.com (redundant) are not used.

Prefer the HKP index for fingerprints, creation dates and UIDs. VKS armored keys are parsed only by a bounded minimal OpenPGP packet reader (public-key and user-ID packets only, length checks, 1 MB cap) with truncated/oversized-packet tests; otherwise VKS records existence only.
Confidence: VKS verified UIDs are PROBABLE identity links; Ubuntu HKP UIDs are 'unverified self-published claim' (anyone can upload any UID), confidence <= 0.3, no pivots, never auto-expanded.
Minimisation at ingestion: keep fingerprints, creation dates and addresses tied to the investigated domain or person; drop every other UID. Fixtures are scrubbed of real UIDs.
Domain-wide HKP searches (@domain) only for org_profile domains, or for the case company's domain inside a case with a recorded purpose.

E-mail lookups run on analyst-typed seeds and org_profile domain addresses and enter the default set only after personal_data_review is recorded (A3 BR8). The key fingerprint stays an attribute until the pgp_fingerprint type exists (P333 second wave), then cross-references vendor keys in darkweb cases (G09).
Timeouts, 403/429 and 5xx give could-not-verify statuses (rule 5); an empty index answer reads 'no key published on <keyserver>', never 'no such person or address'.
Tests with the recorded HKP index fixtures plus a malformed packet case.
P091.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3 on a 3-3 split (osint_investigator, legal_dpo and the architect voted P2). cti_lead and analyst_ux: VKS verified vs HKP self-asserted claims. legal_dpo's floor: domain-wide searches only for own domains or a case with a purpose, unrelated UIDs dropped, scrubbed fixtures. The architect's floor: the HKP index first and a bounded packet reader. Tier community (keys.openpgp.org; Canonical's keyserver is trusted); terms open.
P091.title: PGP keyservers (keys.openpgp.org VKS + keyserver.ubuntu.com HKP)

final_conditions: Only for e-mail addresses the analyst typed (depth-0 seeds), never for pivoted, harvested, generated or permuted addresses: entities with provenance 'generated' (permutation engine, Hunter pattern) are refused, with a unit test.
Only addresses at Proton domains (proton.me, protonmail.com, protonmail.ch, pm.me) or at domains whose MX points to Proton (mail.protonmail.ch); no call for other addresses.
Parse pub:<fpr>:<algo>:<bits>:<created_epoch> and uid: lines of the HKP index; 'info:1:0' gives EMPTY. Store only 'public key published' with the creation date and fingerprint.

Output: 'Proton key published, created <date>' (info), with the caveat that it approximates account creation; a key under 30 days old in a fraud case is suspicious context. Absence reads 'no public key published', never 'no account'.
The account.proton.me users/available method (a registration oracle, rule 2) is never implemented: a test asserts its URL cannot be built. ProtOSINT (MIT) endpoints are adapted with attribution.
As a provider receiving PERSONAL_TYPES it enters the default set only after personal_data_review is recorded (A3 BR8). Tests with the recorded proton_pks_index fixtures.
P092.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3 (osint_investigator voted P2). legal_dpo's floor limits it to analyst-typed seeds, which is stricter than osint_investigator's and redteam_lead's 'or extracted from case evidence', and stores only the key facts. A public key directory is not a reset/sign-up oracle (legal_dpo, osint_investigator), and the registration check stays out. redteam_lead and the architect: guessed addresses can never reach it. cti_lead and analyst_ux: the Proton-domain/MX gate and 'no account' never said. Proton: tier trusted, terms open.
P092.title: Proton Mail public key server (HKP)

final_conditions: Opt-in (default_enabled=False), analyst-typed seed addresses only. GET calendar.google.com/calendar/ical/{email}/public/basic.ics.

Store only that a public calendar exists, the event count, the date range and the timezone. SUMMARY, DESCRIPTION, LOCATION, ATTENDEE and ORGANIZER are dropped at ingestion and never written to evidence or reports; there is no 'unless the analyst asks' exception.
The raw ICS body is never kept in the HTTP cache (no-store, cache_ttl=0). The analyst can open the public ICS URL manually through a privacy-tagged pivot link (seeds only, P311).
Parse with a 1 MB cap and line unfolding, no RRULE expansion. A 404 gives EMPTY with the note 'private or nonexistent' (Google answers 404 for both, so it is not an existence signal).
Results are tagged privacy. A trimmed fixture from a public (holiday) calendar is captured before merge (none exists).
P093.rationale: Approved 4-0 with two defers (cti_lead, analyst_ux: rare hits, privacy-sensitive) at median P3. legal_dpo's floor removes the drafted 'unless the analyst asks' exception because calendar entries can reveal sensitive data (LGPD art. 11) and keeps no raw body in the cache. The architect's floor: bounded parsing, no recurrence expansion, honest 404 wording, a fixture. Google: tier trusted, terms open.
P093.title: Google Calendar public ICS by e-mail

P094.rationale: Rejected 0-6, as the synthesizer proposed. GHunt, Epieos and Gmail-OSINT need logged-in Google sessions or master tokens and Google internal APIs (rule 1), and GHunt is AGPL. The safe keyless parts are covered by P093 (public calendar) and P008 (Digital Asset Links). Recorded in BACKLOG.md as a rejection.
P094.title: GHunt / Epieos / Gmail-OSINT (Google account lookup)

P095.rationale: Rejected 0-6, as the synthesizer proposed. Commercial identity aggregators (OSINT Industries, Predicta Search...) are people-search services built on account-enumeration oracles and data brokers: rules 2 and 4 by proxy, with no lawful basis for a corporate CSIRT under LGPD (legal_dpo). Recorded in BACKLOG.md as a rejection.
P095.title: Commercial identity aggregators (OSINT Industries, Predicta Search, ...)

P096.rationale: Rejected 0-6, as the synthesizer proposed. SMTP RCPT TO probing is mailbox enumeration that touches the target's mail server (rule 2), alerts it and gets the team's egress blocklisted; port 25 is also blocked on corporate networks (architect). legal_dpo would not revisit it even for own domains. Recorded in BACKLOG.md as a rejection; email_hygiene (P088) carries no SMTP checks.
P096.title: SMTP mailbox verification (RCPT TO probing)

P097.rationale: Rejected 0-6, as the synthesizer proposed. holehe-style account enumeration through sign-up, password-reset and login endpoints (holehe, user-scanner, Zehef, Eyes, mailcat, Poastal, Quidam) is exactly what rule 2 forbids, abuses third-party auth flows and can notify the data subject (legal_dpo). The explicit rejection and the P327 lint stop re-adds (analyst_ux). Recorded in BACKLOG.md.
P097.title: Account enumeration via signup/password-reset endpoints (holehe, user-scanner, Zehef, Eyes, mailcat, Poastal, Quidam)

final_conditions: Ship data/pivot_links/email.json in the frozen P311 pack schema (label, template, entity_types, category, host, verified, checked_at, privacy, publishes=false, touches_target, login_required, antibot). The pack is offline data (disclosure 'none'): V3LUM never requests these URLs or any API behind them.

Rendering follows A2/P311: at TLP:AMBER and above every link is non-clickable text with 'opening sends <value> to <host>'; at RED third-party links are hidden from reports and listed only by `v3lum links` with the warning; links are never auto-opened and `links --open` at AMBER+ needs an interactive confirmation naming the host.

CI renders every template with a sample value per declared entity type and with hostile values (quotes, spaces, unicode, newlines): each result must be an https URL on the declared host, built only from whitelisted placeholders through the declared encoder (never str.format, never {raw} in URL position).

Every link host has a provider-registry entry with tier and rationale (A8); unknown-tier hosts get the 'unknown operator' badge and their templates take IOC_TYPES values only (A8 BR4): never PERSONAL_TYPES, CNPJ, company names, keywords, malware or actor names, or other free text (P311 lint).
Initial host tiers for the registry reviewer to confirm: community - email-format.com.

Order: P311 groups links by analyst question with verified links first; inside a group the pack's file order is the curated analyst-value order (a single entry); the terminal shows at most 8 links per seed, the rest go to HTML and `v3lum links`.

Verified links carry checked_at; `v3lum doctor --links` (offline) lists unverified links and links not re-checked for more than 180 days. The pack ships in phase 1 with the other pivot packs (A16), whatever the state of the related automated modules.
Entry: email-format.com/d/{domain} for domain entities (and for a company_name only through its domain when one is known); verified with a domain sample.
The page's sample addresses are personal data: V3LUM never fetches, scrapes or ingests them, and the label reads 'corporate address pattern: use the pattern, never the sample people' (all members).
P098.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3 (osint_investigator and analyst_ux voted P2). One manual template under the common P311 pack schema; every member stressed that only the address pattern is used, never the people listed, which the label and the never-fetched rule enforce. A16 ships every approved pivot pack, so P3 does not delay it.
P098.title: Pivot links: e-mail (email-format.com corporate pattern)

final_conditions: Module username_social/bluesky (disclosure third_party, opsec passive). Hosts public.api.bsky.app and plc.directory only. Endpoints: app.bsky.actor.getProfile, com.atproto.identity.resolveHandle, app.bsky.actor.searchActors and plc.directory/{did}/log/audit.

Registry provider bluesky (Bluesky PBC): tier trusted, terms open (developer guidelines checked 2026-11-26: read-only lookups allowed). It receives usernames (PERSONAL_TYPES): it enters the effective default set only once personal_data_review is recorded (A3 BR8).

Inputs: analyst-typed usernames (run_on='seeds'), normalised to {u}.bsky.social when there is no dot; bsky handle/profile URLs (P333 bsky_handle); domains, via resolveHandle(domain) -> DID -> profile, emitted as an 'official account' pivot.

Status: HTTP 400 {'error':'InvalidRequest','message':'Profile not found'} = ABSENT (presence absent, Status.EMPTY); any other 400 (invalid handle syntax) = SKIPPED reason_code 'not_applicable'; 429, 5xx and timeouts = could not verify (rule 5). Fixtures: found, missing, invalid syntax, handle.invalid.

A custom-domain handle is a CONFIRMED domain link only when getProfile returns that same handle (not 'handle.invalid') and resolveHandle returns the same DID, optionally re-checked with ctx.dns TXT _atproto.<domain> (core DoH). 'handle.invalid' = POSSIBLE. checked_at is recorded because handles can be transferred.

Never fetch https://<handle>/.well-known/atproto-did or a did:web document (https://<host>/.well-known/did.json): that contacts a server the subject controls (LIGHT). DID syntax is validated (did:plc:...) before calling plc.directory; did:web DIDs are never resolved.

PLC audit log capped at 200 entries and stored only as (handle, PDS endpoint, date) tuples, shown as a dated timeline. Previous handles belong to the same DID and become username pivots with expand=False, fed to username_check only on analyst confirmation.

searchActors runs only for analyst-typed keyword/domain seeds: top 10 shown as 'candidate accounts named like X', POSSIBLE, expand=False, never identity links. A verified custom-domain handle becomes a domain pivot for passive modules only. Handle history is case-bound (retention_days).
P099.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. Consolidated: the architect and redteam_lead forbid fetching .well-known/atproto-did or did:web documents (direct contact with a subject-controlled host = LIGHT); osint_investigator, the architect and analyst_ux require that only a verified, DID-consistent custom-domain handle counts as CONFIRMED and that searchActors results stay candidates; cti_lead asked for the check date; legal_dpo keeps handle history case-bound.
P099.title: Bluesky AppView + PLC directory (handle history)

final_conditions: One adapter per platform, each its own module with its own status, terms, min_interval and fixtures (or a P331 declarative spec where the answer is plain JSON): npm registry, PyPI package JSON, Codeberg/Gitea users API and DEV (Forem) users API. Hugging Face users/{u}/overview joins once trimmed found + absent fixtures exist.

HackerOne public GraphQL is not in this build: an undocumented internal endpoint with terms 'unknown' and no trimmed fixture (legal_dpo, architect). BACKLOG.md keeps it until legal records its terms and a fixed read-only query with fixtures exists.

Endpoints: registry.npmjs.org/-/v1/search?text=maintainer:{u} (200 with total=0 = ABSENT); pypi.org/pypi/{package}/json only for package names already in the case (PyPI has no user API); codeberg.org/api/v1/users/{u} (404 = ABSENT); dev.to/api/users/by_username?url={u} (404 = ABSENT).

Never fetch pypi.org/user/* or www.npmjs.com/~{u} (JS 'Client Challenge' / Cloudflare): a challenge anywhere is Status.BLOCKED reason_code 'challenge' via P321, never ABSENT and never bypassed (rule 1). Corporate or self-hosted Gitea/Forgejo instances are target infrastructure, never contacted here.

Seeds only (run_on='seeds'): analyst-typed usernames/e-mails or platform-qualified accounts in the case. Only the e-mail of the maintainer/author whose username equals the investigated one is kept: PROBABLE only when it equals an e-mail already in the case (architect floor), otherwise POSSIBLE with expand=False, also when it recurs on >= 2 of the seed's packages.

Co-maintainer, co-author and organisation e-mails are counted, never stored, listed or pivoted (test with a multi-maintainer npm fixture). E-mail pivots are expand=False unless CONFIRMED or analyst-selected and are never auto-sent to breach/stealer modules (A4).

Output: one summary row per platform (found, created date, package/model count, top 5 packages). A DEV github_username/twitter_username equal to a login already linked to the seed raises that link to PROBABLE (Ceos rule).

npm, PyPI, Codeberg and Docker Hub clients are shared with org_code_footprint (P359), not re-implemented. Registry: npm (GitHub), PyPI (PSF), DEV/Forem and Hugging Face tier trusted, Codeberg e.V. community; all terms open; personal_data_review before default use (A3 BR8).
P100.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. The architect's floor splits the pack into per-platform adapters with fixtures and shares the clients with P359; HackerOne is held back as an undocumented, unknown-terms endpoint (legal_dpo) without a fixture (architect), which keeps the remaining sources 'open' and default candidates. osint_investigator, redteam_lead, legal_dpo and analyst_ux all limit e-mails to the investigated identity and drop co-maintainers; the PyPI/npm web challenges are never touched (rule 1).
P100.title: Developer platform enrichers (npm, PyPI, Codeberg/Gitea, DEV, Hugging Face, HackerOne)

final_conditions: Module username_social/discord_invite: GET https://discord.com/api/v10/invites/{code}?with_counts=true&with_expiration=true only (keyless). Never POST (join/accept) and never any bot or user token (rule 1). Registry provider discord: tier trusted, terms open; invites are PERSONAL_TYPES (P333), so personal_data_review comes before default use (A3 BR8).

Codes come only from discord.gg/{code}, discord.com/invite/{code} and discordapp.com/invite/{code} URLs or the P333 discord_invite entity, found in IOC contexts (kits, configs, channels) or typed by the analyst, and are validated against ^[A-Za-z0-9-]{2,32}$ before any request.

Statuses: 404 with code 10006 'Unknown Invite' = EMPTY 'invalid or expired invite', never 'no such server'; 429 honours the JSON retry_after (RATE_LIMITED when > 15 s); other failures = could not verify. Fixtures: valid (200), expired (404/10006) and rate-limited (429).

Output: guild id, name, member/presence counts and expiry. Guild and inviter snowflakes are decoded to creation dates by the shared P314 decoder (no local copy). Inviter id/username become username pivots with expand=False; avatars are never downloaded.

Discord webhook URLs (discord.com/api/webhooks/{id}/{token}) are never requested: the token is a third-party credential (P165 principle). They are reported as an exfiltration-channel IOC (tag c2), the token kept only as type + first 4/last 4 + SHA-256 (SECRET_TYPES), the webhook id kept, and listed for the abuse/takedown report.
P101.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. cti_lead and osint_investigator add the webhook rule (a webhook token is a third-party credential: masked, never called, as in the rejected P165). legal_dpo keeps inviter data minimal and forbids joining or tokens; the architect requires code validation, the 10006/429 semantics and the shared P314 decoder.
P101.title: Discord invite resolver

final_conditions: Module username_social/dockerhub: hub.docker.com v2 API only (users/{u}, orgs/{o}, repositories/{u}?page_size<=100 and the tag/images endpoint that exposes layer instructions). Declared hosts: hub.docker.com only (keybase.io and hackerone.com removed). Registry provider docker_hub: tier trusted, terms open.

Never GET registry-1.docker.io or auth.docker.io manifests/blobs and never pull layers or run images (architect floor): registry pulls count against the anonymous per-IP pull limit shared by the corporate NAT and its developer CI, and fetch untrusted content.
Caps: <= 5 repositories (most recent), latest tag only, 1 page; x-ratelimit headers honoured; 404 {'message':'User not found'} = ABSENT; 429 = RATE_LIMITED; cache 7 days.

LABEL e-mails (maintainer, org.opencontainers.image.authors) are PROBABLE only when equal to a case e-mail or the account's own verified domain; all other addresses are discarded (not stored, not reported). Labels inherited from base images (official nginx/debian maintainers) or seen across many unrelated images are ignored (fixture: inherited label -> no pivot).

Secrets in layer instructions (ENV/ARG/RUN tokens, passwords, keys) pass the P145/P323 sanitizer: type + first 4/last 4 + SHA-256 only, never validated or used; one exposure finding with repo:tag and instruction index, severity by secret type, high only for org_profile-confirmed accounts.

Personal identifiers output are pivots with expand=False and are never auto-sent to breach/stealer modules (A4); personal_data_review before default use (A3 BR8). Fixtures: user found, user missing, repository list, layer instructions carrying a planted fake secret.
P102.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. osint_investigator's registry-manifest reads conflict with the architect's and redteam_lead's Hub-API-only rule; the architect's floor wins (anonymous pull limits shared by the corporate NAT), and legal_dpo's 'never pull layers' is satisfied. The stricter caps (5 repos, latest tag) are the architect's. Label-e-mail minimisation follows legal_dpo and osint_investigator; secret masking follows redteam_lead and P145.
P102.title: Docker Hub users/orgs/repositories (+ image-label e-mails)

final_conditions: Module username_social/gitlab_user on gitlab.com only: /api/v4/users?username={u} (200 with [] = ABSENT), then /api/v4/users/{id} for public_email, linkedin, twitter and website fields, plus gitlab.com/{u}.keys and gitlab.com/{u}.gpg. Registry provider gitlab: tier trusted, terms open; personal_data_review before default use (A3 BR8).
Self-hosted GitLab instances found on target domains are target infrastructure (LIGHT/ACTIVE with scope) and are never contacted by this module.

.keys and .gpg are plain-text GETs capped at 1 MB. Keys are stored as SHA-256 fingerprints only; GPG UIDs yield e-mails as pivots with expand=False. A key fingerprint equal to one found by github_user (P111) is a PROBABLE cross-platform link between the two accounts.

public_email, linked accounts and website fields are self-published personal data: case-bound (retention_days), pivots with expand=False unless analyst-selected, never auto-sent to breach/stealer modules (A4).

GitLab rate-limit headers honoured (unauthenticated ~500/min per IP via P334); 429, 5xx and timeouts = could not verify. Avatar URLs on Gravatar feed only P114's local Gravatar hash comparison. Fixtures: found user, [] response, .keys and .gpg bodies.
P103.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 with no conditions beyond the notes: redteam_lead's gitlab.com-only rule (self-hosted GitLab is target infrastructure), legal_dpo's case-bound use of self-published data and the architect's size cap and [] = absent semantics are written in; osint_investigator's key-fingerprint cross-link with GitHub is the PROBABLE rule.
P103.title: GitLab users API (+ .keys/.gpg)

final_conditions: Module username_social/keybase: keybase.io/_/api/1.0/user/lookup.json?usernames={u} (plus github=/twitter=/domain= reverse lookups for those seeds) with fields basics, proofs_summary and public_keys only; no full sigchain download. Registry provider keybase (Zoom): tier trusted, terms open; usernames are PERSONAL_TYPES, so personal_data_review comes before default use (A3 BR8).

Status: status.code 0 with them=[null] = ABSENT; code 100 (input error, e.g. > 16 chars) = SKIPPED reason_code 'not_applicable', never absent; any other code = ERROR. Fixtures: a trimmed found user (to capture before merge: only not-found exists), a revoked proof and a missing user.

Confidence (the service is frozen and remote posts may be gone): a proof whose proof_state is OK is PROBABLE, worded 'Keybase-verified proof, signed <date>'; it rises to CONFIRMED only when another module in the case corroborates it (e.g. P111 shows the same key fingerprint or the linked account), never on the Keybase answer alone.

Revoked or broken proofs are historical claims (POSSIBLE) with their date; proofs older than 3 years are labelled 'historical'. PGP UIDs are e-mails asserted by the key owner: POSSIBLE, expand=False. DNS/https proofs yield domain pivots for passive modules only; BTC addresses in proofs become crypto pivots with expand=False.
Every result carries 'Keybase is in maintenance mode: historical, self-asserted evidence' and the data age; sigchain timeline dates are attributes only.
P104.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. Members differed on CONFIRMED: cti_lead and osint_investigator would accept an OK proof_state, while the architect and analyst_ux warn that a frozen service with old proofs must not read as present-tense confirmation. The architect's floor is adopted (PROBABLE on Keybase alone, CONFIRMED only with corroboration), with analyst_ux's dated wording and 3-year 'historical' label and osint_investigator's code 100 rule.
P104.title: Keybase user lookup (proofs, PGP, sigchain)

final_conditions: Passive module username_social/mastodon contacts only instances on a bundled known-instance list (data/fediverse_instances.json: large public instances, each with a registry entry recording tier trusted or community and its terms, refreshed by maintainers). Remote accounts are resolved through a listed instance with /api/v1/accounts/lookup?acct=user@host.

Inputs: explicit @user@instance seeds, fediverse profile URLs and e-mail-shaped inputs only when the domain is on the list. Never WebFinger or nodeinfo an arbitrary e-mail or company domain to find out whether it is an instance: that is contact with the target's own server.

A separate LIGHT module mastodon_instance (opsec light, disclosure target, default_enabled False) may query an instance not on the list only for an analyst-typed @user@host seed, with --mode light after the passive results (A7), through the P376 guard and the core SSRF guard (https, public IPs, no redirect off-host). It merges only after the AR20 safety suite passes.

Endpoints: /.well-known/webfinger?resource=acct:user@host (listed instances only) and /api/v1/accounts/lookup?acct=; unauthenticated v2 search is not used. Per instance: min_interval 1 s and <= 3 requests per input; 404 'Record not found' = ABSENT; 403/429 = could not verify.

rel=me fields with verified_at != null are CONFIRMED links to that website, shown with the verification date; unverified fields are claims (POSSIBLE). Linked URLs become pivots for passive modules only. Lookups are read-only GETs.
The report lists every instance host actually contacted (A8 disclosure ledger). personal_data_review before default use (A3 BR8). Fixtures: found, not found, verified rel=me, 429.
P105.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. All six members identified the same trap: the draft would WebFinger the domain of e-mail inputs, contacting a suspect's or phisher's own server from the corporate egress. The architect's and redteam_lead's known-instance list keeps the default module passive and SSRF-safe; cti_lead, osint_investigator, legal_dpo and analyst_ux route the target's own instance to a LIGHT module under A7 and the P376 guard.
P105.title: Mastodon / fediverse (WebFinger + accounts lookup)

final_conditions: Module username_social/memory_lol: GET api.memory.lol/v1/tw/{handle} (comma-joined batches of <= 20 handles). Registry provider memory_lol: tier community (identifiable operator, public README, track record since 2022), terms 'unknown' (no published service terms; data rebuilt from X/Twitter archives).

Terms 'unknown': disabled in every licence profile until legal reviews the terms and records a class (A1); default_enabled False. Keyless only: login-, approval- or date-gated ranges are never used (rule 1); an optional token (key 'memorylol') only if the team obtains an approved account, and V3LUM never runs the login/device flow.

Anonymous access covers only facts observed in the last 60 days (README, live check 2026-11-26): an empty answer ({'accounts':[]}) reads 'no observation in the public 60-day window', never 'no previous handles'.

Runs only for analyst-typed handles that are case subjects (threat actors, fraud, brand abuse), run_on='seeds'. The numeric account id and previous screen names with dates become uses_username pivots with expand=False, fed to username_check only on analyst selection.

Handle history is personal data: case-bound and never kept beyond retention_days. 429/5xx = could not verify. A trimmed fixture of the documented response shape is captured before merge (none exists).
P106.rationale: Approved 5-0-1 at median P3. osint_investigator deferred because keyless access now covers only 60 days and the operator's terms are unpublished; legal_dpo's floor makes the terms 'unknown' (disabled until reviewed) and the architect sets default_enabled False with honest empty semantics, which addresses that concern without overriding the approval. osint_investigator's unblock note (operator confirmation or another handle-history source) goes to the legal review queue; Wayback CDX through web_archives (P059) remains the history pivot meanwhile (P119's archive path is itself opt-in and unknown-terms).
P106.title: memory.lol X/Twitter handle history

final_conditions: Not a separate fetching module: a shared helper core/profile_ids.py wrapping socid-extractor (MIT, pinned to a tested version, optional extra, attribution in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES) that username_check (P113) and the profile enrichers call on response bodies they already hold. It makes no request, so the caller's disclosure and TLP status are unchanged.
Only parsing functions are called, never helpers that fetch; bodies are capped at 2 MB before regex schemes run in memory; nothing is fetched from extracted URLs.

Extracted stable ids (uid), created_at and similar fields become attributes of that profile. Extracted usernames are filtered by the plausible-username check (maigret is_plausible_username logic, MIT).

Extracted identifiers are listed under 'linked accounts found on profile' with the source page and become pivots with expand=False in the default preset. Recursion depth <= 1, only from PROBABLE+ links, only in --preset deep or on analyst selection, at most 2 auto-expanded handles per seed.
A platform-qualified account the owner linked may be enriched by that platform's own enricher (one request each); bare usernames never go to the username_check pack without analyst confirmation.

Real names, e-mails and phones extracted stay attributes of that profile (POSSIBLE), pivots with expand=False, never auto-pivoted into person_name modules (A3) and never auto-sent to breach/stealer modules (A4).

Extracted links and handles are owner-written (attacker-controlled when the subject is an actor): passive modules only, never LIGHT/ACTIVE. Tests: one trimmed saved-page fixture per enabled scheme (none exist today).
P107.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (osint_investigator voted P1). The architect's floor turns it into a helper inside the fetching modules, because the module API cannot share another module's responses, and sets recursion depth <= 1 (stricter than the depth 2 asked by osint_investigator and analyst_ux, whose 'deep or analyst selection only' and 2-handle cap are kept). legal_dpo's no-auto-expansion of names and contacts and redteam_lead's passive-only rule are included. As a no-network helper: tier 'n/a', terms 'open' (A1 BR20).
P107.title: Profile ID/metadata extraction from found pages (socid_extractor schemes)

final_conditions: Module username_social/reddit_archive: arctic-shift.photon-reddit.com/api/posts/search?author={u} and /api/comments/search?author={u} (limit <= 100, one page each); keyword search only for case-subject brand terms. Registry provider arctic_shift: tier community (identifiable operator, public API documentation, active since 2023), terms 'unknown'.

Terms 'unknown' (volunteer archive with no published terms; Reddit's Data API terms require an agreement for commercial use, verified 2026-11-26): disabled in every licence profile until legal records a class (A1); default_enabled False.

Only for analyst-typed handles/keywords that are case subjects (threat actors, fraud, brand abuse). Records are reduced to id, subreddit, created_utc, permalink and a <= 500-char excerpt before res.raw/evidence; reports quote <= 200 chars and only when an org_profile brand/domain is mentioned.

Never build subreddit-participation profiles, which reveal health, religion, sexuality or politics (LGPD art. 11): the report shows post/comment counts, first/last activity and linked domains only (no per-subreddit ranking).
Items deleted by their authors are labelled 'deleted by author', never quoted, and used only when relevant to the case.

Error JSON inside 200 and 429 handled through P321 error_markers; per-call timeout <= 10 s and module deadline 30 s; failure = could not verify. doctor runs a self-test with a benign query (community service without SLA).
P108.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. legal_dpo and osint_investigator classify the terms as 'unknown' (default off, licence-gated) and require excerpt-only storage. analyst_ux's 'top 5 subreddits' summary is not adopted: legal_dpo's floor forbids subreddit-participation profiles (LGPD art. 11). The architect's size reduction before evidence and P321 handling complete the spec. The tier follows osint_investigator's community assessment.
P108.title: Arctic Shift Reddit archive (Pushshift successor)

final_conditions: Module username_social/hackernews: hacker-news.firebaseio.com/v0/user/{id}.json (HTTP 200 with body 'null' = ABSENT, decided from the JSON, not the status) and hn.algolia.com/api/v1/users/{u} plus search?tags=author_{u} for activity; search?query= for org_profile domain/brand mentions.
The username is validated against [A-Za-z0-9_-]{2,15} before any request. 'about' is HTML-unescaped; URLs and e-mails in it become pivots with expand=False.

Keep only links, dates and items relevant to the case (counts, first/last activity, matched items), never full comment histories. Algolia's 10,000 requests/hour per IP is booked through P334; 429/5xx = could not verify.
Registry providers hacker_news (Y Combinator) and algolia: tier trusted, terms open; personal_data_review before default use (A3 BR8). Fixtures: user, 'null' body, Algolia search.
P109.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3 without conditions; legal_dpo's minimisation note (links, dates and relevant items only) and the architect's 'null'-body absent semantics are written in.
P109.title: Hacker News (Firebase user API + Algolia search)

final_conditions: Module username_social/youtube. Handle -> channel id only through YouTube Data API v3 channels?part=snippet,id&forHandle=@{handle} with the team's key (1 quota unit). The keyless youtube.com/@handle HTML scrape is not built: YouTube's ToS bar automated access other than by public search engines (legal floor).

Keyless published interfaces: channel RSS https://www.youtube.com/feeds/videos.xml?channel_id={id} for known channel ids (core safe XML helper) and oEmbed (https://www.youtube.com/oembed?url=) for video URLs. Channel ids are validated with ^UC[0-9A-Za-z_-]{22}$.

One key 'youtube' in config.KNOWN_KEYS (env V3LUM_KEY_YOUTUBE; V3LUM_YOUTUBE_KEY and V3LUM_YOUTUBE_API_KEY only as aliases), sent in the query string only after AR01 redaction lands; quota units booked through P334 (10,000 units/day); 403 'Permission denied' = NEEDS_KEY; quotaExceeded = QUOTA.
Consent (consent.youtube.com) redirects, interstitials and challenge pages = BLOCKED via P321, never empty. Channel creation date, country and counts become attributes.
YouTube API data follows the YouTube API Services storage policy: cache_ttl <= 30 days (refresh or delete) and redacted evidence; legal confirms the reading of the policy.

Registry provider youtube (Google): tier trusted; Data API source 'key-terms' (plan recorded in key_plans), RSS and oEmbed sources 'open'; personal_data_review before default use for handle inputs (A3 BR8). Fixtures: Data API found and not found, RSS feed, oEmbed.
P110.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. cti_lead, osint_investigator, redteam_lead and the architect would keep the keyless handle-page scrape as a fallback or opt-in; legal_dpo's floor drops it because YouTube's ToS forbid automated access except by search engines, and the Data API forHandle call answers the same question cleanly (cti_lead, osint_investigator). The architect's single key name, id validation and quota booking are kept.
P110.title: YouTube channel resolution (keyless handle -> channel id + RSS + oEmbed; optional Data API)

final_conditions: Module username_social/github_user, REST API only: api.github.com/users/{u}, /users/{u}/events/public and /repos/{r}/commits?author= when event payloads lack commits; github.com/{u}.keys, github.com/{u}.gpg and commit .patch as plain-text GETs capped at 1 MB. No parsing of github.com/search or any other HTML (GitHub AUP s.7).

person_name inputs go to a separate opt-in module github_user_search (default_enabled False, A3) that uses REST /search/users only; its results are POSSIBLE candidates with expand=False, never auto-expanded.

One shared GitHub client and budget for github_user, git_metadata_identity (P115), osv_ghsa (P185) and org_code_footprint (P359): 60 req/h keyless per egress IP, 5,000/h with key 'github', search 10/min; X-RateLimit-Remaining honoured; 403 with rate-limit headers = RATE_LIMITED, never absent; 404 = ABSENT.

Key 'github' (exists; V3LUM_GITHUB_TOKEN alias) comes from a team machine account or GitHub App, never an analyst's personal token (rule 1). doctor refuses classic tokens whose X-OAuth-Scopes header is not empty; docs/KEYS.md documents fine-grained tokens as 'public repositories, read-only, no permissions'.
Without a token: seeds only, and one coverage line ('GitHub anonymous limit 60/h: add a token with v3lum keys setup') instead of per-entity errors.

Commit/event e-mails only for seed accounts. Noreply addresses (^(\d+)\+([A-Za-z0-9-]+)@users\.noreply\.github\.com$) are decoded by one shared helper into an account link and never reported as an e-mail exposure; system addresses are dropped; third-party co-author e-mails are not pivoted.

Commit e-mails: relation commit_email, PROBABLE, grouped per address with commit count and first/last date, expand=False unless they match a case entity, never auto-sent to breach modules (A4), kept no longer than retention_days (GitHub AUP s.8 purpose limit).

.keys/.gpg are stored as SHA-256 fingerprints and GPG UIDs; GPG UID e-mails follow the commit-e-mail rules. The Ceos activity/stack classifier output is attributes only and never infers sensitive traits.

Registry provider github: tier trusted; terms 'key-terms': legal records free_plan_business_use for the GitHub API terms or key_plans.github='business' before corporate use. personal_data_review before default use (A3 BR8).

Trimmed fixtures (user, events, keys, gpg, 404, 403 rate limit) are captured from the team network before merge, because the research proxy blocked api.github.com and no path is verified yet; the module enters the default set only after they pass.
P111.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. Every member drops the github.com/search HTML discovery for REST /search/users (GitHub AUP; legal_dpo's floor), and the person_name path is split into an opt-in module because A3 forbids default person_name modules. The architect's and osint_investigator's shared client and budget, redteam_lead's no-scope token check and legal_dpo's machine-account and purpose rules are consolidated. Terms stay 'key-terms' as drafted and apply to every GitHub REST user in this chunk (P115, P185, P359).
P111.title: GitHub user enrichment (profile, events, SSH/GPG keys, commit e-mails, activity)

final_conditions: Module username_social/telegram_public: unauthenticated GETs of https://t.me/{name} and https://t.me/s/{name} only. Never an account, session, bot token, Telethon or joining (rule 1). Registry provider telegram: tier trusted, terms open (public web preview); Telegram handles are PERSONAL_TYPES, so personal_data_review comes before default use (A3 BR8).

One shared t.me parser (stdlib html.parser, 2 MB page cap) is also used by telegram_channel_watch (P357). t.me/{name} answers HTTP 200 for any handle: FOUND only with the tgme_page_title marker; the generic 'Telegram: Contact @x' page = UNKNOWN 'private or missing: could not read', never ABSENT.
Each result is classified as channel, group, user or bot. Personal user profiles yield presence and display name only; posts are read for channels only.

Posts come from .tgme_widget_message[data-post] with ?before= pagination: <= 2 pages in the default preset (~40 posts), <= 3 in --preset deep; min_interval >= 2 s on t.me; cache 1 h. Runs on typed handles and on t.me links found in the case.

Ingestion scrubbing (P145/AR24) runs before cache, evidence and reports: Luhn-valid 13-19 digit PANs are reduced to BIN6 + last 4, CPF-like numbers masked, third parties' phones and e-mails masked, credentials, combo lines and leaked records dropped. Post HTML is never rendered.

Evidence keeps post id, date, URL and an excerpt of <= 300 chars on each side of each matched IOC/brand term (<= 1,000 chars per post); reports quote <= 200 chars of matching posts only; channel dumps are never stored.

Post text goes through the core IOC extractor (P172). Only infrastructure IOCs (URL, domain, IP, wallet, onion, Telegram/Discord invite) become pivots: deduplicated, warninglisted (t.me, telegram.org, big platforms), hostile-tagged for P376, defanged, expand=False, shown as one block ('12 URLs, 2 wallets from 40 posts', top 5 each).
Forwarded-from channel names become username pivots with expand=False. Media, files, og:image and link previews are never fetched, and links in posts are never visited automatically.
Bot tokens and webhook URLs found in posts are SECRET_TYPES: reported as type + SHA-256 prefix, never used (P165 stays rejected), never in clear in evidence or reports.
Fixtures: real channel page, user page, generic 'Contact @x' page and a private channel; a test asserts that no media URL is ever requested.
P112.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. All members agree on session-free previews, the tgme_page_title FOUND rule and text-only storage. Where numbers differ the stricter applies: <= 3 pages (architect, osint_investigator) with analyst_ux's 2-page default, cti_lead's 2 s interval, and expand=False for every post-derived IOC (analyst_ux, redteam_lead's hostile tagging). legal_dpo's floor sets the P145 scrubbing before cache and evidence and the presence-only rule for personal profiles.
P112.title: Telegram public preview (t.me / t.me/s channel posts)

final_conditions: One checker engine, two modules (A5): username_check, the default pack (run_on='seeds', default_enabled True, <= setting username_default_sites sites, default 100, hard max 150), and username_check_extended (default_enabled False, only -M or --preset deep, <= 600 requests per username: the Maigret curated profile without protection, activation or engine entries, plus the other WMN sites).

Default pack: WhatsMyName entries plus the Ceos calibrated sites, each with explicit presence AND absence markers, selected by measured precision from the team's egress (official claimed account FOUND, random 20-char control ABSENT), BR-tagged and CTI-relevant platforms first. Maigret back-fill of default slots only after legal_dpo's written approval in docs/LEGAL.md.

Data: WhatsMyName (CC BY-SA 4.0, archived 2026-11-09) downloaded at runtime, pinned by SHA-256, attributed in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES and the report footer, never bundled or merged; Maigret DB (MIT) pinned, updates verified with db_meta SHA-256 and applied only by `v3lum data update`. Packs ship as V3LUM selection lists (site ids + dataset SHA-256), never merged data.

Corrections, exclusions and per-site tiers live in v3lum/data/username_overlay.json (A5): V3LUM-authored, never copying or adapting WMN text (corrections are V3LUM's own measured markers); a fix legal deems a WMN adaptation is CC BY-SA 4.0, attributed and never bundled (A6).

Sherlock data is used only for its regexCheck username-syntax patterns (nested-quantifier patterns dropped) and its exclusions list. Platforms whose dedicated module checks presence itself (P099, the P100 adapters, P102-P105, P109, P111, P112, P120) are excluded from both packs; the P116 enricher platforms stay in, because P116 runs only on username_check FOUND.

Rule 2 lint (P327) at pack build and in CI over both packs: entries whose probe URL or body hits sign-up, register, availability, check_username, validate, password-reset, login, exists, attempt or is_taken endpoints are dropped and logged (fixtures: X username_available, Discord username-attempt-unauthed, Fiverr validate_username, Roblox usernames/validate, Steemit and Pikabu signup).

Only unauthenticated GETs of public profile pages or documented profile APIs (legal floor). Excluded: e-mail lookups, any POST body, cookies, activation tokens, TLS impersonation, FlareSolverr/webgate, login-only profiles, the HudsonRock stealer API (rule 3), Tor/I2P; nsfw_sites=false and sensitive_sites=false (dating, religion, health, politics) by default. A test asserts no oracle remains.

Tiers (A8): each site is a provider that receives a username; only sites recorded in the overlay as trusted or community (rationale such as 'major platform' or 'Tranco top-50k on <date>') are queried. Unknown-tier sites, criminal forums included (P195's offline data answers that question), never receive a username at any TLP; at AMBER+STRICT only trusted sites.

Limits: exactly one request per handle per site, no retries (connection error or timeout = UNKNOWN); one control request with a random handle on FOUND sites, counted in the cap; global concurrency <= 8 in a bounded P339 lane; one in-flight request and min_interval >= 1 s per host; per-site timeout 10 s; redirects not followed but evaluated against the markers.

After a 403, 429 or challenge on a host its remaining sites stop. Caps: 150 requests per username in the default pack; pack deadline 120 s, extended pack 600 s (Module.timeout >= deadline, ctx.cancelled() checks), target p50 <= 30 s. UA per P326: neutral 'V3LUM/<version>' or the overlay's common browser UA where a public page needs one, never rotated or used to pass a bot wall.

Tri-state per site: FOUND only on the presence marker with no absence marker; ABSENT only on the absence marker; blocked, challenge, login redirect, 403/429/5xx and timeouts = UNKNOWN (rule 5). Evidence per site: site, state, matched marker, URL, status, checked_at and body SHA-256 (no bodies).

Output: one counts line (found / could not verify / absent / not checked: budget) and FOUND rows only (site, URL, display name); UNKNOWN reasons are aggregated in the coverage appendix (e.g. '22 blocked/WAF, 3 timeouts'). Found profiles become has_account URL pivots with expand=False.

Confidence: every hit reads 'same handle does not prove identity', POSSIBLE; PROBABLE needs a P258 linkage signal (non-default avatar match, extracted ids, bio link to a known entity). Handles < 5 chars, dictionary words or in a bundled common-username/first-name list are flagged high-collision and never raise severity above info (test: 'maria', 'admin').

Privacy: personal_data_review covers every site of the default selection list (one review naming each site, A3 BR8/A8 BR8); packs run only on analyst-typed seeds, never on pivots or pasted-text usernames; a single token read as a username below 0.75 needs a TTY confirmation or a 'username:' prefix; no sensitive traits are inferred from hits.

Health: `doctor --sources` re-tests <= 25 sites a day in rotation; sites failing their claimed/unclaimed self-test or marked wrong >= 3 times are disabled with a doctor notice until they pass. Test: the default pack on recorded fixtures finishes within 30 s simulated and prints the counts line.

Per-site terms (A1 BR2/BR3): each site carries a terms class with evidence in the overlay or provider registry; the default selection list holds only sites recorded 'open', so the module class stays 'open'; other sites run only through per-source filtering (A1 BR11) and appear in coverage. YouTube pages (P110 legal floor), x.com/twitter.com pages (P119) and login-walled LinkedIn are never queried.
P113.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. The drafted 2,700-site Maigret-primary default at concurrency 24 is replaced by the binding A5 decision, which every member's conditions converge on: a WMN-based default of <= 100 sites (hard max 150) with two-sided markers, Maigret as the opt-in extended pack, the rule-2 oracle lint (redteam_lead's live oracle fixtures), one request per handle per site plus the FOUND control, concurrency <= 8 (architect), tier-gated sites (A8) and POSSIBLE wording (cti_lead, osint_investigator, analyst_ux). Members' 'one retry' and concurrency 10 are superseded by A5's stricter limits, and redteam_lead's read-only GraphQL POST exception is not adopted because legal_dpo's floor allows only unauthenticated GETs; redteam_lead's criminal-forum exclusion follows from the unknown-tier rule and cti_lead's rarity rule is kept.
P113.title: Username checker engine (Maigret DB primary, WhatsMyName strict pack, Sherlock regexes/exclusions, Céos calibrated sites)

final_conditions: Module username_social/avatar_correlation runs only when >= 2 FOUND profiles in the case have avatars; <= 30 avatar downloads per case and one download per avatar URL per case.

Avatars are fetched only from http(s) URLs on an allow-list of avatar/CDN hosts of trusted or community platforms in the username pack (e.g. avatars.githubusercontent.com, secure.gravatar.com, cdn.bsky.app, pbs.twimg.com) through the core SSRF guard; redirects only within the allow-list; avatars on other hosts (self-hosted, personal or target domains) are skipped.

Pillow as an optional extra with a pinned patched minimum version; dHash on Pillow alone (no imagehash/numpy/scipy). max_bytes 512 KB; Image.open restricted to JPEG/PNG/GIF/WEBP (SVG never parsed); MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS 16M with DecompressionBombError caught; first frame only.

No face detection, cropping, facial recognition or reverse face search (biometric data, LGPD art. 11): whole-image dHash only, with a test asserting that no face/biometric library is imported. Avatars are processed in memory and discarded; only URL, SHA-256 and dHash are stored; images are never uploaded to reverse-image services.

Matching: Hamming distance <= 8 = 'same avatar image (dHash distance N)', PROBABLE at most and only together with another identity signal, never 'same person' and never CONFIRMED on its own. Flat/default avatars (grayscale stddev < 6) and a bundled per-platform default/placeholder hash list are ignored.

Common images are not identity signals: an image equal to an org_profile brand logo is reported as 'uses <brand> logo' (impersonation signal), and an image seen on > 3 unrelated accounts in the case or in sightings is recorded only as 'same image'.

Gravatar: hash(normalised e-mail) (SHA-256 and legacy MD5) is computed locally and compared with avatar URLs already found; this module never queries Gravatar with a case e-mail's hash (profile lookups by hash belong to gravatar, P087, under its own TLP and privacy gates); only avatar URLs found on profiles are fetched (such a URL already carries its owner's hash).

unavatar.io is not in this build: unknown tier (A8) with unreviewed terms; it may be added only after legal records its terms and tier, never default-enabled, never at TLP:AMBER+ and never sent personal identifiers while unknown.

Reports show each matched pair (profile URLs, dHash distance) as text without thumbnails: only URL, SHA-256 and dHash may be stored (legal floor) and reports load nothing external (P336). Tests use synthetic image fixtures.
P114.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. legal_dpo's floor (no biometrics, store only URL/SHA-256/dHash, unavatar.io gated as unknown tier) and the architect's floor (SSRF guard, host allow-list, decompression limits, patched Pillow) shape the spec; redteam_lead's CDN-only fetching avoids tracking-pixel exposure. analyst_ux's 64 px thumbnails are not adopted because they would store image content against legal_dpo's floor; the brand-logo and common-image exclusions come from cti_lead, osint_investigator and analyst_ux. unavatar.io is held out of the build so the module keeps a community-tier provider set.
P114.title: Avatar correlation (dHash) + Gravatar/unavatar avatar hashes

final_conditions: Module username_social/git_metadata_identity, disclosure third_party (it sends account/repo names to api.github.com). This build reads commit metadata through the shared GitHub REST client and budget of P111 only: repos sorted by pushed, <= 10 repos, one commits page (per_page=100) each, <= 11 requests per account. No git binary and no clone.

Runs only on accounts, orgs or repos already in the case as subjects (malicious repos, phishing kits, leaked code, own org), with the purpose recorded (AR16); never on arbitrary developers. default_enabled False.

Extraction (gitcolombo logic, MIT, attribution header): author/committer names and e-mails, Co-authored-by and Signed-off-by trailers parsed from messages, noreply ids decoded by the shared P111 helper; noreply, system (^(noreply|no-reply|donotreply|do-not-reply)@) and bot addresses dropped.

Identities tied to the investigated account (author/committer of its own commits, its noreply id) are PROBABLE, since git author fields are self-declared and forgeable. Other contributors, co-authors and sign-offs are counted, not listed, unless they match a case entity; contributors to forks/upstream projects are never pivots.

Personal identifiers output (e-mails, names, handles) are pivots with expand=False unless CONFIRMED or analyst-selected, are never auto-sent to breach/stealer modules (A4) and are kept no longer than retention_days (GitHub AUP s.8 purpose limit).

A clone path, if added later, must be one hardened core helper reviewed by the architect: --bare --filter=blob:none --no-tags, no checkout, no submodules, https only on declared forge hosts, core.hooksPath=/dev/null, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1, protocol.file.allow=never, system/global config ignored, size/time caps, temp dir removed.

Terms follow the GitHub REST source of P111 ('key-terms'). Fixtures (repo list, a commits page with trailers and noreply addresses) are captured from the team network before merge; tests use FakeHttp.
P115.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. The architect's floor keeps this build API-only (no external git binary or untrusted clones) with a tight per-account cap, stricter than cti_lead's 30 x 200; redteam_lead's and osint_investigator's clone hardening becomes the requirement for any later clone helper. legal_dpo's floor sets disclosure third_party (the draft's shares_input=False was wrong), case-subject-only use with a recorded purpose and no auto-expansion; osint_investigator's 'count, do not list' contributors rule is kept.
P115.title: Git metadata identity extraction (gitcolombo technique)

final_conditions: One P331 declarative spec per platform (own status, terms, min_interval, error_markers, found/absent rules), each enabled only with found + absent (+ block) fixtures. This build: Steam Community XML (safe XML helper), Chess.com PubAPI, Lichess, Medium RSS, the Snapchat page, the Disqus profile page and Mojang; Pinterest widget, Stack Exchange and Twitch Helix join when fixtures exist.

Duolingo is not built: an undocumented internal API whose ?email= variant is an account-enumeration oracle (rule 2) and the vector of a mass scrape. A lint test asserts that no spec in the pack accepts e-mail or phone inputs or builds an 'email=' URL.

Gate without inter-module calls: specs accept URL entities (the has_account pivots emitted by username_check FOUND) and match their host in applies(), so an enricher runs only for a platform username_check reported FOUND on an analyst-typed or PROBABLE+ handle. default_enabled False (legal_dpo, A3).

Per-spec terms (P377): documented public APIs (Chess.com PubAPI, Lichess, Mojang, Steam Community XML, Medium RSS, Pinterest widget, Stack Exchange API, Twitch Helix with the team's app) are 'open' once recorded; Snapchat __NEXT_DATA__ and the Disqus profile page are 'unknown' and stay disabled in every profile until legal records them (A1).

Found/absent rules: Steam XML is always HTTP 200 (FOUND iff <steamID64>, '<error>' = ABSENT); Chess.com 404 = ABSENT, serial requests only; Lichess 404 = ABSENT, one request at a time, 429 = RATE_LIMITED and no Lichess call for 60 s (no in-run wait beyond P326's 15 s); Medium RSS 404 = ABSENT; Mojang 404 = ABSENT (~600 req/10 min).
Snapchat __NEXT_DATA__ is guarded by a schema check: a layout change = ERROR 'layout changed', never empty; bot/challenge pages = BLOCKED via P321. SnapIntel (AGPL) is used for ideas only.
Optional keys (Steam, Stack Exchange, Disqus, Twitch): a missing key = NEEDS_KEY, never absent. Twitch uses only the team's own app (client id + secret for the app token), never a user token.

Output: one row per site with identity-raising fields only (created date, display name, linked accounts/URLs); linked accounts become pivots with expand=False; bios and content only when relevant to the case; Stack Exchange content attributed (CC BY-SA).

Registry tiers: Valve (Steam), Chess.com, Medium, Snap, Disqus, Microsoft (Mojang), Pinterest, Stack Exchange and Twitch trusted; Lichess community. personal_data_review before any spec enters the default set (A3 BR8).
P116.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. Duolingo is left out of the build, as osint_investigator and analyst_ux asked: its e-mail variant is a rule-2 oracle one parameter away, the architect had no fixture for it, and dropping it meets cti_lead's, redteam_lead's and legal_dpo's 'impossible by construction' requirement more strictly than a unit test. legal_dpo's floor sets per-spec terms (scrapes 'unknown') and default off; the architect's FOUND gate through has_account pivots replaces the inter-module dependency the engine cannot express. Mojang stays (fixtures exist, documented API) despite analyst_ux's low-value note.
P116.title: Community profile enrichers (Steam, Chess.com, Lichess, Duolingo, Medium, Pinterest, Snapchat, Stack Exchange, Disqus, Mojang, Twitch)

P117.rationale: Chair decision on a contested item (yes 3 / defer 3): deferred. Reddit's Data API terms are non-commercial (s.3.1) and the module cannot be built or tested before the team registers its own app and legal records a commercial agreement, while P108 and a manual link cover the need. osint_investigator, redteam_lead and legal_dpo approved only behind that licence decision; cti_lead, the architect and analyst_ux deferred for the same reason, and the architect noted that only an auth/block fixture exists, so the A16 merge gate (trimmed real fixtures) cannot be met. Backlog unblock: (1) the team registers an app under Reddit's developer rules (app-only OAuth client credentials, compliant role UA, never a user login, rule 1); (2) legal records a commercial agreement or licence_allow entry; (3) success fixtures are captured. Conditions to apply then: terms 'noncommercial' until cleared, keys V3LUM_REDDIT_CLIENT_ID/SECRET as one key, keep only account age, karma and matched items, never subreddit-participation lists (LGPD art. 11), manual reddit.com/user/{u} link otherwise.
P117.title: Reddit Data API (OAuth app-only)

final_conditions: Module username_social/tiktok_public: default_enabled False, opt-in per run (-M), analyst-typed handles only (run_on='seeds'), never pivots.

Terms 'license': TikTok's ToS forbid 'automated scripts to collect information' (legal_dpo, checked 2026-11-26). The module runs only with a licence_allow entry whose basis is provider_grant (TikTok's written permission) or under a research_basis recording such a grant; no terms_clause basis exists. Off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared.

One plain GET of https://www.tiktok.com/@{u} per handle per run, min_interval >= 5 s. No request signing or token generation (X-Bogus, msToken, device ids), no headless browser, no cookie replay, no proxy rotation and no retry after a challenge (rule 1).

Parse only the __UNIVERSAL_DATA_FOR_REHYDRATION__ script element (2 MB cap) with a schema check: missing keys = ERROR 'layout changed', never empty. Challenge/verify pages, captcha or empty hydration data = BLOCKED via P321; the host is short-circuited for the rest of the run (A9) and 5 consecutive blocked runs demote it (A3).

Output is limited to handle, display name, verified flag, follower count, bio link (passive-only pivot, expand=False) and the account id with its id-derived creation date (shared P314 decoder). oEmbed is not used for authorship (it returns only embed HTML).

The manual https://www.tiktok.com/@{u} pivot link is always emitted, with 'automation skipped: licence' while the module is not cleared. A doctor self-test on TikTok's own public account detects drift. Fixtures: profile JSON, challenge page, empty hydration data.
P118.rationale: Approved 4-1-1 at median P3; the mechanical approval stands. legal_dpo voted reject without a veto, arguing that TikTok's ToS forbid automated collection with no licensable path; cti_lead deferred. The legal floor is honoured through the licence gate rather than an override: terms 'license' with only a provider_grant basis means the module never runs unless TikTok grants written permission, and it stays opt-in. osint_investigator, redteam_lead, the architect and analyst_ux supplied the single-GET, no-signing (rule 1), schema-check and circuit-breaker conditions. As a P3 item it is built only when cheap (A16).
P118.title: TikTok public profile (SSR hydration JSON)

final_conditions: Module username_social/x_twitter_public needs the tweet/status URL detector pattern (P333). Default path: publish.twitter.com/oembed?url= for twitter.com/x.com status URLs, a published interface.

The cdn.syndication.twimg.com tweet-result adapter is not built: X's ToS allow access only through published interfaces and forbid working around technical limitations without written consent (legal floor; analyst_ux). It may be revisited only with X's written consent recorded by legal.
oEmbed 404 = 'no longer available (deleted, protected or suspended)', never 'deleted' or 'never existed'; 429/5xx = could not verify. twitter.com and x.com pages are never requested directly.

Deleted-post recovery is opt-in per run and goes through the shared Wayback CDX client of web_archives (P059) under the Internet Archive research-purpose decision recorded for P059: collapse=urlkey, limit <= 500, archive hosts only. No crawler or search-engine UA spoofing anywhere (twayback's DuckDuckBot trick excluded); a test asserts no bot UA is sent.

Status ids are decoded offline to timestamps by the shared P314 decoder and labelled 'derived from id'; user.id_str and author handles become username pivots with expand=False. Recovered posts are labelled 'archived copy' and used only for case subjects.

Terms 'unknown' until legal records the X oEmbed terms and confirms the P059 Internet Archive decision for this use: disabled in every profile until then (A1); default_enabled False. Registry: x (X Corp, oEmbed) tier trusted; Internet Archive with the tier recorded for P059.
P119.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. cti_lead, osint_investigator, redteam_lead and the architect would keep the undocumented syndication endpoint as an opt-in or second step; legal_dpo's floor removes it (X's ToS: published interfaces only, no working around technical limits), as analyst_ux also asked. Everyone forbids the twayback crawler-UA trick and the 'deleted' wording on a 404. legal_dpo's 'terms registry entries before corporate use' and 'not default-enabled' make the class 'unknown' until recorded; the architect's shared CDX client avoids a second implementation.
P119.title: X/Twitter public data without login (syndication tweet JSON, oEmbed, deleted-tweet recovery via Wayback)

final_conditions: Module username_social/wikimedia: meta.wikimedia.org/w/api.php?action=query&meta=globaluserinfo (home wiki, edit count, registration) and list=usercontribs (uclimit <= 50) on pt.wikipedia.org and en.wikipedia.org; uciprange for CIDR inputs. Hosts: meta.wikimedia.org, pt.wikipedia.org, en.wikipedia.org. Registry provider wikimedia: tier trusted, terms open.

Wikimedia's UA policy (rule 6): the UA is built at run time as 'V3LUM/<version> (<contact_email>)' from the role-mailbox setting of P326, sent only to Wikimedia hosts and never an analyst's personal address. With contact_email empty the module is SKIPPED reason_code 'config' ('needs contact setting').

IP contributions only for analyst-typed IP seeds and org_profile CIDRs, never for pivot IPs. Results say that IP edits are historical where IP editing is closed or masked (pt.wikipedia since 2020, temporary accounts) and that IP attribution is low confidence (shared NAT, VPN).

For usernames keep counts, dates and the pages relevant to the case, never full edit histories or topic profiles, which can reveal political or religious views (LGPD art. 11). personal_data_review before default use for usernames (A3 BR8).
maxlag=5; error objects inside HTTP 200 detected through P321 error_markers; 1 req/s; 429 = could not verify, never absent. Trimmed fixtures are captured before merge (the sweep only saw the 429).
P120.rationale: Approved 5-0-1 at median P3. analyst_ux deferred for low SOC value and 429s on shared egress; the 1 req/s limit, could-not-verify handling and seed-only IP lookups (cti_lead, osint_investigator, redteam_lead) contain that cost. The UA follows the architect's run-time contact setting and legal_dpo's role-mailbox rule, consistent with P326's veto_lift (identifying UAs only for providers that require them). legal_dpo's minimisation of edit histories is kept.
P120.title: Wikimedia global account + contributions by user/IP

final_conditions: Offline module username_social/x_archive_import (disclosure none, no network; a unit test asserts no HTTP call) for X/Twitter archives the analyst already holds. It runs only when selected (-M or run); default_enabled False.
Only archives lawfully obtained (provided by the account holder or produced under legal process) are imported, with provenance (source, date, legal basis) recorded in the case before import.

Archives are untrusted: read through the core safe-archive helper in memory, never extracted, member names never used as paths, <= 2,000 members, <= 200 MB uncompressed, ratio cap 100x; only data/*.js parsed; the bundled HTML/JS viewer is never opened or rendered; media files are not decoded.

The 'window.YTD.<name>.part0 = ' prefix is stripped and the rest parsed with json.loads, never evaluated. The parser is written from X's documented archive format; twitter-archive-parser (GPL-3.0) is not used as a template (A6).

Automation indicators use the Ceos thresholds (interval CV < 0.5 with >= 20 gaps; > 80% reposts with n >= 20; >= 23 distinct active hours with n >= 50; handle ending in >= 6 digits; default avatar; > 72 posts/day; < 90 days old with > 1,000 posts); likelihood high at >= 3 signals, medium at 2, as an attribute.

Findings from indicators are info/low with confidence <= 0.4 and show the underlying metrics; they are never the sole basis of a decision about a person (LGPD art. 20). A synthetic archive fixture is used in tests, including zip-slip and zip-bomb cases.
P121.rationale: Approved 4-0-2 at median P3. osint_investigator and analyst_ux deferred for low demand; as a P3 item it is built only when cheap (A16). redteam_lead's and the architect's untrusted-archive handling (in-memory reading, caps, no JS evaluation), legal_dpo's provenance and GPL clean-room rules and cti_lead's low-confidence indicators are consolidated. Offline with no registry source: tier 'n/a', terms 'open' (A1 BR20).
P121.title: X/Twitter archive import + automation indicators (Céos port)

P122.rationale: Rejected 0-6. Instagram's anonymous profile reader now hits a login wall and Instagram blocks datacenter egress; working tools need a logged-in session, which rule 1 forbids. Instagram stays covered by username_check presence (where a non-login marker exists) and the manual instagram.com/{u} pivot link, which osint_investigator notes must remain because Instagram is the main channel of Brazilian fake stores.
P122.title: Instagram anonymous profile reader

P123.rationale: Rejected 0-6. Telethon user sessions, MTProto phone logins and Discord self-bots require logged-in third-party sessions (rule 1) and platform-terms violations, and member scraping is mass processing of personal data (legal_dpo); redteam_lead adds that sock-puppet accounts get banned and their phone numbers can identify the company. The session-free previews P112 and P101 cover the lawful part.
P123.title: Account-session Telegram/Discord scrapers (Telethon user sessions, self-bots)

P124.rationale: Rejected 0-6. socialscan relies on registration/availability oracles on every platform and Blackbird's e-mail list is almost all login/registration oracles (rule 2), with CC BY-NC-SA data and GPL code; redteam_lead notes that reset/registration probes can e-mail the account owner and tip off the subject. username_check (P113) covers the legitimate part with one engine and the rule-2 lint.
P124.title: socialscan and Blackbird checkers

final_conditions: Ship data/pivot_links/username_social.json in the frozen P311 pack schema (label, template, entity_types, category, host, verified, checked_at, privacy, publishes=false, touches_target, login_required, antibot). The pack is offline data (disclosure 'none'): V3LUM never requests these URLs or any API behind them.

Rendering follows A2/P311: at TLP:AMBER and above every link is non-clickable text with 'opening sends <value> to <host>'; at RED third-party links are hidden from reports and listed only by `v3lum links` with the warning; links are never auto-opened and `links --open` at AMBER+ needs an interactive confirmation naming the host.

CI renders every template with a sample value per declared entity type and with hostile values (quotes, spaces, unicode, newlines): each result must be an https URL on the declared host, built only from whitelisted placeholders through the declared encoder (never str.format, never {raw} in URL position).

Every link host has a provider-registry entry with tier and rationale (A8); unknown-tier hosts get the 'unknown operator' badge and their templates take IOC_TYPES values only (A8 BR4): never PERSONAL_TYPES, CNPJ, company names, keywords, malware or actor names, or other free text (P311 lint).
Initial host tiers for the registry reviewer to confirm: community - bsky.app (Bluesky PBC), mastodon.social (Mastodon gGmbH) and any other allow-listed instance.

Order: P311 groups links by analyst question with verified links first; inside a group the pack's file order is the curated analyst-value order (Bluesky, then Mastodon); the terminal shows at most 8 links per seed, the rest go to HTML and `v3lum links`.

Verified links carry checked_at; `v3lum doctor --links` (offline) lists unverified links and links not re-checked for more than 180 days. The pack ships in phase 1 with the other pivot packs (A16), whatever the state of the related automated modules.

Bluesky: bsky.app/profile/{handle} only for bsky_handle entities or domain-style handles (containing a dot); a bare username gets the '.bsky.social' form only through a vetted placeholder and only for analyst-typed seeds (architect, analyst_ux).

Mastodon: https://<instance>/@{user} only for full fediverse handles (@user@instance parsed by a vetted placeholder), and only for instances on a curated allow-list whose host is in the provider registry as trusted or community (mastodon.social to start). Any other instance gets no link (A8: unknown operators never receive usernames; P311 host check).

These are privacy=true links: rendered only for analyst-typed seeds, hidden unless the analyst opts in for the case (P311), labelled 'same handle does not prove identity' (A5), and skipped when username_check (P113) already linked the same profile.
P125.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3 (osint_investigator voted P2). The architect's and analyst_ux's conditions prevent dead links (Bluesky only for handle-like inputs, Mastodon only with an instance). Because a generated link sends the username to the instance, legal_dpo's A8 floor limits Mastodon to allow-listed trusted/community instances, which also satisfies P311's declared-host check. legal_dpo's A5 homonym label applies. A16 ships every pivot pack.
P125.title: Pivot links: social profiles (Bluesky, Mastodon)

final_conditions: Offline module phone/phone_parse (disclosure none, no network). python 'phonenumbers' (Apache-2.0) is an optional extra (requires_packages, pure-Python wheel); the core E.164 normalisation is reused (no second implementation); default_region comes from the existing setting (BR).
Output: validity, line type, E.164/national formats, geodescription (DDD -> city/state) and time zones. The carrier is labelled 'original carrier (portability not reflected)'.

Bundled data/br_ddd.json (DDD -> UF and main city) is generated by a maintainer script from Anatel's published numbering plan, with source and date, and registered in the P330 notices registry. The full city list per DDD comes from the brasilapi_ddd dataset (P127) when present.
PhoneNumberMatcher(text, 'BR') runs only inside text/file extraction (P172) with a match cap; extracted phones are PERSONAL_TYPES pivots with expand=False (AR07).
CPF region, DDD and CEP UF mismatches are weak consistency signals (people move): info only, never fraud verdicts.

The Anatel numbering open-data enrichment (number block -> original operator; 0800/0300/0303/4004/4003 holders) is deferred until its dataset URL is verified from the team network (the research egress got CONNECT 502); it will then be a registered dataset fetched by `v3lum data update`.

The current operator after portability is available only manually through ABR Telecom's 'consulta numero portado' page (reCAPTCHA): a manual pivot link (P128), never automated. Tests: BR mobile, landline and 0800 vectors, invalid numbers and the extraction cap.
P126.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. All members want offline parsing with the 'original carrier' wording (portability); legal_dpo adds that region mismatches are weak signals. The architect's floor makes phonenumbers an optional extra, reuses the core E.164 code, bundles a generated DDD table and defers the Anatel part until its URL is verified. Offline: tier 'n/a', terms 'open'.
P126.title: Phone parsing offline (libphonenumber) + BR DDD -> UF table

final_conditions: Folded into phone_parse (P126) as offline data: no per-scan network call.
