A registered dataset brasilapi_ddd (register_dataset, 30-day TTL) is prefetched by `v3lum data update` with one GET of brasilapi.com.br/api/ddd/v1/{ddd} per valid DDD (67 calls, <= 1 req/s); requests carry only the 2-digit DDD, never a phone number.

Scan-time answers are offline lookups (disclosure none). When the dataset is missing, the bundled DDD -> UF table answers and coverage says 'city list unavailable (run v3lum data update brasilapi_ddd)'.

Report: UF + main city + 'N cities in DDD', with the full city list behind a toggle in HTML and in JSON only. Attribution: BrasilAPI (MIT code) over Anatel data, in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES. Registry provider brasilapi: tier community, terms open.
P127.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3 (legal_dpo voted P2). cti_lead, the architect and analyst_ux asked to fold this static data into phone_parse instead of calling an API per number; that is adopted as a prefetched dataset that sends only DDDs. Offline at scan time: tier 'n/a' (the dataset provider BrasilAPI is community tier), terms 'open'.
P127.title: BrasilAPI DDD (cities per area code)

final_conditions: Data-only pivot pack v3lum/data/pivot_links/phone.json for the P311 engine: spamcalls.net (https://spamcalls.net/en/num/{e164}, labelled 'user reports, unverified') and, after URL verification, ABR Telecom's 'consulta numero portado' page (current operator after portability; CAPTCHA, manual only). V3LUM never fetches any of these links.

Messaging links wa.me/{digits} and t.me/+{e164} are off by default (setting phone_messaging_links=false). When enabled they carry 'manual: opens the app with YOUR account; nothing is sent unless you type; use a team research device' and are never used as presence checks (P131 stays rejected).

Core links gets an {e164}/{digits} placeholder and encoder (today's placeholders cannot express digits without '+'), with tests; every template passes the P311 lint (https, declared host, value only in the path/query, no CPF).

TLP: at AMBER and above the links render as non-clickable text with 'opening sends <number> to <host>' (A2). privacy=true (P311): the links apply only to analyst-typed phone seeds, never to auto-discovered numbers, and stay hidden unless the analyst opts in for the case.

Link hosts carry registry tiers: spamcalls.net community, wa.me and t.me trusted, ABR Telecom trusted; the P311 lint rejects unknown-tier hosts for phone templates (A8). As a pivot-link pack it ships in phase 1 with the P311 engine (A16 BR1/BR4).
P128.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3; priority raised to P1 because A16 BR1 and BR4 (binding) ship every approved pivot-link pack in phase 1 even if related modules slip, and osint_investigator rated it P1 as the only step past parsing for phones. legal_dpo's floor makes the messaging links opt-in (they invite the presence checks rejected in P131) and non-clickable at AMBER+; analyst_ux's opsec label and the architect's placeholder work are included. A data pack with no network: tier 'n/a', terms 'open'.
P128.title: Phone pivot links (spamcalls.net)

P129.rationale: Rejected (yes 1 / reject 3 / defer 2). For Brazilian numbers Numverify, AbstractAPI and Veriphone return what phone_parse (P126) computes offline (validity, line type, pre-portability carrier) while sending the full number to foreign vendors. Backlog note: revisit only for a provider with licensed current-portability data for Brazil; then default off, TLP:CLEAR/GREEN only, keyed with a company plan whose business use legal records, an international-transfer basis recorded (provider terms/DPA under Res. CD/ANPD 19/2024), one call per number after offline parsing (legal_dpo, redteam_lead).
P129.title: Keyed phone validation (Numverify, AbstractAPI, Veriphone)

P130.rationale: Rejected (yes 1 / reject 5). AreaCodeCheck is NANP-centric, unknown-tier and receives the full number (A8 forbids sending phone numbers to unknown-tier operators); OVH detailedZones adds nothing libphonenumber (P126) does not already give offline. legal_dpo's conditional approval (OVH only, after terms are recorded) did not carry the council; no backlog action.
P130.title: Minor keyless numbering lookups (AreaCodeCheck, OVH detailedZones)

P131.rationale: Rejected 0-6. Caller-ID apps (Truecaller, Getcontact, Sync.me) rely on harvested contact books behind logged-in mobile APIs, and WhatsApp/Telegram presence checkers are account-existence oracles behind logged-in sessions (rules 1, 2 and 4; LGPD); redteam_lead adds that such lookups can tip off the subject. The manual wa.me/t.me links of P128 (opt-in, never fetched) are the permitted path.
P131.title: Caller-ID apps and WhatsApp/Telegram presence checkers

final_conditions: Keyless catalogue endpoints only: /api/v3/breaches (also ?domain=), /breach/{name}, /latestbreach and /dataclasses. HIBP's terms allow them 'for any lawful purpose, including within commercial products' (verified 2026-11-26).

/breaches is a registered dataset (24 h TTL, stale copy kept on failure); domain lookups are answered locally from it, so they disclose nothing. HIBP rejects requests without a User-Agent: the default neutral 'V3LUM/<version>' UA (P326) is sent.

One shared breach-catalogue helper (lookup by normalised name and domain) is used by every breach module (P133, P134, P135, P137, P140) to add breach dates, data classes and the IsVerified, IsFabricated, IsSpamList, IsStealerLog and IsSensitive flags and the breach category. No module keeps its own copy.

The flags propagate downstream: IsSensitive and sensitive-category breaches (adult, dating, health, religion, sexual orientation, politics) are shown as 'sensitive breach (name withheld)' by default; IsSpamList/IsFabricated breaches never count as exposure.
The password FORM is derived from the breach description (Céos forma_senha port: plaintext, or hashed: <algorithm>), the only password-related fact kept (A4).
?domain= means 'this service was breached', never 'accounts at my domain'; that wording is visible in reports.
Attribution 'Have I Been Pwned' (CC BY 4.0) with a link wherever results are shown. Tests with the recorded catalogue, single-breach, by-domain and dataclasses fixtures.
P132.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1 (redteam_lead voted P2). legal_dpo's floor: attribution, the UA HIBP requires and flag propagation so sensitive breaches are masked downstream. The architect's floor: one shared catalogue helper as a dataset. analyst_ux: the ?domain= wording. HIBP is an established service with published terms allowing commercial use: tier trusted, terms open.
P132.title: Have I Been Pwned breach catalogue (+ domain filter, latest, data classes)

final_conditions: Company-paid key only (key 'hibp' in the hibp-api-key header), recorded in licence_allow as the HIBP subscription (budget: Core 1, from US$4.39/month: 10 RPM, one own domain, no stealer logs). Off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared (that subscription recorded). HIBP's Permitted Purpose is on-demand queries within the plan's rate limit.

min_interval from a tier setting (default 6 s for 10 RPM); Retry-After honoured. breachedaccount?truncateResponse=false. A 404 is a declared meaningful absence worded 'not found in HIBP', never 'never breached'.

Breach scope (A4): run_on='own_assets' (addresses on txt_verified/attested org_profile domains). Third-party addresses only as analyst-typed seeds with --breach-scope all and --purpose, giving context only (earliest breach date, data classes), severity at most MEDIUM and no exposure score; never pivots or addresses from text.

Domain search and any stealer-log endpoint are run_on='own_assets_only' (A11 BR4: txt_verified or attested domains). Related entities' or customers' domains only with a plan that expressly allows it (HIBP terms). Stealer logs exist only on Pro plans and are used only if such a plan is recorded.
Pastes: metadata only; paste content is never fetched (a manual link at most).

Breach names are enriched through the P132 catalogue helper. IsSensitive/sensitive-category breaches read 'sensitive breach (name withheld)', are never scored on category, and support no inference about the person (LGPD art. 11). IsSpamList/IsFabricated never count; breaches older than 3 years lower severity unless the data classes include passwords and no rotation is known.

Findings are merged per normalised breach name across HIBP, XposedOrNot, LeakCheck and Leak-Lookup into one finding listing all sources and the breach date (with P146), so one breach is not counted 3-4 times by the noisy-OR. Each finding states its data classes and a next step ('password exposed in a 2019 breach: confirm it was changed and not reused').

HIBP is a sensitive provider: the P145 schema applies before the HTTP cache (sanitized payload, TTL <= 7 days). Generic/role/test addresses are flagged and never scored (A4). Employees' addresses are checked under the security policy/privacy notice; the processing is in the ROPA; attribution shown.

As a provider receiving PERSONAL_TYPES, HIBP enters the default set only after personal_data_review {basis, reviewer, date} is recorded in the registry (A3 BR8, LGPD art. 33 transfer basis); until then it runs only when explicitly selected in a case with a recorded purpose (Status.SKIPPED reason_code 'privacy').
Tests: the recorded 401 fixture (missing key), a synthetic breachedaccount answer, the 404 wording, and the same breach from 3 sources giving 1 finding with 3 sources.
P133.rationale: Approved 6-0. The tally median is P2 (cti_lead and analyst_ux voted P1); the chair keeps P2 because it needs a purchased key, while the budget item is recorded for the team. legal_dpo's floor: a company-paid key, own verified domains for domain search, purpose for third parties, sensitive breaches withheld, pastes metadata only, ROPA. A4 binds the own-assets scope. The architect: header key, tier-based interval, 404 wording, the shared catalogue. analyst_ux: cross-source merging and next steps. HIBP: tier trusted; terms license (paid subscription). Auditor: A3 BR8 personal_data_review gate added (HIBP receives e-mail addresses).
P133.title: HIBP per-account breaches/pastes (paid key)

final_conditions: veto_lift (1): the P145 sanitizer schema for Hudson Rock (provider flagged sensitive) is a field ALLOWLIST applied before the HTTP cache, evidence, logs and graph. Per stealer keep only date_compromised, stealer family, total_corporate_services and total_user_services; at top level only the counts. Everything else is dropped, so schema drift cannot leak.

Dropped fields include top_passwords, top_logins, computer_name, ip, malware_path, antiviruses, operating_system (not on the A4 BR4/P145 kept list) and any new field; the top-level message only maps the status and is never stored. The cache stores only the sanitized JSON (or no-store), TTL <= 7 days (A4).
veto_lift (2): only scrubbed fixtures are committed: live_osint__hudsonrock_email.json (a victim's computer name, Windows user path and partial IP) is rebuilt with synthetic values in those fields.

veto_lift (3): terms 'unknown' (A1 BR16): disabled in every profile until Hudson Rock confirms its terms in writing or legal records a licence_allow entry/reclassification; coverage says 'licence: terms unknown', never empty. default_enabled=False while the terms are unknown (A3 BR2).

veto_lift (4): urls-by-domain only for org_profile domains (run_on='own_assets_only', A11 BR4), with query strings and user-identifying path segments stripped (scheme + host + path). Results are url entities with expand=False: attack-surface context, never contacted automatically.

veto_lift (5): generic/test/role addresses (data/generic_addresses.json, or >= 5 computers for one address; test@example.com returns 5) are flagged, capped at POSSIBLE and never scored (info 'generic address').

veto_lift (6) and A4: search-by-email/username uses run_on='own_assets' (verified org_profile domains); employees' addresses only under the security policy/privacy notice. Third-party identities only as analyst-typed seeds with --breach-scope all and --purpose, as context (at most MEDIUM, no exposure score). search-by-ip only for org_profile CIDRs.

Severity for own identities follows P146 CR09: CRITICAL only on a verified org_profile domain with date_compromised <= 12 months; older logs with corporate services > 0 HIGH, other older ones MEDIUM 'historical exposure, verify rotation', with the date shown. search-by-domain is a stealer domain search: run_on='own_assets_only' (A11 BR4), counts only.

Each finding carries next steps: reset the password, revoke sessions/tokens, check MFA, identify the infected device's owner. Leaked data is never used for login attempts, spraying or validation in any mode or engagement (A4 BR12).

30 s per-request timeout (the domain search hung > 70 s); timeouts give ERROR reason_code 'timeout' (could not verify). A unit test asserts none of the dropped keys or values reach cache, evidence, logs, case DB, reports, events or --debug output, and the end-to-end grep of A4 BR13 runs over the synthetic fixtures.
P134.rationale: Vetoed by legal_dpo (5-1 otherwise, median P1): the raw answers carry masked passwords and victims' machine identifiers that the HTTP cache would keep, a committed fixture holds a victim's data, and the terms are unknown. veto_lift adopted: all six lift conditions are in this spec, and they match A4/P145, cti_lead, osint_investigator, redteam_lead and analyst_ux, who all asked to scrub before the cache. The architect's floor turns the scrub into an allowlist. Because the terms are unknown (A1 BR16) the module ships disabled and default_enabled false until legal clears it; P1 keeps it ready for that decision. analyst_ux and cti_lead: recency-graded severity and next steps. Hudson Rock is an identifiable company whose free tools publish no terms: tier community, terms unknown. Auditor: operating_system and the message are dropped from the allowlist because A4 BR4 and P145 keep only the listed metadata (legal floor); severity follows P146 CR09; search-by-domain is own-asset-only under A11 BR4.
P134.title: Hudson Rock Cavalier free OSINT endpoints (infostealer exposure metadata)

final_conditions: Terms 'unknown' (A1 BR16; no terms page reachable on 2026-11-26): disabled in every profile until legal records LeakCheck's terms. default_enabled=False while unknown.

osint_investigator's evidence (LeakCheck API docs, checked 2026-11-26: the Public API is 'Free, including commercial use' with a 'Powered by LeakCheck' link) is queued for that review; if cleared, the class becomes open with that attribution in the report footer and `v3lum info`.

URL allow-list: only GET leakcheck.io/api/public?check=<value>. The authenticated v2 'lookup' API (raw records with passwords) is never implemented or subscribed to; a test asserts its URL cannot be built.
Store only the found count, source names and dates, and field NAMES as breach data classes, never values. LeakCheck is a sensitive provider: P145 schema before the HTTP cache.
found >= 100 flags a generic/shared address (A4: test@example.com returns found=1715): info only, never scored.
429/'limit' bodies give RATE_LIMITED/QUOTA with the provider marked exhausted for the day, shown once per scan; min_interval >= 1 s (documented 1 RPS).

Source names are normalised (domain suffix stripped) through the P132 catalogue helper and merged with HIBP/XposedOrNot per normalised name: LeakCheck alone never adds a separate scored finding for a breach already reported. Sensitive-category source names are masked as 'sensitive breach'.
Scope (A4): run_on='own_assets'; third-party addresses and usernames only as analyst-typed seeds with --breach-scope all and --purpose, as context, not score.
Tests with the recorded test@example.com, e-mail and username fixtures.
P135.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (osint_investigator voted P1). The council split on terms: osint_investigator found documentation allowing commercial use, while legal_dpo found no terms page and A1 BR16 binds 'unknown'; a chair may only be stricter, so the module ships disabled until legal records the terms, with osint_investigator's evidence queued for that review. default_enabled therefore false (A3 BR2). The architect's floor: URL allow-list and field names only. cti_lead and analyst_ux: the >= 100 generic rule and cross-source merging. Tier community (identifiable operator without published terms).
P135.title: LeakCheck public API (breach sources + field names)

final_conditions: Terms 'unknown': the only Webz.io terms found (webz.io/terms, for its free News API Lite) limit data derivatives to non-commercial use and none cover the Lunar endpoint. Disabled in every profile until Webz.io confirms in writing or legal records the terms (A1). default_enabled=False while unknown.

Runs only for org_profile own domains and analyst-typed seed domains (e.g. suppliers inside a case with a recorded purpose); never for pivoted domains, webmail/free-provider domains or noise-list domains (gmail.com counts are meaningless).
Aggregate counts only (events in 12 months, top stealer families, OS, AV, top login hosts, months), never records. Lunar is a sensitive provider: the P145 schema keeps only these aggregate fields.

Presented as an info/low 'domain exposure card': context, not the compromise of a specific account. Implausible volumes (> 100k events, test domains such as example.com) carry an 'unreliable/generic' caveat.
Results are confidential case data with a minimum marking of TLP:AMBER: tagged confidential, shown in AMBER-marked report sections and excluded from CLEAR/GREEN exports and shareable reports.
Cache 24 h; error bodies mapped to ERROR/RATE_LIMITED. Tests with the recorded lunar_domain_exposure fixture.
P136.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. legal_dpo's floor classes the terms unknown (osint_investigator found only non-commercial Webz.io terms, so it would be noncommercial at best); unknown is the stricter class, so the module ships disabled and opt-in until reviewed (A3 BR2). cti_lead, osint_investigator, legal_dpo and analyst_ux: own and supplier domains only, aggregate counts, confidential handling and the junk-domain caveat. The architect found it simple. Webz.io is an established company: tier trusted.
P136.title: Lunar (Webz.io) domain exposure API (aggregate only)

final_conditions: Terms (A1 BR15): keyless XposedOrNot = noncommercial ('Commercial use of our data requires a proper licensing agreement', verified 2026-11-26); xonAPI+ = key-terms with key_plans.xon='business' (from US$9/month), xonEnterprise+ for own-domain monitoring. Off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared; keyless use only through licence_allow or the research profile.

Endpoints: check-email and breach-analytics (lowercased e-mail); the breaches catalogue (~645 KB) as a daily dataset joined offline through the P132 helper (?domain= = 'was this SERVICE breached'); domain-breaches only with key 'xon' for txt_verified/attested own domains (run_on='own_assets_only', A11 BR4), because it returns employees' e-mails (access restricted to the case).
Breach scope (A4): check-email uses run_on='own_assets'; third-party addresses only as analyst-typed seeds with --breach-scope all and --purpose, as context (at most MEDIUM, no exposure score).

Limits: 2 req/s, 25/hour, 100/day per egress IP: min_interval 0.5 s with hourly and daily windows in the P334 block. Keyless exhaustion gives RATE_LIMITED/QUOTA, shown once per scan with the key hint.
Metadata only; XposedOrNot is a sensitive provider (P145 schema before the HTTP cache). Sensitive-category breaches are masked by default. Logos (external images) are never loaded.

As a provider receiving PERSONAL_TYPES, XposedOrNot enters the default set only after personal_data_review {basis, reviewer, date} is recorded in the registry (A3 BR8, LGPD art. 33 transfer basis); until then it runs only when explicitly selected in a case with a recorded purpose (Status.SKIPPED reason_code 'privacy').
Breach names are merged with HIBP/LeakCheck per normalised name (P133/P146). Generic addresses (test@example.com returns 216 breaches) follow the A4 generic rule.

401 {'detail':'Invalid or missing API key'} gives NEEDS_KEY; a licence skip reads 'licence' in coverage, never empty. Tests with the recorded check-email, breach-analytics, catalogue and by-domain fixtures.
P137.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. legal_dpo's floor, shared by cti_lead and osint_investigator: commercial use needs xonAPI+ (A1 BR15 classes keyless use noncommercial), domain-breaches only for verified own domains, sensitive breaches masked. The architect's floor: hourly plus daily windows, the shared catalogue, logos ignored. analyst_ux: licence wording and cross-source merging. It stays a licence-gated default candidate (A3 BR4). XposedOrNot is a community project: tier community. Auditor: A3 BR8 personal_data_review gate added (XposedOrNot receives e-mail addresses).
P137.title: XposedOrNot (check-email, breach-analytics, catalogue, domain-breaches)

final_conditions: Requires key 'grayhat' in config.KNOWN_KEYS (V3LUM_GRAYHAT_KEY as alias), Bearer header; 401 without it gives NEEDS_KEY. Key-terms: a company/team account on a plan recorded by legal before it runs under corporate.

Queries only GrayhatWarfare's index for org_profile brands/domains and analyst-typed seeds. Bucket and file NAMES and URLs only: there is no code path that lists or downloads objects from any cloud provider (rule 3, LGPD).
File names can contain personal data: names with CPF patterns, e-mails or person names are masked before storage; reports show counts and extensions.

Brand-named buckets are candidates: LOW 'exists, ownership unverified' until linked to the organisation (org_profile, CNAME, website reference). Only confirmed own buckets may be handed to the ACTIVE bucket check within an authorized scope.
Result cap 100. Merge only with a trimmed real success fixture captured with the team key (none exists).
P138.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3 (redteam_lead voted P2). legal_dpo's floor: key-terms, names only, never downloads, masked file names. redteam_lead and cti_lead: brand-named buckets are unverified candidates and only confirmed own buckets reach ACTIVE checks. The architect's floor: header key, no download path, cap, real fixture. Opt-in as drafted. GrayhatWarfare is a small identifiable operator: tier community.
P138.title: GrayhatWarfare open buckets / shorteners search (names only)

final_conditions: Selector/phonebook metadata only. Endpoint allow-list: phonebook and intelligent search plus result polling; a test asserts that file/preview/view/read/download endpoints can never be built (leaked content is forbidden, rule 3).
x-key header (key 'intelx' registered). Key-terms: a company/team account; legal records the free-account plan and terms before it runs under corporate. Daily credits via the P334 block.
Async search with bounded polling (<= 5 polls, <= 30 s in total) and a terminate call.
Store only system id, bucket name, date and selector type. Sensitive bucket names are masked. IntelX is a sensitive provider (P145 schema before the HTTP cache).

Phonebook e-mail harvesting is own-asset-only (run_on='own_assets_only', A11 BR4: txt_verified or attested org_profile domains): harvesting third parties' e-mails from a leak index is people-search over leaks (rule 4). For non-own selectors only bucket names and dates are kept, and e-mail selectors follow the A4 scope (own assets; third parties only as seeds with --breach-scope all and --purpose).
The manual link https://intelx.io/?did={systemid} is offered for analysts (privacy rules of P311 apply). Merge only with a trimmed real success fixture. default_enabled=False.
P139.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. legal_dpo's floor: metadata only, never content, phonebook harvesting only for own domains (rule 4), masked bucket names, key-terms. A11 BR4 binds the own-asset verification. The architect's floor: endpoint allow-list with a test, bounded polling, real fixture. cti_lead and osint_investigator: third-party selectors keep bucket names and dates only. Intelligence X is an established company: tier trusted.
P139.title: Intelligence X selector metadata (phonebook/search metadata only)

final_conditions: PUBLIC key mode only (company-registered), under one canonical key 'leaklookup' in config.KNOWN_KEYS (V3LUM_LEAKLOOKUP_KEY/V3LUM_LEAKLOOKUP_PUBLIC_KEY as aliases), sent in the POST body. The private/records tier is never subscribed to or wired.
Type allow-list excludes 'password'; only breach names are kept, and sensitive-category names are masked. Leak-Lookup is a sensitive provider (P145 schema before the HTTP cache).
HTTP 200 {'error':'true','message':'MISSING API KEY'} and other error:true bodies map through a P321 marker to NEEDS_KEY or ERROR, never EMPTY. Limited daily public searches go into the P334 budget.
Breach names go through the P132 catalogue helper and are merged with the other breach sources per normalised name (P133).

Scope (A4): org-domain addresses (run_on='own_assets') or analyst-typed case seeds with --breach-scope all and --purpose; usernames only as such seeds. Key-terms: legal records the plan before it runs under corporate. Generic, role and test addresses follow the A4 generic rule (data/generic_addresses.json): flagged, capped at POSSIBLE, never scored.
Merge only with a trimmed real success fixture captured with the company public key. default_enabled=False.
P140.rationale: Approved 5-0 with one defer (cti_lead: a fourth breach-name source) at median P3. legal_dpo's floor: public key only, the records tier never bought, no type=password, sensitive names masked, org-domain or case seeds only. The architect's floor: one key name, type allow-list, error-in-200 mapping, the shared catalogue, a real fixture. Tier community; terms key-terms.
P140.title: Leak-Lookup public key (breach names only)

final_conditions: Not a registered module (architect floor): a core helper v3lum/core/pwned.py callable only by secret_scanner (P312) for credential-type findings, so no analyst input, CLI argument or text_blob path can reach it (unit test). It is off unless setting secret_scanner_pwned_check is true.
The SHA-1 is computed in memory (uppercase hex); only the 5-char prefix is sent to api.pwnedpasswords.com/range/{prefix} with the Add-Padding: true header; the 35-char suffix is compared in memory.

The plaintext and the full hash exist only in memory during the call and are never logged, cached, placed in res.raw or evidence, or shown (test asserts). Only the public range response may be cached.
The result is stored on the already-masked finding as 'appears N times in public breach corpora'. A k-anonymity range lookup never validates a credential against its service.
Attribution to HIBP (CC BY 4.0). Tests with the recorded range fixtures (5BAA6).
P141.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. The architect's floor makes it an internal helper so the rule-3 guarantees are testable and no password can be typed into it. legal_dpo's floor: in-memory only, prefix only, count only, no input path. cti_lead, osint_investigator and redteam_lead found the k-anonymity design safe and marginal. HIBP Pwned Passwords: tier trusted, terms open (CC BY 4.0).
P141.title: HIBP Pwned Passwords k-anonymity check (internal use by secret scanner)

P142.rationale: Rejected 0-6, as the synthesizer proposed. Library of Leaks (Aleph) and DiscordLeaks return leaked document contents with third parties' personal data (rule 3, LGPD) and no metadata-only mode is implementable (architect); there is no corporate legal basis (legal_dpo). Recorded in BACKLOG.md as a rejection.
P142.title: Library of Leaks (Aleph) / DiscordLeaks search

P143.rationale: Rejected 0-6, as the synthesizer proposed. ProxyNova COMB, BreachDirectory, DeHashed/Snusbase/Scylla/WeLeakInfo, probiv bots and psbdmp return plaintext or partial passwords, hashes or full records (rule 3), probiv-style people search (rule 4) and data of illicit origin (legal_dpo). The deny-list is kept at endpoint level, as cti_lead asked: the LeakCheck v2 lookup and the Leak-Lookup private tier are excluded while their metadata endpoints (P135, P140) stay. Recorded in BACKLOG.md and enforced by the P327 lint. The record's host list also names cavalier.hudsonrock.com and api.pwnedpasswords.com, but only as the acceptable metadata subset: they stay approved separately as P134 (scrubbed metadata only) and P141 (k-anonymity range helper) and are not part of this deny-list.
P143.title: Plaintext-credential leak services (ProxyNova COMB, BreachDirectory, DeHashed/Snusbase/Scylla/WeLeakInfo, probiv bots, psbdmp)

final_conditions: Not an entity template (architect): the link is emitted by the breach modules through ModuleResult.link() (or one report-renderer helper) next to each breach name, as https://haveibeenpwned.com/breach/{Name} with the name URL-encoded through the P311 encoder. No template is attached to keyword entities.

The link is emitted only for breach names taken from HIBP responses (their Name field) or matching an HIBP Name exactly (case-insensitive) in data already in the case; other providers' breach names get no HIBP link, so no dead links are generated.
Metadata only (rule 3): the link carries the breach name, never the investigated e-mail or any subject identifier, and V3LUM never fetches the page.

Rendering follows A2/P311 like every manual link: non-clickable text with the host warning at TLP:AMBER and above, hidden from reports at RED, never auto-opened. haveibeenpwned.com is a trusted-tier registry entry; breach pages are CC BY 4.0, attributed 'Have I Been Pwned'.
A unit test renders the link for a breach name with spaces and unicode and asserts a valid https URL on haveibeenpwned.com. Ships in phase 1 with the pivot packs (A16).
P144.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3 (osint_investigator, legal_dpo and analyst_ux voted P2). The architect's technical condition is adopted: breach names are attribute values, so the link comes from the breach module output rather than an entity template on keyword. Every member noted it is metadata only and consistent with rule 3; legal_dpo sees no personal data of the subject in the link.
P144.title: Pivot links: HIBP breach pages

final_conditions: core/sanitize.py runs as a mandatory engine stage in Engine.run_module right after Module.run returns. It covers res.raw, attributes, findings.data, pivot notes and links, before graph merge, evidence, case DB, events/live feed, reports, STIX/MISP exports and --debug output. Modules cannot opt out.
Fail closed: if sanitizing raises, the raw payload is dropped and the run ends Status.ERROR with reason_code 'sanitizer'.

Per-source ALLOW-list schemas for breach_leak, infostealer and people-data sources keep only declared metadata: breach name, breach date, data classes, counts, stealer family, log/compromise date, corporate/user service counts, and the password FORM (plaintext, or hashed: <algorithm>). A sensitive module without a schema cannot register.

Second net for those categories (case-insensitive, nested): drop password, passwd, pass, pwd, senha, hash, password_hash, salt, top_passwords, top_logins, masked/hint fields, cookies, session, token, autofill, computer_name, infected-host ip, malware_path and combo/line fields.

Value detectors drop (never mask) email:password and user:pass@host combos in every module result and in text/file inputs, before anything is stored, extracted or shown (a pasted combo keeps only the e-mail). Inside breach, infostealer and people-data payloads, bcrypt/argon/MD5/SHA hex values next to a credential are dropped too.
Category-scoped: the denylist does not apply to malware/hash modules, which keep their sha256/md5/'hash' fields (regression test with a MalwareBazaar fixture).

HTTP cache (P326 veto_lift): bodies from providers flagged sensitive in the registry are sanitized with the source schema before cache.put and before they reach the module, or fetched no-store when no schema exists. They are never stored raw in http_cache.db.
Secrets found by detectors or by LIGHT/ACTIVE modules (API keys, tokens, private keys, connection strings, .env values) are stored as type + first 4/last 4 + SHA-256 only.
Evidence records a redacted_fields list. Reports show data classes and the password form in plain words ('passwords: plaintext', 'hashed: bcrypt').

Golden tests with trimmed Hudson Rock, LeakCheck, XposedOrNot and HIBP fixtures and an exposed .env sample: a grep of http_cache.db, evidence, case DB, HTML/MD/JSON/STIX/MISP outputs, events and --debug output finds no masked password or login, computer name, victim IP or malware path.
P145.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1; it is a phase-0 and A4 item. All members found the same gap: the HTTP cache stores raw breach bodies for the TTL, so a module-level sanitizer cannot satisfy rule 3. legal_dpo's floor: one fail-closed choke point that also covers cache, exports and --debug. The architect's floor: an engine stage modules cannot opt out of, plus cache handling and golden tests. cti_lead set allow-list schemas first with the denylist as a second net. redteam_lead extended the rule to recon secrets. analyst_ux scoped the 'hash' rule so malware analysis keeps file hashes.
P145.title: Breach data-minimisation sanitizer (never store passwords or combo lines)

final_conditions: Rules CR09 corporate_credentials_in_infostealer, CR10 email_in_multiple_password_breaches, CR11 generic_or_shared_email_suppression and CR12 breach_predates_domain read only P145-sanitized metadata (breach names, dates, data classes, counts, stealer family). They replace the existing breach_and_infostealer rule, and their output passes the P145 sanitizer.

Suppression runs first and only downgrades, with a visible label; it never deletes. CR11 caps at POSSIBLE, and never scores as exposure, any address in data/generic_addresses.json and any hit with LeakCheck found >= 100 or Hudson Rock >= 5 computers.

data/generic_addresses.json holds role/test local parts (test, info, contato, contact, sac, admin, noreply, no-reply, suporte, support, vendas, financeiro, rh, webmaster, postmaster, abuse) and example.* / IANA test domains.
CR12 needs the domain creation date (RDAP) and stays silent when it is unavailable. A breach that predates the domain downgrades confidence, with that criterion.

CR09 is CRITICAL only when the address is on a verified org_profile domain AND the stealer log is <= 12 months old. Older own-domain logs with corporate services > 0 are HIGH, other older ones MEDIUM (decay tau 1 year). Third-party addresses are context only, at most MEDIUM, never CRITICAL.
CR10 (>= 3 verified breaches, or confirmed by 2 sources, at least one within the last 3 years) is HIGH for own-domain addresses. For third-party addresses it is context only, at most MEDIUM.
Third-party addresses are evaluated only when the A4 breach scope allows it (--breach-scope all + purpose, analyst-typed seeds only), and their findings carry no exposure score.
Breach counts from the same upstream (aggregators re-serving HIBP-type data) count once.

Ceos verdict heuristics (IsFabricated against, spam-list alert, compilation doubt, >= 2 sources agree, profile on the breached service plausible) are named, individually tested functions, each emitting a P322 criterion. The suggested verdict (positive / false positive / inconclusive) is shown with the 2-3 criteria that drove it.
Emit attribute first_seen_breach (earliest breach date) to the timeline as account-age evidence, with no score.

Wording is a suggestion. Reports state that infostealer findings about employees go to incident response and are not a basis for disciplinary decisions without human review (LGPD art. 20). Leaked credentials are never tested in any mode.

Tests: positive and negative graph fixtures per rule. test@example.com with 5 generic stealers is capped at POSSIBLE with no CRITICAL; a recent own-domain log is CRITICAL; a 2-year-old log is HIGH or MEDIUM.
P146.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. cti_lead pointed out that 'or corporate services > 0' would turn 4-year-old logs into CRITICALs, so CRITICAL now requires an own-domain address and a recent log. This matches osint_investigator, analyst_ux and legal_dpo's floor (third parties at most MEDIUM, and only under the A4 breach scope). Suppression only downgrades (all members). osint_investigator added first_seen_breach as an account-age pivot. legal_dpo required the LGPD art. 20 notice. The architect's floor: sanitized inputs only, named tested heuristics. redteam_lead: credentials are never tested.
P146.title: Correlation pack: breach & infostealer validation (CR09-CR12 + Céos breach heuristics)

final_conditions: Module honeypot_intel: OffSeq Mirage daily CSVs (CC BY 4.0, TLP:CLEAR: open) as a registered dataset (If-Modified-Since, every 6-24 h) parsed with the csv module (field-size limit) into a compact local index: tags, services, CVEs, KEV, ATT&CK, confidence, first/last seen. HoneyDB (free for research/defensive use: key-terms, company key) as a separate adapter with its own status.
OffSeq's known-scanners list feeds the core noise-provider hook: those IPs are tagged benign_scanner, never malicious (P171 suppression).

HoneyLabs and James Brine feeds publish no licence: they ship as a separate module honeypot_intel_extra (default_enabled=False, terms 'unknown', tier unknown), disabled in every profile until legal records their terms.

If cleared: HoneyLabs keyless /api/cves/{cve} (actively_exploited, 'actors' capped at the top 20 IPs; IP lookups need a free key); James Brine iplist.txt/csv through the shared IP index (not the 14 MB JSON).

HoneyDB: two registered keys (honeydb_api_id, honeydb_api_key) sent in headers; the old /api/netinfo/lookup returns 410, so the client is built from the current docs and merges only with a fixture from the current API. 401 'Invalid API Credentials' gives NEEDS_KEY.

Semantics: honeypot sightings mean opportunistic scanning/exploitation: tag scanner, at most MEDIUM alone, with observed first/last seen and a 30-day decay. IP -> CVE uses a new relation attempted_exploit (added to core/vocab.py), never has_vuln, so attack-surface rules never mark the attacker as vulnerable.
UDP-derived source IPs are excluded from verdicts (spoofable), as HoneyLabs itself does.
Pivots: asn, each CVE (joined with KEV/EPSS) and each ATT&CK technique. CC BY 4.0 attribution to OffSeq in the report footer and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
Tests with the recorded OffSeq attackers/anonymizers/known-scanners slices, the HoneyLabs CVE fixtures (for the extra module) and a UDP-only observation case.
P147.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (cti_lead voted P1). legal_dpo's floor: OffSeq is CC BY 4.0, HoneyDB fine with a company key, HoneyLabs and James Brine have no licence, so the chair splits those into an opt-in module that stays disabled until reviewed and keeps the default module's terms reviewable (A3 BR2). cti_lead: benign scanners, the attempted_exploit relation, MEDIUM cap with decay, UDP exclusion (also osint_investigator and the architect). The architect's floor: datasets, the noise hook, per-source status, a current-API HoneyDB fixture. Tier community (OffSeq, HoneyDB operators).
P147.title: Honeypot intelligence (OffSeq Mirage, HoneyLabs, HoneyDB, James Brine)

final_conditions: Terms: the GreyNoise EULA (last modified 2025-05-07, verified 2026-11-26) offers free subscriptions 'for non-commercial purposes' (s.2.3) while s.3.1 allows 'internal business purposes or noncommercial purposes': the community tier is classed noncommercial.

Off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared: a company key plus a licence_allow entry (scope: internal defence, no resale or redistribution; written confirmation requested from GreyNoise) or a paid plan.

Key-first: key 'greynoise' (already registered) in the header. The keyless plan reports rate_limit '25-W' (25 lookups per week per egress IP) and a free key ~50/week: a weekly window in the P334 block (until it exists daily_quota=3), seeds (depth 0) only, never bulk pastes or pivots.

HTTP 404 'IP not observed scanning the internet' is a declared meaningful absence, worded 'not observed scanning by GreyNoise' (info), never 'benign'. 429 gives RATE_LIMITED ('could not verify'), shown once per scan with the free-key hint, never 'benign'.
riot=true: known_good tag with the service name ('Google Public DNS'); it dampens only that IP's reputation, never URLs or domains hosted on it, and caps blocklist-derived findings on that IP at LOW.

noise=true with benign classification: 'known benign scanner (<name>)', blocklist-derived score capped at LOW. noise=true with malicious classification: 'opportunistic mass scanner' at MEDIUM, explained as 'scans the whole internet, not targeting you specifically'.
riot/benign flags lower scores through named suppression rules (P322) but never delete other sources' findings. The viz.greynoise.io/ips/{ip} page is the manual link.
Tests with the recorded community fixture and the two 429 fixtures.
P148.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (cti_lead and analyst_ux voted P1). legal_dpo's floor classes the ambiguous free tier noncommercial (cti_lead and osint_investigator read the EULA the same way), so it is a licence-gated default candidate (A3 BR4) that shows up as coverage lost until legal records a decision. The architect's floor: key-first with a weekly window, 404/429 semantics. analyst_ux and cti_lead: riot/noise dampening limited to the IP and never deleting findings (osint_investigator). GreyNoise is an established company: tier trusted.
P148.title: GreyNoise Community API

final_conditions: Per-feed terms registry with an enable flag per feed. Open (run under corporate): Spamhaus DROP/EDROP/ASN-DROP (free for protection, no resale), Feodo Tracker and SSLBL (abuse.ch CC0, A1 BR14), IPsum (Unlicense), Binary Defense Artillery (internal use, no resale).

Noncommercial, off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared: blocklist.de, CINS, ET compromised IPs, GreenSnow and DataPlane (A1 BR16), VoIPBL, and the FireHOL level1 aggregate (it embeds noncommercial upstreams such as DShield). Restricted feeds are never redistributed outside the team: STIX/MISP exports drop their provenance.

Core dataset manager: conditional GET (ETag/If-Modified-Since), per-feed TTL (Feodo 15 min, Spamhaus DROP >= 1 h as Spamhaus asks, others 6-24 h), validation so a challenge page or empty file never replaces a good copy, and provenance (feed, fetched_at, dataset SHA-256) on every hit. A feed older than 3x its TTL is reported 'stale'.

All IP/CIDR feeds load into the shared core IP-range index (P034); bogon/RFC 1918 entries are dropped at load (FireHOL level1 includes them) and never reported. Parsers are tested on trimmed fixtures, including Spamhaus NDJSON (last line = metadata) and the SSLBL CSV (cert SHA1; the JA3 list is retired).
Each feed declares its upstreams: FireHOL level1 and IPsum count as the families they embed (P171), so a hit in an aggregate and in one of its constituents is one vote.

Per-feed fidelity: C2/criminal lists (Feodo, SSLBL, Spamhaus DROP/EDROP) single hit = HIGH; curated attack lists (ET compromised, CINS) = MEDIUM; noisy scanner/fail2ban lists (blocklist.de, GreenSnow, IPsum count < 3, FireHOL L1) = LOW; >= 2 independent families raise one level (CR27). Warninglists (P169) apply before scoring.
Hits on CDN/shared-edge IPs (P034) are capped at LOW with 'shared/reassignable IP'; hits on IaaS compute keep their severity with a verdict lifetime <= 14 days (P034).

Every hit shows the feed name and listing date/feed age; an IP seen earlier but absent from the current feed is historical. Matching is local (disclosure 'none', allowed at TLP:RED). Attribution where a feed requires it.
P149.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. legal_dpo's floor sets per-feed gating; A1 BR16 (binding, a chair may only be stricter) classes ET, blocklist.de, CINS, GreenSnow and DataPlane noncommercial, and the chair also classes the FireHOL level1 aggregate noncommercial because it embeds such lists (stricter than legal_dpo's vote). The architect's floor: conditional downloads, provenance, the shared index, one registry entry per feed. cti_lead: upstream dedupe and history. analyst_ux: per-feed fidelity, reconciled with cti_lead's P034 edge/IaaS split. osint_investigator: dataset validation. Terms noncommercial for those feeds only; tier community is the lowest maintainer (Spamhaus and abuse.ch are trusted).
P149.title: Downloadable IP blocklists matched locally (Spamhaus DROP, FireHOL L1, IPsum, blocklist.de, CINS, ET, GreenSnow, Feodo, SSLBL, Binary Defense, DataPlane, VoIPBL)

final_conditions: IPGuardian and NetAPI are terms 'unknown' and tier unknown: disabled in every profile until legal records their terms (A1); then default_enabled=False, excluded at AMBER and above, --allow-unknown at CLEAR/GREEN, IOC_TYPES only.

Local first: NetAPI's downloadable compromised IP/URL feeds (daily) are matched locally through the shared index (disclosure 'none') and, once their terms are recorded, are added as a feed of P149 instead of per-IP calls.

The IPGuardian /api/check adapter has its own status, terms label and fixture. The blocklist names it returns are deduplicated against the P149 feeds; the module counts as ONE vote and never raises severity above LOW on its own.
One-source hits are 'suspicious', never 'malicious'. Use the P331 declarative collector where it fits.
Tests with the recorded IPGuardian check, NetAPI check and NetAPI feed fixtures.
P150.rationale: Approved 5-1 at median P3 (cti_lead rejected it: IPGuardian re-aggregates the lists P149 already matches while disclosing IPs to an operator with unknown terms). legal_dpo's floor: unknown terms and tier, never default, excluded at AMBER and above, local feeds preferred. cti_lead's objection is answered by folding NetAPI's feed into P149 and by analyst_ux's dedupe and one-vote cap. The architect, osint_investigator and redteam_lead: local matching first.
P150.title: Keyless IP/URL compromise checks (IPGuardian, NetAPI)

final_conditions: Terms: SANS ISC data is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (noncommercial, A1 BR15), but the ISC API page allows commercial use 'to protect your own company's network ... do not resell'. Off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared: legal records a licence_allow entry citing that clause (day-1 queue).
Allow-list scope: defence of the company's own networks only, no resale, no inclusion in paid deliverables to third parties.

Send Accept: application/json and ?json on /api/ip/{ip}, /api/asnum/{asn} and /api/threatcategory. A redirect to /blockme.html (detected from Response.url/history, not only body markers, P321) gives BLOCKED ('could not verify') with backoff.

ISC asks API users to identify themselves: the profile uses the identifying UA with the team role contact (setting contact_email, P326); without it the source is SKIPPED reason_code 'config'. No personal data is hard-coded.
min_interval >= 1 s, cache 24 h. Attack counts carry first/last seen; DShield sightings are opportunistic scanning: tag scanner, at most MEDIUM alone.
Attribution 'SANS ISC / DShield' in reports. Tests with the recorded IP, ASN and threat-feed fixtures plus a blockme redirect.
P151.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (cti_lead voted P1). legal_dpo, cti_lead and osint_investigator call it the model case for the licence allow-list: noncommercial by default, enabled under corporate only through a recorded own-network-defence entry. The architect's floor: Accept header, blockme detection from the final URL, a configured contact UA. cti_lead: opportunistic-scanning semantics. It remains a licence-gated default candidate (A3 BR4). SANS: tier trusted.
P151.title: SANS ISC / DShield IP API

final_conditions: Module threat_intel_ioc/crowdsec_cti: GET https://cti.api.crowdsec.net/v2/smoke/{ip} with header x-api-key; key 'crowdsec' registered in config.KNOWN_KEYS (env V3LUM_KEY_CROWDSEC; V3LUM_CROWDSEC_KEY alias). Registry provider crowdsec: tier trusted, terms key-terms.

Licence (legal floor): the Community key is described for testing and personal servers; under the corporate profile it runs only with a company-account Premium or paid key whose plan legal records (key_plans.crowdsec='business'); otherwise SKIPPED reason_code 'licence' with the manual CrowdSec CTI link.

Quota: the free Community plan is 120 lookups per month (docs, 2026-11-26): a P334 monthly quota block (setting crowdsec_monthly_quota, default 120 or the recorded plan's limit). run_on='seeds' (analyst-typed IPs only, never pivots or bulk pastes); private/reserved and CDN/cloud noise IPs and IPs answered in the last 72 h are skipped (cache 72 h).
Statuses: 404 = EMPTY 'not in CrowdSec data' (never benign); 403 {'message':'Forbidden'} = NEEDS_KEY; 429 = RATE_LIMITED; monthly budget exhausted = QUOTA.

Mapping: classifications.false_positives and benign/known-crawler reputation (CDN, search-engine bot) are info context that dampens other malicious votes (P171), never known_good suppression; behaviors -> tags (scanner, botnet...), background-noise scanners low; attack_details -> uses_technique ATT&CK pivots with expand=False; cves -> has_vuln.
CVEs from attack_details read 'attempted exploitation of CVE-X seen by CrowdSec', expand=False, and never trigger own-asset vulnerability rules (CR15).

Provider data is not redistributed: excluded from STIX/MISP/JSON exports shared outside the company (verdict, link and source name only; EULA internal use). Success, 404 and 429 fixtures are captured with the team key (only 403 bodies exist).
P152.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (cti_lead and the architect voted P1). legal_dpo's floor requires a SOC-compatible plan from a company account and no redistribution; cti_lead found the 120-lookups-per-month limit, which makes the seeds-only rule and 72 h cache necessary. The architect's 404 = 'not in data' (never benign) and analyst_ux's CVE wording that avoids 'we are vulnerable' complete the spec.
P152.title: CrowdSec CTI smoke API (keyed)

final_conditions: Two module classes sharing one parser: otx (requires key 'otx', header X-OTX-API-KEY, default_enabled True, NEEDS_KEY without a key) and otx_keyless (no key, 'general' section only, default_enabled False, because keyless calls take ~25 s and hit 429 on shared egress: A3 latency rule).

Endpoints: otx.alienvault.com/api/v1/indicators/{IPv4|IPv6|domain|hostname|url|file|cve}/{value}/{section}: 'general' for all types; passive_dns only for seeds; url_list and malware only when pulse_count > 0 or in --preset deep. Read-only: never create pulses or submit indicators.

Terms: the OTX terms page is JS-only and was not verified (2026-11-26): legal records the OTX terms for a company account; source class 'key-terms', so under corporate it runs only with free_plan_business_use=true or key_plans.otx='business'. Registry provider otx (LevelBlue): tier trusted.

Bounds: per-call timeout 20 s in the default preset and 60 s in --preset deep, always within the scan deadline (timeout = could not verify); max_bytes 5 MB (truncated = partial, never parsed as complete); pulses capped at 50 by recency; cache 24 h. 403 with a key = NEEDS_KEY (bad key); 429 = RATE_LIMITED, never 'not listed'.

Pulse membership is not a verdict: validation[]/whitelist entries and warninglist hits give info/noise and no malicious finding. Tag malicious only with >= 2 pulses from distinct authors modified in the last 365 days or 1 pulse by the AlienVault/LevelBlue labs account; otherwise 'mentioned in N community pulses' (low).

Findings show the pulse count and the top 3 pulse names/authors/dates at low-medium confidence; pulse dates feed observed_first/observed_last (STIX valid_from). Pulses relaying abuse.ch count as the abuse.ch upstream family (P171).

adversary, malware_families and attack_ids -> attributed_to/family/uses_technique pivots with expand=False, normalised through the actor alias index (P295). E-mail and username indicators taken from community pulses are pivots with expand=False.
Fixtures: general for 8.8.8.8 (whitelisted), a domain with pulses, keyless passive_dns 429 and a bad-key 403.
P153.rationale: Approved 6-0. The tally median is P2 on a 3-3 tie (cti_lead, the architect and analyst_ux P1; the others P2); the chair raises it to P1 because, with abuse.ch MalwareBazaar/URLhaus/ThreatFox licence-gated and VirusTotal public non-commercial, OTX with the recommended free key (A15) is one of the few sources that can meet the A3 minimum answer set (2 default-ready reputation sources per type under corporate). legal_dpo's floor makes the terms 'key-terms' with a company account (stricter than the draft's 'open'). The architect's key-only default (keyless is opt-in for latency), cti_lead's pulse thresholds and analyst_ux's bounded sections are consolidated.
P153.title: AlienVault/LevelBlue OTX indicators (general, reputation, passive DNS, URL list, malware)

final_conditions: Module threat_intel_ioc/maltiverse is keyed only in this build (requires key 'maltiverse'; NEEDS_KEY without it). Keyless community use stays unbuilt until legal records its terms: it counts as 'unknown' (the terms page is JS-only, unverified 2026-11-26).

The key comes from a company/team account on a plan whose terms permit internal business use, recorded by legal (key_plans.maltiverse='business'), never an analyst's personal free account (rule 1). Registry provider maltiverse: tier trusted, terms key-terms.

Endpoints: api.maltiverse.com/ip/{ip}, /hostname/{host}, /url/{sha256 of the URL normalised exactly as Maltiverse expects, unit-tested} and /sample/{sha256}. Error bodies inside 200 and quota messages -> RATE_LIMITED/QUOTA via P321; quota per the recorded plan via P334; cache 24 h.

Aggregator semantics: blacklist[].source and dates are kept per hit as upstream provenance; Maltiverse is not counted as an independent vote in CR27 (P171) when all its listing sources are queried directly (URLhaus, ThreatFox, Feodo, Spamhaus, P159 feeds). Findings list the blacklist sources and dates.

classification whitelist/neutral dampens other votes; sinkhole/tor/vpn/proxy/scanner booleans become context tags, never malicious. Family names in blacklist[].description become malware_family pivots with expand=False.
P154.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. legal_dpo's floor (company key on a recorded plan; keyless community use 'unknown' until recorded) means a keyless path could not run in any profile, so this build is keyed only and stays a default candidate; the keyless path is added when legal records its terms. cti_lead's and analyst_ux's provenance dedupe (no circular reporting) and the architect's URL normalisation and P321 handling are kept.
P154.title: Maltiverse IoC lookup

final_conditions: Module threat_intel_ioc/ibm_xforce: api.xforce.ibmcloud.com ipr/{ip}, url/{url} and malware/{hash} lookups only; never submit files or collections. default_enabled False (opt-in).

Credentials as one key 'xforce' holding 'key:password' in config.KNOWN_KEYS (V3LUM_XFORCE_KEY/V3LUM_XFORCE_PASSWORD as aliases); the module builds the Basic header; AR01 redaction covers it and the cache key includes a hash of credential-bearing headers (P326).

The key comes from a company account on a plan legal records as business-compatible (IBM sells a separate X-Force Exchange Commercial API; the free-tier terms page is JS-only, unverified): under corporate it runs only with key_plans.xforce='business'. Registry provider ibm_xforce: tier trusted, terms key-terms.

Monthly free quota through a P334 monthly quota block; 401 = NEEDS_KEY, quota exceeded = QUOTA, never clean. Mapping: risk score >= 7 -> malicious, 4-6 -> suspicious; categories -> tags; one vendor vote in consensus. A success fixture is captured with the team key (only 401 exists).
P155.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. legal_dpo's key-terms floor (a free key is not automatically business-compatible), the architect's credential and cache-key handling and cti_lead's score mapping and opt-in default are consolidated.
P155.title: IBM X-Force Exchange (keyed)

final_conditions: Module threat_intel_ioc/abusech covers the URLhaus, ThreatFox and MalwareBazaar query APIs and their v2 exports, plus Feodo Tracker and SSLBL. One key 'abusech' (exists; V3LUM_ABUSECH_KEY and V3LUM_ABUSECH_AUTH_KEY only as aliases) comes from a company account, is sent as header Auth-Key on every call (terms s.2.1) and is shared with yaraify, offline_hash_sets and structural_hash_pivots.

Licence per source (A1 BR14): MalwareBazaar, URLhaus and ThreatFox are 'license' (terms 2026-10-21 s.4.1): off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared (a Spamhaus subscription or a written abuse.ch/Spamhaus decision in licence_allow). Feodo Tracker and SSLBL are 'open' (CC0 incl. commercial use, s.3.4) and run through ctx.allowed_sources.

Lands only after AR01 redaction: v2 export URLs embed the key in the path (https://{urlhaus|threatfox|mb}-api.abuse.ch/v2/files/exports/{AUTH_KEY}/...) and must never reach the cache url column, events, errors, evidence or reports; the dataset registry stores an {AUTH_KEY} template.
Read-only by construction: a per-API query allow-list with a test proves that get_file, sample downloads, uploads, ThreatFox submit_ioc and URLhaus submissions are never built (rule 7).

query_status is mapped centrally: ok; no_result(s) -> EMPTY; illegal_* -> SKIPPED reason_code 'not_applicable' (input error shown once); anything else -> ERROR. 401 -> NEEDS_KEY. The legacy keyless exports (410 Gone) are never used.

Bulk: pasted lists of > 20 IOCs are matched against local exports, not per-IOC API calls (s.7.3 forbids high-volume scripted harvesting). Exports go through the dataset manager: recent.csv by default, refreshed at most hourly; full.csv.zip only via `v3lum data update --full` with safe_extract caps; one local SQLite index.

Severity: URLhaus online or last_online <= 30 days -> high; offline > 90 days -> low 'historical'; ThreatFox confidence_level < 50 -> suspicious and feeds the P322 label. A URLhaus host that is a popular file-hosting/CDN domain (P169 warninglists) -> info 'abused legitimate service', never malicious.

All abuse.ch feeds are one upstream family for consensus (P171). Malpedia-style family ids are normalised through the alias index (P295). Returned URLs, domains and IPs are hostile-tagged for the P376 guard. Feodo Tracker and SSLBL are registered once in the dataset manager and shared with ip_blocklists (P149) and ioc_feeds_offline (P159), never downloaded twice.

Without the key: one coverage line per scan ('needs abuse.ch Auth-Key, free: v3lum keys setup') plus manual URLhaus/ThreatFox/MalwareBazaar links, not per-entity errors. Findings name platform, status (online/offline), family and first/last seen; abuse.ch attribution is kept in exports.
Success fixtures are captured with the team key before merge (only 401/410 bodies exist).
P156.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. Every member confirms the 2026-10-21 terms: corporate use of MalwareBazaar, URLhaus and ThreatFox needs a Spamhaus subscription or a written decision, while Feodo Tracker and SSLBL are CC0 (A1 BR14); A3 BR4 keeps the module a default candidate that is off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared, with the open feeds running meanwhile. The architect's redaction-first sequencing, redteam_lead's query allow-list, cti_lead's freshness rules and bulk-export path, and analyst_ux's single coverage line are consolidated.
P156.title: abuse.ch platforms with one Auth-Key (URLhaus, ThreatFox, MalwareBazaar APIs + bulk exports)

final_conditions: Module threat_intel_ioc/abuseipdb: GET https://api.abuseipdb.com/api/v2/check?ipAddress={ip}&maxAgeInDays=90 without 'verbose', so report comments are never fetched, cached or stored; check-block only for ranges <= /24. Header Key with key 'abuseipdb' (exists). report, bulk-report and clear-address are never called (unit test).

Licence (legal floor): AbuseIPDB's terms (verified 2026-11-26) forbid commercial use of Free plans and several free accounts per organisation. Under corporate it runs only with a Basic or higher paid plan recorded by legal (key_plans.abuseipdb='business'); otherwise SKIPPED reason_code 'licence' with the manual AbuseIPDB link. Registry: tier trusted, terms key-terms.
Quota: 1,000 checks and 100 block checks per day via P334 (or the recorded plan's limits); 429 and quota bodies -> RATE_LIMITED/QUOTA.

Mapping: abuseConfidenceScore >= 75 with numDistinctUsers >= 3 -> malicious medium (high only when corroborated by an independent family, P171, and lastReportedAt <= 30 days); 25-74 -> low suspicious; < 25 -> info attribute. isWhitelisted, usageType CDN or Search Engine Spider dampen; usageType 'Mobile ISP' (CGNAT is common in Brazil) caps at low.

Findings show distinct reporters, last report date, usageType, ISP and categories (tags scanner, spam, botnet, phishing). Provider data is not redistributed: excluded from STIX/MISP/JSON exports shared outside the company (verdict, link and source name only). A success fixture is captured with the team key.
P157.rationale: Approved 6-0. The median is P2 on a 3-3 tie and stays P2 because under the corporate profile it can run only after a paid plan is bought. legal_dpo's and cti_lead's floor: the free key is expressly non-commercial (Basic plan from US$25/month). The architect's no-'verbose' call removes reporter comments at the source; analyst_ux's CGNAT cap and corroboration rule and redteam_lead's read-only test are kept. Note for the human team: A15 lists AbuseIPDB among recommended free keys, but its free plan cannot be used under the corporate profile.
P157.title: AbuseIPDB check (keyed)

final_conditions: Module threat_intel_ioc/virustotal (key 'virustotal', header x-apikey). The public API may not be used in business workflows: under corporate it runs only when legal records a VirusTotal premium/enterprise licence in licence_allow (basis licence); a public key runs only in the research profile. Off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared.

Read-only by construction: GET lookups only; a method/path allow-list with a test asserts that no POST /files or /urls, /analyses rescan, comment or vote is ever built (a URL submission makes VirusTotal fetch and publish it: rule 7).

Budget: public keys get 4 req/min and 500/day as a P334 token bucket that defers instead of sleeping in an engine worker, plus a per-scan budget (setting virustotal_case_budget, default 20 lookups, seeds first; a Module.case_budget contract field only through an architect-approved migration, A16). Pending entities are listed once as 'VT: not run (quota)'; the scan never waits on VT.

Relationship endpoints (subdomains, resolutions, contacted_*, communicating_files) are read one page each with caps and cursors not followed by default, cached, filtered through warninglists and emitted with expand=False unless the sample itself is malicious.

Verdict wording 'N/M engines flagged (last analysis <date>)' with the top 3 labels: >= 5 engines (or a configured trusted-vendor set) -> malicious; 3-4 -> suspicious; 1-2 -> low 'few engines'. URL ids are base64url without padding; 404 = EMPTY (unknown to VT).

The VT GUI link is always emitted, key or not. Provider data is not redistributed: excluded from STIX/MISP/JSON exports shared outside the company (verdict, link and source name only). The keys wizard does not offer the public key under corporate (A15). Registry: tier trusted; terms noncommercial (public API) and license (premium). Success fixtures are captured with a key.
P158.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. All members agree the public API is non-commercial (A1 BR14) and build for a licensed key, so the module is a default candidate that is off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared (A3 BR4). redteam_lead's GET-only allow-list (no submissions or rescans that tip off actors), the architect's non-blocking budget and analyst_ux's 'never wait on VT' are consolidated; cti_lead's >= 5-engine threshold is combined with analyst_ux's lower bands.
P158.title: VirusTotal API v3 (keyed)

final_conditions: Offline module threat_intel_ioc/ioc_feeds_offline (disclosure none, TLP:RED-safe) on the core dataset manager: per-feed ETag/TTL, provenance, reliability grade, expected update interval and last successful update; one local SQLite IOC index (value -> feed, family, first/last seen) shared with P071/P149, so pasted lists cost zero API calls.

Feeds in this module, terms recorded in the registry, all 'open': TweetFeed (CC0, LICENSE verified 2026-11-26; today/week lists), CIRCL MISP OSINT feed (TLP:CLEAR, attribute CIRCL), Meta threat-research (MIT), Neo23x0 signature-base hash and C2 lists (DRL 1.1, attribution) and SSLBL (CC0), matched from the one SSLBL dataset registered for abusech (P156) or P149, never downloaded twice.

Feeds without recorded terms form a separate module ioc_feeds_unreviewed (terms 'unknown', default_enabled False): C2IntelFeeds (no licence), the ViriBack C2 Tracker dump (no terms, A1 BR16) and ThreatView (until its site terms are recorded). They stay disabled in every profile until legal records a class and, where needed, a licence_allow entry.

Load pipeline: refang (ThreatView headers are defanged) -> validate (drop bogon/non-routable entries such as 0.0.0.2) -> MISP warninglists (P169) and CDN/cloud ranges (P034) -> index. A feed parsing to 0 rows marks the dataset unhealthy (doctor) instead of 'no hits'; a feed whose newest entry is older than 3x its interval is marked stale and skipped.

The CIRCL MISP OSINT feed is synced incrementally from manifest.json (If-Modified-Since): last 365 days by default, per-event size cap, same host only. signature-base: hash and C2 lists only; filename-iocs (untrusted regexes, ReDoS risk) excluded. The Bert-JanP catalog is used only as a directory to evaluate new feeds.

Findings: one grouped finding per indicator naming every feed that lists it ('seen in 3 feeds: ...') with per-feed confidence (TweetFeed and C2IntelFeeds 'Possible' labels = low; CIRCL, Meta, signature-base = medium) and listing age; a single-feed hit is medium at most unless corroborated; IP/URL hits older than 90 days are low.

Feeds reposting URLhaus/ThreatFox are not independent votes (P171 upstream families). Every IP, URL or domain matched from a C2/phishing feed is hostile-tagged for P376; panel and C2 URLs in feed data are never visited; downloads are untrusted and never executed.

Refresh runs out of band (`v3lum data update`); the stale copy is served during scans and dataset age is shown in coverage. Tests: a trimmed fixture per feed, a defanged ThreatView header and a 0-row feed marked unhealthy.
P159.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. legal_dpo's per-feed floor runs only feeds with recorded open terms under the corporate profile and skips C2IntelFeeds and ViriBack until legal decides (cti_lead and osint_investigator also hold ThreatView back until its terms are recorded). Because A3 forbids default-enabling a module with 'unknown' terms, the unreviewed feeds are a separate disabled module and the default module is 'open' (chair-file terms and default refer to it). The architect's index, validation and unhealthy-feed rules, redteam_lead's hostile tagging and analyst_ux's grouped, family-deduplicated findings complete the spec.
P159.title: Offline IOC feeds matched locally (TweetFeed, C2IntelFeeds, ThreatView, CIRCL MISP OSINT feed, Meta threat-research, signature-base IOCs)

final_conditions: Module threat_intel_ioc/pulsedive is keyed only in this build (key 'pulsedive', exists); keyless community use stays unbuilt until legal records its terms (it counts as 'unknown'; the terms pages are JS-only, unverified 2026-11-26). The key comes from a company account on a plan recorded as business-compatible (key_plans.pulsedive='business').

Path allow-list enforced by a unit test: only https://pulsedive.com/api/info.php?indicator= and explore.php; analyze.php and any probe, scan or submit endpoint are never built, because they make Pulsedive actively scan the indicator (target contact and rule 7).
Statuses: risk none/unknown = no finding (not clean); 'retired' indicators info only; {'error': ...} inside 200 -> P321 error_markers; invalid key (401) = NEEDS_KEY; daily quota via P334; cache 24 h.

Findings only for risk >= medium. feeds[] is kept as upstream provenance and deduplicated against the local feeds (P171/P159): memberships already counted locally are not counted again. Registry provider pulsedive: tier community, terms key-terms.
P160.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. Every member requires that analyze.php be structurally impossible (it makes Pulsedive probe the target). legal_dpo's floor treats keyless community use as 'unknown' until its terms are recorded, so this build is keyed only and stays a default candidate; osint_investigator's and redteam_lead's concern about keyless use at AMBER+ is thereby moot. cti_lead's and analyst_ux's provenance dedupe and thresholds are kept.
P160.title: Pulsedive indicator info

P161.rationale: Chair decision on a contested item (yes 3 / defer 3): deferred. Only a guessed-endpoint 401 fixture exists, the free tier is 250 calls/month, and its aggregated '500+ feeds' verdict has no demonstrated per-feed provenance, so it cannot be deduplicated against V3LUM's own feeds (P171) and would inflate consensus. osint_investigator, legal_dpo and analyst_ux approved it as a last-resort gap filler; cti_lead (provenance), redteam_lead (duplicated coverage, e-mails to a small operator) and the architect (no fixture; 'only when free sources found nothing' needs engine ordering) deferred. legal_dpo found the terms compatible with internal business use but removed e-mail inputs under A8. Backlog unblock: a success fixture from a company key showing per-feed provenance, P339 lanes with skip_keyed_when_answered, and the provider tier recorded. Conditions then: keyed, ipv4/domain/url/wallet inputs only (no e-mail until legal records tier and transfer basis), only for indicators still unknown, within the monthly quota, one vote in consensus.
P161.title: isMalicious API (keyed)

final_conditions: Module threat_intel_ioc/kaspersky_opentip: default_enabled False and disabled until compliance records that the company's vendor/sanctions policy permits sending IOCs to Kaspersky (provider-registry flag vendor_policy_ok, set centrally by legal/compliance and shown in doctor) and legal records the OpenTIP API terms for corporate use (page JS-only, unverified).

401 returns an EMPTY body and is handled by status code (empty fixture files kept) as NEEDS_KEY. Zones: Red -> malicious (high); Orange -> suspicious (low); Grey -> no finding; Green -> known_good only for file hashes. One vendor vote in consensus. A success fixture is captured with the team key. Registry: tier trusted, terms key-terms.
P162.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. All members make enabling a company vendor-policy decision (legal_dpo cites the US measures against Kaspersky since 2024); the architect's central registry flag lets legal exclude it in one place. cti_lead's zone mapping and the empty-body 401 handling are kept.
P162.title: Kaspersky OpenTIP (keyed)

P163.rationale: Deferred (yes 2 / defer 4). ScamSearch sends e-mails, phones and usernames to a small operator whose terms say nothing about query data and returns unverified, user-submitted accusations about people (a people-search/LGPD flag); legal_dpo wants its tier, transfer basis and data quality reviewed (A8), the architect has no fixture, and Chainabuse (P204) covers crypto scams. P163.title: ScamSearch.io scam reports (keyed)

final_conditions: Module threat_intel_ioc/stopforumspam (StopForumSpam only): GET https://api.stopforumspam.org/api?json with ip, emailhash (MD5 of the normalised lower-cased address; the plaintext address is never sent) and username (only in registration-abuse cases). Licence: StopForumSpam's terms are non-commercial but let 'any commercial system' use the data for internal use only, with no resale (verified 2026-11-26): terms 'noncommercial'; off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared (legal records a licence_allow entry with scope 'internal use only, no resale'). Registry provider stopforumspam: tier community.

'success':0 bodies -> ERROR via P321. Findings only when lastseen <= 90 days and confidence >= 25: severity low, wording 'reported as forum spammer N times, last <date>', tag spam; frequency < 3 -> info. IP hits in mobile/CGNAT or cloud ranges (P034/P035 tags) are info only.
