P164.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. BotScout is left out because cti_lead, analyst_ux and osint_investigator found its precision unacceptable (it flags 8.8.8.8) and the architect would only ship it disabled; legal_dpo limited it to IP queries, so dropping it is the stricter reading. legal_dpo's verified SFS terms make the class 'noncommercial' with an allow-list candidate ('internal use only, no resale', like SANS ISC in A1 BR15), so the module is a default candidate that is off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared. Hash-only e-mails and the low caps follow the draft and all members.
P164.title: Spam/bot reputation (StopForumSpam, BotScout)

P165.rationale: Rejected 0-6. Calling api.telegram.org (getMe/getChat/getUpdates) with a criminal's bot token is authenticating with a third-party credential (rule 1), can tip off the actor (getUpdates even consumes queued messages) and risks unauthorised-access liability (Codigo Penal art. 154-A). Offline detection of bot tokens stays in the detector/secret scanner (P323/P333): tokens are masked, never used, and recommended for reporting to Telegram abuse.
P165.title: Operating Telegram bot tokens found in malware (getMe/getChat)

P166.rationale: Rejected 0-6. ThreatMiner (Cloudflare 522), InQuest Labs (empty reply), CRXcavator (502/no connect), Virushee (no connect) and the botvrij ioclist (empty) are dead or broken; old SpiderFoot/IntelOwl modules that use them are not ported. osint_investigator's dead-source registry note is kept as a backlog item so these sources do not return with unknown terms.
P166.title: Dead or broken TI APIs (ThreatMiner, InQuest Labs, CRXcavator, Virushee, botvrij ioclist)

P167.rationale: Rejected (reject 5 / defer 1). No TLS-fingerprint input exists in this build, the old JA4DB endpoint moved, and JA4+ (JA4S/JA4X/JA4H) is under the FoxIO License 1.1 with non-commercial limits (the JA4 client fingerprint itself is BSD-3). Backlog note (redteam_lead): revisit when JA4 values come from indexed scan data (Shodan/Censys) or analyst-supplied pcaps and the FoxIO licence is cleared; V3LUM never handshakes suspected C2 servers to compute JA4S/JA4X from the corporate egress.
P167.title: JA4 fingerprint DB (FoxIO)

P168.rationale: Rejected 0-6. C2-Tracker is archived, RST Cloud and DigitalSide are stale, CyberCure (520), Intercept (503) and VX Vault (no connect) are down, and the Talos blocklist and CoinBlockerLists sit behind Cloudflare challenges or terms acceptance that must not be scripted around (rule 1). Stale feeds are a false-positive factory; the P159 freshness check keeps similar feeds out automatically.
P168.title: Dead, stale or blocked feeds (C2-Tracker, RST Cloud, Talos IP list, CoinBlockerLists, CyberCure, Intercept, VX Vault, DigitalSide)

final_conditions: Bundle: a compact build made by a reproducible dev script pinned to a MISP warninglists commit, CI size budget <= 3 MB gzip, only string, hostname and cidr list types (regex lists excluded: Python re has no timeout; substring lists only if bounded). Refresh through the dataset manager (`v3lum data update warninglists`, weekly TTL); doctor shows the age.

Matching is offline (disclosure 'none') and lazy (loaded on first use, not at start-up): CIDR lists go into the one shared IP interval index used for noise, blocklists and cloud ranges; hostnames into sets keyed by PSL registrable domain plus subdomain match; no string suffix matching. It merges into core/noise.py (AR06).

Three outcomes. SUPPRESS (infrastructure values only: bare IP, CIDR, domain, hash): reserved/RFC ranges, public resolvers, empty-file hashes; recorded, not pivoted, shown as 'likely benign because <list> (<version date>)'. TAG: cloud, CDN, scanner, Tor, VPN, sinkhole, dynamic DNS, URL shortener, disposable mail, user-content hosting.
TOP-SITE (Tranco, Umbrella, Radar lists) only tags 'popular site' and down-weights registrable-domain reputation; it never suppresses URL-level, subdomain or hash verdicts (cti_lead, analyst_ux).

User-content and dynamic-DNS parents (docs/sites/drive/forms.google.com, storage.googleapis.com, *.blob.core.windows.net, SharePoint, github.io, blogspot, firebaseapp, pages.dev, workers.dev, ngrok, duckdns...) are never suppressed, even in a top list. A URL with a path or query on any listed domain is tagged hosted_on_legit_platform and still investigated (AR06).

Never silent and never destructive: a hit never deletes findings or entities; SUPPRESS lowers the confidence of verdicts on that entity, TAG lists add context only and never lower a direct malicious finding, and a match never overrides a malicious TI finding on the same entity (it is displayed next to it). The analyst can override per entity.

Sinkholes: a match sets is_sinkhole; a domain resolving to a sinkhole is tagged sinkholed (formerly malicious), never counted as live C2, with 'hits = infected clients, not attacker infrastructure'. EICAR and test-file hashes are tagged test_file and shown. Sinkhole and parking-NS lists ship with the bundle and vocab gains sinkhole, parked, benign_scanner (AR06).

Display: the terminal shows one collapsed line 'N indicators suppressed as known-benign (lists...)'; HTML/JSON list each match with list name and version. Cloud/CDN/scanner tags feed the P378 third_party_hosted tag and the A7 CDN exclusion.

Licence (A6): MISP warninglists are CC0 and may be bundled; the X4BNet-derived VPN/datacenter lists keep their MIT notice in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES. Heavy top-1M and known-good-hash lists are optional `v3lum data update` downloads, never bundled or fetched mid-scan.

Tests: fixtures for 8.8.8.8, 1.1.1.1, google.com, a CDN IP, a sinkhole IP and the EICAR hash, plus regressions: a phishing-feed URL on docs.google.com stays flagged and a sites.google.com phishing URL extracted from a pasted e-mail is investigated and scored (today core/noise.py marks it as noise).
P169.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1: the main false-positive control for every IOC verdict (CR27 needs it). The architect's floor sets the build: pinned compact bundle under 3 MB, no regex lists, lazy load, one shared IP interval index, merge into core/noise.py. cti_lead, osint_investigator and analyst_ux insisted that abused big platforms must never be silenced, so SUPPRESS applies to infrastructure values only and top-site lists only tag. The confidence conflict (architect: hits lower confidence; analyst_ux: tags never lower a malicious finding) is resolved per outcome. legal_dpo confirmed CC0/MIT bundling under A6. The dataset provider (MISP project) is trusted, terms open.
P169.title: MISP warninglists compact bundle (false-positive suppression + context tags)

final_conditions: Ship data/pivot_links/threat_intel_ioc.json in the frozen P311 pack schema (label, template, entity_types, category, host, verified, checked_at, privacy, publishes=false, touches_target, login_required, antibot), plus the optional per-link max_tlp field that the phase-0 schema must include. The pack is offline data (disclosure 'none'): V3LUM never requests these URLs or any API behind them.

Rendering follows A2/P311: at TLP:AMBER and above every link is non-clickable text with 'opening sends <value> to <host>'; at RED third-party links are hidden from reports and listed only by `v3lum links` with the warning; links are never auto-opened and `links --open` at AMBER+ needs an interactive confirmation naming the host.

CI renders every template with a sample value per declared entity type and with hostile values (quotes, spaces, unicode, newlines): each result must be an https URL on the declared host, built only from whitelisted placeholders through the declared encoder (never str.format, never {raw} in URL position).

Every link host has a provider-registry entry with tier and rationale (A8); unknown-tier hosts get the 'unknown operator' badge and their templates take IOC_TYPES values only (A8 BR4): never PERSONAL_TYPES, CNPJ, company names, keywords, malware or actor names, or other free text (P311 lint).

Initial host tiers for the registry reviewer to confirm: trusted - CESNET NERD, FortiGuard (Fortinet), GreyNoise Visualizer; community - URLVoid, ThreatBook (CN); unknown - HoneyLabs, MultiRBL (valli.org), CyberCrime-Tracker.

Order: P311 groups links by analyst question with verified links first; inside a group the pack's file order is the curated analyst-value order (NERD, GreyNoise Visualizer, FortiGuard, URLVoid, MultiRBL, HoneyLabs, CyberCrime-Tracker, ThreatBook); the terminal shows at most 8 links per seed, the rest go to HTML and `v3lum links`.

Verified links carry checked_at; `v3lum doctor --links` (offline) lists unverified links and links not re-checked for more than 180 days. The pack ships in phase 1 with the other pivot packs (A16), whatever the state of the related automated modules.

Entries: NERD IP page, FortiGuard search (the verified search-results variant only; the iprep/webfilter variants are re-derived in a browser before use), GreyNoise Visualizer /ips/{ip}, HoneyLabs lookup page (HTML, not the keyed JSON), MultiRBL lookup, URLVoid page, CyberCrime-Tracker search (domain, IP, URL), ThreatBook research page.

URLVoid runs a fresh check on view: touches_target=true, rendered only for analyst-typed values, hidden at TLP:AMBER and above and for hostile entities unless expanded (legal_dpo, redteam_lead), otherwise defanged and non-clickable with the warning.

ThreatBook carries the 'foreign provider (CN): queries are logged abroad' badge and max_tlp=green: hidden from reports at TLP:AMBER+ and listed only by `v3lum links` (redteam_lead). It is kept only if its page shows a verdict without signing in; otherwise login_required=true and the P311 lint drops it.

Unknown-tier hosts here receive IOC values only (IP, domain, URL; a CyberCrime-Tracker malware_family template only after a recorded promotion to community tier, A8 BR4); MultiRBL and HoneyLabs results are manual context, while automated DNSBL checks go through DNS modules, never public resolvers for Spamhaus.
P170.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (osint_investigator voted P1). Pure data under the P311 pack schema (architect). legal_dpo's and redteam_lead's touches_target handling for URLVoid and the foreign-provider treatment of ThreatBook (cti_lead, legal_dpo, analyst_ux; hiding at AMBER+ from redteam_lead) are adopted. analyst_ux's wish to rank these after VirusTotal/AbuseIPDB/OTX/Talos is applied inside P311's verified-first rule.
P170.title: Pivot links: reputation pages (NERD, FortiGuard, GreyNoise viz, HoneyLabs, MultiRBL, URLVoid, CyberCrime-Tracker, ThreatBook)

final_conditions: Rules: CR27 multi_source_malicious, CR28 anonymized_infrastructure, CR29 favicon_clone_cluster and CR30 jarm_matches_known_c2. CR27 replaces the existing multi_source_malicious (CRITICAL at 2 module names), with a test documenting the change.

Independence: Finding.source (a registry source id) maps to an upstream family in the provider registry (AR11). The abuse.ch feeds (URLhaus, ThreatFox, MalwareBazaar, Feodo Tracker, SSLBL, YARAify) form one family, and Spamhaus another. Consensus counts distinct families, never modules, and records which sources were deduplicated.
Aggregators: FireHOL/IPsum aggregates count as the families they embed, and OTX pulses relaying abuse.ch count as abuse.ch.
CR27 is HIGH when >= 2 independent families list the entity inside the type's decay window (ip/url 30 days, domain 90 days), and MEDIUM with 1. Older hits are shown as history and not counted.
Suppression runs before CR27 and only downgrades, never deletes: warninglists (P169), sinkholes, benign scanners (GreyNoise 'benign', known research scanners) and noise/CDN ranges.
IPs in noise/CDN/shared-hosting ranges never give CR27 consensus to the domains behind them. Feeds disabled by the licence profile (P377) are not counted.
CR28: Tor exit / VPN / proxy membership is context only. It never exceeds LOW and is never tagged malicious, because these are lawful privacy tools.

CR29 needs at least one extra non-similarity signal (young domain, typosquat, phishing tag). An org_profile brand favicon served by a non-owned host, plus one extra signal, gives HIGH 'brand favicon clone'. Indexed favicon hashes are used first; fetching a hostile site's favicon is LIGHT and passes the P376 guard.

CR30 uses passive JARM values from indexed scan data. A live JARM probe is ACTIVE and runs only on in-scope authorized targets (A7); for hostile or other out-of-scope hosts only indexed values are used, whatever the egress. CR30 needs at least one extra signal and is low confidence otherwise.
Evidence lists the contributing sources, their upstream families, last_seen dates and terms class.
Graph fixtures: two modules sharing one upstream feed count once; a stale hit is not counted; a CDN IP does not taint co-hosted domains.
P171.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. cti_lead and the architect showed that 'independent' means 'two module names' today, so URLhaus plus ThreatFox, or a FireHOL aggregate, double-count one upstream. Hence upstream families in the registry (architect floor) plus decay windows (cti_lead, analyst_ux). legal_dpo's floor: anonymity networks never above LOW, licence-disabled feeds not counted, terms class in evidence. redteam_lead: JARM/favicon from indexed data first, live probes gated. osint_investigator: brand favicon clones from org_profile.
P171.title: Correlation pack: threat-intel consensus (CR27-CR30)

final_conditions: One implementation in core/ioc.py, with detect.extract_iocs and modules/utility/ioc_extract.py as thin wrappers. Stage order: decode layers -> refang -> span-masked extraction (URLs, e-mails, domains, IPs, hashes, CVE/ATT&CK, crypto) -> validation -> warninglist annotation -> pivot.

Licences: MIT patterns from ninoseki ioc-extractor and ioc-fanger are adapted with attribution in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. InQuest iocextract (GPL-2) and ioc-finder (LGPLv3+) are study material only, and there is no ioc-finder/pyparsing dependency.

Validation: ipaddress, IANA TLD + PSL, checksums (P217), ATT&CK ids against the bundled ATT&CK index (P292), plausible CVE years. Bogon/private IPs are kept but marked. TLDs that look like file extensions (.zip .mov .py .sh .md) get low confidence unless defanged, with a scheme, or resolving.
Bounds: decode depth <= 3, decoded output <= 2x input and <= 20 MB, base64 only for plausible blocks, embedded archives never decompressed. The 5,000-IOC limit is kept and reported when hit.
Performance tests: every regex is reviewed for catastrophic backtracking, with a pathological-input test (1 MB of dots/hyphens < 2 s); 1 MB of text extracts in < 2 s and 10 MB in < 10 s.

Brazilian scam text: national phone formats without '+' ((11) 98765-4321, 11 98765-4321, 0800), validated against the ANATEL DDD list; wa.me/<digits> and api.whatsapp.com/send?phone= -> phone; t.me/<name> and t.me/+<invite> -> telegram types (P333); instagram/tiktok/x profile URLs -> platform-qualified accounts; PIX BR Code (000201...6304+CRC) handed to P233; 14-digit CNPJ with a valid DV.

Privacy (legal floor): from text/file inputs only IOC_TYPES auto-expand. PERSONAL_TYPES (every e-mail, org_profile addresses included, phones, usernames, person names, CPF) become expand=False pivots listed for analyst selection (AR07). org_profile domains, the sender's own domain and warninglisted values are listed but not auto-pivoted.
CPFs and card numbers found in text are masked in every output (CPF as ***.456.789-**; a PAN truncated to BIN6 + last 4 at extraction) and are never expanded.

Pasted material is attacker-controlled. Extraction is static and offline (disclosure 'none'): files are never rendered, and remote templates, UNC paths, URLs and images are never resolved. IOCs from text are passive-only pivots: LIGHT/ACTIVE modules never run on them automatically.
URLs carrying a recipient identifier (an org_profile e-mail in plain, URL-encoded or base64 form) are flagged 'recipient token' and never fetched automatically (A7).

Output is defanged by default in terminal, HTML and Markdown (--no-defang disables it) and raw in JSON/STIX/MISP. Each IOC keeps its span (offset/line) as provenance. In interactive mode a one-screen preview ('37 IOCs: 12 domains, 5 IPs, 4 low-confidence') precedes scanning, with confirmation above 25 IOCs.

Tests: the existing test_detect/extract cases pass unchanged. A corpus test (real CTI reports and phishing e-mails, including a PT-BR SMS/WhatsApp text with personal data replaced) has precision/recall targets and an expected entity list.
P172.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1; core of 'paste anything'. Licences follow A6: no GPL/LGPL code or dependency, with ioc-finder not adopted (cti_lead, osint_investigator, architect floor; legal_dpo would only have allowed it as an optional extra). legal_dpo's privacy floor stops personal identifiers in pasted text from being auto-investigated. osint_investigator added the Brazilian scam-text formats, redteam_lead static parsing, passive-only pivots and recipient tokens. The architect's floor: one bounded, ReDoS-tested engine. analyst_ux asked for speed and the preview, cti_lead for defanged reports.
P172.title: IOC extraction engine upgrade (decode -> refang -> span-masked extract -> validate -> warninglist)

final_conditions: Module malware_hash/circl_hashlookup: GET https://hashlookup.circl.lu/lookup/{md5|sha1|sha256}/{h} and the bulk endpoints (/bulk/md5, /bulk/sha1) for pasted lists. 404 = 'not in hashlookup' (EMPTY, no finding, coverage only; absent_statuses {404}), never clean. Registry provider circl (national CERT): tier trusted, terms open.

A hit is not automatically known-good: a record carrying KnownMalicious (EICAR -> malshare.com) gives a malware finding (medium); known_good is set only when the record has no KnownMalicious field and comes from NSRL/OS/vendor sets.

Wording 'known file: <product/OS> (<source set>)', never 'clean'. known_good dampens AV-consensus votes but never suppresses specific listings (KnownMalicious, MalwareBazaar, ThreatFox), LOLDrivers/LOLBAS/LOLRMM context (P268), YARA hits or internal sightings (P348); a conflict is shown as 'conflict: known file vs listed'.

parent/children records give other hash forms (hash expansion) as pivots. Internal file hashes disclose possession: disclosure third_party, so the TLP:RED gate applies. Fixtures: NSRL hit, EICAR KnownMalicious, 404; a test with a LOLDrivers hash present in NSRL keeps the BYOVD finding.
P173.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. The KnownMalicious gap fill is unanimous; cti_lead and analyst_ux add that 'known file' never hides BYOVD/LOLBin context or specific listings, and legal_dpo notes the TLP:RED gate because hashes disclose possession.
P173.title: CIRCL hashlookup (known-good / NSRL + hash expansion)

final_conditions: Module malware_hash/hybrid_analysis: key 'hybridanalysis' (exists; V3LUM_HYBRID_KEY only as an alias), headers api-key, accept: application/json and a non-empty User-Agent; POST /api/v2/search/hash and report-summary reads only.
Path allow-list with a test: no /submit/* or /quick-scan/* endpoint is ever built, because a public-sandbox submission publishes and detonates the sample (rule 7). Vetting-gated fields are optional.

Licence (legal floor): the terms page is JS-only (unverified 2026-11-26): legal records whether the team's vetted free key permits corporate use (key_plans.hybridanalysis='business'); otherwise a CrowdStrike licence is required before it runs under the corporate profile. Registry: tier trusted (CrowdStrike), terms key-terms.
Mapping: verdict, threat_score and vx_family; no specific threat -> no finding; 404 or [] -> EMPTY; 403 'API key is missing/incompatible' -> NEEDS_KEY.

Hosts and domains contacted in sandbox reports are filtered through warninglists (OS update, OCSP/CRL, CDN, telemetry) and emitted as communicates_with with confidence <= 0.5 and expand=False unless the report marks them as IOCs/C2; they are hostile-tagged for the P376 guard. A success fixture is captured with the team key (only 403 exists).
P174.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. redteam_lead and the architect make submissions structurally impossible, legal_dpo requires the key's corporate use to be recorded, and cti_lead's warninglist filtering keeps benign sandbox infrastructure out of pivots.
P174.title: Hybrid Analysis API v2 (hash search, keyed)

final_conditions: Module malware_hash/yaraify: POST https://yaraify-api.abuse.ch/api/v1/ with {'query':'lookup_hash','search_term':<hash>} only; file scan and upload endpoints are never built (unit test). Terms 'open': YARAify is CC0 for commercial and non-commercial use (abuse.ch terms s.3.4, A1 BR14), so it runs under corporate even while MalwareBazaar is licence-gated.

The shared abuse.ch Auth-Key ('abusech') is sent on every call (terms s.2.1: authenticated users only; a keyless answer is not a permission). Without the key the module returns NEEDS_KEY with the manual YARAify link. The key is redacted everywhere (AR01).
query_status no_results = EMPTY 'unknown to YARAify' (not clean); illegal_* -> SKIPPED reason_code 'not_applicable'.

At most 5 matched rule names with authors, mapped to a family when the rule is family-specific (alias index P295); generic/heuristic rules (SUSP_, PUA, Generic, Heuristic, packer/UPX/installer rules) are low-confidence context and never above low alone.
Metadata imphash/ssdeep/tlsh/telfhash/gimphash/dhash_icon become structural attributes for P351. YARAify belongs to the abuse.ch upstream family (P171). Fixtures: EICAR hit, no_results, 401.
P175.rationale: Approved 6-0. The median is P2 (cti_lead and legal_dpo voted P1); the chair raises it to P1 because, as cti_lead argued, it is the corporate-safe hash source while MalwareBazaar is licence-gated and VirusTotal public is non-commercial, and the A3 minimum answer set needs default-ready sha256 reputation sources under corporate from the first phase; effort S. cti_lead's and osint_investigator's reading of terms s.2.1 (send the Auth-Key; keyless answers are not relied upon) is stricter than the draft and adopted; analyst_ux's generic-rule cap is kept.
P175.title: YARAify lookup_hash (abuse.ch)

final_conditions: Module malware_hash/cymru_mhr: TXT query {hash}.hash.cymru.com through ctx.dns (core DoH resolver with ECS disabled, P029), not raw HTTP; applies() only to MD5/SHA-1, because SHA-256 labels exceed 63 characters and are unsupported.

Licence: Team Cymru states 'MHR is free for non-commercial use' (verified 2026-11-26): terms 'noncommercial'; off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared (a commercial MHR agreement or a licence_allow entry recorded by legal); in the research profile only with a recorded legal basis and the licence banner.
NXDOMAIN = EMPTY 'not in MHR' (no finding, never clean); malformed TXT = ERROR; SERVFAIL and timeouts = could not verify. The 'epoch pct' parser is unit-tested.

Wording 'AV detection N% (Team Cymru MHR, last seen <date>)': N >= 30% -> malicious (medium); 10-29% -> low; < 10% -> info. The notice states that the DoH provider also sees the hash. Fixtures: the six recorded DoH answers. Registry provider team_cymru: tier trusted.
P176.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. legal_dpo verified the non-commercial terms, so the module is a default candidate that is off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared (A3 BR4, A1 BR16 lists Team Cymru MHR as noncommercial). The architect's ctx.dns implementation, redteam_lead's ECS rule and the detection bands of cti_lead and analyst_ux are consolidated.
P176.title: Team Cymru Malware Hash Registry (DNS via DoH)

final_conditions: One module per provider, each with its own key in config.KNOWN_KEYS, status, terms, quota and success fixture, all default_enabled False: triage (Recorded Future Triage, Bearer), metadefender (OPSWAT, apikey), malshare (api_key), polyswarm (Authorization) and virusshare (apikey; key required even though an empty key answered). Order: Triage, then MetaDefender, then the rest.

Per-provider path allow-lists with tests prove that no sample download (MalShare action=getfile, VirusShare download, Triage sample files, MetaDefender downloads) or submission endpoint is ever built: search/metadata only.

Licence (legal floor, verified 2026-11-26): Triage's free Individual/Researcher licences are non-commercial and make analyses public, so corporate use needs a commercial Triage licence; OPSWAT licenses free use 'solely for Your personal use', so MetaDefender needs a paid plan.

Classes: triage free 'noncommercial' (commercial licence 'license'); metadefender free 'noncommercial' (paid plan 'key-terms'); malshare, polyswarm and virusshare 'unknown' until legal records their terms. Each adapter runs under corporate only once its plan or licence is recorded; empty-key answers are ignored.

Triage: malware config extraction gives C2 IOCs as communicates_with pivots, hostile-tagged for P376 and never contacted. Each adapter is one vote; same-vendor sources (MetaDefender and Filescan are both OPSWAT) count once in consensus (P171). Daily budgets via P334.
Registry tiers: Recorded Future, OPSWAT and PolySwarm trusted; MalShare and VirusShare community. Each adapter ships only with a success fixture (today only VirusShare has one).
P177.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. The architect's floor splits the five providers into separate adapters with their own status, terms and fixtures; legal_dpo's verified terms make Triage and MetaDefender free tiers non-commercial and the others unknown until recorded, so all stay opt-in. cti_lead's Triage-first order, redteam_lead's no-download/no-submit allow-lists and the OPSWAT single-vote rule are kept.
P177.title: Keyed hash lookups (Triage, MalShare, MetaDefender, PolySwarm, VirusShare)

final_conditions: Module malware_hash/filescan_reputation: the keyless filescan.io reputation/hash?sha256= lookup only; uploads and scan endpoints are never built (unit test).

Terms 'unknown' (A1 BR16 initial class, which a chair may only make stricter; OPSWAT licenses free use 'solely for Your personal use'): disabled in every profile until legal records the class and, where needed, a licence_allow entry or a commercial plan; default_enabled False.

The ~800 KB response is streamed with max_bytes 2 MB; truncation = ERROR 'response too large', never parsed; res.raw keeps only verdict, tags and Filescan report ids. A complete trimmed response fixture is captured (the existing one is a 1.5 KB head).
It counts as the same OPSWAT vote as MetaDefender (P177). The search page is an SPA: manual report link only. Registry provider opswat_filescan: tier trusted.
P178.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. legal_dpo found that OPSWAT's own terms limit free use to personal use and asked for 'noncommercial' pending confirmation; A1 BR16 binds Filescan to 'unknown', which is stricter and stays until legal records the class, so the module is off by default (also asked by cti_lead, osint_investigator, redteam_lead and analyst_ux). The architect's size cap and reduction before evidence are kept.
P178.title: Filescan.io hash reputation (OPSWAT)

P179.rationale: Rejected (yes 1 / reject 4 / defer 1). hashdd and Malprob are value-2 sources from unknown operators with unknown terms that both returned nothing for EICAR; CIRCL hashlookup (P173) already answers known-good, and the 'only when primary sources are silent' ordering is not implementable today (architect). Backlog note (osint_investigator, legal_dpo): revisit only if CIRCL hashlookup and the keyed sources leave a measured gap and the terms are reviewed; even then unknown tier means never default, excluded at TLP:AMBER+ and hash inputs only.

final_conditions: Module vulnerability_cve/circl_vulnlookup: vulnerability.circl.lu /api/vulnerability/{id} (CVE, GHSA, PySec and CSAF ids), plus the sightings and EPSS endpoints; optional key 'circl_vuln' (V3LUM_CIRCL_VULN_KEY alias); 404 -> EMPTY; x-ratelimit 20 per 60 s honoured through P334. Registry provider circl: tier trusted, terms open (CC BY 4.0 where applicable, attribution).

One shared CVE JSON 5 parser and attribute normaliser (cvss, cvss_vector, cwe, affected, kev, epss) for circl_vulnlookup, cve_record (P183) and cve_offline_mirror (P352): CIRCL returns the CVE 5 schema for CVE ids, so there is no second parser.

P181.title: CIRCL Vulnerability-Lookup (+ sightings, EPSS, CWE)

final_conditions: Offline module vulnerability_cve/cisa_kev: known_exploited_vulnerabilities.json from www.cisa.gov registered with register_dataset (TTL 6 h; US public domain) and indexed locally by cveID; zero per-CVE requests (disclosure none, TLP:RED-safe).
It sets kev=true, dateAdded, dueDate, vendor/product and knownRansomwareCampaignUse on the CVE entity; knownRansomwareCampaignUse='Known' is shown as its own flag.

Asset severity is decided only by CR15 (P291): a KEV CVE inferred from a version string or CPE (InternetDB/Shodan banners) caps at HIGH, labelled 'version-inferred, backports not considered'; CRITICAL needs verified evidence on an own or in-scope asset.

'Not in KEV' never reads 'not exploited'. Dataset age is shown in coverage and doctor flags a copy older than 48 h. kev stays CISA-only: VulnCheck, CIRCL, MSRC and EUVD exploitation evidence goes to the exploited attribute.
P182.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. redteam_lead's condition binds severity to the verified/inferred split of P291 (backported banners are the classic false CRITICAL); analyst_ux adds the 'not in KEV' wording. Offline dataset: tier 'n/a', terms 'open'.
P182.title: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities

final_conditions: Module vulnerability_cve/cve_record. Precedence: offline mirror (P352) when present -> cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/{id} (CNA and CISA ADP containers: CVSS, SSVC, KEV ADP) -> NVD 2.0 services.nvd.nist.gov/rest/json/cves/2.0?cveId= only when CPE configurations are needed (seed CVEs or has_vuln on an org asset) or key 'nvd' is set. NVD web pages are an SPA: links only.

NVD keyless 5 req/30 s (50 with key 'nvd', V3LUM_NVD_KEY alias, from a team account) as a P334 token bucket that defers instead of sleeping in a worker; per-case NVD budget of 10 keyless calls. CWE names come from a registered CWE dataset, never a per-CVE CWE REST call.

CVE fan-out rule shared by P181, P183, P184's API fallback, P185, P186, P188-P191 and the P354 VEX adapter: online per-CVE calls run for seed CVEs and for at most setting cve_fanout_budget (default 20) pivot CVEs per case, KEV/EPSS-ranked first; the rest are answered offline (P182, P184, P352) or listed as deferred.
One shared CVE 5 parser (with P181 and P352). REJECTED/RESERVED records -> info, never scored. Cache 24 h.

One consolidated CVE card per CVE (P335 grouping): CVSS with source/version, EPSS + percentile with date, KEV (dateAdded, ransomware use, due date), exploitation evidence by source, exploit availability (curated count + links), vendor fix (KB/advisory/fixed versions) and affected products; the other CVE modules add fields with provenance instead of separate findings.

One plain-words priority line (e.g. 'KEV + EPSS 0.97: patch now'). A bare CVE lookup shows that patch-priority label instead of a case risk level unless the CVE is linked to an own asset (CR15). Test: 5 CVE modules on one CVE fixture give one card and no CRITICAL case level.

Notices: 'This product uses data from the NVD API but is not endorsed or certified by the NVD.' wherever NVD data appears (v3lum info, report footer); MITRE's CVE/CWE copyright designation and licence in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES. Registry providers mitre and nist_nvd: tier trusted, terms open.
P183.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. legal_dpo's notices, the architect's precedence, token bucket and fan-out budget (NVD's keyless rate would stall workers when InternetDB yields 30 CVEs per IP) and analyst_ux's consolidated CVE card with a patch-priority line are combined; the fan-out rule is defined here once for every per-CVE module in this chunk.
P183.title: CVE record (MITRE cveawg + NVD 2.0 + CWE)

final_conditions: Offline module vulnerability_cve/epss (disclosure none, TLP:RED-safe, default_enabled True): the daily bulk CSV (gz) registered with the dataset manager (safe decompression, size cap) and indexed locally; zero per-CVE calls, so 500-CVE scanner exports cost nothing.

A separate module epss_api (disclosure third_party; one disclosure class per module, A8 BR7; default_enabled True) calls api.first.org/data/v1/epss?cve= only for CVEs missing from the day's file, one CVE per run (modules run per entity), under the CVE fan-out rule (P183); it shares epss's parser and is skipped at TLP:RED.

Stores epss, percentile and the model date; the CVE card shows them in plain words ('top 1%: likely to be exploited soon'). FIRST attribution in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES (free, no registration, attribution requested). Registry provider first: tier trusted, terms open; the daily file's current host (epss.empiricalsecurity.com per the research) is declared.
P184.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. cti_lead and the architect make the daily CSV primary (offline, no fan-out; the engine runs per entity, so API batching cannot be used as drafted); legal_dpo's attribution and analyst_ux's plain wording are added.
P184.title: FIRST EPSS

final_conditions: Module vulnerability_cve/osv_ghsa: api.osv.dev/v1/vulns/{id} for CVE/GHSA ids (fixtures exist; 404 -> EMPTY); GHSA advisories via REST advisories?cve_id= through the shared GitHub client and budget of P111, with its no-scope machine-account token rule; the GHSA path is re-tested from the team network with fixtures before merge. Per-CVE calls follow the CVE fan-out rule (P183).

Sources: OSV (CC BY 4.0, per-source licences, attribution) 'open'; GHSA through the GitHub REST API 'key-terms' (as P111). Per-source filtering (ctx.allowed_sources) lets OSV run when the GitHub source is not cleared.

package@version querybatch is built only once a purl/package entity type exists (a later P333 wave); until then it is not built. Package queries would disclose the internal software inventory and follow the TLP gate like any shared input.
OSV distro records (Debian/Ubuntu/Alpine, e.g. DEBIAN-CVE-*) are read for CVE ids to show per-release fixed versions on the CVE card; the banner-revision backport check is done offline by P355.
Affected ranges are stored compactly (ecosystem, package, introduced/fixed) instead of whole records in evidence. Registry providers osv (Google) and github: tier trusted.
P185.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. cti_lead's distro ecosystems and the architect's compact storage and package-entity precondition are adopted; redteam_lead's backport check needs a package entity this build does not have, so it is delivered offline by P355 for Debian banners. legal_dpo's attribution and machine-account token rule apply. Terms follow the most restrictive source (GitHub REST, 'key-terms').
P185.title: OSV.dev + GitHub Advisory Database

final_conditions: Module vulnerability_cve/vulncheck: key 'vulncheck' (Bearer) required; default_enabled False. If the community tier offers the vulncheck-kev index backup, the module is offline on that daily SQLite index (disclosure none); otherwise it makes per-CVE calls (disclosure third_party) under the CVE fan-out rule (P183). A module declares one disclosure class (A8 BR7).

Licence: VulnCheck's site licence is 'personal, internal and non-commercial' while its Service Terms (rev. 6 Jul 2026) treat a community version as a Free Offering: legal records that the team's community key falls under the Service Terms, or a paid plan, in key_plans before corporate use. The key comes from a company account, never a personal one (rule 1).

VulnCheck KEV hits go to the exploited attribute with source 'vulncheck_kev' and reference URLs, never kev=true (kev stays CISA KEV with BOD 22-01 dates). VulnCheck data is not made available to third parties: exports carry only CVE ids and the flag.
401 {'error':true,'errors':['unauthorized']} = NEEDS_KEY. A success fixture is captured with the team key (only 401 exists). Registry provider vulncheck: tier trusted, terms key-terms.
P186.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. cti_lead keeps the two KEV lists apart; legal_dpo's floor requires the community key's terms to be recorded and blocks onward sharing; the architect's offline index preference and default off are kept.
P186.title: VulnCheck KEV / NVD++ (keyed)

final_conditions: Implemented as a registered dataset plus a correlation rule, not a per-keyword module (the engine never auto-expands keywords): dataset endoflife (weekly) downloads endoflife.date/api/v1/products/{slug} for the slugs of a curated mapping table data/eol_products.json (technology name -> slug). No per-scan request, so the investigated stack is never disclosed.
The mapping is pinned (no fuzzy guessing): unmapped technologies are skipped. Version parsing (major/minor/cycle) is unit-tested per product.

The rule fires an EOL/unsupported finding only when an explicit version string was detected (banner, meta generator, header) and maps to a release cycle, with the version's source shown; inferred or major-only versions give info with confidence <= 0.4, labelled 'version-inferred'.
Distro packages with backports are not reported as upstream EOL; EOL findings cap at medium unless the version is authoritative.

One grouped finding per asset lists all EOL components: medium/low on own or in-scope assets (org_profile), info on third-party or attacker infrastructure (CDN/SaaS edges are context). Attribution: endoflife.date (MIT data). Registry provider endoflife: tier community (dataset source).
P187.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. The architect's floor reshapes it into a dataset plus a correlation rule because the drafted web_fingerprint -> keyword -> module flow does not exist in the engine; cti_lead, osint_investigator, redteam_lead and analyst_ux require explicit versions, honest version-inferred labels and own-asset scoping. Offline at scan time: tier 'n/a', terms 'open'.
P187.title: endoflife.date product lifecycle

final_conditions: Module vulnerability_cve/securitycontext_cve: GET api.securitycontext.com/v1/cves/{id} only. POST /v1/scans and any MCP create tool are never built (submissions). Product/version and /v1/stack queries are not built: they disclose the software inventory, and keywords are not IOC_TYPES that an unknown-tier provider may receive.

Terms 'unknown' (no terms published; operator ProjectDiscovery per the homepage, checked 2026-11-26; A1 BR16) and provider tier 'unknown' (A8): disabled in every profile until legal records terms; default_enabled False; even then excluded at TLP:AMBER+ and run at CLEAR/GREEN only with --allow-unknown until promoted.
Descriptive UA; 60 req/min per address with 429 + Retry-After honoured (RATE_LIMITED when > 15 s, within the scan deadline); cache 24 h; per-CVE calls under the CVE fan-out rule (P183).

Schema check on the undocumented JSON (missing keys -> ERROR). Values fill CVE-card fields with provenance and are compared with the primary modules (conflicts shown), never the sole source of an attribute; NVD, EPSS, KEV and exploit_index stay the default chain.
nuclei template references are informational only: this module never downloads or executes templates.
P188.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. All members gate it on the missing terms (A1 BR16 classes SecurityContext 'unknown'); analyst_ux notes the unknown tier, which A8 turns into opt-in only, never at AMBER+. cti_lead's and analyst_ux's GET-only rule, the architect's schema check and fallback role and redteam_lead's informational templates are consolidated. It is built in phase 2 but runs only after legal review.
P188.title: SecurityContext CVE intelligence (vulnx backend)

final_conditions: Module vulnerability_cve/shodan_cvedb: cvedb.shodan.io/cve/{id} and /cves?product=&is_kev= (product search only for analyst-typed queries); per-CVE calls under the CVE fan-out rule (P183); fixtures exist. default_enabled False (redundant with CIRCL + EPSS + KEV).

Licence: 'free for non-commercial use! If you're using the CVEDB API to make money, then you need an enterprise license' (verified 2026-11-26): terms 'noncommercial' (A1 BR14); off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared by a recorded enterprise licence or a licence_allow entry reading internal defensive use as outside 'making money' (scope and review date).

When it is disabled there is no fallback to active probing; CIRCL + EPSS + KEV cover the gap. A commercial Shodan licence bought for InternetDB (A15) is checked for CVEDB coverage. Registry provider shodan: tier trusted.
P189.rationale: Approved 5-0-1 at median P3. cti_lead deferred as redundant and non-commercial; default off and the licence gate (legal_dpo, the architect, redteam_lead's no-active-fallback) address that.
P189.title: Shodan CVEDB

final_conditions: Split by disclosure. Offline module exploit_index (disclosure none): Exploit-DB files_exploits.csv (from gitlab.com/exploit-database raw; GPL-2.0 repository, downloaded at runtime only, never vendored), Metasploit modules_metadata_base.json (~11 MB, BSD-3) and nuclei-templates cves.json (NDJSON, MIT), indexed at weekly refresh by the dataset manager.

Separate adapter poc_index (disclosure third_party: the CVE id leaves the machine): PoC-in-GitHub per-CVE JSON (raw.githubusercontent.com/nomi-sec/PoC-in-GitHub/master/{year}/{CVE}.json; 404 = none) and trickest/cve markdown ('#### Reference' / '#### Github' sections), under the CVE fan-out rule (P183). Both are link indexes only (no data licence) and never redistributed.

Maturity in vocab attribute exploit_maturity: a Metasploit module or Exploit-DB entry -> 'weaponised' (exploit_available); a nuclei CVE template -> 'detection template'; PoC-in-GitHub/trickest -> 'poc_claimed (N repos)' with confidence <= 0.4. exploit_available is set only from curated sources (Exploit-DB, Metasploit, nuclei, KEV).
Exploit or PoC availability raises priority only: it never turns a version-inferred match into a verified vulnerability or sets CRITICAL by itself (P291).

PoC repository URLs are untrusted references: defanged, top 5 by stars/recency, labelled 'unverified code, may be malicious: never run outside an isolated lab', expand=False. V3LUM never clones, downloads, renders READMEs of or runs PoCs; Metasploit and nuclei entries are references only (the nuclei runner stays the gated ACTIVE P369).

Datasets come from pinned source URLs, are refreshed out of band and show their age; attributions (Exploit-DB GPL-2.0 runtime data, Metasploit BSD-3, nuclei MIT) are generated from the registry. Registry providers github and gitlab (raw hosts): tier trusted, terms open.
P190.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (cti_lead and redteam_lead voted P1). The architect's floor splits the per-CVE GitHub fetches into a third_party adapter (the draft wrongly marked everything offline, breaking TLP:RED); legal_dpo's runtime-only GPL data and link-only PoC indexes, cti_lead's maturity levels, redteam_lead's 'never CRITICAL by itself' and analyst_ux's capped, labelled PoC links are consolidated. GPL data fetched at runtime with attribution is 'open' under the A1 definitions.
P190.title: Exploit/PoC indexes (PoC-in-GitHub, Exploit-DB CSV, Metasploit metadata, nuclei cves.json, trickest/cve)

final_conditions: Module vulnerability_cve/euvd: euvdservices.enisa.europa.eu/api/enisaid?id={CVE} and search?text=&size=<=10; default_enabled False (opt-in); per-CVE calls under the CVE fan-out rule (P183).
max_bytes 1 MB per response (the log4j record is ~492 KB); truncation = ERROR. EUVD ids are stored as aliases only; the exploited flag goes to the exploited attribute with source 'euvd'.
ENISA source acknowledgement in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES. Registry provider enisa: tier trusted, terms open. Fixtures: CVE record, search, large-response truncation.
P191.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3, opt-in as cti_lead and the architect asked, with the architect's size cap and legal_dpo's acknowledgement.
P191.title: ENISA EU Vulnerability Database (EUVD)

P192.rationale: Deferred (yes 1 / reject 2 / defer 3). CVEdetails, OpenCVE and VulDB are three more keyed adapters with low marginal value over cveawg, NVD, EPSS, KEV, CIRCL, OSV, MSRC and CSAF, and no success fixtures exist. Backlog unblock (osint_investigator, analyst_ux): a team subscription already paid for, or a coverage gap the free sources leave. Conditions then (legal_dpo): each key from a company account on a plan whose terms legal records as business-compatible (VulDB commercial ToS and OpenCVE terms per key); OpenCVE (AGPL-3.0) for ideas only; fields added to the CVE card (P183) with provenance, never separate findings.
P192.title: Minor keyed CVE sources (CVEdetails, OpenCVE, VulDB)

P193.rationale: Rejected 0-6. The KEVin mirror is dead (530 / Cloudflare 1033); cisa_kev (P182) downloads the CISA KEV catalogue directly from the source.
P193.title: KEVin API (CISA KEV mirror)

final_conditions: Ship data/pivot_links/vulnerability.json in the frozen P311 pack schema (label, template, entity_types, category, host, verified, checked_at, privacy, publishes=false, touches_target, login_required, antibot). The pack is offline data (disclosure 'none'): V3LUM never requests these URLs or any API behind them.

Rendering follows A2/P311: at TLP:AMBER and above every link is non-clickable text with 'opening sends <value> to <host>'; at RED third-party links are hidden from reports and listed only by `v3lum links` with the warning; links are never auto-opened and `links --open` at AMBER+ needs an interactive confirmation naming the host.

CI renders every template with a sample value per declared entity type and with hostile values (quotes, spaces, unicode, newlines): each result must be an https URL on the declared host, built only from whitelisted placeholders through the declared encoder (never str.format, never {raw} in URL position).

Every link host has a provider-registry entry with tier and rationale (A8); unknown-tier hosts get the 'unknown operator' badge and their templates take IOC_TYPES values only (A8 BR4): never PERSONAL_TYPES, CNPJ, company names, keywords, malware or actor names, or other free text (P311 lint).
Initial host tiers for the registry reviewer to confirm: trusted - CIRCL Vulnerability-Lookup, Rapid7 Vulnerability & Exploit DB; unknown - Sploitus.

Order: P311 groups links by analyst question with verified links first; inside a group the pack's file order is the curated analyst-value order (CIRCL Vulnerability-Lookup, Rapid7 DB, Sploitus); the terminal shows at most 8 links per seed, the rest go to HTML and `v3lum links`.

Verified links carry checked_at; `v3lum doctor --links` (offline) lists unverified links and links not re-checked for more than 180 days. The pack ships in phase 1 with the other pivot packs (A16), whatever the state of the related automated modules.

Entries: vulnerability.circl.lu/vuln/{cve} (cve), rapid7.com/db/?q={q}&type= (cve, keyword), sploitus.com/?query={q} (cve only: Sploitus is unknown tier and may receive IOC_TYPES values only, A8 BR4); all verified.

Sploitus aggregates exploit code of uneven quality: its label reads 'exploit listings - view only, never download or run code', and V3LUM never downloads, stores or executes exploit code (all members).
P194.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. CVE reference pages with exploit context help prioritise exposed vulnerabilities (redteam_lead, with KEV/EPSS). The Sploitus view-only caution asked for by every member and legal_dpo's 'exploit code is never downloaded' are kept; the standard pack schema applies (architect).
P194.title: Pivot links: CVE pages (CIRCL Vulnerability-Lookup, Sploitus, Rapid7 DB)

final_conditions: Offline module cti_framework/threat_actor_handles (disclosure none): the spmedia Threat-Actor-Usernames-Scrape dataset (MIT) through the dataset manager (weekly), indexed at refresh into SQLite (lower-cased handle -> forum, list date), never a 1.1M-entry in-memory set; default_enabled False (opt-in per scan).

The threatactorusernames.com API is not in this build: an unknown-tier operator with no terms (2026-11-26), and A8 forbids sending usernames to unknown-tier providers. It may be added later as a separate opt-in module (disclosure third_party) only after legal records terms and a tier of community or higher.
Exact, case-folded match only. Handles shorter than 5 chars, purely numeric or in a bundled common-username/first-name list are skipped; dictionary words are labelled 'common handle: low signal'.

A hit is info/low: 'a user with the same handle appears on forum lists: X, Y (scrape date)', confidence POSSIBLE (<= 0.3), 'handle collision likely' (benign 'octocat' matched two carding forums); never auto-expanded, never counted in CR27, never raises the score alone or creates an identity link.

Runs only on analyst-typed usernames and threat_actor entities, never on identifiers whose provenance is an org_profile identity (local part of an own-domain e-mail, org public-members lists) except in an insider case with a recorded purpose (test with such a provenance chain).
Reports show only the matched handle, forum names and list date; the dataset is never exported or redistributed. A trimmed dataset fixture is captured before merge (only API fixtures exist).
P195.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. Every member makes the offline dataset the default path and keeps the signal weak because of handle collisions. legal_dpo's floor bars sending usernames to the unknown-tier API, so the API adapter waits for a legal review instead of shipping as an opt-in that A8 could never allow. The architect's on-disk index, redteam_lead's employee-provenance exclusion and analyst_ux's default-off wording are kept. Offline: tier 'n/a', terms 'open'.
P195.title: Threat-actor handle lookup (spmedia forum users dataset; TAU API)

final_conditions: Module darkweb_ransomware/ransomlook. Per-entity lookups via ransomlook.io/api/search?q=<normalised name or domain> (bounded, max_bytes 2 MB), plus a local index synced daily from /api/posts/period/{d1}/{d2} and /api/groups through the dataset manager (offline matching on that path).
/api/group/{name}, /api/posts and /api/export (3-163 MB) are never called during a scan.

Victim-name normalisation (accents folded; LTDA, S.A., S/A, EIRELI, ME, EPP, Inc and 'Grupo' stripped) and group-alias normalisation are shared core helpers used by P197, P356 and P357; cross-tracker dedupe ('corroborated by N trackers': victim + group alias + date +/- 3 days) is one correlation rule, not code in each module.

Matching: an exact domain/website or CNPJ match -> high, critical when the victim is an org_profile entity or a listed supplier, worded 'claimed by <group> on <date> (actor claim, unverified)'; name-only matches -> POSSIBLE 'possible match - verify victim identity', medium at most (e.g. 'Unimed' names hundreds of separate cooperatives).
One grouped finding per victim across trackers (P335), counted once in the score. Misses read 'not listed by <trackers> (data as of <date>)', never 'not breached'.

Posts are claims stored as metadata and excerpts of <= 300 chars; victims who are natural persons get no description text. Onion and claim URLs are never fetched and screenshots/images never downloaded (they can show leaked documents, rule 3); listed infrastructure is hostile-tagged and defanged.

Licence: content CC BY 4.0 with commercial use allowed (ransomlook.io/about, verified 2026-11-26): attribution 'Source: RansomLook (CC BY 4.0)' in every report and export using it; the AGPL service code is not copied. Registry provider ransomlook: tier community, terms open.
P196.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. The licence-clean leak-site tracker for the corporate default. cti_lead, osint_investigator and analyst_ux require domain/CNPJ evidence for severity and POSSIBLE name-only matches; the architect's bounded search plus daily index and the shared normaliser and dedupe rule avoid the 163 MB dumps and duplicated code; legal_dpo's claims wording and redteam_lead's never-fetch rule complete it.
P196.title: RansomLook API

final_conditions: Module darkweb_ransomware/ransomware_live. Corporate code path: the PRO API (api-pro.ransomware.live, header X-API-KEY) with one key 'ransomwarelive' (V3LUM_RANSOMWARELIVE_KEY alias; one team token, never several keys). Keyless v2 (api.ransomware.live) runs only in the research profile.

Licence (legal floor): the T&C s.5.2 (verified 2026-11-26) strictly prohibit commercial use without the owner's prior written approval, and keyless v2 is 'not intended for corporate or business use'. Source classes: v2 'noncommercial' (A1), PRO 'license'. Under corporate it needs a company-account PRO key AND that approval in licence_allow: off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared.
Until it is cleared, RansomLook (P196) and ransomfeed (P356) are the corporate defaults. Without a key or licence: one coverage line plus the manual ransomware.live victim-search link.

searchvictims/{name} by normalised company name and by domain through the shared normaliser (P196); recentvictims through the dataset manager for watch; the same victim matching, grouping and 'not listed' wording as P196; dedupe through the shared ransomware correlation rule.

Cache >= 30 min (never poll faster than its cache: fair use) and <= 60 req/min. Raw records are never re-served as an API or re-published (STIX/MISP export only to internal platforms). Attribution 'Source: Ransomware.live' with a link wherever shown (s.6).

claim_url onions and screenshot URLs are never fetched or embedded (screenshots can show leaked documents) and are shown as links with a warning. Ransom-note contacts (onions, qTox, e-mail) and group IOCs become hostile-tagged pivots with expand=False. The PRO key is redacted everywhere (AR01).
PRO success fixtures are captured with the team key (only v2 fixtures exist). Registry provider ransomware_live: tier community.
P197.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1 (cti_lead and legal_dpo voted P2). cti_lead and legal_dpo verified that the free PRO key alone does not clear corporate use (written approval required), which is stricter than A1 BR15's 'key-terms' for PRO and is adopted as the legal floor; the module is a default candidate that stays off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared (A3 BR4). The architect's single PRO code path and fixtures, osint_investigator's screenshot rule and redteam_lead's hostile tagging are kept.
P197.title: ransomware.live (v2 keyless + PRO key)

final_conditions: Offline module darkweb_ransomware/deepdarkcti_index (disclosure none): the deepdarkCTI markdown lists downloaded weekly at runtime only through the dataset manager (GPL-3.0 data: never vendored, attribution in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES, A6).

A tolerant markdown-table parser ('|Name|Status|...'), shared with P357's channel list, skips malformed rows; a parse below an expected row count marks the dataset unhealthy (doctor) instead of returning empty.

Only onion hosts (core onion v3 validator, P217) and t.me handles are indexed (onion host / Telegram handle -> actor/group and category); each entry keeps its Status column and the repository commit date.

A match reads 'listed in deepdarkCTI as <category> of <group> (status ONLINE/OFFLINE, list date <commit date>)': info/medium context, not attribution; OFFLINE or stale entries are labelled historical.
Listed onion, Telegram and forum addresses are hostile-tagged, rendered defanged and never fetched by any module.
P198.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. GPL-3.0 data used at runtime with attribution (legal_dpo, A6) is 'open' under the A1 definitions; cti_lead's status/date rule, the architect's parser-health check and redteam_lead's never-fetch rule are consolidated. Offline: tier 'n/a'.
P198.title: deepdarkCTI source index (onion leak sites / Telegram channels -> actors)

final_conditions: Module darkweb_ransomware/onion_lookup: AIL onion-lookup (CIRCL) GET https://onion.ail-project.org/api/lookup/{onion} only for onions already in the case (never bulk), after the v3 checksum is validated locally (P217); disclosure third_party (CIRCL sees the address). No Tor connections in this module.

The Ahmia banned/CSAM MD5 list (md5 of the onion host, one per line) is a registered dataset (refreshed at most daily) exposed as a core safety filter is_banned_onion(); every module applies it before any onion is displayed, stored, enriched or fetched. It is used as Ahmia offers it (filtering) and registered as an 'open' source for that use, with Ahmia's offer quoted as evidence (A1 BR2).
A banned-list hit shows only 'onion on Ahmia's abuse (banned) list: details withheld'; nothing else is stored or displayed and the onion is never enriched further.
The core HTTP and DNS layers refuse .onion hosts outside a configured Tor profile (test), so onion names never reach the corporate resolver or DoH providers.

The Ahmia onion index list is not downloaded in this build: Ahmia's ToS (25 Sep 2026) forbid replicating the service without permission; it may be added as a 'license' dataset only with Ahmia's written permission recorded. Ahmia search stays manual-only (rotating form token).
AIL titles are shown as plain text, first/last seen dated, tags as attributes. Registry provider circl (AIL): tier trusted, terms open. Fixtures: found and not found.
P199.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. The CSAM filter is mandatory for every onion-displaying module (all members; the architect moves it into core). legal_dpo's floor limits the Ahmia onion list to recorded permission, so it stays out of this build; redteam_lead's .onion refusal in the HTTP/DNS layers and analyst_ux's 'details withheld' display rule are kept.
P199.title: Onion metadata (AIL onion-lookup + Ahmia onion index and banned list)

P200.rationale: Chair decision on a contested item (yes 3 / reject 1 / defer 2): deferred. RansomPosts mirrors ransomware.live, whose T&C forbid commercial use and redistribution without written approval, so its EUPL label cannot grant corporate rights (legal_dpo); RansomLook and ransomfeed local indexes already cover supplier screening. redteam_lead, legal_dpo and analyst_ux approved only if legal confirms the chain of title; cti_lead rejected it as laundering the upstream restriction; osint_investigator and the architect deferred until RansomLook/ransomfeed prove insufficient. Because five of six members left the door open, it is deferred rather than rejected. Backlog unblock: ransomware.live's written approval (P197) covering derived datasets, or a legal record that RansomPosts collects independently, plus a supplier-screening need that P196/P356 indexes cannot meet. Conditions then: offline matching only (supplier lists never leave the machine), HTML anchors stripped, links never fetched, attribution to both sources, results sorted by match strength with name-only matches POSSIBLE.
P200.title: RansomPosts bulk datasets + Atom feed

P201.rationale: Vetoed by legal_dpo and the architect (yes 0 / reject 2 / defer 4); the veto is not lifted, so the proposal is rejected. Adopting both veto_lift sets would still give yes 2 / defer 4 (deferred by the tally, never approvable), and the four other members deferred because it touches criminal infrastructure for value 3 at effort L. legal_dpo: it automates onion search engines whose ToS forbid scraping (Ahmia) and sends company keywords to unknown operators. The architect: the only module that would make V3LUM itself connect to criminal infrastructure, with no isolation, engine allow-list or fixtures. Backlog note: re-proposal only in the combined veto_lift form. legal_dpo: no engine that forbids automation or gates search with tokens/challenges (Ahmia excluded; others need recorded permission or API terms); otherwise only analyst-selected .onion URLs already in the case, text only, size cap, no media/forms/logins/link following; shares_input True, unknown tier, never default, refused at AMBER+, no personal identifiers; Tor on a dedicated non-corporate egress (A13) with --mode active and a REF to a legal-approved dark-web procedure naming the analysts; Ahmia banned list and a CSAM keyword filter before every request (any CSAM indicator stops the run, stores nothing and triggers the SaferNet/PF reporting procedure); P145-scrubbed excerpt + SHA-256 only; one audit record per run. Architect: separate v3lum[tor] extra (PySocks only there); verified Tor socks5h, never a clearnet or corporate fallback; reviewed engine allow-list with fixtures and doctor self-tests; only engine result pages fetched (<= 1 MB, <= 3 pages per engine, per-run deadline, no redirects off .onion); <= 300-char snippets; per-request audit; fuzz-tested parsers. Defer members add: the A13 Tor egress profile, an isolated research segment agreed with the SOC, no LLM step, public identifiers (brand, domain) only.
P201.title: Gated Tor search/fetch (Robin-style multi-engine onion search)

P202.rationale: Rejected 0-6. Breach.House is paid, publishes leaked-data samples (*_sample1k.csv with personal fields) and proxies leak-site pages, which conflicts with team rule 3 (metadata only, never leaked file contents); Have I Been Ransomed (DarkEye) is unverified (404) and duplicates the metadata already provided by RansomLook, ransomware.live and ransomfeed. Backlog note: HIBR may be revisited only as metadata-only (group, title, date) with a key if a coverage gap appears.
P202.title: Keyed breach/ransomware trackers (Breach.House, Have I Been Ransomed?)

final_conditions: Ship data/pivot_links/darkweb.json in the frozen P311 pack schema (label, template, entity_types, category, host, verified, checked_at, privacy, publishes=false, touches_target, login_required, antibot), plus the optional per-link max_tlp field that the phase-0 schema must include. The pack is offline data (disclosure 'none'): V3LUM never requests these URLs or any API behind them.

Rendering follows A2/P311: at TLP:AMBER and above every link is non-clickable text with 'opening sends <value> to <host>'; at RED third-party links are hidden from reports and listed only by `v3lum links` with the warning; links are never auto-opened and `links --open` at AMBER+ needs an interactive confirmation naming the host.

CI renders every template with a sample value per declared entity type and with hostile values (quotes, spaces, unicode, newlines): each result must be an https URL on the declared host, built only from whitelisted placeholders through the declared encoder (never str.format, never {raw} in URL position).

Every link host has a provider-registry entry with tier and rationale (A8); unknown-tier hosts get the 'unknown operator' badge and their templates take IOC_TYPES values only (A8 BR4): never PERSONAL_TYPES, CNPJ, company names, keywords, malware or actor names, or other free text (P311 lint).
Initial host tiers for the registry reviewer to confirm: community - ransomlook.io, ransomware.live; unknown - onionsearchengine.com.

Order: P311 groups links by analyst question with verified links first; inside a group the pack's file order is the curated analyst-value order (ransomware group pages first, then onion search); the terminal shows at most 8 links per seed, the rest go to HTML and `v3lum links`.

Verified links carry checked_at; `v3lum doctor --links` (offline) lists unverified links and links not re-checked for more than 180 days. The pack ships in phase 1 with the other pivot packs (A16), whatever the state of the related automated modules.

Group pages: ransomlook.io/group/{slug} and ransomware.live/group/{slug}, with the per-site slug resolved through the P295 alias index (trackers name groups differently, e.g. lockbit3 vs lockbit); when no slug is known the site's search URL is used instead of a guessed path (architect, cti_lead).
Rule 3: claim pages, leak-file, download and victim-file URLs are never linked or generated; the P311 lint rejects such paths.

OnionSearchEngine is unknown tier: its template exists only for IOC values (domain, onion), never for company names, brands or keywords (A8: unknown operators receive IOC_TYPES only), with max_tlp=green so it is hidden from reports at TLP:AMBER+ (cti_lead, redteam_lead).

Onion-search and .onion links carry the warning 'illicit content, possibly child sexual abuse material (possession is a crime, ECA art. 241-B): open only in the team's isolated browsing environment'; .onion addresses render as non-clickable text and nothing is ever auto-fetched (legal_dpo, redteam_lead).
P203.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (osint_investigator voted P1). The architect's slug mapping through P295 prevents 404 links. legal_dpo's floor adds the isolation warning (ECA art. 241-B) and rule 3 (no claim or leak-file URLs). Because OnionSearchEngine is an unknown-tier operator, the A8 floor limits it to IOC values, which is stricter than osint_investigator's 'org brands or typed seeds' and keeps company names away from it; cti_lead and redteam_lead's hiding at AMBER+ is adopted.
P203.title: Pivot links: ransomware group pages + clearnet onion search

final_conditions: Module crypto/chainabuse: GET https://api.chainabuse.com/v0/reports?address= (basic auth with key 'chainabuse', exists) with a page cap; addresses are validated with the core validators (P217) before sending; domains are accepted too.

Licence (legal floor): the Chainabuse Terms of Use (TRM Labs, updated 2025-01-20) license content 'solely for your personal, non-commercial use': terms 'noncommercial'; off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared through a licence_allow entry backed by TRM Labs' written commercial permission.

Reports are user-submitted: wording 'N community reports (unverified): categories, last report <date>'. Kept: category, report count, first/last date and checked/trusted flags; free-text descriptions are masked (PII) and kept as short excerpts only.

Severity: 1 report -> suspicious (low); >= 3 reports or a verified/trusted flag -> fraud (medium); above medium only when corroborated by sanctions (P205), Ransomwhere, GoPlus or exchange labels. Categories -> tags (fraud, ransomware, phishing); one vote in consensus.

Without a key or licence: the manual Chainabuse address-page link (SPA). Success, empty and 401 fixtures are captured with the key (only a no-key body exists). Registry provider trm_chainabuse: tier trusted.
P204.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. The draft's 'key-terms' is replaced by legal_dpo's verified 'noncommercial' (personal, non-commercial use only), so the module is a default candidate that is off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared (A3 BR4). cti_lead's and analyst_ux's report-count severity and corroboration rule, osint_investigator's masking of victims' narratives and the architect's validation and fixtures are kept.
P204.title: Chainabuse scam reports (keyed)

final_conditions: Two modules split by disclosure. crypto_sanctions_offline (disclosure none, TLP:RED-safe): the 0xB10C OFAC sanctioned-address lists (MIT lists over US public-domain OFAC data) via the dataset manager, daily, per chain; matching EVM lowercase, base58 exact, bech32 lowercase; list date/commit kept per match.

crypto_sanctions_onchain (disclosure third_party): the Chainalysis sanctions oracle eth_call isSanctioned(address) (selector 0xdf592f7d), USDT isBlackListed (0xe47d6060) and USDC isBlacklisted (0xfe575a87) on a configurable eth_rpc setting (default PublicNode), plus TronGrid triggerconstantcontract on the USDT-TRC20 contract, all in the first build.

One EVM JSON-RPC helper shared with evm_explorers (P212) and the TronGrid client shared with tron_explorer (P207); ABI encoding unit-tested; per-chain oracle/contract addresses kept in data with their source; checksums through the P217 pure-Python Keccak.

A result other than 0x..00/0x..01, a JSON-RPC error or a timeout -> ERROR (could not verify), never 'not sanctioned'. Chainalysis REST (key 'chainalysis') is a second check covering non-EVM chains; its 403 HTML 'IP not on the Chainalysis Allowed IPs List' -> BLOCKED/NEEDS_KEY.

Labels: an OFAC list or Chainalysis oracle/REST hit -> tag sanctions, critical: 'address on the OFAC SDN list (US)' citing SDN entity, programme and list date, with 'stop transactions and escalate to compliance'; a USDT/USDC issuer blacklist hit -> tag issuer_freeze, high, 'frozen by issuer (Tether/Circle)', never 'sanctioned'.

A list match is not a legal determination: escalate to compliance/legal and take no automated adverse action against natural persons (LGPD art. 20). Stale lists are flagged; misses read 'not on OFAC lists as of <date>', never 'not sanctioned' (rule 5). GoPlus 'sanctioned' flags are not authoritative: the sanctions tag comes only from this module.

Terms: OFAC lists 'open'; oracle and stablecoin calls 'open' (public contracts, RPC provider ToS recorded); TronGrid and Chainalysis REST 'key-terms' (company accounts, plans recorded). Registry tiers: Chainalysis, PublicNode (Allnodes) and TronGrid (TRON DAO) trusted.
P205.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. The architect's floor splits offline lists and RPC calls so the offline part stays TLP:RED-safe and RPC errors never read as 'not sanctioned'; osint_investigator puts the TRON USDT freeze check in the first build; cti_lead, legal_dpo and analyst_ux separate sanctions from issuer freezes and forbid automated adverse action. Chair-file terms and tier describe the most restrictive source and the lowest tier across both modules.
P205.title: Crypto sanctions (OFAC address lists, Chainalysis oracle + REST, USDT/USDC on-chain blacklists)

final_conditions: Module crypto/goplus_security: GoPlus api.gopluslabs.io address_security/{addr}?chain_id= and token_security (keyed by lowercase contract) for EVM/TRON addresses; phishing_site only for URLs/domains with crypto context in the case (wallet, token or drainer tags), never for every URL; Honeypot.is only for token contracts (404 'No pairs found' = not applicable, no row).
GET lookups only; no report or submission endpoints. URLs sent to phishing_site are stripped of query strings, fragments and userinfo (victims' e-mails, tokens) unless the analyst opts in per URL.

Responses {'code':1,'message':'ok','result':{...}}: code != 1 -> ERROR via P321; string flags '0'/'1' are cast to bool. Each flag maps to a named finding with its data_source; specific flags (phishing_activities, stealing_attack, cybercrime, money_laundering, blackmail_activities) -> tags; doubt-type flags (e.g. blacklist_doubt) are low.
GoPlus 'sanctioned' is not authoritative: the sanctions tag comes only from P205. One vote in consensus.

Terms (legal floor): GoPlus and Honeypot.is terms could not be verified (docs JS-only, 2026-11-26): class 'key-terms'; under corporate only after legal records the terms (free_plan_business_use) or a company key plan; optional key 'goplus' (app key/secret) from a company account. Honeypot.is is queried only if its registry review records tier community or higher.
Registry: GoPlus Security tier community; Honeypot.is per its review. Fixtures: address_security, token_security, phishing_site and the Honeypot.is 404.
P206.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. legal_dpo's floor applies the key-terms rule (terms unverified) and strips victims' data from URLs; redteam_lead limits phishing_site to crypto contexts so ordinary CSIRT URLs are not sent to a Web3 vendor; cti_lead keeps GoPlus 'sanctioned' non-authoritative; analyst_ux's named flags and the architect's string/code semantics are kept.
P206.title: GoPlus address/token security + Honeypot.is

final_conditions: Module crypto/tron_explorer: TronGrid api.trongrid.io/v1/accounts/{addr} and /v1/accounts/{addr}/transactions/trc20 (limit 50, <= 2 pages, newest first, pagination via meta.fingerprint); key 'trongrid' sent as the TRON-PRO-API-KEY header (never in the query); keyless works but is throttled.

The address is validated with the core base58check validator (T prefix, version byte 0x41, P217) before any call. Amounts are converted from sun/decimals with Decimal and shown with units; {'success': false} bodies -> ERROR via P321; throttling = RATE_LIMITED (could not verify).

Summary: TRX/USDT balances, first/last activity, tx count and the top 5 counterparties by USDT value with labels (P358); counterparties are transacted_with pivots with expand=False (expansion is decided by P213).
Tronscan (apilist.tronscanapi.com) only with key 'tronscan' (401 without); without that key there is no Tronscan row (labels come from P358).

Key-terms: keys from a company/team account on a plan whose terms permit internal business use, recorded by legal (key_plans) before corporate use; never personal free accounts (rule 1). Registry: TronGrid/Tronscan (TRON DAO) tier trusted. Fixtures: account, TRC20 page, invalid address, throttled answer.
P207.rationale: Approved 6-0. The median is P2 on a 3-3 tie (cti_lead, osint_investigator and the architect voted P1); the chair raises it to P1 because USDT-TRC20 is the dominant cash-out rail in Brazilian PIX-to-crypto fraud (noted by five members), P205 (P1) needs the same TronGrid client for its first-build freeze check and P217 makes TRON a day-one chain; effort S. legal_dpo's key-terms rule, the architect's validation and pagination bounds and analyst_ux's summary output are consolidated.
P207.title: TRON (TronGrid, Tronscan)

final_conditions: Module crypto/walletexplorer: GET walletexplorer.com/api/1/address-lookup?address={a}&caller={caller_id} at ~1 req/s. caller comes from the shared operator-identifier setting caller_id (default: the P326 role mailbox contact_email), a generic team identifier, never an analyst's name, personal e-mail, case id or investigated value; unset = SKIPPED reason_code 'config'.

found:false -> EMPTY. Labels are shown as 'WalletExplorer label (name database not updated since 2016, per its info page)' with attribution; a label is a lead for a legal request to that service, not proof of ownership.

Service labels (exchange, mixer, service) become stop-node tags for graph expansion (P213), and the finding names the exchange to which a legal request can be sent. updated_to_block is compared with the chain tip from btc_explorers to show data lag. Registry provider walletexplorer: tier community, terms open.
P208.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. The provider asks callers to identify (rule 6): osint_investigator, redteam_lead, legal_dpo and the architect require a configurable role identifier that reveals neither analyst nor case; legal_dpo's stale-database wording (LGPD accuracy) is adopted.
P208.title: WalletExplorer (Bitcoin wallet clustering + service labels)

final_conditions: Module crypto/ens_resolver: api.ensdata.net/{name}.eth or /{address}; 404 'no reverse record' = EMPTY (no name), never an absent wallet.

Text records (twitter, github, url, email) are self-asserted by the ENS owner: POSSIBLE, labelled 'self-asserted by the ENS owner'; PROBABLE only when the linked profile points back to the ENS name or wallet (found by another module in the case).

URL, domain and e-mail pivots from text records are attacker-controllable: passive modules only, never LIGHT/ACTIVE contact, rendered defanged, expand=False for personal identifiers. Registry provider ensdata: tier community, terms open. Fixtures: name, address and 404.
P209.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. cti_lead, legal_dpo and the architect accepted PROBABLE as drafted, while osint_investigator and analyst_ux showed that anyone can write any handle into a text record; osint_investigator's rule (POSSIBLE unless the profile links back) reconciles both. redteam_lead's passive-only rule is kept.
P209.title: ENS resolution (ensdata.net)

final_conditions: Offline module crypto/ransomwhere (disclosure none): api.ransomwhe.re/export registered with the dataset manager (live check: ~5.6 MB JSON, 11,186 BTC addresses, last update 2024-10-29), refreshed weekly by `v3lum data update` (above 5 MB, never mid-scan) and loaded into a dict at refresh.

A match gives ransomware family and payment amounts, with attributed_to pivots expand=False. Findings are labelled historical (dataset stale since 2024-10, crowdsourced and skewed to older families); a miss means nothing.
Citation of the Ransomwhere Zenodo dataset in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES. A trimmed fixture is cut from the export (none exists).
P210.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3 with the architect's staleness labelling and legal_dpo's citation requirement. Offline: tier 'n/a', terms 'open'.
P210.title: Ransomwhere ransomware payment addresses

final_conditions: Module crypto/btc_explorers: one Esplora parser for Blockstream, mempool.space and litecoinspace.org (balance = funded_txo_sum - spent_txo_sum, in sats); a configured self-hosted esplora_url is always tried first. With one disclosure class per module (A8 BR7), the self-hosted path is also a class btc_esplora_internal (disclosure 'internal', no public failover) for TLP:AMBER+ and RED cases.

Fallbacks in this build: Blockchain.com rawaddr/multiaddr (%7C separators) and BlockCypher (LTC/DOGE/DASH; optional token 'blockcypher', sent only after AR01 redaction). Bitaps and SoChain are dropped (value 2). Blockchair only with a commercial key 'blockchair' (keyless use is personal/non-commercial, and our egress got HTTP 430 on the second call).

Failover is sequential and only on error, never a fan-out of the same address to every provider: the first successful provider wins; total explorer time <= 15 s per address; the answering provider, failover order and per-provider status are recorded. Without a self-hosted URL the report lists which public explorers received the address.

Per-host P334 buckets; 429/430 -> RATE_LIMITED and that host is short-circuited for the run, never empty. Addresses are validated with the core validators (P217) to choose chain and provider; transaction pagination <= 2 pages.

Summary: balance, tx count, first/last activity and data freshness; the top 10 counterparties by value become transacted_with pivots with expand=False (only P213 decides expansion), labelled 'counterparty (role unknown)'; uninvolved counterparties' balances and histories are not kept beyond the case.

Per-adapter terms recorded: Esplora, mempool, litecoinspace and Blockchain.com 'open'; BlockCypher and Blockchair 'key-terms'. Registry tiers: Blockstream, Blockchain.com, BlockCypher and Blockchair trusted; mempool.space and litecoinspace community.
P211.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (the architect voted P1). The architect's floor trims seven providers to one Esplora parser plus two fallbacks; cti_lead, redteam_lead and analyst_ux require sequential failover so only one operator sees each address and a self-hosted Esplora first; legal_dpo requires Blockchair's commercial key and minimises counterparties; osint_investigator leaves expansion to P213.
P211.title: Bitcoin/Litecoin explorers with failover (Esplora, mempool.space/litecoinspace, Blockchain.com, BlockCypher, Blockchair, Bitaps, SoChain)

final_conditions: Module crypto/evm_explorers: Blockscout v2 (eth.blockscout.com; keyless; is_scam flag, public tags, ENS, /search?q= for name.eth) first; Etherscan V2 (chainid parameter) only with key 'etherscan' (exists); Ethplorer only with the team's own key 'ethplorer', never the shared 'freekey' test key; OKLink only with key 'oklink' and a success fixture.

PublicNode or the configured eth_rpc through the EVM JSON-RPC helper shared with crypto_sanctions (P205) for balance and code (contract vs EOA). EIP-55 through the P217 pure-Python Keccak-256 with test vectors (hashlib.sha3_256 is not Keccak).
