Etherscan HTTP 200 with status '0' (e.g. 'NOTOK', 'Missing/Invalid API Key') -> ERROR or RATE_LIMITED via P321 markers (rule 5), never empty. Keys in query strings only after AR01 redaction; per-provider status and P334 buckets.

First successful provider wins, total <= 15 s per address. Summary: balance, top 5 token holdings, tx count, first/last, contract vs EOA; Blockscout is_scam/public tags become findings naming the source (suspicious/fraud); counterparties expand=False (P213 decides expansion); a contract's creatorAddress becomes an eth_address pivot with expand=False.

Per-adapter classes (A1 BR3): Blockscout keyless and PublicNode RPC 'open' (free public APIs, terms recorded, as in P205 and P211); Etherscan, Ethplorer and OKLink 'key-terms' (company keys on recorded plans). Etherscan's terms page sits behind a Cloudflare challenge (rule 1), so legal records it by another channel. Tiers: Etherscan, OKLink, PublicNode trusted; Blockscout, Ethplorer community.
P212.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. legal_dpo's floor replaces the shared Ethplorer 'freekey' (which the architect would have used) with the team's own key and records each adapter's terms; the architect shares the RPC helper and Keccak with P205; cti_lead's and osint_investigator's error-in-200 and EIP-55 points and analyst_ux's failover summary are kept.
P212.title: EVM explorers (Blockscout v2, Etherscan v2 multichain, Ethplorer, PublicNode RPC, OKLink)

final_conditions: Not a module with its own BFS: an engine policy on transacted_with pivots (core expansion rules, AR07) with depth 1 by default, 2 only with an explicit flag (--crypto-depth 2), top-N counterparties ranked by value/frequency by the explorer modules and a per-case crypto request budget (setting crypto_case_budget). No new hosts. Opt-in: setting crypto_expand=false by default.

Stop-nodes are never expanded: labelled exchanges, mixers, bridges and pools (crypto_address_labels P358, walletexplorer P208, Blockscout tags), sanctioned addresses (P205) and high-degree addresses (> 1,000 counterparties).

Direction: expansion follows outgoing flows (cash-out toward exchanges). Addresses that only sent funds into an investigated address are labelled 'possible victim', counted, never expanded and not listed by default.
Counterparties outside the analyst's selection stay expand=False, labelled 'counterparty (role unknown)', and are never scored malicious by association alone (P302 caps transferred risk).

Output: a 'where the money went' summary (labelled endpoints reached, hop count, amounts, time window) that highlights the first labelled exchange (the legal-request target), plus a JSON/GraphML export; never a list of hundreds of addresses. Orbit (GPL-3.0) is used for ideas only (A6).
P213.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. The architect's floor makes it an engine policy rather than a second BFS that would bypass the guard rails. osint_investigator's victim-protection rule (incoming senders are possible victims, never expanded), cti_lead's and redteam_lead's stop-nodes, legal_dpo's no guilt by association and analyst_ux's summary output are consolidated. An engine policy, not a data source: tier and terms 'n/a'.
P213.title: Transaction-graph expansion with stop-nodes (Orbit-style BFS)

final_conditions: Module crypto/ton_explorer: Toncenter v3 at 1 rps keyless (key 'toncenter' as X-API-Key header raises it to 10 rps); user-friendly TON address decoding (base64url, 36 bytes, CRC16-XMODEM) in core validators with tests. default_enabled False (opt-in).

phone input applies() only to +888 anonymous numbers and username input only to collectible Telegram usernames, already in the case as fraud/threat subjects with the purpose recorded; never ordinary phone numbers, never enumeration of number or username ranges, never auto-expanded.

+888 number or collectible username -> NFT -> current owner wallet (a_TON_of_privacy flow, MIT attribution), reported as 'current NFT owner wallet of the collectible number/username (ownership can change; transfer date shown)': a PROBABLE lead with expand=False, never identity proof.

On-chain resolution through Toncenter only; tonapi.io and getgems.io receive identifiers only after legal records their terms and tier (A8). Fixtures for the address and NFT endpoints are captured before merge (only the chain endpoint was exercised). Registry provider toncenter: tier community, terms open.
P214.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. legal_dpo's floor restricts this de-anonymising lookup to +888 numbers and collectible usernames of case subjects with a purpose and holds tonapi/getgems until reviewed; cti_lead, osint_investigator, redteam_lead and analyst_ux keep the owner wallet a dated lead; the architect requires the validator and fixtures.
P214.title: TON (Toncenter + Telegram +888 / collectible username owner lookup)

final_conditions: Module crypto/solana_rpc: getBalance and getSignaturesForAddress (limit <= 25) on a configurable Solana RPC (default api.mainnet-beta.solana.com); public RPC limits (~100 req/10 s per IP, 40 req/10 s per method) through P334; default_enabled False.

Runs only on explicitly typed Solana inputs (sol: prefix, TYPE override or analyst confirmation) or pivots from a Solana-specific source; a bare base58 string is never auto-detected as a Solana address (no checksum: arbitrary tokens would be sent to the RPC).
Output: balance and recent signatures only. Registry provider solana_foundation: tier trusted, terms open (public RPC, best effort, no SLA).
P215.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. Every member restricts it to explicit inputs because base58 without a checksum would send random tokens to a public RPC (P217 keeps Solana low-confidence).
P215.title: Solana public JSON-RPC

final_conditions: Ship data/pivot_links/crypto.json in the frozen P311 pack schema (label, template, entity_types, category, host, verified, checked_at, privacy, publishes=false, touches_target, login_required, antibot). The pack is offline data (disclosure 'none'): V3LUM never requests these URLs or any API behind them.

Rendering follows A2/P311: at TLP:AMBER and above every link is non-clickable text with 'opening sends <value> to <host>'; at RED third-party links are hidden from reports and listed only by `v3lum links` with the warning; links are never auto-opened and `links --open` at AMBER+ needs an interactive confirmation naming the host.

CI renders every template with a sample value per declared entity type and with hostile values (quotes, spaces, unicode, newlines): each result must be an https URL on the declared host, built only from whitelisted placeholders through the declared encoder (never str.format, never {raw} in URL position).

Every link host has a provider-registry entry with tier and rationale (A8); unknown-tier hosts get the 'unknown operator' badge and their templates take IOC_TYPES values only (A8 BR4): never PERSONAL_TYPES, CNPJ, company names, keywords, malware or actor names, or other free text (P311 lint).
Initial host tiers for the registry reviewer to confirm: trusted - Blockchain.com, Blockchair; community - mempool.space, WalletExplorer, BitcoinWhosWho, Ethplorer; unknown - bitref.com.

Order: P311 groups links by analyst question with verified links first; inside a group the pack's file order is the curated analyst-value order (BTC: mempool.space, Blockchair, WalletExplorer, BitcoinWhosWho, Blockchain.com, bitref; EVM: Ethplorer, Blockchair); the terminal shows at most 8 links per seed, the rest go to HTML and `v3lum links`.

Verified links carry checked_at; `v3lum doctor --links` (offline) lists unverified links and links not re-checked for more than 180 days. The pack ships in phase 1 with the other pivot packs (A16), whatever the state of the related automated modules.

Chain-aware templates: each entry declares the address formats it accepts, checked with the P217 validators (BTC base58/bech32, LTC, EVM 0x, TRON T-base58), so analysts never land on 'invalid address' pages. EVM addresses are normalised (lowercase for matching, checksum for display) exactly as P219's OFAC matching does.

Etherscan, BscScan, Tronscan and Arkham return Cloudflare/JS shells to automated clients: they are not dropped but shipped in the unverified pack (P304) with antibot=true and the badge 'opens in browser; may require challenge' (TRON USDT and EVM stablecoins dominate Brazilian scams). Arkham is kept only if its address page renders without login (otherwise the P311 lint drops it).
BitcoinWhosWho report pages are included here and Chainabuse address reports (an SPA) in P304; no wallet-connect, payment, swap or donation page is ever linked.
P216.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (osint_investigator voted P1, redteam_lead P3). cti_lead and osint_investigator asked for chain-aware templates and for keeping the Cloudflare-fronted explorers analysts actually use as unverified browser links (P304) rather than dropping them; the architect agreed. Address normalisation follows P219 (osint_investigator). Crypto addresses are IOC values, so the unknown-tier bitref link only needs the badge.
P216.title: Pivot links: blockchain explorers (multi-explorer set, BitcoinWhosWho, WalletExplorer, Blockchain.com, Blockchair, Ethplorer)

final_conditions: Stdlib-only validators in core/validators.py, ported from the research prototype (all test vectors pass): onion v3 checksum (SHA3-256); BTC/LTC/DOGE/DASH/TRON base58check version bytes; bech32 vs bech32m by witness version; EIP-55 with a pure-python Keccak-256 (hashlib.sha3_256 is NOT Keccak); Monero block-base58 + Keccak checksum; the XRP alphabet.
Solana addresses stay low-confidence (no checksum). MD5-looking strings are never typed as BTC without a passing checksum.
TRON base58check is supported from day one, because USDT on TRON is a common payment rail in Brazilian scams. The validated chain selects the right explorer and pivot links.
The validators are offline (disclosure 'none') and add no dependency. Each format has positive and negative test vectors, and the existing detect tests pass unchanged.
P172 extraction and P333 typing use these validators. A failing checksum means the value is not typed, or gets low confidence when the context (TYPE:value prefix) is explicit.
P217.rationale: Approved 6-0 with no conditions from any member; the median is P2 (osint_investigator, legal_dpo and the architect voted P1). Offline, stdlib-only and already passing its vectors; osint_investigator stressed TRON for Brazilian fraud. The conditions restate the synthesizer's spec so it stands alone. Auditor: priority raised from the median P2 (a 3-3 tie) to P1 because P172 (P1) depends on these validators in phase 1 (A16 BR4); osint_investigator, legal_dpo and the architect voted P1 and the effort is S.
P217.title: Checksum validators for crypto addresses and onion v3

final_conditions: Requires key 'networksdb' in config.KNOWN_KEYS (V3LUM_NETWORKSDB_KEY as alias), sent only in the X-Api-Key header, never as the apikey query parameter. Missing key ({'error':'required header X-Api-Key ...'}) gives NEEDS_KEY.
Key-terms: a company/team account on a plan whose terms permit internal business use, recorded by legal before it runs under corporate. Monthly quota through the P334 block.
Organisation search is fuzzy: ranges are candidates (expand=False, confidence <= 0.4) until rdap (P003) or nicbr_asn (P038) confirms them; they never form an ACTIVE scope by themselves.
The corptrace (AGPL) flow is re-implemented; no code is copied. Merge only with a trimmed real success fixture (only the missing-key error exists).
P218.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. legal_dpo's floor: key-terms and the AGPL re-implementation. The architect's floor: header key, candidate-only pivots with low confidence, a real fixture. cti_lead, redteam_lead and analyst_ux: ranges stay candidates until RDAP/NIC.br confirm. Opt-in as drafted. NetworksDB is a small identifiable operator: tier community.
P218.title: NetworksDB.io organisation -> IP ranges (keyed)

final_conditions: Sources: OFAC SDN CSV from the Sanctions List Service (US government work, public domain), UN consolidated XML (UN public information) and EU FSF CSV (EU open data, reuse with attribution; the Commission's public token is a config value). Legal floor: api/data.opensanctions.org are removed from this module (CC BY-NC data belongs to P222 only).
Providers (dataset downloads, no value sent): OFAC/US Treasury, UN Security Council and the European Commission, all trusted tier.

Datasets only through the dataset manager (`v3lum data update sanctions`; TTL 24 h for OFAC and UN, 3 days for EU FSF ~25.5 MB), each validated (format and minimum rows) before replacing the previous copy, with source date, fetched_at and sha256 recorded. Scans never download them (A6: > 5 MB).

Matching is local (disclosure 'none', allowed at TLP:RED). A missing list gives UNAVAILABLE reason_code 'dataset' ('run v3lum data update sanctions'); a list fetched more than 7 days ago gives 'could not screen against <list> (dated <date>)' in coverage. Neither case ever reads 'no match'.

Parsing: UN XML through the core safe XML helper, built with this P1 item if absent and shared by every XML parser (DOCTYPE and entity declarations rejected, size caps); EU FSF is ';'-separated with a BOM; OFAC 'Digital Currency Address' remarks are indexed per chain.

One shared matcher, core/namematch.py: NFKD accent strip, casefold, legal-suffix removal (LTDA, S.A., EIRELI, ME, EPP, LLC, LTD...), a token blocking index built once per list version, deterministic token-set Jaro-Winkler in pure Python (rapidfuzz only as an optional accelerator with identical scores, both paths tested). P240, P244, P254 and P221 reuse it.

Wallets: exact match of normalised addresses (base58/bech32 as-is, EVM and TRON normalised) against OFAC remarks gives a CRITICAL 'sanctioned wallet' finding, confidence CONFIRMED, with programme (e.g. CYBER2, DPRK3), SDN uid and list date. 'Sanctioned' is used only for exact identifier matches (wallet, IMO, registration number, CNPJ).

Names: score >= 0.90 (named constant) gives 'possible match - confirm identity', confidence POSSIBLE (<= 0.6), severity at most MEDIUM unless a second identifier also matches (DOB, nationality, document, address, wallet, IMO); never CRITICAL.
Person hits are lowered by the P252 homonym score and common-name hits stay INFO. At most 5 candidates per list, each with list, programme, listing date, matched alias and score.

Legal floor: person names are screened only for subjects the analyst entered in a due-diligence case with a recorded purpose, or QSA partners of a CNPJ under that due diligence when the analyst enables the due-diligence option; never names from pivots or free text (reason_code 'privacy' otherwise). No 'sanctioned' verdict on a natural person without analyst confirmation.

threat_actor inputs resolve through the P295 alias index and match SDN/UN names: a designated actor's card shows 'OFAC/UN designated (<date>) - payments may be prohibited, escalate to legal'. Company names of the case's companies and wallets from any source are screened.

Only matched entries are kept in the case (A10). The previous list version is kept so delistings show as 'formerly listed (<date>)'. Reports carry the UN/EU attribution line and each list's publication date.

Performance and tests: < 300 ms per name on a synthetic 50k-alias list (benchmark test). Fixtures: an SDN row with a digital-currency remark, an EU FSF row (';' + BOM), a UN XML entry, a common-name non-match; tests for the wallet exact hit, fuzzy hit, homonym downgrade and stale-list message.
P219.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1 (redteam_lead voted P2). Offline screening discloses nothing and answers the ransomware-payment question for OFAC wallets. legal_dpo's floor removes the CC BY-NC OpenSanctions hosts and purpose-gates person names with no 'sanctioned' label on people. The architect's floor: dataset manager only, never 'no match' on a missing or stale list, a safe XML parser and one shared pure-Python matcher with a benchmark. Severity follows analyst_ux and the architect (CRITICAL only for exact wallet matches, consistent with AR08), and cti_lead's second-identifier cap, osint_investigator's scope and the delisting history are kept. It stays default-on as an offline module (A3), with person-name screening gated by purpose.
P219.title: Sanctions name screening offline (OFAC SDN, UN consolidated, EU FSF)

final_conditions: One GLEIF client in a shared helper used by this module and by P361; no second client. Host api.gleif.org, keyless, CC0 (attribution courtesy line), documented 60 req/min: min_interval 1 s and a registry quota.
The registeredAs filter always sends the formatted CNPJ (entities.display_value, e.g. 00.000.000/0001-91); raw digits are never sent because they return 0 hits. Fixtures cover both forms.
Bounded: JSON:API page size <= 10 and at most 4 requests per entity (record, direct parent, ultimate parent, first page of children); children capped at 10.

Default scans use only CNPJ and exact company_name inputs. fuzzycompletions/fulltext (keyword) runs only when the module is selected explicitly, and its hits are hypotheses (expand=False, confidence <= 0.5).

Exact CNPJ/LEI matches pivot with relation partner/company_of; parents and children beyond one level are expand=False so a conglomerate cannot flood the graph. Results are ownership hints, never scope: they may be proposed by `v3lum org seed` for analyst confirmation but never extend org_profile or an ACTIVE scope by themselves.

Attributes: LEI, legal name, registration status (ISSUED/LAPSED/RETIRED), last update, direct and ultimate parent, shown on one line. No record is INFO 'no LEI' (most Brazilian SMEs have none), never a risk signal.

Rule 5: 401/403/429, timeouts, 5xx and error-in-200 bodies mean could not verify (P321/P328 statuses: BLOCKED, RATE_LIMITED, QUOTA, ERROR), never EMPTY or 'not found'; such responses are never cached. 404 is a declared meaningful absent status (absent_statuses {404}).

Merge gate (A16): offline tests with FakeHttp (unmatched requests fail, network guard active) over trimmed real fixtures without personal data (the 7 trimmed GLEIF captures), a provider-registry entry for every host, the registry contract test and the P327 lint.
P220.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. CC0 legal-entity data with no legal objection (legal_dpo). The architect's conditions (one shared client with P361, formatted CNPJ only, request caps, fuzzy hits as hypotheses) and analyst_ux's one-line output with no fuzzy keyword noise in default scans are adopted. cti_lead's expansion limit and 'no LEI is not a risk signal' and redteam_lead's 'ownership hints, never scope' complete the spec.
P220.title: GLEIF LEI API

final_conditions: Legal floor (rule 4, chair's reading): ICIJ Offshore Leaks is a leak-derived database, so person-name search in it is people-search over leaked data. The module searches entities only: company_name values (analyst-typed company names, razao social and nome fantasia resolved from a CNPJ, PJ partners); 'person_name' is removed from accepts.
Officers and intermediaries appear only as nodes linked to a matched entity; natural persons' addresses are never displayed, and linked persons are never pivoted or expanded.

Local first: the bulk CSV (ODbL database + CC BY-SA contents, several hundred MB) is imported into SQLite only by `v3lum data update icij` through the dataset manager, never bundled (A6) and never downloaded during a scan. Matching is local (no disclosure) with the shared core/namematch.py matcher (score >= 0.90, at most 5 candidates).

Without the local index the reconcile API (offshoreleaks.icij.org, one POST per entity, <= 5 candidates) is used only at TLP:CLEAR/GREEN or when the analyst selects the module explicitly; otherwise the result is UNAVAILABLE reason_code 'dataset' ('run v3lum data update icij'), never 'no match'.
Opt-in (default_enabled=False): runs on -M icij_offshore or --preset deep, only on seeds and CNPJ-resolved names, never on pivoted partner names (cti_lead).

Findings are POSSIBLE matches at INFO/LOW only, never tagged malicious, never risk-scored above LOW, expand=False, showing node id, leak (Panama/Paradise/Pandora...), jurisdiction, intermediary, dates and a manual node link, worded 'appears in ICIJ Offshore Leaks - not evidence of wrongdoing' plus ICIJ's own disclaimer.
No leaked document text is stored. The web search page (202 + JS challenge) is never fetched (rule 1). ODbL/CC BY-SA attribution goes into the report footer and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.

Rule 5: 401/403/429, timeouts, 5xx and error-in-200 bodies mean could not verify (P321/P328 statuses: BLOCKED, RATE_LIMITED, QUOTA, ERROR), never EMPTY or 'not found'; such responses are never cached.

Merge gate (A16): offline tests with FakeHttp (unmatched requests fail, network guard active) over trimmed real fixtures without personal data (the captured reconcile response plus a no-candidate response and a trimmed bulk-CSV sample), a provider-registry entry for every host, the registry contract test and the P327 lint.
P221.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. legal_dpo's floor limits it to entity search and asked the chair to confirm rule 4's scope: the chair confirms that a person-name search over a leak-derived database is people-search over leaked data (rule 4), so person names are removed, which is stricter than the person-by-flag designs of osint_investigator, cti_lead and analyst_ux. Local-first matching (cti_lead, osint_investigator, legal_dpo, analyst_ux) is combined with the architect's dataset-manager rule for the large share-alike bulk and his reconcile fallback, which runs only at CLEAR/GREEN or on explicit request. cti_lead's opt-in default and analyst_ux's wording keep juniors from reading presence as guilt. ODbL/CC BY-SA are met by runtime download and attribution, so terms are open (A1).
P221.title: ICIJ Offshore Leaks (reconcile API + bulk CSV)

final_conditions: Licence (A1): OpenSanctions data is CC BY-NC 4.0 (class 'noncommercial'); this module uses only the business-licensed path, registered as class 'license'. The free data and API path is never used under corporate.

It runs only when the company holds an OpenSanctions commercial licence (in-house Screening licence or bulk data licence) recorded in the provider registry and licence_allow; otherwise it is skipped under the corporate profile with reason_code 'licence'.

Preferred path with a bulk data licence: the licensed targets dataset through the dataset manager (`v3lum data update opensanctions`, never mid-scan) matched locally with the P219 core/namematch.py matcher (disclosure 'none'). Bulk datasets are never downloaded without that licence.

With only a Screening API licence: the /match API with requires_keys=('opensanctions',), key only in the Authorization header (never in URLs), a monthly query budget in config with a hard stop and QUOTA status, and no automatic credit purchase. 401 without a key -> NEEDS_KEY.

default_enabled=False. It runs after the offline lists (P219, P240) in an explicit due-diligence run, on seed companies and persons and on QSA partners of a CNPJ under that due diligence; never automatically on every QSA partner, from pivots or from names extracted from text.

Legal floor: person-name matching only for subjects the analyst entered in a due-diligence case with a recorded purpose (reason_code 'privacy' otherwise). Results are 'possible match' with score, threshold, dataset and entity id, lowered by the P252 homonym score; PEP hits are INFO context; no 'sanctioned' label on a natural person without analyst confirmation.
Crypto addresses (other_crypto_address) are matched exactly after the P219 normalisation. The opensanctions.org website stays a manual link in P231 (their FAQ: free to use in a browser).

Rule 5: 401/403/429, timeouts, 5xx and error-in-200 bodies mean could not verify (P321/P328 statuses: BLOCKED, RATE_LIMITED, QUOTA, ERROR), never EMPTY or 'not found'; such responses are never cached.

Merge gate (A16): offline tests with FakeHttp (unmatched requests fail, network guard active) over trimmed real fixtures without personal data (the captured bulk index and the 401 no-key response; a success fixture captured with the licensed key before enabling), a provider-registry entry for every host, the registry contract test and the P327 lint.
P222.rationale: Approved 4-0-2 at median P3 (cti_lead and analyst_ux deferred until a licence exists). legal_dpo and the architect set the floor: a recorded commercial licence or nothing, licensed bulk data matched locally preferred over the API, the key never in URLs, person matching purpose-gated. osint_investigator's licensed Screening API path is kept as the alternative when only that licence is bought, with a hard budget. The binding A1 classes apply: free data 'noncommercial', the business-licence source 'license'.
P222.title: OpenSanctions (API + bulk datasets)

final_conditions: Identifying UA (P326): 'V3LUM <contact_email>' built from the contact_email setting (a team role mailbox, never a personal address), used only in the sec.gov, data.sec.gov and efts.sec.gov host profiles as the SEC fair-access policy requires. Without contact_email the module is SKIPPED reason_code 'config' ('needs contact UA'); no made-up contact.
Rate: <= 2 req/s (min_interval 0.5 s, well below SEC's 10 req/s cap) with backoff on 403/429. A 403 caused by the UA is BLOCKED with the UA hint, never 'no filings' (rule 5).
company_tickers.json is a daily dataset (dataset manager) matched locally, so the company name is not disclosed for that step; CIK is padded to 10 digits for submissions.

Full-text search (efts.sec.gov) only for the counterparty name, first page only (<= 10 hits per entity), restricted to 8-K/8-K/A filings with Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incident) and 6-K mentions for foreign issuers.

Output: the company's CIK/ticker and cyber-incident disclosures (form, date, company, filing URL) as INFO/LOW supplier-incident context. Name-to-company matches are POSSIBLE unless CIK or ticker matches. Filing metadata and links only, no filing bodies stored.
Opt-in (default_enabled=False); inputs company_name (keyword only when selected explicitly). US government work, public domain.

Merge gate (A16): offline tests with FakeHttp (unmatched requests fail, network guard active) over trimmed real fixtures without personal data (the captured EFTS full-text search and submissions responses plus a 403 sample), a provider-registry entry for every host, the registry contract test and the P327 lint.
P223.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3 (US-listed suppliers are infrequent for this team). Every member asked for the SEC-required identifying UA with a role mailbox, which P326 scopes to SEC hosts; the architect's config skip, local ticker matching and first-page cap are adopted. The rate is cti_lead's and osint_investigator's 2 req/s, stricter than legal_dpo's 10. analyst_ux limited the output to the one question that matters: did the supplier disclose a material cyber incident.
P223.title: SEC EDGAR (company tickers, submissions, full-text search)

final_conditions: One Wikidata client shared with P361. Identifying UA with the contact_email role mailbox only on www.wikidata.org (wbsearchentities/wbgetentities/wbgetclaims API) and query.wikidata.org (Wikimedia UA policy; a UA without contact got 429); SKIPPED reason_code 'config' ('needs contact UA') when contact_email is unset.

Rate: min_interval >= 1 s; 429 -> RATE_LIMITED (rule 5). Requests: wbsearchentities plus wbgetentities/wbgetclaims for P6204 (CNPJ), P856 (official website), P749 (parent) and P355 (subsidiary); free-form SPARQL is never sent: any SPARQL is a fixed template with LIMIT <= 20 and a 20 s timeout.

Default scans: company_name and domain inputs, organisation items only (instance/subclass of business or organization), accepted only on an exact label/alias match or a P6204 CNPJ match; a P6204 exact match is the only automatic company link.
Person items only for public figures the analyst typed as seeds and only when the module is selected explicitly; never in default scans or from pivots (legal_dpo, architect).

P856 official website becomes a domain pivot (company_of) at confidence <= 0.7, labelled 'official site per Wikidata (community-edited)'. It never sets known_good and never drives own-asset or typosquat suppression without registry evidence (RDAP, BCB DominiosVerificados); it is called 'official' only when RDAP or CNPJ data agree.
Parent/subsidiary (P749/P355) become company_of pivots at depth 1 only. Coverage is small (~2,900 items carry a CNPJ), so no item is no signal. One-line output. CC0.

Merge gate (A16): offline tests with FakeHttp (unmatched requests fail, network guard active) over trimmed real fixtures without personal data (the captured wbsearchentities and SPARQL responses and a 429 sample), a provider-registry entry for every host, the registry contract test and the P327 lint.
P224.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3 (osint_investigator, legal_dpo and analyst_ux voted P2). The architect's floor: one client shared with P361, fixed queries instead of free SPARQL, the identifying UA from config and 1 req/s. cti_lead and osint_investigator warned that crowd-edited claims must never whitelist a domain, so P856 stays a 0.7 hint. legal_dpo and the architect keep people out of automatic runs. It stays default-on for organisations (trusted provider, CC0, bounded requests).
P224.title: Wikidata (wbsearchentities + SPARQL)

final_conditions: Needs the eu_vat entity type (P333, may slip to P3): detected only with a 2-letter EU country prefix plus that country's national pattern/checksum, or an explicit eu_vat: prefix; never inferred from bare digits. Collision tests against CNPJ, phone and hash inputs.
Official VIES REST only (ec.europa.eu .../ms/{CC}/vat/{number}). VATComply is dropped: it wraps the same service and its terms are unknown (A1 unknown terms never run; architect).

Tri-state: valid; invalid only when VIES answers isValid=false without a userError; userError values such as MS_UNAVAILABLE, MS_MAX_CONCURRENT_REQ or TIMEOUT inside a 200 body, timeouts and HTTP errors -> UNAVAILABLE/RATE_LIMITED/ERROR (could not verify), never 'invalid'.

Single lookups for seeds only; no bulk validation. The returned name becomes a company_name pivot (expand=False) only when it carries a legal-entity form (S.A., SARL, GmbH, BV, Ltd...); a VAT number that may belong to a sole trader is personal data, so it is never pivoted and its address is not displayed (legal_dpo).
Opt-in (default_enabled=False). Official EC service, free; tier trusted.

Merge gate (A16): offline tests with FakeHttp (unmatched requests fail, network guard active) over trimmed real fixtures without personal data (the captured valid VIES response plus a synthetic MS_UNAVAILABLE body), a provider-registry entry for every host, the registry contract test and the P327 lint.
P225.rationale: Approved 4-0-2 at median P3 (cti_lead and analyst_ux deferred for low value and the new entity type). The architect's floor drops VATComply and makes in-body member-state errors 'could not verify', never 'invalid'; this also follows A1, since VATComply's terms are unknown (legal_dpo had allowed it only at CLEAR). osint_investigator's strict eu_vat detection and tri-state, and legal_dpo's no bulk and no pivots from sole traders, are kept.
P225.title: EU VIES VAT validation (+ VATComply wrapper)

final_conditions: BACKLOG unblock: the team budgets an OpenCorporates commercial plan, or legal records a licence_allow entry; then implement with terms='license', requires_keys, default_enabled=False, skipped under the corporate profile until the plan or allow entry is recorded, ODbL attribution in reports (share-alike only if a derived database is redistributed).

BACKLOG unblock (architect merge gate): the api_token query parameter is covered by the central redactor (AR01) in cache rows, live feed and errors; 401 'Invalid Api Token' -> NEEDS_KEY; a trimmed real success fixture captured with the team's token exists. Meanwhile foreign counterparties use GLEIF, Wikidata, Companies House and manual links.
P226.rationale: Contested 3-3 (3 yes, 3 defer); the chair defers. Commercial use needs a paid plan (free tokens are only for approved public-benefit projects), so under the corporate profile it would be a permanent licence-blocked module, and the architect's merge gate (a real success fixture captured with the team's token) cannot be met without a purchase. cti_lead, osint_investigator and analyst_ux deferred for budget; redteam_lead and legal_dpo approved only as a licensed, disabled-by-default source. GLEIF (P220), Wikidata (P224) and Companies House (P227) cover the common foreign-company questions meanwhile.
P226.title: OpenCorporates API

final_conditions: requires_keys=('companies_house',): the key is sent as the HTTP basic-auth username, never in URLs, and registered with the central redactor (AR01). Keyless 401 'Empty Authorization header' -> NEEDS_KEY.

Key-terms (A1): the key belongs to a company/team account created under the corporate identity (never an analyst's personal free account) on a plan whose terms permit internal business use; legal records plan and terms URL in the provider registry (key_plans / free_plan_business_use) before it runs under the corporate profile.
Scope: UK counterparties only, opt-in (default_enabled=False). Company search and profile by name or company number.

Officers and PSC: keep name, role and appointment dates only; dates of birth, nationality and addresses are dropped at parse time. They become person_name pivots (relation officer_of/psc_of) with expand=False, never auto-pivoted into person modules.
Rate: the documented 600 requests per 5 minutes is respected through the P334 provider budget; 429 -> RATE_LIMITED (rule 5). OGL attribution in reports.

Merge gate: trimmed real fixtures (search, company profile, officers, 404) captured with the team's key, since research captured none; offline FakeHttp tests, a provider-registry entry and the P327 lint (A16).
P227.rationale: Approved 4-0-2 at median P3 (cti_lead and analyst_ux deferred: UK counterparties are rare and P231 offers the manual web search). legal_dpo's floor: a company-owned key on a business-compatible plan recorded before it runs, and officer data minimised to name, role and dates. The architect's floor: basic-auth key, a capture gate for real fixtures, officers never auto-expanded. osint_investigator's relation names and rate handling are kept.
P227.title: UK Companies House API

final_conditions: Dataset: iana.org enterprise-numbers.txt downloaded monthly through the dataset manager and parsed offline (disclosure 'none' for matching). Records are 4-line blocks (number / organisation / contact / e-mail with '&' for '@').

Legal floor: only the PEN number, the organisation name and the contact e-mail DOMAIN are kept; contact person names and full e-mail addresses are dropped at parse time and never reach the index, evidence or reports. The module produces domain (not email) pivots with expand=False, never for webmail domains.
Forward lookup: company_name or domain -> PEN number(s), with organisation names matched through the shared core/namematch.py matcher (possible-match wording below an exact match).

Reverse lookup (the more useful direction, cti_lead, osint_investigator, analyst_ux): a core helper pen_lookup(number) maps OIDs 1.3.6.1.4.1.<n> found by other parsers (certificate extensions, SNMP/syslog text) to the organisation, offline.
Opt-in (default_enabled=False). IANA public registry. Fixture: a trimmed excerpt of the real file with synthetic contacts; a test asserts that no contact name or full address survives parsing.
P228.rationale: Approved 4-1-1 at median P3 (analyst_ux rejected, cti_lead deferred: little value as a company module, and the registry lists individual contacts). legal_dpo's floor limits the output to organisation-level data (domain, not e-mail) and the architect drops contacts at parse time. The reverse OID -> organisation helper asked for by osint_investigator, cti_lead and analyst_ux is the main deliverable.
P228.title: IANA Private Enterprise Numbers registry

final_conditions: BACKLOG unblock: US counterparties become frequent in cases; even then a manual link may suffice (osint_investigator).
P229.rationale: Rejected mechanically (2 yes, 2 reject, 2 defer; defers do not outnumber rejects). cti_lead and analyst_ux see no CTI use for a Brazilian corporate team in US political-influence data; osint_investigator and redteam_lead deferred it as rarely relevant (value 2). legal_dpo and the architect would accept it only as an opt-in P3. Wikidata and GLEIF cover corporate relationships.
P229.title: LittleSis power-network API

final_conditions: BACKLOG unblock: only if offline screening (P219, P240) proves insufficient, as an analyst-triggered check of an ambiguous offline match through one licensed provider behind the same matcher semantics (the OpenSanctions path of P222), never W System (x402 micropayments) and never sending person names to unknown-tier operators.
P230.rationale: Rejected mechanically (0 yes, 4 reject, 2 defer). It duplicates the offline OFAC/UN/EU and CGU screening of P219/P240 and sends person and company names to small commercial operators (unknown tier, A8): legal_dpo cites LGPD necessity (art. 6 III), osint_investigator the x402 micropayments after the free calls, analyst_ux the confusing second opinion without a tie-break.
P230.title: Online sanctions screening second opinions (W System, dilisense)

final_conditions: Ship data/pivot_links/company_org.json in the frozen P311 pack schema (label, template, entity_types, category, host, verified, checked_at, privacy, publishes=false, touches_target, login_required, antibot). The pack is offline data (disclosure 'none'): V3LUM never requests these URLs or any API behind them.

Rendering follows A2/P311: at TLP:AMBER and above every link is non-clickable text with 'opening sends <value> to <host>'; at RED third-party links are hidden from reports and listed only by `v3lum links` with the warning; links are never auto-opened and `links --open` at AMBER+ needs an interactive confirmation naming the host.

CI renders every template with a sample value per declared entity type and with hostile values (quotes, spaces, unicode, newlines): each result must be an https URL on the declared host, built only from whitelisted placeholders through the declared encoder (never str.format, never {raw} in URL position).

Every link host has a provider-registry entry with tier and rationale (A8); unknown-tier hosts get the 'unknown operator' badge and their templates take IOC_TYPES values only (A8 BR4): never PERSONAL_TYPES, CNPJ, company names, keywords, malware or actor names, or other free text (P311 lint).
Initial host tiers for the registry reviewer to confirm: trusted - OpenSanctions, UK Companies House, OpenCorporates, GLEIF; community - ViewDNS.

Order: P311 groups links by analyst question with verified links first; inside a group the pack's file order is the curated analyst-value order (company search (OpenSanctions, Companies House, OpenCorporates, GLEIF) first, then ViewDNS reverse WHOIS); the terminal shows at most 8 links per seed, the rest go to HTML and `v3lum links`.

Verified links carry checked_at; `v3lum doctor --links` (offline) lists unverified links and links not re-checked for more than 180 days. The pack ships in phase 1 with the other pivot packs (A16), whatever the state of the related automated modules.

Entries: ViewDNS reverse WHOIS (verified) for company_name, domain, email and person_name; OpenSanctions website search (free in a browser per its FAQ; routine screening needs P222); Companies House web search for company inputs.
Also OpenCorporates and GLEIF web company search as manual alternatives to the paid or declined APIs (osint_investigator), verified=false until checked in a browser; OpenCorporates antibot=true.

Person-name and e-mail templates (ViewDNS reverse WHOIS) are privacy=true: rendered only for analyst-typed seeds in a case with a recorded purpose, never for discovered QSA partners, registrants, employees or customers, and hidden unless the analyst opts in for the case (P311; enforced in links.py and tested with a QSA partner fixture).

Company and domain templates are unrestricted. Reverse-WHOIS results are ownership candidates for the analyst, never scope or own-asset evidence by themselves (redteam_lead). ViewDNS reverseip and iphistory (Cloudflare-challenged) are not in this pack.
P231.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (cti_lead voted P3). legal_dpo's floor makes person-based reverse WHOIS case- and purpose-bound; the architect's enforceable form ('analyst-typed seeds only') matches P311's privacy=true rule, which is stricter than allowing case registrants and is applied. osint_investigator's manual alternatives for licensed or declined APIs (OpenSanctions, OpenCorporates, GLEIF, Companies House) are added. redteam_lead: results are ownership candidates, never scope.
P231.title: Pivot links: companies (ViewDNS reverse WHOIS, OpenSanctions web, Companies House web)

final_conditions: Offline module: disclosure 'none' (no network at all; ScopedHttp refuses any request), terms 'open', provider tier 'n/a'; allowed at TLP:RED. Pure-stdlib extension of core/validators.py.

Alphanumeric CNPJ (IN RFB 2.229/2024, issued from July 2026): regex ^[0-9A-Z]{12}[0-9]{2}$ (DVs stay numeric), char value ord(c)-48, weights 5,4,3,2,9,8,7,6,5,4,3,2 then 6,5,4,3,2,9,8,7,6,5,4,3,2, r = sum % 11, DV = 0 if r < 2 else 11 - r; HQ CNPJ derived from the 8-digit root. Vectors: 12.ABC.345/01DE-35, 00.000.000/0001-91 and invalid-DV cases.

CPF (rule 4 floor): validated offline only (mod 11, weights 10..2 and 11..2, repeated digits rejected); never a lookup key online or against datasets, never generated, enumerated or completed from masked forms. A unit test asserts that a text with a valid CPF makes zero HTTP requests.

The CPF fiscal-region digit is an info-only cross-check worded 'CPF issued in fiscal region N (UFs)', never residence. Wording everywhere separates 'check digits valid (format only)' from existence or registration.

Masking (AR24): one core masking function, with tests, masks CPF as ***.456.789-** in display_value, terminal, HTML/MD/JSON/STIX, evidence filenames, logs, --debug and the case-DB index; CPFs are never pivoted. --show-personal unmasks a single view and is recorded in the case audit.

PIS/NIS, titulo de eleitor, RENAVAM, CNS and CNH get validators and masking only: they are never auto-detected entity types (several are 11 digits and collide with CPF and phones), never pivots, and the P327 lint rejects any module accepting them as lookup keys. Their validators ship only with official test vectors.

Typing gate: an 11-digit string is typed CPF only with valid check digits AND context (CPF label, the ###.###.###-## mask or a form field); in phone context (DDD prefix, tel/whats/zap words, wa.me) it is a phone. A fixture of valid-DV phone numbers must not become CPFs.

The BR entity extractor is a rule set inside the shared P172 extraction engine, not a second extractor: regex candidates, then checksum gating, priority BR Code > boleto (47/48) > CNJ (20 digits, mod 97) > CNPJ > CPF > phone, each entity with provenance and a type confidence. Tests on BR scam-message fixtures.

Plates: validation and old<->Mercosul conversion only, with test vectors (both forms usable for text search); no owner lookups. CEP format and PIX key types (CPF, CNPJ, phone, e-mail, EVP) are validated offline.
Tests: the 18 research vectors plus the RFB alphanumeric example, the phone/CPF collision fixture and the masking tests in every renderer.
P232.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1: every Brazilian flow starts here and the alphanumeric CNPJ is already issued. legal_dpo's rule 4 floor (CPF never a lookup key, universal masking, other identifiers masked and never pivoted, no CPF generation) and the architect's floor (stdlib, one masking function, no auto-detected 11-digit types, the extractor inside P172) are adopted. cti_lead and osint_investigator supplied the phone/CPF typing gate, analyst_ux the format-only wording. Offline: terms open, tier n/a, default-on (A3).
P232.title: Brazilian identifier validators/parsers (CNPJ alnum, CPF region digit, plate old<->Mercosul, PIS/titulo/RENAVAM/CNS/CNH, BR entity extractor)

final_conditions: Offline pure-Python parsers. Boleto bancario (47): linha digitavel -> barcode bank(3)+currency(1)+K+factor(4)+value(10)+free(25); field DVs mod 10, general DV mod 11 (weights 2..9; 0/10/11 -> 1). Arrecadacao (48): mod 10 when the 3rd digit is 6/7, the mod-11 variant (r 0/1 -> 0, r 10 -> 1) when 8/9; segment decoded.
Due date: the factor wrapped on 2025-02-22 (9999 = 2025-02-21, new 1000 = 2025-02-22); compute both cycles, choose the date nearest to today and flag ambiguity, showing both dates when ambiguous.

PIX BR Code: EMV TLV parser bounded (payload <= 512 bytes, nesting depth 2), merchant account template 26-51 with br.gov.bcb.pix, CRC16/CCITT-FALSE (poly 0x1021, init 0xFFFF) over the payload through '6304', checked against the BCB manual vector (1D3D). Extract merchant name/city, key type, key, txid and amount; a bad CRC reads 'altered or corrupted payload'.

Keys (legal floor): CPF keys are masked and never pivoted (rule 4); e-mail and phone keys become entities (relation pix_key_of) with expand=False and trigger no automatic breach, stealer, username or phone-reputation lookup, only analyst-initiated ones; CNPJ keys pivot to the P236 chain (who receives the money); merchant names of natural persons are not pivoted to person modules.

Legal floor: the dynamic BR Code location URL is never fetched in any mode (fetching is a payer-side action that returns payee personal data); only its host becomes a defanged domain pivot with expand=False; the full location URL stays a masked attribute, never a url entity. No DICT lookups (no lawful public DICT access for third parties).

Verdicts: barcode bank differing from the bank named in the document or OCR text is HIGH 'boleto bank mismatch: possible tampering' (PROBABLE); a PIX merchant name or key CNPJ root that does not match the claimed brand (org_profile brands, P360, P236) is MEDIUM 'payee differs from claimed brand'. Neither is ever labelled malicious on its own.
Check-digit or CRC failure reads 'invalid or altered code (typed or altered line)'; when the input came from OCR (P363) or a QR decode (P261) it reads 'could not verify (OCR)' instead.

Plain-language verdict line first (e.g. 'Boleto: check digits OK - bank 341 (Itau), due 2026-12-01, R$ 1.234,56' or 'CHECK DIGIT MISMATCH: altered or mistyped'); PIX shows merchant, city, key type (masked key), txid, amount and CRC status.

Bank, ISPB and PIX-participant tables are full-list datasets (BCB STR CSV with UTF-8 BOM and ',' separator; BrasilAPI banks and PIX participants), refreshed weekly by the dataset manager with a bundled BCB snapshot so triage works offline; never per-value API calls (disclosure 'none'). Each table shows its refresh date. Tiers: BCB trusted, BrasilAPI community.
Fixtures: the BCB manual vector, a tampered boleto and BR Code, both due-date cycles, and the STR/BrasilAPI lists re-captured untruncated (the research samples are truncated).
P233.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1 (redteam_lead voted P2): boleto and PIX tampering is a top Brazilian fraud pattern. legal_dpo's floor sets key handling (CPF masked, e-mail/phone keys without automatic fan-out) and forbids fetching the dynamic payload URL, so osint_investigator's optional LIGHT fetch is not adopted (redteam_lead and the architect also wanted no automatic fetch). The architect's floor: offline parsers with bounds and vectors, full-list tables through the dataset manager plus a snapshot, no per-value API calls. Severities: osint_investigator's HIGH for a boleto bank mismatch, labelled as possible tampering, and cti_lead's MEDIUM payee mismatch with no 'malicious' label. Tier community is the lowest of the dataset providers (BrasilAPI); terms open. Audit: the payload URL yields a domain pivot only, as legal_dpo's condition requires.
P233.title: Boleto and PIX BR Code parsers + bank tables (BCB STR participants, BrasilAPI banks/PIX participants)

final_conditions: Online chain, stop at the first success, 5 s per provider, per-provider status in coverage (no fan-out): BrasilAPI CEP v2 -> ViaCEP -> OpenCEP. AwesomeAPI is dropped (429 QuotaExceeded on the first keyless call, no fixture). IBGE localidades normalises municipality codes.

Tiers (A8): BrasilAPI and ViaCEP community, IBGE trusted. OpenCEP is used only after the registry reviewer records it as community tier; while it is unknown it receives no value (unknown tier receives IOC values only) and the chain ends at ViaCEP.
ViaCEP returns {'erro': true} inside HTTP 200 for an unknown CEP: that documented marker means EMPTY; every other error-in-200, 403/429, timeout or 5xx means could not verify (rule 5).

One normaliser to the shared vocab (address, city, region, country=BR, ibge_code). BrasilAPI coordinates are labelled 'CEP centroid (approximate)', never a person's location; a coordinates pivot exists only when a provider supplies one and is never auto-expanded.

ViaCEP reverse address search (ws/{UF}/{city}/{street}/json, >= 3 chars per segment) only for an address the analyst typed or a company address from CNPJ records; never from text blobs and never for addresses tied to natural persons (QSA partners, MEI owners).
CEP UF vs DDD vs CNPJ UF mismatches are weak info attributes for correlation; they never raise the score on their own (people and companies move).
Cache TTL 30 days (bounded by cache_max_age_days and retention_days).

Merge gate (A16): offline tests with FakeHttp (unmatched requests fail, network guard active) over trimmed real fixtures without personal data (the 9 captured BrasilAPI, ViaCEP, OpenCEP and IBGE responses plus a ViaCEP erro body), a provider-registry entry for every host, the registry contract test and the P327 lint.
P234.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (cti_lead voted P3). The architect's floor: offline range table first, a short first-success chain with per-provider status, ViaCEP's in-body marker handled, AwesomeAPI dropped, coordinates never auto-expanded. osint_investigator and the architect limit reverse address search to typed or company addresses, never people; analyst_ux keeps cross-check mismatches as context. OpenCEP waits for a tier review because A8 lets unknown operators receive IOC values only; legal_dpo had no objection to area-level data.
P234.title: CEP lookup (BrasilAPI v2, ViaCEP, OpenCEP, AwesomeAPI, IBGE localidades, offline CEP->UF)

final_conditions: Reference data, not a collector (architect): bundled v3lum/data/br/cnae.json, natureza_juridica.json, porte and situacao codes and sensitive_divisions.json, each with source, version and retrieval date (Receita/IBGE attribution), plus a core helper used by cnpj_lookup and correlation rules. No module makes network calls per query (disclosure 'none').
The IBGE CNAE API (servicodados.ibge.gov.br) is only a `v3lum data update cnae` refresher of the full tree, never called per CNPJ.
CNPJ cards render human-readable CNAE, legal nature, size and situation labels, also when a fallback provider returns codes only.

The sensitive-division map covers business-risk sectors only (64-66 financial and insurance, payment and crypto activities, 80 private security, 92 gambling and betting) and is reviewed data with tests. Its tags are info context and never raise risk on their own; correlation rules may combine them (e.g. new company + financial CNAE + lookalike domain).

Legal floor (LGPD art. 5 II and 11): CNAE classes that reveal religious, political or trade-union affiliation (9491-0/00, 9492-8/00, 9420-1/00 and the rest of division 94) are never used as risk signals and never propagated as attributes to natural persons such as QSA partners.
Tests map sample CNAE subclasses to descriptions and divisions and assert that division-94 classes produce no risk tag and no partner attribute.
P235.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. The architect's design is adopted: bundled reference data plus a helper, with the IBGE API only as a refresher. legal_dpo's floor keeps religious, political and union classes out of risk signals and away from natural persons. cti_lead, osint_investigator and analyst_ux insisted that sector tags are context, never risk on their own. Open government data, trusted provider, default-on as offline data.
P235.title: CNAE and Receita code tables (IBGE CNAE API + bundled tables, sensitive-division map)

final_conditions: Sources at release (class open, legal_dpo): BrasilAPI and Minha Receita (MIT code, RFB open data; one shared parser), publica.cnpj.ws public API (only free source of state IE) and Querido Diario company/partners. Tiers: BrasilAPI, Minha Receita, CNPJ.ws and Querido Diario (Open Knowledge Brasil) community. Default-on by A3 decision; a CPF is never looked up.

OpenCNPJ, CNPJa open and ReceitaWS are coded behind the same normaliser but registered as sources only after legal records their terms (A1: unknown terms run in no profile) and the reviewer records a trusted/community tier (A8: unknown tiers never receive a CNPJ). Until then they are not called and coverage lists them as 'pending terms review'.

Chain: stop at the first full record, 8 s per provider, 25 s chain budget, per-provider status in coverage. Per-provider budgets come from the registry (P334): publica.cnpj.ws and ReceitaWS 3/min (honour x-ratelimit-remaining/reset), CNPJa ~5/min; an empty bucket skips to the next provider instead of sleeping (no wait > 2 s); 3/min providers only as last resort.

One normaliser to one schema: names, situacao with its date, opening date, CNAEs (labels via P235 once it lands; raw codes until then), legal nature, size, capital, Simples/MEI, address + IBGE code, phones, e-mails, QSA, state IE.

Every field keeps its provider and the provider's freshness field (updated, ultima_atualizacao, data_situacao_cadastral); when several providers answered, conflicts are shown with their source and the freshest wins.

Not found (rule 5): a valid-DV CNPJ is 'not in RFB open data as of <snapshot date> (companies opened after the last dump may be missing)' only after not_found from two providers with different upstreams; a not_found from a dump-based provider triggers at most one such fallback. One 404 while others error, 429, 5xx or all failing = could not verify.
ReceitaWS {'status':'ERROR'} inside HTTP 200 is ERROR (P321 marker). Alphanumeric CNPJs are accepted (providers answer 404 not_found, not 400). Cache TTL 72 h.

Registry contacts: RFB e-mail/phone are attributes plus pivots with relation rfb_contact and expand=False, labelled 'registry contact (often the accounting firm)'; never auto-expanded into breach, stealer, username or phone-reputation modules; correlation rules never treat a shared contact as same owner; contacts shared by > 20 CNPJs (via P238 when installed) are tagged shared_contact.

Contact domains: free and BR webmail domains (gmail, hotmail, outlook, yahoo, bol, uol, terra, ig...) never become domain pivots; other contact domains pivot with expand=False unless registro.br RDAP ties the domain to the same CNPJ root.

QSA (rule 4, legal floor): natural-person partners become person_name pivots (relation partner_of), shown only in the CNPJ card with the RFB-masked CPF digits as given, never unmasked, completed or joined across sources (no rule joins on CPF fragments), age band only in the QSA table, never auto-expanded; only offline sanctions/PEP screening in due-diligence cases.

PJ partners are CNPJ pivots and the engine's depth and entity budget decide (no recursion inside the module): default depth 1 for partner companies (configurable to 2), at most 20 companies per seed. Partner and branch CNPJs and their domains are third parties: passive modules only, never LIGHT/ACTIVE seeds, never added to org_profile or a scope automatically.

MEI/EI: CPF digits embedded in the razao social are masked at ingestion, before display, evidence and indexes; their e-mails and phones are personal data (domain pivots only for non-webmail domains, no automatic breach/stealer/phone modules). Evidence keeps the response in this masked form under A10 retention.

Findings: situacao other than ATIVA (INAPTA, SUSPENSA, BAIXADA, NULA) is a MEDIUM finding with its date and meaning; opening date and company age are attributes for P258 (CR33), with no age-only finding. The card header shows provider used, data date, plain-language status, opening date and age. The legal-name pivot never triggers cnpj_name_resolver (P361).

Merge gate (A16): offline tests with FakeHttp (unmatched requests fail, network guard active) over trimmed real fixtures without personal data (the 11 captures plus a 404 and a 429 per provider, the alphanumeric-CNPJ 404 and the ReceitaWS 200-ERROR body), a provider-registry entry for every host, the registry contract test and the P327 lint.
P236.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1: the core Brazilian pivot, default-on by A3. legal_dpo's floor decides the sources (terms-recorded providers by default) together with A1/A8: unreviewed providers run in no profile and unknown tiers never receive a CNPJ, so OpenCNPJ, CNPJa and ReceitaWS wait for review, which also keeps Module.terms 'open'. It also sets the CPF/QSA and MEI masking. The architect's floor: registry-driven per-provider budgets that skip instead of sleeping, one normaliser, no recursion inside the module, the two-upstream not-found rule. cti_lead, osint_investigator, redteam_lead and analyst_ux supplied the accountant-contact trap handling, provenance, time budget, third-party rule and card layout. cti_lead's MEDIUM status finding is kept as a fact, and osint_investigator's age-as-attribute rule as well.
P236.title: CNPJ resolver with fallback chain (BrasilAPI, Minha Receita, OpenCNPJ, CNPJa open, publica.cnpj.ws, ReceitaWS, Querido Diario company)

final_conditions: requires_keys=('transparencia',), key in the chave-api-dados header only, registered with the team's institutional gov.br account (never a personal or borrowed key), never logged or stored in URLs (AR01). CGU open data: key_plans business-compatible (free_plan_business_use true per the registry evidence).

Without a key: one hint line per scan ('add V3LUM_TRANSPARENCIA_KEY for contracts/leniency; sanctions already checked keyless by tcu_certidoes/cgu_sanctions_bulk') instead of a NEEDS_KEY row per entity; the 401 'Chave de API nao informada' body maps to NEEDS_KEY.

Rule 4 floor: no CPF or NIS is ever sent. /pessoa-fisica, /ceaf?cpfSancionado, /peps?cpf, servidores by CPF and the benefit endpoints (Bolsa Familia, BPC, auxilios, seguro-defeso) are not implemented, and a test asserts that no cpf/nis parameter is ever built.

Default endpoints are CNPJ-centric: CEIS, CNEP, CEPIM, acordos de leniencia, contracts and convenios by CNPJ. PEP and servidores are queried by name only for a person the analyst typed as a due-diligence subject with a recorded purpose (reason_code 'privacy' otherwise).

Sanctions are not parsed twice: when the P240 bulk lists are fresh (< 48 h) CEIS/CNEP/CEPIM/Leniencia come from P240 and this module adds contracts, convenios, spending and sanction detail; when they are stale or absent the API rows go through P240's normaliser. One finding per listing across P237/P239/P240 (dedup key = list + sanction id).

Ceos guard: rows that do not contain the queried CNPJ mean the filter was ignored -> ERROR, never findings. Bodies declared ISO-8859-1 are decoded as such; error JSON inside responses is detected (rule 5).

Limits: the documented 90 req/min (06:00-23:59) and 300 req/min (00:00-05:59) per key are a P334 provider quota; 429 -> RATE_LIMITED; pagination capped at 3 pages (15 items per page); Module.max_requests = 10 per entity (A3 BR2), beyond it the run is partial with stop_reason 'request_cap'. Contract output = count, total value and the 5 most recent.
API only: the portal's web pages return 202 bot challenges and are never fetched (A9); a manual link to the web search is P250.

Merge gate: trimmed success fixtures captured with the team's key for every endpoint used (research has only the 401), plus FakeHttp tests for the CNPJ-mismatch guard, the ISO-8859-1 body and the no-CPF assertion (A16).
P237.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (legal_dpo voted P1). legal_dpo's rule 4 floor removes every CPF/NIS endpoint (the draft's person endpoints would have sent CPFs) and limits PEP/servidores to name queries for a recorded due-diligence subject. The architect's floor: header key, success-fixture gate, the Ceos filter guard, no second sanctions parser, quota and page caps. cti_lead's freshness rule and the shared dedup key (cti_lead, osint_investigator, analyst_ux) stop the same CEIS hit appearing three times; analyst_ux's one-line no-key hint is kept. A key-required source may be default (A3).
P237.title: Portal da Transparencia API (CGU, keyed): CEIS/CNEP/CEPIM/Leniencia/PEP/contracts

final_conditions: A separate command, `v3lum data import-rfb`, that a scan never triggers. It shows download size and required disk first, refuses when free space < 3x the download, and is resumable with progress. One RFB importer is shared with P361 (table selection, e.g. --names light vs full QSA), not two.

Legal floor: only the WebDAV share token RFB itself publishes on its official open-data page (configured with that source URL recorded); never a token taken from third-party code if it differs; stop if RFB requires a login. A rotated or invalid token gives UNAVAILABLE with a doctor hint, never 'no companies'.

Robust ETL (architect): PROPFIND parsed with the safe XML helper; streaming, resumable Range downloads to unique temp files with size/etag checks; zip members streamed, latin-1 ';' CSV parsed row by row, batched inserts, indexes built after load; peak memory < 500 MB, checked on a 1M-row synthetic file in a slow test. Import logic re-implemented from minha-receita (MIT) with attribution.

Minimisation at import (rule 4, legal floor): CPF digits embedded in MEI/EI razao social are stripped; natural-person partner rows keep only RFB's masked CPF, never completed or brute-forced and never used as a join key (no CPF-fragment joins); faixa etaria is not stored for display.

Storage: SQLite under ~/.v3lum/datasets (dir 0700, file 0600) with schema version and source month, never exported; superseded monthly dumps are deleted after a successful import (storage limitation).

Lookups: CNPJ root -> branches on request; person-centric reverse lookups (partner name, e-mail, phone, address -> CNPJs) only as explicit analyst queries on analyst-typed seeds inside a case with a recorded purpose, logged in the audit trail, capped at the top 50 plus a total count per query and with a per-case limit (no bulk enumeration).

Results are company-centric hypotheses: CNPJ pivots with expand=False; partner-name matches across companies are POSSIBLE (name only); no free-text person search command, no person dossiers and no export of person-centric lists.

Shared contacts: an e-mail, phone or address shared by >= 20 CNPJs is tagged shared_contact ('possible accountant/virtual office') and excluded from same-owner rules (P258). Every finding cites 'RFB snapshot YYYY-MM'.

Opt-in (default_enabled=False); offline once imported (disclosure 'none'). When the index is absent the module is UNAVAILABLE reason_code 'dataset' ('run v3lum data import-rfb'). Tests import a tiny synthetic zip in the real layout end to end on a temp home.
P238.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (analyst_ux voted P3): the only lawful route to partner -> companies and shared-contact clustering (laranjas, shell rings). legal_dpo's floor makes it proportionate: the RFB-published token only, purpose-bound and audited person-centric lookups with caps, minimisation at import, no dossiers, deletion of superseded dumps; it also forbids CPF-fragment joins, so cti_lead's and osint_investigator's use of the visible CPF digits as a homonym key is not adopted and name-only matches stay POSSIBLE. The architect's floor: a separate, resumable, memory-bounded importer shared with P361. analyst_ux's honest 'unavailable' status and the shared-contact threshold (cti_lead, osint_investigator) are kept.
P238.title: RFB CNPJ open-data bulk import (offline reverse lookups)

final_conditions: One keyless call per CNPJ to certidoes-apf.apps.tcu.gov.br with the formatted CNPJ and seemitirpdf=false always (no PDF generation); <= 1 req/s; cache 24 h. Default-on by A3 decision.

Results are trusted only when seCnpjEncontradoNaBaseTcu=true. When it is false (a fictitious CNPJ also gets 200 NADA_CONSTA), every list reads 'could not verify: CNPJ not found in the TCU base - not evidence of a clean record'; CNPJ existence comes only from P236.

Per-list tri-state attribute for TCU inidoneos, CNJ CNIA, CEIS and CNEP: consta / nada_consta ('no record in <list> as of <dataHoraEmissao>') / unknown. SISTEMA_INDISPONIVEL (P321 marker), a missing entry, 5xx or a timeout = unknown, listed in coverage as 'could not verify <list>', never clean (rule 5).

Any CONSTA is a HIGH finding tagged sanctions naming the list, emitter, dates and the manual consultation link. It shares the dedup key (list, CNPJ, sanction id) with P237 and P240, so one sanction is one finding with several sources (no noisy-OR inflation).
The certificate timestamp (dataHoraEmissao) and the per-list states are stored in evidence.

Merge gate (A16): offline tests with FakeHttp (unmatched requests fail, network guard active) over trimmed real fixtures without personal data (the captured 200 response plus synthetic CONSTA, seCnpjEncontradoNaBaseTcu=false and SISTEMA_INDISPONIVEL variants), a provider-registry entry for every host, the registry contract test and the P327 lint.
P239.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1 (redteam_lead voted P2). Every member flagged the NADA_CONSTA trap for unknown CNPJs; the architect's and analyst_ux's per-list tri-state with 'could not verify' (rule 5, legal_dpo) is the spec. cti_lead's and osint_investigator's HIGH finding with the manual link and analyst_ux's shared dedup key with P237/P240 are adopted. Default-on by A3 (TCU certidoes).
P239.title: TCU consolidated certificates (TCU inidoneos + CNJ CNIA + CEIS + CNEP)

final_conditions: Datasets through the dataset manager only (`v3lum data update cgu`): daily zips (PEP monthly) from portaldatransparencia.gov.br/download-de-dados/{ceis|cnep|cepim|acordos-leniencia|pep}/{YYYYMMDD}, walking back at most 7 days on 404; never fetched during a scan. Each download is validated (';' ISO-8859-1 CSV, minimum rows) before replacing the previous copy, and superseded copies are deleted.

Zips go through the safe archive helper (single expected CSV member, size and ratio caps); the CSV is parsed streaming into an indexed local store (CNPJ, CNPJ root, normalised names), not in-memory sets. Matching is local (disclosure 'none') with the shared P219 core/namematch.py matcher.

CNPJ: an exact 14-digit match with a sanction in force is a HIGH finding tagged sanctions with list, sanction type, sanctioning body, start/end dates and link; a match on the 8-digit root of another establishment is MEDIUM 'related establishment' (match type always stated); expired sanctions are INFO 'formerly sanctioned (<end date>)'.
One finding per listing across P237/P239/P240 (dedup key list + CNPJ + sanction id).

Legal floor: person-name matching only for subjects the analyst entered in a due-diligence case with a recorded purpose, or QSA partners of a CNPJ under that due diligence; never automatically from pivots. Matches are 'possible match' (score >= 0.90, confidence <= 0.5) lowered by the P252 homonym score.

Rule 4: person rows keep only the name and the CPF exactly as published (masked), displayed masked, never used as a lookup key and never joined with QSA CPF fragments; only matched rows enter the case.
PEP file matches are INFO 'PEP (possible match)' context, never risk on their own, and only for typed persons or QSA partners in due diligence.

A missing dataset, or one older than 3 days (40 days for the monthly PEP file), gives UNAVAILABLE reason_code 'dataset' or a coverage warning 'not screened against <list> (<date>)', never 'not sanctioned'. The file date appears in every finding.

Merge gate: trimmed real fixtures (a zip with header plus a few rows per list, personal rows synthetic) captured before merge, since research has none; tests for in-force, expired, root-only, homonym and stale cases (A16).
P240.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1 (redteam_lead and analyst_ux voted P2): keyless, offline, official screening by CNPJ, default-on by A3. The architect's floor: dataset manager with the 7-day walk-back, safe archive handling, an indexed store and the shared matcher, 'not screened' instead of 'not sanctioned'. legal_dpo's floor: purpose-bound person matching, masked CPFs never used as keys, superseded copies deleted. Severity HIGH follows cti_lead and osint_investigator and matches P239, so one sanction is one finding. Using visible masked-CPF digits to raise confidence (cti_lead, osint_investigator, analyst_ux) is not adopted: legal_dpo forbids CPF-fragment joins across sources (P236, P238).
P240.title: CGU bulk sanctions downloads (CEIS, CNEP, CEPIM, Leniencia, PEP)

final_conditions: Licence (legal floor): terms='noncommercial'. DataJud Termo de Uso v1.2 (27/11/2023) offers the API 'exclusivamente para fins legais, nao comerciais e autorizados' (3.3) and forbids commercial exploitation (3.8).

Off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared by a licence_allow entry (CNJ's written confirmation, or a recorded legal opinion that internal incident/litigation-risk analysis is not commercial use), reported as coverage lost with reason_code 'licence'.

Offline part (always available): the CNJ unified-number parser NNNNNNN-DD.AAAA.J.TR.OOOO in core validators, valid iff int(N+AAAA+J+TR+OOOO+DD) % 97 == 1, with the routing table to the 91 tribunal aliases (J=8 TR in UF order, J=4 trf1-6, J=5 trt1-24 / TR 00 tst, J=6 tre-xx) and test vectors such as 0700055-10.2018.8.01.0022 -> api_publica_tjac.

A cnj_process entity type (P333) replaces the keyword/text_blob inputs; at most 5 process numbers per text input. Numbers found while pivoting (gazettes, DJEN) are pivots with expand=False, so the slow API never runs automatically on them.

API key: config value, defaulting to the 'APIKey atual' CNJ publishes on datajud-wiki.cnj.jus.br/api-publica/acesso (a public key, not a borrowed one). On 401 one refresh per run fetches that official page and extracts the key with a strict pattern; never taken from third-party code, never logged, stored only in config, redacted (AR01).

Queries only by a validated process number routed by J.TR; no party, name, CNPJ or CPF search (terms 3.11, 4.2). Output metadata only: court, class, subjects, filing date, last movements, link. Sealed or absent processes read 'not found in public DataJud', never 'no case'.

Latency 25-30 s (expected_latency declared): default_enabled=False (A3); a per-run deadline of 60 s with ctx.cancelled() checks in a threaded run, never delaying the report. 429 es_rejected_execution_exception -> RATE_LIMITED ('could not verify: DataJud overloaded'), retried once with backoff. Rate <= 120 req/min (terms 3.13).
DataJud-derived data is never shared with third parties or included in STIX/MISP exports (terms 4.6), and the module is never used to screen employees or job candidates.

Merge gate (A16): offline tests with FakeHttp (unmatched requests fail, network guard active) over trimmed real fixtures without personal data (the 5 DataJud captures including the 429 overload body), a provider-registry entry for every host, the registry contract test and the P327 lint.
P241.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (cti_lead and redteam_lead voted P3). legal_dpo's floor relabels it noncommercial per the CNJ terms (3.3, 3.8), so it is off under the corporate profile until legal records an allow entry, and it adds the rate, export and screening limits. The architect's floor: parser and router in core validators, a cnj_process type, the strict key refresh from the official page, a 60 s deadline, honest rate_limited, no automatic runs on pivots. The 25-30 s latency makes it opt-in under A3, which matches cti_lead. osint_investigator's and analyst_ux's metadata-only output and wording are kept; the public CNJ key is not a borrowed key (redteam_lead).
P241.title: DataJud (CNJ) by CNJ process number + offline CNJ number parser

final_conditions: Legal floor (A9 BR8): www.in.gov.br/robots.txt disallows all robots ('Disallow: /', checked 2026-11-26), so the public search page is never scraped. Automation uses only the official DOU open-data dumps (XML published by Imprensa Nacional), downloaded by `v3lum data update dou` through the dataset manager and matched locally (disclosure 'none'), never during a scan.

INLABS (daily XML behind a login) is not built in this build: it needs a team account created by an authorised employee (A15) and a P327 lint decision on authenticated downloads (BACKLOG). The manual pivot link is the public search URL (in.gov.br/consulta/-/buscar/dou?q=), emitted as Module.manual_link.

Without the dataset the module is UNAVAILABLE reason_code 'dataset' ('run v3lum data update dou'), aggregated into one coverage line, with the manual link; results always say 'DOU dump as of <date>' because recent acts may be missing. The local index covers a configurable window (default the last 24 months) and older months are pruned.

Source: the official dump URL is recorded in the provider registry with evidence after a check from the team network, and a trimmed real dump excerpt is captured before merge; if no lawful dump is reachable, only the manual link ships.
Parsing: XML through the core safe XML helper with size caps; a dump whose structure does not match the expected schema is ERROR 'format changed', never 'no mentions' (fixture with a broken dump).

Matching: the formatted CNPJ (and its digits) and the exact razao social of CNPJ seeds and analyst-typed company names by default; person names only for a typed person seed in a due-diligence case with a recorded purpose, never QSA names automatically; keyword only on explicit request.

Output: hit count plus the 5 most recent excerpts (date, section, organ/act type, link), with excerpts containing penalty terms (penalidade, inidoneidade, rescisao, multa, sancao, suspensao) ranked first. Routine mentions are INFO and never raise the risk score.

Case data keeps per hit only title, date, section, organ, URL and an excerpt of at most 300 chars; no full act text. Person names in excerpts are never pivoted; CNJ process numbers in excerpts become P241 pivots with expand=False.
Tests: a trimmed real dump excerpt (one act with a CNPJ, one with a penalty term, one routine), a no-match case and the broken-format case; registry entry and P327 lint (A16).
P242.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (cti_lead voted P3). legal_dpo's floor is decisive: the portal's robots.txt forbids all robots and A9 binds V3LUM to respect it, so the scrape of the search page planned by the synthesizer, the architect and osint_investigator is replaced by the official open-data dumps matched locally. INLABS, the other official channel legal_dpo allows, is backlogged because it needs a team login and a lint decision. The architect's loud-failure rule, cti_lead's and analyst_ux's query and output limits, and osint_investigator's excerpt size and CNJ routing are applied to the dump parser.
P242.title: Diario Oficial da Uniao search (Imprensa Nacional)

final_conditions: Host api.queridodiario.org.br only; the old api.queridodiario.ok.org.br fails TLS and is removed (never a fallback; the Ceos port must be fixed). <= 1 req/s, cache 24 h, ~3 s per query. Open Knowledge Brasil open data with attribution in reports.

Queries: the formatted CNPJ in quotes and the exact razao social/nome fantasia, by default only for CNPJ seeds and analyst-typed company names; default date window 2 years; keyword only on explicit request. Person names only for a typed person seed in a due-diligence case with a recorded purpose, never QSA names automatically (legal_dpo).

Bounded output: at most 10 excerpts per query; the analyst sees the count plus the 5 most recent excerpts with penalty terms (penalidade, inidoneidade, rescisao, multa, sancao, suspensao) ranked first (a large CNPJ hits 2,000+ gazettes). Routine mentions are INFO and never raise the score.

Minimisation: each hit keeps municipality, date, gazette URL (as a link) and an excerpt of at most 300 chars as finding data; no bulk storage of gazette texts and no PERSON entities extracted from excerpts.

Derived pivots: CNJ process numbers found by the shared parser become cnj_process pivots with expand=False (P241, under its licence gate); other CNPJs in excerpts become cnpj pivots with expand=False (hypotheses, not confirmed links).

Empty results read 'not found in covered gazettes (Querido Diario indexes only part of Brazil's municipalities)', never 'no mentions'. Rule 5: 401/403/429, timeouts, 5xx and error-in-200 bodies mean could not verify (P321/P328 statuses: BLOCKED, RATE_LIMITED, QUOTA, ERROR), never EMPTY or 'not found'; such responses are never cached.

Merge gate (A16): offline tests with FakeHttp (unmatched requests fail, network guard active) over trimmed real fixtures without personal data (the 4 Querido Diario captures plus an empty result and a 5xx), a provider-registry entry for every host, the registry contract test and the P327 lint.
P243.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (cti_lead voted P3). Every member asked for the new host only; the architect's bounded excerpts and non-expanding derived pivots, analyst_ux's count-plus-5 presentation shared with dou_search, cti_lead's coverage caveat and osint_investigator's excerpt limits are combined. legal_dpo's floor keeps person searches purpose-bound and storage to excerpts. Open Knowledge Brasil is recorded as community tier.
P243.title: Querido Diario municipal gazettes search

final_conditions: Each list is a dataset with its own refresh, fetched only by `v3lum data update` (size shown), never mid-scan: MTE 'lista suja' CSV on www.gov.br (weekly, ';' ISO-8859-1), CVM registries (companhias abertas, intermediaries, sanction proceedings; daily) through one CVM loader shared with P360/P361, BrasilAPI CVM brokers list, and PGFN divida ativa (quarterly, multi-GB).

PGFN is opt-in: a separate `v3lum data update pgfn` import, streamed into an on-disk index keyed by CNPJ root (never loaded in memory) and not part of the default update set. The CAPTCHA-protected listadevedores.pgfn.gov.br app is never used (rule 1); CVM stop orders exist only as HTML news and are not automated.

Structural minimisation (architect, rule 4): natural-person rows (CPF debtors or employers) are dropped at import unless `--include-persons` is passed and recorded. With it, individuals are matched by name only for due-diligence subjects with a recorded purpose (possible match, P252 homonym score); a CPF is never a lookup key, shown masked and never pivoted.
