Matching is local (disclosure 'none') through core/namematch.py; exact CNPJ (or root, stated) matches produce findings with list, amount band and date; only matched rows enter the case.

Severity table (documented and tested): MTE lista suja = HIGH (labour/ESG); CVM sanction proceeding = MEDIUM; PGFN divida ativa = LOW context with debt nature (previdenciaria, FGTS, demais), amount band and situation, because debt is common among legitimate companies.

CVM registries and the BrasilAPI brokers list answer 'is this broker/adviser/platform authorised?' by CNPJ or exact name and feed P360. Absence reads 'not found in CVM registries as of <date>', never fraud.

A missing or stale dataset reads 'not screened against <list> (<date>)' (UNAVAILABLE reason_code 'dataset'), never 'clean'. Tiers: PGFN, MTE and CVM trusted, BrasilAPI community; CVM data share-alike obligations apply only if redistributed.
Merge gate: trimmed real fixtures for PGFN and MTE captured before merge (only a CVM head exists today), person rows synthetic; offline tests and the P327 lint (A16).
P244.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. legal_dpo's rule 4 floor and the architect's structural minimisation (person rows dropped at import unless recorded) protect individuals in these lists. The architect's dataset rules, cti_lead's shared CVM loader and opt-in PGFN, analyst_ux's severity table and osint_investigator's CVM authorisation answer are adopted. Scheduling (A16 BR1): P3 with effort M, so it is not built in this build (only effort-S P3 items are); BACKLOG.md keeps this spec as the target, and P360 owns the shared CVM loader meanwhile.
P244.title: BR offline risk lists by CNPJ (PGFN divida ativa, MTE lista suja, CVM registry + brokers)

final_conditions: BACKLOG unblock (legal_dpo veto_lift plus the architect's scope): only small local Camara/Senado member lists and elected-candidate lists as PEP context (office, mandate period, source) if PEP context beyond the CGU PEP file of P240 is still needed; 'cpf' never in accepts; TSE donor data never imported or matched for natural persons; party affiliation never stored or shown.

BACKLOG unblock (continued): person matching only for due-diligence subjects the analyst entered or QSA partners of the CNPJ under that due diligence, as 'possible match' with the P252 homonym score and a recorded purpose; CNPJ appearances as campaign or CEAP suppliers may be matched; A9 BR-egress only, Akamai 403 = could not verify; A10 retention.

final_conditions: Ship the verified half first (architect): BNDES CKAN datastore_search (dadosabertos.bndes.gov.br) and SALIC incentivadores (api.salic.cultura.gov.br, HAL JSON _embedded/_links), with their fixtures; per-provider status in coverage.

A9: automated only from the team's own Brazilian egress, never through a VPN or proxy exit chosen to defeat a geo-block, never with IP rotation; 403, challenge, geo-block or an empty reply = BLOCKED ('could not verify') with the manual link, never 'no contracts'.

CNPJ-centric queries only, at most 20 rows per provider; output limited to contract/operation id, organ, value, dates and URL. SALIC individual proponents and sponsors are never matched, stored or pivoted (legal_dpo).

Opt-in (default_enabled=False). Official open data (BNDES, MinC, PNCP), tier trusted. Federal contracts also come through P237, so findings share P237's contract dedup key where the same contract appears.

Merge gate (A16): offline tests with FakeHttp (unmatched requests fail, network guard active) over trimmed real fixtures without personal data (the BNDES CKAN and SALIC captures now; PNCP/Compras success fixtures from BR egress before those two are enabled), a provider-registry entry for every host, the registry contract test and the P327 lint.

P247.title: Escavador API v2 (lawsuits by CNPJ, paid)

final_conditions: Dataset: ANAC dados_aeronaves.csv from sistemas.anac.gov.br through the dataset manager (daily TTL), parsed offline (disclosure 'none') after skipping the 'Atualizado em' preamble line and the UTF-8 BOM (';' separated), validated before replacing the previous copy; findings cite the dataset date.

Minimisation at import (architect, stricter than masking): natural-person owners' and operators' names and CPFs are dropped; only company owners/operators identified by CNPJ are kept, so no person can be matched or pivoted.

Matching by owner/operator CNPJ, exact company name and aircraft registration mark with a strict pattern (PP-, PR-, PS-, PT-, PU- prefixes) via an explicit TYPE:value prefix or applies(); never from bare tokens and never by person name.
Opt-in (default_enabled=False). Output: mark, model, owner/operator company and registration status.
Merge gate: a trimmed real fixture captured before merge (none exists), with synthetic person rows to prove they are dropped; offline tests and the P327 lint (A16).

The architect's floor drops natural-person rows at import, which is stricter than legal_dpo's masking and answers the privacy objection; osint_investigator's strict mark pattern and dataset-date citation are kept. final_conditions: Not automated: Casa dos Dados (Cloudflare challenge, rule 1) and similar walled sources may appear only as manual links in the unverified pack (P304), as osint_investigator noted; reverse CNPJ lookups come from the RFB bulk import (P238).
P249.rationale: Rejected unanimously (0-6), as the synthesizer proposed: Casa dos Dados sits behind a Cloudflare challenge (rule 1, A9: manual link only), Brasil.IO is stale and keyed, the dados.gov.br catalogue has no entity-level value and the Open Ownership register is dead. Reverse lookups come lawfully from P238.
P249.title: Blocked/stale company sources (Casa dos Dados, Brasil.IO, dados.gov.br catalog, Open Ownership)

final_conditions: Ship data/pivot_links/brazil.json in the frozen P311 pack schema (label, template, entity_types, category, host, verified, checked_at, privacy, publishes=false, touches_target, login_required, antibot). The pack is offline data (disclosure 'none'): V3LUM never requests these URLs or any API behind them.

Rendering follows A2/P311: at TLP:AMBER and above every link is non-clickable text with 'opening sends <value> to <host>'; at RED third-party links are hidden from reports and listed only by `v3lum links` with the warning; links are never auto-opened and `links --open` at AMBER+ needs an interactive confirmation naming the host.

CI renders every template with a sample value per declared entity type and with hostile values (quotes, spaces, unicode, newlines): each result must be an https URL on the declared host, built only from whitelisted placeholders through the declared encoder (never str.format, never {raw} in URL position).

Every link host has a provider-registry entry with tier and rationale (A8); unknown-tier hosts get the 'unknown operator' badge and their templates take IOC_TYPES values only (A8 BR4): never PERSONAL_TYPES, CNPJ, company names, keywords, malware or actor names, or other free text (P311 lint).

Initial host tiers for the registry reviewer to confirm: trusted - Portal da Transparencia (CGU), Receita Federal, Sintegra/CCC, consumidor.gov.br, REDESIM/juntas comerciais, Jusbrasil, Reclame Aqui; community - Escavador, Casa dos Dados.

Order: P311 groups links by analyst question with verified links first; inside a group the pack's file order is the curated analyst-value order (Portal da Transparencia, Reclame Aqui, consumidor.gov.br, Jusbrasil, Escavador, Receita comprovante, Sintegra/CCC, REDESIM/juntas, Casa dos Dados); the terminal shows at most 8 links per seed, the rest go to HTML and `v3lum links`.

Verified links carry checked_at; `v3lum doctor --links` (offline) lists unverified links and links not re-checked for more than 180 days. The pack ships in phase 1 with the other pivot packs (A16), whatever the state of the related automated modules.

Portal da Transparencia: portaldatransparencia.gov.br/busca?termo= with the formatted CNPJ through the vetted {cnpj_fmt} placeholder (or digits, if verified and recorded) or the company name. The /pessoa-juridica/{cnpj} page (202 bot challenge) is not used as a template.

Rule 4 (legal floor): no template ever takes a CPF and no person-name or people-search template exists in this pack; CNPJ and company types only (the P311 lint rejects CPF templates, people-search panels and BNMP, P255).

BR company pack extensions (osint_investigator), each verified or shipped unverified with antibot=true when challenge-walled: Receita 'Comprovante de Inscricao' (CAPTCHA solved by the analyst in the browser), CCC/Sintegra state registration, Jusbrasil and Escavador web search by CNPJ/company.
Also Casa dos Dados, Reclame Aqui company search, consumidor.gov.br, and REDESIM/junta comercial pages where a stable URL exists (verified or unverified as above).
CNPJ templates use the P311 encoders (formatted, digits, 8-digit root) as each site expects; complaint sites (Reclame Aqui, consumidor.gov.br) are labelled 'consumer complaints: context, not proof'.
P250.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (osint_investigator voted P1). legal_dpo's rule 4 floor and the architect's formatted-CNPJ placeholder define the core link; osint_investigator's person-search links are not adopted because legal_dpo allows only CNPJ or company values here. His extension list is adopted as manual links: where automation is impossible (CAPTCHA, Cloudflare, geo-blocks), A9 makes manual links the lawful channel. A16 ships every pivot pack.
P250.title: Pivot links: Portal da Transparencia web search

final_conditions: One shared offline core helper (core/permute.py, disclosure none), reused by the e-mail pattern modules: NFKD accent stripping; particles {de, da, do, das, dos, e, di, du, del, van, von} dropped; suffixes {junior, jr, filho, neto, sobrinho} handled; last surname primary; Ceos priority patterns (f+l, f.l, f_l, f[0]+l...) plus maigret Permute 'strict' (MIT) in deterministic order.

<= 15 candidates per person. Corporate e-mail candidates only for domains in the case or org_profile, ranked by the domain's format inferred from observed addresses (commit e-mails, public pages) and shown with the number of samples behind it.

Candidates are hypotheses: a collapsible 'candidates (unverified guesses)' list, never findings and never scored; all are pivots with expand=False labelled 'generated'. The top 3 are offered first and reach username_check only after the analyst selects them; results for generated handles start at POSSIBLE.

Generated e-mails are never sent automatically to breach, stealer, reputation or validation services (a breach hit on a guessed address is an existence oracle by proxy, rule 2) and are never validated by SMTP (VRFY/EXPN/RCPT), login, sign-up or reset flows.

Category person_name: the module (name_permutations) is default_enabled False and runs only when the analyst selects it on an analyst-typed person_name seed (A3 BR2); the core helper itself stays available to the e-mail pattern modules. Unit tests: accents, particles, suffixes (fixture 'Jose Carlos de Oliveira Junior' with and without accents), the cap and the order.
P251.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. legal_dpo's floor makes every generated candidate a non-expanding hypothesis that only the analyst can send on; the architect's proposal to auto-expand the top 3 is therefore reduced to 'offered first'. osint_investigator's and redteam_lead's oracle-by-proxy and SMTP bans (rule 2), the architect's shared helper and cap, and analyst_ux's 'unverified guesses' presentation are kept. The draft's default_enabled True is lowered to False because A3 BR2 (legal floor) keeps person_name modules out of the default set. Offline: tier 'n/a', terms 'open'.
P251.title: Name -> username/e-mail permutations (accent and particle aware)

final_conditions: Core helper first (architect): homonym scoring lives in core/namematch.py and a correlation rule that lowers the confidence of every name-only match (P219, P221, P222, P240, P242, P243, P244, P254) by a documented curve. It emits no standalone findings and is always active, offline and allowed at TLP:RED.

Offline data: the IBGE first-name ranking (aggregate Census statistics, open data with attribution) as a dataset fetched by `v3lum data update`, plus a curated list of the most common Brazilian surnames (Silva, Santos, Oliveira, Souza, Pereira, Lima, Ferreira, Costa, Rodrigues, Almeida...), since IBGE covers first names only (cti_lead).

Online lookup (servicodados.ibge.gov.br censos/nomes/{first_name}) runs only inside the ibge_name_frequency module, through ScopedHttp and the policy gate (A8 BR10: the core helper makes no request): only the normalised first name, only for a name that already produced a name-only match and is missing from the offline table, never at TLP:RED; cached 365 days.

The thin module ibge_name_frequency for person seeds is opt-in (default_enabled=False, A3 person_name category); the helper above does not depend on it: without the module, names missing from the offline table get a neutral 'frequency unknown' score. An empty IBGE array means 'rare/unknown name', never an error.

Rendering: one short phrase on the match, e.g. 'very common first name: name-only matches are unreliable'. The frequency is never used to infer anything about the person (no per-UF origin, gender or age inference, P256).
Tests: 'JOSE DA SILVA' -> high homonym risk, a rare name -> low risk, an empty IBGE answer, and the confidence curve applied in P219 and P240; fixtures: the 4 IBGE captures.
P252.rationale: Approved 6-0. Priority raised from the tally's P2 (a 3-3 split: cti_lead, osint_investigator and analyst_ux voted P1) to P1 because the P1 screening modules P219 and P240 need the homonym score when they ship (dependency, effort S). The architect's floor makes it a shared helper in the matcher plus a thin opt-in module (A3: person_name modules are never default), and the default path is offline as analyst_ux asked; cti_lead added the surname list and the RED rule. legal_dpo: aggregate statistics, first name only, serving data quality (LGPD art. 6 V). Audit: the online IBGE lookup runs only inside the declared module (A8 BR10), never from the core helper.
P252.title: IBGE first-name frequency (homonym risk)

final_conditions: Source: GDELT DOC 2.0 (api.gdeltproject.org, community tier), keyless; its terms allow commercial use with citation, so reports cite 'The GDELT Project'. Format json preferred (RSS only through the safe XML helper).

Google News RSS is not automated: it is an unofficial endpoint with unknown terms, and A1 lets unknown-terms sources run in no profile (research included), which is stricter than the members' 'research profile only'. news.google.com/search?q= stays the manual pivot link (Module.manual_link).

Rule 6: one request per entity, the PT risk terms combined in one OR query; a provider-level token bucket of 1 request per 5 s per egress IP shared by every module and analyst (P334, team-shared quota DB behind one NAT); the 429 'limit requests' text body -> RATE_LIMITED, never 'no news'.

Query: distinctive name tokens in quotes plus the versioned PT risk-term list in data/ (fraude, corrupcao, preso, investigado, condenado, denuncia, golpe, lavagem, estelionato, improbidade, operacao, desvio, propina; for organisations vazamento, ransomware, ataque hacker, incidente, dados expostos, invasao; EN equivalents) with sourcelang:portuguese or sourcecountry:brazil.

Opt-in (default_enabled=False, A3 person_name category). Company names by default; person names only for subjects the analyst entered in a due-diligence case with a recorded purpose, never QSA partners or pivots, never for employment screening (legal_dpo).

Output: at most 10 headlines containing the exact name AND a risk term, clustered by story across outlets (title-similarity threshold as a named constant), each with outlet/source domain, date and URL only; articles are never fetched or scraped.
Hits are 'mentions' at INFO/LOW, never risk-scored until the analyst confirms, with the P252 homonym phrase on person names.
Merge gate: a positive GDELT fixture captured from the team network before merge (research has only '{}' and 429 bodies), plus the 429 body and an empty answer (A16).
P253.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3 (osint_investigator and legal_dpo voted P2). All members made GDELT primary and kept Google News RSS out of the corporate profile; A1 goes further (unknown terms never run), so Google News is a manual link only. The architect's floor: one combined query, a provider-level shared bucket, a positive fixture first, headline-level storage. legal_dpo's purpose-bound person queries and no employment screening, analyst_ux's 10-headline cap and osint_investigator's mention-not-finding rule complete it.
P253.title: Adverse-media search via Google News RSS

final_conditions: FBI Wanted (api.fbi.gov, US government public information): the cyber subject list is fetched as a dataset (daily, paged, <= 25 pages) and matched locally against threat_actor aliases from the P295 index, so no name is sent at query time (disclosure 'none' for matching).

Default use (still opt-in): threat_actor inputs, rendered on actor cards as 'N indicted individuals linked to <actor> - FBI' with poster links. person_name only for analyst-typed person seeds, matched locally; never QSA partners, pivots or names from text; no keyword lookups.

INTERPOL is not automated: its terms are unknown (A1: no profile) and the API sits behind Akamai bot protection (A9: manual link only). The red-notice web search is a manual pivot link; yellow notices (missing persons) are excluded entirely. No browser-UA spoofing or other evasion; a block is BLOCKED.
Matches are 'possible match - not identity proof' at INFO/MEDIUM, with name, aliases, charges and poster URL; photos are never downloaded, stored or compared (no biometrics).
Opt-in (default_enabled=False, A3 person_name category).

Merge gate (A16): offline tests with FakeHttp (unmatched requests fail, network guard active) over trimmed real fixtures without personal data (the FBI cyber capture plus a 403 sample), a provider-registry entry for every host, the registry contract test and the P327 lint.
P254.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. Local matching of the FBI list against actor aliases (cti_lead, the architect, legal_dpo, analyst_ux) keeps names on the host. INTERPOL is dropped from automation: legal_dpo found its terms unknown and A1 runs unknown terms in no profile, and A9 makes Akamai-walled sources manual links (cti_lead also excluded it). osint_investigator's no-biometrics and yellow-notice exclusion and analyst_ux's actor-card focus are kept.
P254.title: FBI Wanted (incl. Cyber's Most Wanted) + INTERPOL public notices

final_conditions: Never to be revisited: no module, dataset or pivot template for people-search panels, CPF-keyed personal lookups (Valores a Receber, Cadastro Pre), CPF brute force or warrant data; the P327 lint and the P311 link lint reject such hosts (team rules 2 and 4, LGPD).
P255.rationale: Rejected unanimously (0-6), as the synthesizer proposed: leaked-database 'paineis', CPF-keyed lookups meant for the data subject, CPF brute force and criminal-warrant data are exactly what team rule 4 (no people-search, CPF validated offline only), rule 2 and LGPD exclude. osint_investigator: no pivot templates for them either.
P255.title: Brazilian people-search panels and personal lookups (Tudo Sobre Todos, BuscaPrime, BCB Valores a Receber, Cadastro Pre, CPF brute force, BNMP)

final_conditions: Never to be revisited: no gender, age, nationality or ethnic-origin inference from names in any module (LGPD art. 5 II and 11, no sensitive-data inference).
P256.rationale: Rejected unanimously (0-6), as the synthesizer proposed: inferring gender, age or nationality from names has no investigative value, approximates ethnic origin (sensitive data, LGPD art. 5 II and 11) and sends names to a third party.
P256.title: Genderize / Agify / Nationalize name inference

final_conditions: Ship data/pivot_links/person.json in the frozen P311 pack schema (label, template, entity_types, category, host, verified, checked_at, privacy, publishes=false, touches_target, login_required, antibot), plus the optional per-link max_tlp field that the phase-0 schema must include. The pack is offline data (disclosure 'none'): V3LUM never requests these URLs or any API behind them.

Entry: webmii.com/people?n={name} for person_name, labelled 'people search engine - homonyms likely', with privacy=true (P311): rendered only for person entities the analyst typed as seeds and only when the analyst opts in for the case; never for QSA partners or names from text/documents (enforced in links.py, tested with a depth-1 QSA partner).
Legal floor: max_tlp=clear, so the link is rendered only in TLP:CLEAR cases; at any other TLP it appears only in `v3lum links` with the disclosure warning.

A8 gate: the provider registry must record Webmii as community tier (identifiable operator, terms, >= 2 years) before the link ships; if the reviewer records it as unknown, the link is dropped because unknown operators never receive person names.
The pack is opt-in (default_enabled=False) and hidden unless person_name modules are enabled for the case (architect). V3LUM never fetches the page.

CI renders every template with a sample value per declared entity type and with hostile values (quotes, spaces, unicode, newlines): each result must be an https URL on the declared host, built only from whitelisted placeholders through the declared encoder (never str.format, never {raw} in URL position).
P257.rationale: Approved 5-1 at median P3 (cti_lead rejected it as low value with privacy cost). legal_dpo's floor limits it to analyst-entered subjects at TLP:CLEAR with the people-search label; the architect's links.py seed-only gate and the 'hidden unless person modules are enabled' rule are adopted, with the homonym warning from osint_investigator and analyst_ux. A8 makes the link conditional on a community tier for Webmii. Opt-in, so default_enabled is false.
P257.title: Pivot links: person web presence (Webmii)

final_conditions: Rules CR32 shared_registrant_cluster, CR33 shell_company_indicators and CR34 identity_link_strength, plus the Ceos anti-homonym and cross-company heuristics. These correlations never create pivots and never expand anything.

CR34 levels: CONFIRMED only for cryptographic proof or an analyst decision. PROBABLE only with an explicit linkage signal kept as evidence (linked profile, non-default avatar dHash <= 8, Gravatar hash, PGP UID, Docker label). POSSIBLE = same handle only, labelled 'same handle does not prove identity'.
Links between natural persons are capped at PROBABLE without analyst confirmation, and an automatic level never rises above an analyst decision.

Avatar matching is image re-use detection only: dHash via the optional Pillow extra, on images already fetched by an approved passive module. Images are never stored (hash only), per-platform default avatars (a hash blocklist) never count, and there is no face recognition and no biometric template (LGPD art. 11).

CR33 is titled 'shell-company indicators (n of m)', never 'shell', 'laranja' or 'front', and is MEDIUM at most. It uses only official RFB fields (situacao, abertura, natureza juridica, porte/MEI, capital social, QSA). Named constants: opened < 1 year or lived < 2 years, AND MEI or capital < R$5,000, AND a shared address/phone/e-mail/co-partner. Each indicator is listed with its source.
Shared address/phone/e-mail signals are discounted when the contact is shared by >= 20 companies in the source, and labelled 'possible accountant/virtual office'.

Partner matching across companies needs the name plus compatible masked-CPF digits from QSA. A name-only match stays POSSIBLE, and IBGE name frequency (P252) lowers common names. Filiation, date of birth and other 'painel' attributes are never used.

Person names enter these rules automatically only from official registers (QSA/RFB) with the masked-CPF check above; any other name (free text, pages, pivots, RDAP legalRepresentative) is used only after analyst confirmation.

CPF is used only when the analyst supplied it or it is already present in collected official open data. It is masked in every output (***.456.789-**), never a pivot, and never looked up or sent to any third party (rule 4).

Person names from QSA and from RDAP legalRepresentative are never auto-expanded. Every CR32-CR34 finding is tagged privacy and excluded from STIX/MISP exports unless the analyst selects it (--include-personal).

The rules run only in cases with a recorded purpose (AR16). Outputs are suggestions requiring analyst validation, never the sole basis for a decision about a person (LGPD art. 20). Linked profiles are never used to infer sensitive data (art. 11).

Presentation: every identity link shows its level and evidence chain. POSSIBLE links appear only in the entity map and HTML details, never in the terminal top findings. Analyst decisions win and survive re-runs.

Tests: positive and negative graph fixtures, including a homonym case that stays POSSIBLE with the label, a default-avatar match that does not count, and an accountant contact shared by 20+ companies.
P258.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. These rules profile natural persons, so legal_dpo's floor governs: PROBABLE cap without analyst confirmation, CPF minimisation, no biometrics, no sensitive inference, a recorded purpose, art. 20. The architect's floor: never escalate or expand automatically, hashes only via the optional extra, named constants, a homonym fixture. osint_investigator removed the two classic false links (shared accountant contacts, default avatars). cti_lead asked for export exclusion, analyst_ux for visibility of level and evidence. redteam_lead found the synthesizer conditions sufficient. Auditor: cti_lead's export exclusion and analyst-confirmed names restored. default_enabled stays true because P258 is an offline, purpose-gated correlation pack, not a person_name source module (A3 BR2 as clarified).
P258.title: Correlation pack: identity links & company signals (CR32-CR34 + Céos identity/company heuristics)

final_conditions: FILE input only: this passive module never fetches URLs. An analyst-typed URL is downloaded only by the shared LIGHT file fetcher (--mode light, after the passive lane, P376 hostile-host guard fail closed, core address guard, 20 MB cap, P334 LIGHT budget, P324 ledger, archived copy preferred), which hands the module a file.

Parsing runs in the shared file-analysis sandbox core/sandbox.py: a python -I child process with a wall timeout, POSIX rlimits (memory <= 1 GiB, CPU, no file writes), input cap 100 MB and JSON output cap 1 MB; doctor reports the reduced isolation on Windows. Downloaded data is never executed.

Pillow (optional extra) with Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS set; DecompressionBombError becomes an ERROR result with a clear reason; ExifRead (BSD-3) is the optional fallback for HEIC/RAW; ExifTool (GPL) only as an external binary on PATH (A6).

Extracted: EXIF/XMP/IPTC dates, camera make/model/serial and software as attributes; editing software (Photoshop, GIMP...) as an INFO tag; an EXIF thumbnail whose aspect ratio differs from the main image flagged 'possible crop/edit'.

GPS becomes a coordinates pivot (relation photo_taken_at) with the privacy tag, never auto-expanded: no automatic reverse geocoding, map, Wi-Fi or other lookup; map links are privacy=true manual links shown only after the analyst confirms for that image (legal_dpo).

Legal floor: no face detection or recognition of any kind (no biometrics). GPS, camera serials and owner fields are stripped from STIX/MISP exports unless the analyst opts in for the case, and GPS is shown only inside the case report.

Plain-language summary first ('taken 2026-03-01 14:22 with <make/model>, GPS present'), stating that missing EXIF is normal (WhatsApp, Telegram, social platforms and screenshots strip it) and that EXIF can be edited; missing EXIF is never a finding.
Tests use synthetic images generated in the tests (the research JPEG prototype with GPS) plus a decompression-bomb image and a truncated file. Offline: disclosure 'none', default-on (A3).
P259.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (osint_investigator, legal_dpo and the architect voted P1). The architect's floor removes the url input from this passive module and sandboxes the parser. redteam_lead, cti_lead and osint_investigator's LIGHT-only download through the egress guard becomes one shared fetcher. legal_dpo's floor forbids face processing, automatic geocoding and GPS in exports. analyst_ux's and osint_investigator's wording on missing or editable EXIF and the thumbnail check are kept.
P259.title: Image metadata (EXIF/XMP/IPTC/GPS, camera serials)

final_conditions: Ship data/pivot_links/geo_image.json in the frozen P311 pack schema (label, template, entity_types, category, host, verified, checked_at, privacy, publishes=false, touches_target, login_required, antibot), plus the optional per-link max_tlp field that the phase-0 schema must include. The pack is offline data (disclosure 'none'): V3LUM never requests these URLs or any API behind them.

Rendering follows A2/P311: at TLP:AMBER and above every link is non-clickable text with 'opening sends <value> to <host>'; at RED third-party links are hidden from reports and listed only by `v3lum links` with the warning; links are never auto-opened and `links --open` at AMBER+ needs an interactive confirmation naming the host.

CI renders every template with a sample value per declared entity type and with hostile values (quotes, spaces, unicode, newlines): each result must be an https URL on the declared host, built only from whitelisted placeholders through the declared encoder (never str.format, never {raw} in URL position).

Every link host has a provider-registry entry with tier and rationale (A8); unknown-tier hosts get the 'unknown operator' badge and their templates take IOC_TYPES values only (A8 BR4): never PERSONAL_TYPES, CNPJ, company names, keywords, malware or actor names, or other free text (P311 lint).
Initial host tiers for the registry reviewer to confirm: trusted - Google Lens/Maps, Yandex (RU jurisdiction), TinEye, OpenStreetMap Foundation; unknown - ImgOps (URL values only).

Order: P311 groups links by analyst question with verified links first; inside a group the pack's file order is the curated analyst-value order (TinEye, Google Lens, ImgOps, Yandex for images; OSM first, then Google Maps for coordinates); the terminal shows at most 8 links per seed, the rest go to HTML and `v3lum links`.

Verified links carry checked_at; `v3lum doctor --links` (offline) lists unverified links and links not re-checked for more than 180 days. The pack ships in phase 1 with the other pivot packs (A16), whatever the state of the related automated modules.

Reverse-image templates (lens.google.com/uploadbyurl?url=, yandex.com/images/search?rpt=imageview&url=, tineye.com/search?url=, imgops.com/<encoded url>) only for public http(s) image URLs (known image extension or content type): never page URLs (they may carry victim identifiers), file://, data:, private IPs or internal hosts, and never FILE entities (no upload path).

Legal floor (no biometrics, LGPD art. 11): a standing label above the reverse-image links reads 'not for identifying people from facial images: use for impersonation, fake-profile and cloned-logo checks within the case purpose'; no links are generated for images extracted from documents or files.

Yandex carries 'foreign provider (RU): the URL goes to a Russian operator' and max_tlp=green, so at TLP:AMBER+ it is listed only by `v3lum links` (redteam_lead, analyst_ux); the other engines follow the default A2 rendering.

Map templates (openstreetmap.org/?mlat=&mlon=, google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=) take lat/lon from the normalised coordinates through a vetted placeholder and are privacy=true: shown only for coordinates already in the case after the analyst opts in. Image templates use the URL-encoded value, never {raw}.
P260.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (osint_investigator voted P1, cti_lead P3). legal_dpo's floor keeps reverse-image search away from facial identification (P266 rejects face engines) with the label osint_investigator also asked for. The architect's placeholder rules make the templates injection-safe. redteam_lead's image-URL-only rule and his and analyst_ux's hiding of the Russian engine at AMBER+ are adopted; maps are privacy-gated per P311 and P259.
P260.title: Pivot links: reverse image search & maps (Google Lens, Yandex, TinEye, ImgOps, Google Maps, OSM)

final_conditions: Offline module: disclosure 'none' (no network at all; ScopedHttp refuses any request), terms 'open', provider tier 'n/a'; allowed at TLP:RED. FILE input only; an analyst-typed image URL is downloaded only by the shared LIGHT file fetcher defined in P269 (--mode light, typed seeds, P376 guard, address guard, 20 MB cap).

Decoder: zxing-cpp as an optional extra v3lum[qr] (Apache-2.0, small binary wheels for Linux, macOS and Windows, CPython >= 3.11; it also reads the ITF barcodes printed on boletos). OpenCV and pyzbar (system zbar) are not used. A missing extra gives UNAVAILABLE reason_code 'package' ('pip install v3lum[qr]').

Parsing runs in the shared file-analysis sandbox core/sandbox.py: a python -I child process with a wall timeout, POSIX rlimits (memory <= 1 GiB, CPU, no file writes), input cap 100 MB and JSON output cap 1 MB; doctor reports the reduced isolation on Windows. Downloaded data is never executed. Pillow's pixel cap applies; each payload is capped at 4 KB.

Every code in the image is decoded and reported. Routing: URLs become url entities with provenance qr and go only to passive URL reputation, never fetched or opened (a tokenised QR URL would confirm the scan to the phisher); PIX payloads and boleto ITF codes go to the P233 parser functions called directly; other text goes to the shared P172 IOC extractor.
Display: payload type and defanged value ('QR -> URL hxxps://...'). No code decoded reads 'no QR/barcode found', never 'clean'.
Fixtures: small QR and ITF PNGs generated once with a dev-only encoder and committed (benign URL, PIX BR Code with a valid CRC, boleto line), plus a multi-code image and an oversized image.
P261.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (osint_investigator and legal_dpo voted P1): quishing and tampered PIX QR codes are common in Brazil. The architect's floor picks zxing-cpp, which also covers the boleto barcodes osint_investigator wanted, instead of OpenCV or pyzbar, inside the shared sandbox. Every member agreed decoded URLs are never fetched (redteam_lead: fetching confirms the scan). cti_lead's and analyst_ux's routing and wording are kept.
P261.title: QR/barcode decoding from images (quishing, PIX QR)

final_conditions: Nominatim (nominatim.openstreetmap.org) per the OSMF usage policy: identifying UA with the contact_email role mailbox only on OSM hosts (P326; SKIPPED reason_code 'config' without it), provider bucket 1 req/s per installation, no bulk geocoding, cache 30 days; 403 'Access denied' -> BLOCKED (rule 5).
Photon (photon.komoot.io, returns [lon, lat]) is the only fallback. Overpass and geocode.xyz are dropped (unreachable or throttled, no success fixtures). Tiers: OSMF trusted, komoot community.

Inputs: coordinates and cep; text_blob is removed (geocoding pasted text would disclose it) and keyword is accepted only as an explicit address-style TYPE:value. Address search falls back street -> postal code -> city.

Legal floor: reverse geocoding runs by default only for coordinates the analyst typed as seeds; coordinates from photos (EXIF), devices or other sources that may locate a natural person are geocoded only after a per-entity analyst confirmation. Forward geocoding of company addresses (CNPJ/CEP records, typed addresses) runs on explicit request.

Coordinates are PERSONAL_TYPES (A8): the module enters the effective default set only after personal_data_review is recorded for these providers; until then it runs only when selected in a case with a recorded purpose (reason_code 'privacy'). Coordinates are never auto-expanded.

Results are labelled 'approximate place (OSM)' with the precision level (street/postcode/city) and 'an address is not proof of residence'; reports carry '(c) OpenStreetMap contributors' (ODbL). Map links come from P260. Places derived from coordinates that may locate a person stay in the case and are left out of STIX/MISP exports unless the analyst opts in (as P259 GPS).

Merge gate (A16): offline tests with FakeHttp (unmatched requests fail, network guard active) over trimmed real fixtures without personal data (the Nominatim and Photon captures plus a 403 sample), a provider-registry entry for every host, the registry contract test and the P327 lint.
P262.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3 (osint_investigator, legal_dpo and analyst_ux voted P2). The architect's floor: identifying UA from config, a 1 req/s provider bucket, Photon as the only fallback, no text_blob input. legal_dpo's and osint_investigator's floor: coordinates that may locate a person are geocoded only on analyst confirmation. analyst_ux's default of reverse geocoding typed coordinates is kept behind the A3/A8 personal-data review.
P262.title: Geocoding / reverse geocoding (Nominatim, Photon, Overpass, geocode.xyz)

final_conditions: BACKLOG unblock: legal clears at least one source (WiGLE free accounts are non-commercial; beaconDB and Mylnikov publish no terms) and a purpose-bound design exists: multi-value input with >= 2 BSSIDs, considerIp=false, case justification and privacy tag (architect, legal_dpo).
P263.rationale: Deferred mechanically (1 yes, 1 reject, 4 defer). Every source is non-commercial or unknown-terms, so under the corporate profile the module would do nothing (legal_dpo); geolocating access points can locate people's homes (cti_lead); and the per-entity API cannot pass the >= 2 BSSIDs beaconDB needs (architect). P315 gives vendor context offline meanwhile.
P263.title: Wi-Fi BSSID geolocation (beaconDB, Mylnikov, WiGLE)

final_conditions: Offline module: disclosure 'none' (no network at all; ScopedHttp refuses any request), terms 'open', provider tier 'n/a'; allowed at TLP:RED. Opt-in (default_enabled=False).

Parsing runs in the shared file-analysis sandbox core/sandbox.py: a python -I child process with a wall timeout, POSIX rlimits (memory <= 1 GiB, CPU, no file writes), input cap 100 MB and JSON output cap 1 MB; doctor reports the reduced isolation on Windows. Downloaded data is never executed.
JPEG inputs only: PNG and other lossless images (most PIX-receipt screenshots) are SKIPPED reason_code 'not_applicable' with 'ELA not meaningful for lossless images'.

Method: Pillow re-save at a fixed quality (q90) and ImageChops.difference. Output: numeric metrics (mean/max error level, region statistics) as attributes plus an optional ELA PNG in the case directory, embedded in HTML reports only as a data: image.

Wording: severity INFO with 'heuristic, not proof of tampering'; it never raises severity or the score on its own. The terminal shows only 'ELA map in the HTML report (heuristic, not proof)', never a bare tamper number (analyst_ux's concern).
Tests use synthetic fixtures generated in the tests: an original and an edited JPEG, a PNG that must be skipped.
P264.rationale: Approved 4-2 at median P3 (cti_lead and analyst_ux rejected: ELA misleads on recompressed images). The objections are met structurally: JPEG only (osint_investigator, architect), numeric informational output that never raises severity, and no tamper number in the terminal. The architect's sandbox and data:-image rules apply, and it is opt-in.
P264.title: Error Level Analysis (image tamper heuristic)

final_conditions: Not revisited: evidence images are never uploaded to third-party recognition services, plate-to-owner lookups stay forbidden (LGPD, Detran), and offline plate validation lives in br_validators (P232).
P265.rationale: Rejected unanimously (0-6), as the synthesizer proposed: it uploads evidence images to a third party for low value (2), plate-to-owner lookups are forbidden anyway, and br_validators already validates plates offline.
P265.title: Plate Recognizer ALPR API

final_conditions: Never to be revisited: no facial-recognition search, face-engine upload or pivot link to face engines in any module or pack (no biometrics, LGPD art. 11); the P311 link lint rejects PimEyes, FaceCheck.ID, Search4faces and similar hosts.
P266.rationale: Rejected unanimously (0-6), as the synthesizer proposed: facial-recognition search is biometric processing of sensitive personal data (LGPD art. 11), breaks the team's no-biometrics rule and uploads evidence to paid third parties; osint_investigator adds no links to face engines either.
P266.title: Facial-recognition search engines (PimEyes, FaceCheck.ID, Search4faces...)

final_conditions: Offline module file_analysis/file_hashing (disclosure none): regular files only (os.stat S_ISREG; FIFOs, devices and sockets are refused so /dev/zero cannot hang a run), streamed in 1 MB chunks with ctx.cancelled() checks; MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256 and SHA-512 always.

ssdeep via ppdeep (pure Python, Apache-2.0, optional extra) only for files <= 50 MB. TLSH computation is omitted in this build because py-tlsh ships no wheels; TLSH values returned by providers are kept as attributes.

Hash-type identification is a shared detector helper with ambiguity flagged (sha256 vs certificate fingerprint): non-TTY runs try both readings, a TTY may let the analyst choose. Identification only: no cracking and no plaintext lookup (hashes.com, CrackStation, ntlm.pw excluded); password-hash formats are only labelled.
Emitted hash entities feed the hash chain (P173 first). Tests: a regular file, FIFO refusal, large-file streaming and the ambiguity handling.
P267.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. The architect's floor (regular files only, no wheel-less compiled dependency) and analyst_ux's non-TTY 'try both' rule are added to the unanimous identification-only scope. Offline: tier 'n/a', terms 'open'.
P267.title: Local file hashing (MD5/SHA-1/SHA-256/SHA-512, ssdeep via ppdeep, TLSH) + hash type identification

final_conditions: Offline module malware_hash/lol_datasets (disclosure none) on the dataset manager, refreshed weekly out of band (the stale copy is served during scans): LOLDrivers drivers.json (36 MB, Apache-2.0), LOLBAS api/lolbas.json (GPL-3.0 data), HijackLibs (GPL-3.0, LICENSE verified 2026-11-26) and LOLRMM api/rmm_tools.json (Apache-2.0).
LOLBAS and HijackLibs are downloaded at runtime into ~/.v3lum/datasets and never bundled (A6); LOLDrivers and LOLRMM are attributed in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.
LOLDrivers is indexed at refresh into a slim projection (sha256/sha1/md5/authentihash -> driver id, category, verified, ATT&CK); the full JSON is never memoised in memory.

Mapping: a LOLDrivers hash hit is a finding: malicious driver -> malware (high); vulnerable driver -> vulnerable/BYOVD (medium, high on an org asset); ATT&CK ids -> uses_technique pivots. Hash matching comes first.

LOLBAS, HijackLibs and LOLRMM name matches are info context only (never scored, never malicious alone), shown once per binary with the abuse technique; file names collide, so name matches are low confidence; the rmm_tool tag is context because legitimate IT use is common. CIRCL known-file status never suppresses them (P173).
P268.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. legal_dpo's runtime-only GPL data (HijackLibs licence verified), the architect's slim index instead of a 36 MB in-memory JSON, and cti_lead's and analyst_ux's 'hash hits are findings, name hits are context' are consolidated; osint_investigator's LOLRMM note on fake bank call-centre scams supports the rmm_tool tag. GPL data at runtime is 'open' under the A1 definitions; offline: tier 'n/a'.
P268.title: LOLDrivers, LOLBAS and HijackLibs datasets

final_conditions: FILE input only: this passive module never fetches URLs. An analyst-typed URL is downloaded only by the shared LIGHT file fetcher (--mode light, after the passive lane, P376 hostile-host guard fail closed, core address guard, 20 MB cap, P334 LIGHT budget, P324 ledger, archived copy preferred), which hands the module a file.

Ownership: core/sandbox.py (used by P259, P261, P264, P271, P272, P287, P363, P364, P367, P368) and the shared LIGHT file fetcher (used by P259, P261, P287, P364) are core pieces built with this P1 item; no module writes its own (no chunk-D AR action owns them).

The fetcher is LIGHT target contact (A7): analyst-typed seed URLs only (never pivots, BR5), GET only, ua_light UA, <= 1 req/s and <= 25 requests per host per scan, manual redirects re-checked by the guards. URLs that probably carry a per-recipient token (an org_profile e-mail in plain, URL-encoded or base64 form, or an opaque token >= 16 chars) need a per-URL confirmation (BR15).

Merge gate for the fetcher: it is LIGHT, so it is not merged or enabled before the AR20 safety suite passes (A16 BR6); until then URL inputs of the file modules get the manual pivot link and the passive modules keep working on FILE inputs.

Parsing runs in the shared file-analysis sandbox core/sandbox.py: a python -I child process with a wall timeout, POSIX rlimits (memory <= 1 GiB, CPU, no file writes), input cap 100 MB and JSON output cap 1 MB; doctor reports the reduced isolation on Windows. Downloaded data is never executed. The wall timeout matters: pypdf has had infinite-loop CVEs on crafted PDFs.

Formats: PDF info and XMP via pypdf (BSD-3; dates D:YYYYMMDDHHmmSSOHH'mm' parsed to ISO); OOXML/ODF docProps through the core safe archive helper (member count, total size and ratio caps) and the safe XML helper (DOCTYPE and entity declarations rejected); OLE metadata and VBA presence via olefile (BSD); .msg through olefile streams (__substg1.0_*), not the GPL extract-msg.
oletools is only an optional extra for olevba keywords (it pulls extra dependencies); macros are never executed, documents never rendered, and encrypted files never decrypted with guessed passwords.

External relationships (TargetMode=External, attachedTemplate, remote OLE/frame links, UNC and WebDAV paths, external hyperlinks) become hostile url/domain pivots tagged remote_template, for passive modules only; they are never fetched or resolved over HTTP, SMB or WebDAV (fetching is the beacon that tells the sender the document was opened).

Severity table (tested): remote template / external relationship = HIGH (T1221); auto-exec macro (AutoOpen, Document_Open, Workbook_Open), XLM 4.0 macro sheets and DDE fields = HIGH, worded 'suspicious' unless a hash/family source confirms; macro present = MEDIUM; PDF /Launch or /JavaScript with /OpenAction = HIGH, /EmbeddedFile = MEDIUM; PDF URIs = url pivots.

Personal data (legal floor): author, lastModifiedBy and company are INFO attributes; author names become person_name pivots (relation document_author) and C:\Users\<name> paths username pivots (relation local_account), both expand=False with the privacy tag and never auto-checked by username, e-mail or person modules (A5).
Internal paths, usernames and author names are redacted in external sharing exports (STIX/MISP) unless the analyst passes --include-personal (recorded). One summary line per document.
Tests on synthetic fixtures built in tests: the research PDF/DOCX prototypes, a docx with a remote template, an XXE docx, a zip-bomb docx, a macro-bearing OLE file and a PDF with OpenAction.
P269.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1: phishing attachments are a daily input. The architect's floor sets the sandbox, FILE-only input, safe archive/XML helpers and the olefile baseline with oletools optional. redteam_lead, cti_lead and osint_investigator insisted that remote templates and UNC links are recorded and never touched. legal_dpo's floor keeps author names and usernames from triggering sweeps and out of exports. analyst_ux's severity table is adopted with cti_lead's 'suspicious, not malicious' wording. Audit: this item also owns core/sandbox.py and the shared LIGHT file fetcher, which carries the A7 LIGHT limits, the token-URL rule and the AR20 gate.
P269.title: PDF/Office metadata (authors, software, internal paths, macros, remote templates)

final_conditions: Offline module: disclosure 'none' (no network at all; ScopedHttp refuses any request), terms 'open', provider tier 'n/a'; allowed at TLP:RED. Exposed as a library function that every file module calls, so routing logic is not duplicated.

An own magic table (bundled data with offsets, tested per type) is the default and needs no dependency. It covers at least PE, ELF, Mach-O, ZIP, OOXML, OLE, PDF, RAR, 7z, ISO, LNK, MSI, OneNote, APK/JAR and script types (HTA, JS, VBS, PS1, batch by heuristics), so every approved file parser is reachable.
It reads at most the first 64 KB plus the zip central directory (through the safe archive helper) to tell OOXML, APK and JAR apart.
Licences (A6): filetype.py (MIT) may be an optional extra; Magika (onnxruntime) and python-magic (system libmagic) are not used in this build; hachoir (GPL-2.0) is never imported or bundled.

Findings, tested: executable content behind a document or image extension, or a double extension such as invoice.pdf.exe = HIGH; other extension/content mismatches = MEDIUM; polyglots (e.g. PDF+ZIP) = MEDIUM at POSSIBLE confidence. Shown as 'claimed .pdf, actually PE32 executable'.
Fixtures: tiny synthetic files per type generated in tests, plus a double-extension PE and a PDF+ZIP polyglot.
P270.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1 (redteam_lead voted P2). The architect's floor: a dependency-free bundled magic table, a 64 KB read limit, no Magika/libmagic in this build and a shared routing function. legal_dpo and every member keep hachoir (GPL) out, per A6. cti_lead's coverage list makes every approved parser reachable; analyst_ux's severity and wording are adopted.
P270.title: File type detection (own magic table; filetype/Magika/libmagic optional; hachoir ideas)

final_conditions: Offline module: disclosure 'none' (no network at all; ScopedHttp refuses any request), terms 'open', provider tier 'n/a'; allowed at TLP:RED. FILE input only; the sample is never executed.

pefile (pure Python, MIT) with fast_load, parsing only the IMPORT, EXPORT, RESOURCE and DEBUG directories, with caps on section and import counts.

Outputs: compile timestamp (zero, future or pre-2000 values such as the Delphi 1992 stamp flagged 'unreliable/forged'), imphash, Rich header hash, sections with entropy, imports, packer hints, Authenticode presence with signer subject/issuer/serial recorded as 'signed, not verified' (no claim of validity), and the PDB path.

Pivots: imphash and the signer become pivots with expand=False for hash-lookup modules once the P333 types exist (until then attributes, never free-text keywords); md5/sha256 of the file are hash pivots; the Rich hash stays an attribute.
Privacy: PDB paths and the usernames or machine names inside them are attributes with the privacy tag, never username entities, so they never trigger username checks (osint_investigator, legal_dpo).

Packer hints and high entropy are context, not verdicts; they are downgraded when a known-good source in the case marks the hash (CIRCL hashlookup without KnownMalicious, P169 known-good lists), because a hashlookup hit alone is not proof of good.
Fixtures: small benign PE files built for the tests (no malware in the repository; EICAR string only) plus a truncated and a malformed PE.
P271.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (cti_lead and legal_dpo voted P1). The architect's floor: pefile in the shared sandbox with fast_load and caps, no claim of signature validity, benign fixtures only. cti_lead's outputs (Rich hash, signer, unreliable timestamps, known-good check) and osint_investigator's rule that PDB usernames stay attributes are adopted.
P271.title: PE header/imports/imphash triage (pefile)

final_conditions: yara-python (Apache-2.0) as the optional extra v3lum[yara]; its wheels cover CPython 3.10-3.13, so on other versions or without the extra the module is UNAVAILABLE reason_code 'package' ('pip install v3lum[yara]'). Opt-in (default_enabled=False).

Rules come only as source from the YARA Forge release zip on GitHub through the dataset manager (sha256 recorded), are compiled locally per source file with failures isolated and counted, and are cached compiled locally (yara.Rules.save); compiled rules are never loaded from the network. Rule packs are downloaded at runtime, never bundled or redistributed (A6).

Licence (legal floor, per rule from meta): permissive (MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, CC0, CC BY) and DRL 1.1 rules (author attribution kept) are class open and load under the corporate profile. Non-commercial rules are class 'noncommercial': off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared.
Rules with an unknown or missing licence meta are never loaded in any profile. Excluded rules are counted in the coverage table ('N rules excluded: licence').
YARA Forge core package by default (lowest false-positive rate); extended/full only by flag.

Downloaded data is never executed. Local files only, with a 30 s match timeout per file.

Results: rule name, author, reference, score and package version per hit. Generic or heuristic rules (SUSP_, HKTL_, PUA_ prefixes or score < 70) give 'suspicious' low-severity context only; a malware_family pivot (low confidence) is created only from a family-specific rule with a family meta; never a 'malicious' verdict from hunting rules alone.

The architect's floor: optional extra, local compilation from source only, sandboxed scans with a 30 s timeout. cti_lead, osint_investigator and analyst_ux limit family attribution to family-specific rules and default to the core pack. The provider (YARA Forge, a community project on GitHub) is community tier.
P272.title: Optional YARA scanning (YARA Forge core pack, signature-base rules)

final_conditions: Offline module: disclosure 'none' (no network at all; ScopedHttp refuses any request), terms 'open', provider tier 'n/a'; allowed at TLP:RED. Opt-in (default_enabled=False).

Legal floor: runs only on documents attached to the current case (analyst-provided files and text) and for person seeds the analyst typed; a cpf input only searches inside those documents and never triggers any lookup (rule 4).

Works on the text produced by P269/P363 through the shared P172 extraction engine and the P232 CPF validator (no own PDF parsing). Name windows are bounded (<= 200 characters); only the CPF nearest to the subject's name counts, so a neighbour's CPF cannot attach to the subject; a city near the name is a strong signal, a UF only a weak one.

Never creates CPF entities: the nearest CPF is stored only masked (***.XXX.XXX-**) in attributes and evidence, never pivoted, never sent, and never compared automatically with QSA or other sources' masked CPFs (no CPF-fragment joins, P236 legal floor); the analyst reads the pair.

No cross-case name<->CPF index is ever built or persisted: name-CPF pairs are excluded from the P375 sightings index (even as HMAC) and from STIX/MISP exports; results carry the privacy tag and follow A10 retention.
Tests use synthetic text fixtures: a gazette-style list with several names and CPFs (nearest-CPF rule), a name with no CPF nearby and a masked-output assertion in every renderer.
P273.rationale: Approved 5-0-1 at median P3 (analyst_ux deferred). legal_dpo's floor keeps it inside the case's own documents with no persistent name-CPF index, so osint_investigator's HMAC entry in the sightings index is not adopted. cti_lead's automatic confirmation against QSA masked CPFs is not adopted either, because legal_dpo forbids CPF-fragment joins across sources. The architect's floor reuses the shared extractor and never creates CPF entities.
P273.title: Identity signals in free text / PDFs (name windows + nearest CPF) - Céos port

final_conditions: Requires key 'leakix' (already registered), sent in the api-key header; 401 'Invalid API key' gives NEEDS_KEY. Key-terms: a company/team account on a plan recorded by legal before it runs under corporate; free 3,000 requests go into the P334 budget.

LeakIX is a sensitive provider: a field ALLOWLIST at ingestion, before res.raw and the HTTP cache (P145 schema): host, port, protocol, path, event type, plugin/leak type, severity and first/last seen. 'summary' and any leak, dataset or excerpt content are dropped; a test asserts the evidence JSON contains no summary text from the fixture.
Metadata only: leaked content, credentials and database samples are never fetched, stored or printed (rule 3).

Runs on seeds and org_profile own assets; events on pivoted third-party assets are recorded as counts only (existence, type, severity counts). Exposed database/config findings on org_profile assets are HIGH, with the LeakIX page as manual link.

Events older than 90 days are historical ('re-verify'). A leak is never confirmed by fetching the exposed resource from the target outside an ACTIVE authorized scope, and then only status and size, never contents.
Hits on CDN/shared IPs (P034) are attributed to the hostname, not to the IP owner.
Merge only with a trimmed real success fixture captured with the team key, plus the recorded 401 fixtures.
P274.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (architect and analyst_ux voted P3). The architect's floor and redteam_lead: LeakIX summaries embed the exposed data, so an allowlist scrub runs before the cache and evidence. legal_dpo's floor: key-terms, metadata only, no leaked content. cti_lead and osint_investigator: own assets first, counts for third parties, 90-day history, HIGH for own exposed databases. Key-required sources may be default-enabled (A3 BR5). LeakIX is a small identifiable operator: tier community.
P274.title: LeakIX (exposed services and leaks, keyed)

final_conditions: Core ctx.tls handshake helper first (architect floor), shared with core/tls.py (P329): stdlib ssl through the core socket connector honouring the egress profile (CONNECT via the profile proxy, SOCKS via optional PySocks, names resolved through the profile), 10 s timeout, returning the DER chain; no raw socket leaves outside the profile.

LIGHT module: default_enabled=False, not merged or enabled before the AR20 safety suite passes. Analyst-typed seeds only, never pivots, after the entity's passive lane, through the P376 egress guard (hostile hosts only via a non-corporate egress, fail closed).

One handshake per host per run within the P334 LIGHT budget; protocol/cipher probing stays in the ACTIVE tls_protocol_scan. Public addresses only unless the IP is in an authorized scope. In passive mode certificate facts come from CT (P001) and indexed scan data.

Interception detection: when the system store verifies and a context loaded only with certifi's Mozilla bundle fails ('self-signed certificate in chain'), record intercepted_by=<issuer> per egress profile and suppress all certificate findings.
Suppression is never silent: a banner in terminal and HTML ('TLS interception by <issuer> detected on this network: certificate findings suppressed'), a coverage note, and doctor shows it (P329).
Analysis is a pure function over the chain; certificates are parsed with the optional 'cryptography' extra, with a stdlib getpeercert() fallback for chains that verify.

Hygiene findings (expired HIGH, < 14 d MEDIUM, < 30 d LOW, hostname mismatch HIGH, self-signed MEDIUM, RSA < 2048 / EC < 256 MEDIUM, SHA-1 MEDIUM) apply only to org_profile own assets and in-scope targets.

For other hosts they are info context; on hostile hosts cert facts are attributes (issuer, fingerprint for hunting), and phishing-relevant signals (cert issued < 7 days, free DV cert on a brand lookalike) feed correlations.

SANs become cert_san domain pivots; SANs outside the queried apex are expand=False. Certificates with > 20 SANs across > 5 registrable domains, or CDN/shared-hosting certificates (P034), give an attribute only and are excluded from CR31. The fingerprint becomes a cert_fingerprint pivot.

Tests use a FakeTls (tests/fakes.py) with real PEM fixtures, no network: an intercepted chain gives the banner and no cert findings; an expired own-asset certificate gives HIGH; the same certificate on a third-party host gives info.
P275.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1 (cti_lead and osint_investigator voted P2). A handshake is LIGHT, so the module is opt-in (A3 BR2) and gated on the safety suite (A16); passive certificate facts come from CT, as osint_investigator noted. The architect's floor: an injectable ctx.tls helper with FakeTls tests, a pure analysis function, the optional cryptography extra. redteam_lead: the socket must follow the egress profile, one handshake per host, seeds only. cti_lead, redteam_lead and analyst_ux: ownership-scoped severity, shared-certificate rule, visible interception banner. Target contact: tier n/a; stdlib/Apache code: terms open.
P275.title: TLS certificate inspection with interception detection

final_conditions: Two modules over one fingerprint helper (opsec is per class, architect): takeover_candidates (PASSIVE, default_enabled=True as a DoH-based DNS module, A3) and takeover_verify (ACTIVE, default_enabled=False). The chair-file default refers to the ACTIVE verifier.

Fingerprints: can-i-take-over-xyz fingerprints.json (CC BY 4.0, attribution in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES and reports), pinned by commit and SHA-256 (data/active.lock), refreshed only by `v3lum data update` with a diff summary. Only 'Vulnerable' rows give a candidate, 'Edge case' rows MEDIUM, 'Not vulnerable' rows are never reported.

takeover_candidates: CNAME chain through the core DoH resolver (ECS disabled, P029) for analyst-typed seeds, org_profile domains and names under the typed apex; SAN affiliates and names outside the apex are not checked. Dangling evidence = NXDOMAIN of the CNAME target confirmed by a second resolver, tested with ctx.dns.wildcard so Cloudflare NOERROR/NODATA zones are not misread.

Rule 5: SERVFAIL, REFUSED or a timeout on the chain = could not verify, never 'not vulnerable'. Candidate wording: 'possible takeover candidate (DNS evidence only)' with the CNAME chain and fingerprint, HIGH at PROBABLE confidence on own assets and typed seeds (CR07, T1584.001), INFO on third-party domains.
Dangling A/AAAA records pointing at released cloud IPs are reported from passive evidence only (CR08): the current holder of the IP is another customer and is never contacted.

ACTIVE gate (A7): runs only with --mode active, a non-empty --authorized REF and a --scope FILE on every path (scan, run, shell, watch, batch; non-interactive runs refuse without both), on scope-file matches only after resolution and per redirect hop, never on pivots or on entities extracted from text/files; CDN/shared-hosting/SaaS IPs excluded unless listed.

A7 ceilings enforced by the core client and socket connector: <= 10 requests/probes per second and <= 2 concurrent connections per target host, the case ACTIVE budget, the kill switch (traffic stops within 2 s), proxy_active egress profile (A13), the hostile-host guard, and every request in the hash-chained P324 ledger; the report banner carries REF, scope SHA-256, window and egress.

takeover_verify: HTTP GET/HEAD of the in-scope name through the core client to match the provider's body fingerprint, plus a random-label wildcard probe under the same parent. Results are tri-state: confirmed (confidence CONFIRMED) / not observed / could not test (blocked egress, proxy or errors), never 'safe'.

Forbidden (A7): claiming, registering or creating the dangling resource, and any provider API call; a unit test asserts that only GET/HEAD reach the target and no provider API host is contacted. For non-owned candidates the report shows the owner's security.txt contact; notification is a manual, separately approved action and nothing is verified further.

Merge gate: takeover_verify is not merged or enabled before the AR20 safety suite passes (A16); fixtures: the CNAME DoH captures, a Cloudflare NODATA zone and recorded provider error pages (e.g. S3 'The specified bucket does not exist').
Licences (A6): the multi-resolver and wildcard verifier logic is re-implemented from theHarvester's documented behaviour (GPL-2.0, ideas only); no code is copied.
P276.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (redteam_lead and the architect voted P1). The architect's floor splits it into a PASSIVE candidate module and an ACTIVE verifier over one helper; redteam_lead's and legal_dpo's A7 floor gate the verifier (scope-file names only, ledger, never claim). The A7 limit of 2 connections per host, stricter than legal_dpo's 4, applies. analyst_ux wanted MEDIUM before active proof: the chair keeps cti_lead's and redteam_lead's HIGH for 'Vulnerable' rows but labels DNS-only evidence PROBABLE, with CONFIRMED reserved for the verifier. The passive half is default-on; the ACTIVE verifier never is.
P276.title: Subdomain takeover detection (can-i-take-over-xyz fingerprints + multi-resolver verifier)

final_conditions: Extension of the P275 TLS inspection: it reuses the P275 connector (injectable ctx.tls, sockets only from the core connector) and its interception detection; no second TLS client. Opsec ACTIVE, disclosure 'target', default_enabled=False.

ACTIVE gate (A7): runs only with --mode active, a non-empty --authorized REF and a --scope FILE on every path (scan, run, shell, watch, batch; non-interactive runs refuse without both), on scope-file matches only after resolution and per redirect hop, never on pivots or on entities extracted from text/files; CDN/shared-hosting/SaaS IPs excluded unless listed.

A7 ceilings enforced by the core client and socket connector: <= 10 requests/probes per second and <= 2 concurrent connections per target host, the case ACTIVE budget, the kill switch (traffic stops within 2 s), proxy_active egress profile (A13), the hostile-host guard, and every request in the hash-chained P324 ledger; the report banner carries REF, scope SHA-256, window and egress.
Probes: at most 4 extra handshakes per host:port per run (TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1, up to two weak-cipher sets) with SECLEVEL=0 contexts, 10 s timeout, no application data sent.
Only host:port pairs where P275 found no interception on the same egress profile are probed; otherwise the result is 'intercepted, not tested'.

Tri-state per protocol and cipher: accepted / refused / could not test. A client-side refusal (OpenSSL built without TLS 1.0/1.1, SECLEVEL) or a proxy refusing the port is 'could not test', never 'disabled on server' (rule 5).
Findings carry the protocol or cipher and the egress profile as evidence and feed CR17 weak_or_expired_tls (P084) for owned assets.
Tests run against local loopback TLS servers configured per protocol; merge only after the AR20 safety suite passes (A16).
P277.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3 (redteam_lead, legal_dpo and the architect voted P2). The A7 gate (legal_dpo, redteam_lead) applies with A7's 2-connection ceiling, stricter than legal_dpo's 4. The architect's floor reuses the P275 connector and requires honest client-side 'could not test' semantics, which cti_lead, osint_investigator and analyst_ux also stressed; redteam_lead's interception rule and handshake limits are kept.
P277.title: TLS protocol/cipher checks (TLS 1.0/1.1 acceptance, weak ciphers)

final_conditions: Implemented as a correlation rule over facts other modules already produced (architect): historical A records from passive DNS (P006 SecurityTrails, P015, under their own licence and key-terms rules), certificate SAN/fingerprint matches, favicon mmh3 and title matches. It makes no network calls (disclosure 'none') and never re-queries SecurityTrails or Censys itself.

CDN and cloud ranges are excluded through the shared IP interval index (P169 warninglists, cloud ranges); no subdomain brute force or active resolution, and quota exhaustion of the history sources never falls back to either.

Scoring with explicit weights (cti_lead): certificate SAN/fingerprint match on a non-CDN IP = strong; pre-CDN historical A record = medium, decaying with age; favicon or title match = weak (phishing kits copy favicons); an IP hosting more than 50 domains = weak.

Output: relation origin_candidate with score and evidence, expand=False, labelled 'possible origin (hypothesis)'; never a seed for LIGHT/ACTIVE modules. For hostile sites it is an abuse-reporting aid (candidate hoster/ASN and the CDN abuse-form link).

No connection to candidate IPs in this build. A later verification module (https://<ip>/ with Host: <domain>) would be ACTIVE under A7 and only for IPs listed in the scope file itself, because a domain in scope does not put its old IPs in scope; never for third-party or attacker origins (BACKLOG).

Licences (A6): CloakQuest3r (MIT) logic adapted with a header and notice; Cloudmare (AGPL) ideas only. Opt-in (--preset deep or -M). Tests use synthetic graph fixtures (strong, medium, weak and CDN-only cases).
P278.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3 (osint_investigator, redteam_lead and the architect voted P2). The architect's floor turns it into a deterministic correlation rule over facts from P006/P015 and certificate/favicon modules, so legal_dpo's SecurityTrails key-terms condition is enforced where the calls happen (P006). redteam_lead's and osint_investigator's rule that historical IPs are never probed unless listed in the scope removes the active step from this build. cti_lead's weights and the hypothesis wording (analyst_ux) handle the false-positive risk; it stays opt-in. Scheduling (A16 BR1): P3 with effort M, so it is not built in this build; BACKLOG.md keeps this spec as the unblock target.
P278.title: CDN origin-IP hypotheses (CloakQuest3r technique)

final_conditions: ACTIVE gate (A7): runs only with --mode active, a non-empty --authorized REF and a --scope FILE on every path (scan, run, shell, watch, batch; non-interactive runs refuse without both), on scope-file matches only after resolution and per redirect hop, never on pivots or on entities extracted from text/files; CDN/shared-hosting/SaaS IPs excluded unless listed.

A7 ceilings enforced by the core client and socket connector: <= 10 requests/probes per second and <= 2 concurrent connections per target host, the case ACTIVE budget, the kill switch (traffic stops within 2 s), proxy_active egress profile (A13), the hostile-host guard, and every request in the hash-chained P324 ledger; the report banner carries REF, scope SHA-256, window and egress.
This module is slower still: <= 2 req/s per host, and a host is stopped at the first 429 or challenge (BLOCKED, could not verify).

Paths: a fixed list of < 30 paths as data pinned in data/active.lock (.git/HEAD, .git/config, .env, common backup names, .DS_Store, server-status, phpinfo, source maps...), one GET per path, GET/HEAD only; HEAD is never trusted alone.
One forced-browsing helper shared with P285: soft-404 calibration with two random paths first, then content-signature matching; a redirect to a login page is a miss. Never confirm by HTTP 200 alone.

Read at most the first KB: GET with Range: bytes=0-1023 plus a client-side max_bytes=1024 cut-off. Signatures: .git/HEAD ^(ref: refs/|[0-9a-f]{40}); .git/config '[core]'; .env ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+=; .DS_Store magic 00 00 00 01 42 75 64 31; zip 'PK\x03\x04'; source map '"mappings"'.

Forbidden follow-ups (A7): never fetch .git/objects, .git/index or packed refs (no repository reconstruction), never download whole backups or dumps, never call endpoints named in leaked configs, never use or test found credentials.

Evidence keeps path, status, size, matched signature, a hash and a masked excerpt; for .env only the variable NAMES. Values, secrets (P312 detector plus the central redactor), server-status client lines, phpinfo environment and SQL dump rows are dropped before cache and evidence; responses are no-store in the HTTP cache.

Results are tri-state (confirmed / not observed / could not test): blocked egress, a proxy, 403/429, a challenge or a timeout is 'could not test', never closed, absent or safe (rule 5). Merge only after the AR20 safety suite passes (A16). Only confirmed exposures are listed, with a count of paths tested; findings map to T1213 / T1552.001 and CR23 (P084).
Tests: a local loopback HTTP server and FakeHttp fixtures including soft-404 pages, a login redirect, a .env with values that must not reach evidence, and a 429 stop.
P279.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (cti_lead and osint_investigator voted P3). The A7 floor of legal_dpo and redteam_lead gates it, with A7's 2-connection ceiling. redteam_lead set the line between detection and data theft (first KB only, no follow-ups, variable names only), and legal_dpo kept secrets and personal data out of evidence and cache. The architect's shared soft-404 helper and stricter 2 req/s, and analyst_ux's confirmed-only listing, are adopted.
P279.title: Sensitive file exposure checks (.git/HEAD, .env, backups, .DS_Store, server-status...)

final_conditions: BACKLOG unblock: only if passive WAF signatures (P072 header/cookie/server subset plus CDN ranges) prove inconclusive in practice, as one fixed inert probe per in-scope host under A7 (no SQLi/LFI/RCE/XXE/time-based or command strings, no forms or login endpoints), with a JSON signature table shared with P072 and wafw00f BSD-3 attribution.
P280.rationale: Contested 3-3; the chair rejects. The active mode exists to send attack-like strings (XSS/SQLi/LFI) that provoke block pages: cti_lead, redteam_lead (owner of the active-module lens) and analyst_ux rejected it because it raises incidents in the team's own SOC and gets the egress blocked for little gain, and legal_dpo's floor reduces it to inert canaries that add little over passive signatures. P072 web_fingerprint already carries the passive wafw00f header/cookie subset with the BSD-3 notice, and the red team runs wafw00f under its own ROE.
P280.title: Active WAF fingerprinting (wafw00f attack-request signatures)

final_conditions: ACTIVE gate (A7): runs only with --mode active, a non-empty --authorized REF and a --scope FILE on every path (scan, run, shell, watch, batch; non-interactive runs refuse without both), on scope-file matches only after resolution and per redirect hop, never on pivots or on entities extracted from text/files; CDN/shared-hosting/SaaS IPs excluded unless listed. Only zones in the scope file.

Name servers are resolved through the core DoH resolver. An NS is contacted only if its name or resolved IP matches the scope; NS of managed DNS providers (data list matched by NS name/ASN: Cloudflare, Route 53, Azure DNS, Google Cloud DNS, NS1, UltraDNS, Akamai, registro.br...) are skipped as 'not tested: managed provider'.

Semantics (captured fixtures): 404 NoSuchBucket = absent; 403 AccessDenied/AllAccessDisabled = exists-private (LOW); 301 PermanentRedirect = exists in another region; ListBucketResult = public listing; anything else = could not verify. XML parsed with the safe XML helper.

final_conditions: Rules CR07 subdomain_takeover_candidate, CR08 dangling_cloud_ip, CR13 exposed_remote_admin, CR14 exposed_database_or_cache, CR15 known_exploited_vuln_on_asset, CR16 outdated_version_disclosed, CR25 stale_host, CR26 shadow_it_outlier and CR31 certificate_san_affiliate (INFO). They replace the existing exploitable_exposure rule, which gets the same caps.
Rules consume only vocab facts (open_ports, services, cpes, vulns, kev, epss, cvss, CNAME/NXDOMAIN facts) and KEV/EPSS through core/datasets. Rules make no network calls.

CR15 is CRITICAL only when (KEV or EPSS >= 0.5) AND the vulnerability is verified AND the asset is an org_profile own asset or in-scope target. Verified means: the source marks it verified, evidence specific to the CVE goes beyond a version string, or an authorized ACTIVE check confirmed it. CVSS >= 9 alone never yields CRITICAL.

Version-inferred matches (InternetDB/Shodan CPE, CR16) are POSSIBLE, capped at HIGH when in KEV and at MEDIUM otherwise, with the label 'version-inferred, distro backports not considered: confirm on the host'. They produce one finding per host+product, not one per CVE.

Ownership: CR13-CR16, CR25 and CR26 keep their severity only for org_profile own assets or in-scope targets; third-party hosts get INFO context. On entities tagged malicious/phishing/c2 the same facts are INFO pivots for infrastructure fingerprinting.

CR07 needs a CNAME to a service fingerprint marked vulnerable (pinned, attributed list) AND dangling evidence (NXDOMAIN of the CNAME target, or the provider's unclaimed-resource fingerprint). It is worded 'candidate' and never claims or registers the resource.
CR08 is POSSIBLE unless the evidence is strong, and never re-acquires IPs. CR07/CR08 use passive evidence unless an ACTIVE module ran under the gate.
CR13/CR14 carry the observation date; data older than 30 days lowers confidence by one level. CR25 stale_host needs >= 3 bad signals, and a missing security.txt is not one.
CR26 (outlier <= 10% of assets) runs only with >= 20 org assets (configurable threshold).
Findings outside org_profile are labelled third_party and never trigger ACTIVE verification automatically. SAN affiliates (CR31) and co-hosted domains never join the active scope.
Tests: positive and negative graph fixtures per rule. An nginx host with 20 CPE CVEs and one KEV entry gives one HIGH POSSIBLE finding, not 20 CRITICALs.

The members agree that version-inferred CVEs are the biggest false-positive generator: CRITICAL now needs verification plus KEV/EPSS on an owned or in-scope asset (redteam_lead, analyst_ux, cti_lead; the architect's floor enforces the caps in code). legal_dpo's floor: takeover candidates are never verified by claiming, third-party findings never trigger ACTIVE work. osint_investigator turned exposure on attacker infrastructure into INFO pivots, and redteam_lead kept SAN affiliates out of scope.

final_conditions: A compact offline index (Enterprise + Mobile + ICS ATT&CK; CAPEC 2.1 optional; ~0.27 MB gzip) with ATT&CK version, build date and the MITRE notice (data/NOTICE and the report footer). Matching is offline (disclosure 'none'); the index loads in < 100 ms.

Shipping (A6): the prebuilt index ships inside the release only after legal records that the MITRE ATT&CK/CAPEC Terms of Use (royalty-free, commercial use allowed with the notice reproduced) are permissive for bundling; until then `v3lum data update attack` builds it on first run (first-run hint).

Rebuild: the ~55 MB STIX bundles (raw.githubusercontent.com attack-stix-data, index.json for versions) are streamed through the dataset manager and parsed object by object (no json.load of the whole bundle); a slow test on a synthetic 50 MB bundle asserts bounded memory. Never during a scan. TAXII 2.1 (attack-taxii.mitre.org) only detects a newer version.

Revoked and deprecated objects are dropped and a revoked-by map kept (T1656 -> T1684.001); an analyst-typed revoked id renders 'revoked -> replaced by T1684.001', never a silent rewrite. Tactic names and order are read from the data (v18+ renames, e.g. Stealth and Defense Impairment); none are hard-coded.
Detection normalises T1059/001 and t1059.001 to T1059.001; text_blob inputs are handled by the P172 extractor. Detections come from x-mitre-detection-strategy objects.

Exports: STIX uses the official ATT&CK STIX ids (attack-pattern--..., intrusion-set--...), MISP uses galaxy tags (misp-galaxy:mitre-attack-pattern="Name - T1059.001"); no regenerated ids. The ATT&CK version is recorded per case and in report footers.
