Cards show name, tactics from the data, at most 10 related groups/software and the attack.mitre.org link. Group/software 'uses' edges are context, never attribution evidence; CWE -> CAPEC -> ATT&CK links carry low confidence.
Provider: MITRE (trusted tier); downloads only, no value sent. Fixtures: a trimmed real bundle slice (Enterprise, Mobile, ICS objects incl. a revoked technique) plus the TAXII captures.
P292.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1: ATT&CK is the shared language with SOC rules and partners. The architect's floor sets a prebuilt compact index, a streaming rebuilder and no hard-coded tactics. cti_lead requires official STIX ids and MISP galaxy tags, osint_investigator Mobile ATT&CK for Android banking trojans, and analyst_ux an instant offline answer. legal_dpo accepts the MITRE notice; the chair makes shipping the index inside the release conditional on legal recording that these terms are permissive under the A6 bundling list (ATT&CK's own licence is not on it).
P292.title: MITRE ATT&CK compact index (STIX bundle at runtime + TAXII update check)

final_conditions: Legal floor (A1): ORKL publishes no terms readable from the research egress (JS-only site), so terms='unknown': the module runs in no profile until legal records the terms in the provider registry. No unknown-terms source is default at release, so default_enabled=False.

Tier (A8): unknown until the registry reviewer records otherwise. While unknown it is excluded at TLP:AMBER+, runs at CLEAR/GREEN only with --allow-unknown, and receives only IOC_TYPES values (cve, mitre_technique); threat_actor and malware_family queries need a recorded promotion to community tier. Victim company names are never sent.
Queries: library/search?query=&limit= with limit <= 10, min_interval 1 s, cache 7 days. Error fields inside HTTP 200 bodies -> ERROR; timeouts and errors = could not verify (rule 5).
Output: report title, publisher, date and URL as links (terminal shows the 5 most recent, HTML up to 10). No PDF or report-file download; excerpts truncated (publishers keep copyright).

IOC extraction from report plain_text is off by default; with an explicit option the text is truncated first and IOCs are tagged 'from report <title> (<date>)', low confidence, warninglist-filtered (P169) and never verdicts (reports carry example and benign IOCs).

Merge gate (A16): offline tests with FakeHttp (unmatched requests fail, network guard active) over trimmed real fixtures without personal data (the captured search response plus an empty result), a provider-registry entry for every host, the registry contract test and the P327 lint.
P293.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (legal_dpo voted P3). legal_dpo's floor classifies the terms as unknown and the operator as unknown tier, so under A1/A3/A8 it cannot be default and stays off until legal records the terms; A8 also limits an unknown-tier operator to IOC values until promoted. cti_lead's and analyst_ux's input limits, link-only output and opt-in report IOCs, and the architect's bounds, are the spec.
P293.title: ORKL CTI report library

final_conditions: Prefer the D3FEND ATT&CK mapping export as a bulk dataset through the dataset manager (version recorded), matched locally (disclosure 'none', works at TLP:RED), over one API call per technique.
If the per-technique API (d3fend.mitre.org/api/offensive-technique/attack/{T}.json) is used as a fallback: only the technique id is sent, cache 30 days, and 404 means 'no mapping', never an error.
Output: at most 5 countermeasures per technique in a 'recommended controls' section (INFO/recommendations only) with links to d3fend.mitre.org/offensive-technique/attack/{id}/.

Licence (legal floor): reproduce MITRE's D3FEND copyright designation and licence text in data/NOTICE, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES and every report that shows D3FEND content (Terms of Use checked 2026-11-26: royalty-free for research, development and commercial purposes with the notice).
Merge gate: a trimmed real fixture of the mapping export (and of one API answer if the fallback is kept) captured before merge, since research captured none (architect, analyst_ux).
P294.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3 (legal_dpo, the architect and analyst_ux voted P2). cti_lead and the architect prefer the bulk mapping matched offline; legal_dpo's notice requirement and analyst_ux's 5-control cap are adopted, and the missing fixture is a merge gate.
P294.title: MITRE D3FEND (ATT&CK -> defensive techniques)

final_conditions: Sources (legal floor): bundle only the MISP galaxy clusters (dual CC0/BSD-2; keep their notices, MITRE-derived clusters keep the ATT&CK notice) and the Microsoft threat actor naming map (CC BY 4.0, attributed). ETDA/ThaiCERT Threat Group Cards have no licence: fetched at runtime (getmisp.cgi export, weekly), attributed, never bundled or redistributed.

ETDA publishes no licence or terms, so under A1 its source class is 'unknown' until legal records it in the provider registry (legal_dpo's 'runtime fetch, attribution, no redistribution' is the proposed basis). Until then ETDA is not fetched, the index runs on the galaxy and MSTIC sources, and Module.terms stays 'open'.

APTmap (CC BY 4.0, GitHub Pages URL; raw path 404) is an optional dataset outside the default update set; CyCat is excluded until a useful fixture exists. Malpedia family ids come from the bundled galaxy 'malpedia' cluster, so joins never depend on the non-commercial Malpedia API. Source versions are recorded.

No transitive mega-clusters: every alias edge keeps source, kind (synonym vs overlaps/similar/associated), date and confidence. An exact synonym resolves to its cluster; overlapping clusters are listed as overlaps_with, never merged. Clusters merge only through the same MITRE G/S id, an explicit MSTIC mapping or a source's explicit synonym assertion, never on normalised-name equality alone.

Over-merge guards (architect): a stop-list of generic aliases (unknown, apt, group, team, short tokens); no merge that would put two different MITRE G ids or two Malpedia actor ids in one cluster; no merge through an alias present in clusters of several sources without a shared id; a cluster-size alarm and a build-time collision report that fails CI unless reviewed.

Ambiguity: umbrella names (Lazarus, Winnti/APT41, TA505, FIN7/Carbanak...) are flagged and return candidates with a disambiguation note; a lookup hitting more than one primary actor returns the alternatives ('X: APT41 (MISP) / Winnti (ETDA)'). Actor and malware namespaces stay separate, so an ambiguous input returns both cards.

Normalisation: lowercase and strip spaces, dashes and underscores ('APT 28' -> 'apt28'). Cards show the canonical name, up to 10 aliases with the source asserting each ('X = Y according to <source>'), worded 'vendor assessment, not identity'. ETDA card links use ?u={uuid}.

Offline lookup (disclosure 'none'); refresh weekly through the dataset manager. Dataset providers: MISP project/CIRCL, Microsoft, MITRE and ETDA/ThaiCERT, all trusted tier. Used by P203, P219, P254, P372 and the console to tell malware names from usernames (AR18).

Regression tests: APT28 vs APT29, Lazarus vs Kimsuky, Conti vs Black Basta stay separate; Brazilian banking families (Grandoreiro, Mekotio, Casbaneiro, Guildma/Astaroth, Mispadu) resolve through galaxy/Malpedia ids; fixtures include known conflicting aliases.
P295.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1 (redteam_lead voted P2). Every member except redteam_lead warned about over-merging, so the architect's guards and cti_lead's, osint_investigator's and analyst_ux's provenance-per-edge design replace the synthesizer's plain union-find. legal_dpo's floor sets the licence handling (bundled galaxy and MSTIC with attribution, ETDA runtime-only). APTmap becomes optional because its operator tier is unreviewed and its data mostly derives from the other sources, and CyCat waits for a fixture (architect). Audit: ETDA has no published terms, so it waits for a recorded legal class (A1) and the module stays 'open' and default-on.
P295.title: Threat-actor/malware alias index (MISP galaxy bundled + ETDA cards + APTmap + CyCat)

final_conditions: Licence (A1 initial class, legal floor): Malpedia content is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0, class 'noncommercial': off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared. The licence_allow entry requires a written Fraunhofer FKIE agreement ('alternative agreements' per its ToS); under a recorded research basis it runs with the licence banner.

Endpoint allow-list in code: list/families, find/actor, get/actor and get/family only. The URL builder rejects /api/get/sample/* and every sample, YARA or other download endpoint by construction (unit test on the module's URL set; P327 lint); no binary ever reaches the analyst machine.

Optional team-account token in the Authorization header only. Non-public material from the token tier carries the source TLP:AMBER, stays inside the case, never appears in lower-TLP reports and is never exported.

Under the corporate profile, family/actor ids and reference URLs come from the bundled MISP galaxy Malpedia cluster (P295) and joins on Malpedia ids from ThreatFox/galaxy work without this API; this module only adds live detail. Manual Malpedia pages stay available through P300.
Caching: list/families 7 days; actor ids are lowercase slugs (apt28, lazarus_group) and family ids '<platform>.<name>'. Opt-in (default_enabled=False).

Merge gate (A16): offline tests with FakeHttp (unmatched requests fail, network guard active) over trimmed real fixtures without personal data (the 6 Malpedia captures), a provider-registry entry for every host, the registry contract test and the P327 lint.
P296.rationale: Approved 5-0-1 at median P3 (analyst_ux deferred until legal clears the non-commercial licence). legal_dpo's floor and the binding A1 class make it noncommercial with a written FKIE agreement as the path. The architect's and redteam_lead's sample-download prohibition is enforced by construction. cti_lead's and osint_investigator's galaxy fallback keeps the value under the corporate profile.
P296.title: Malpedia (families, actors, references)

final_conditions: BACKLOG unblock: MalwareIntel publishes terms that legal reviews (or the team buys a plan) and the API carries per-record upstream attribution.

BACKLOG unblock (then): opt-in only, unknown tier until promoted (never default, excluded at TLP:AMBER+), only actor/family/technique names sent and never case IOCs, P171 provenance so upstream feeds are not double-counted, result cap 20, error fields in 200 bodies -> ERROR, doctor health check.
P297.rationale: Contested 3-3 (3 yes, 3 defer); the chair defers. MalwareIntel's terms are 'unknown' (A1 initial class, binding) and its site says premium plans unlock API access (osint_investigator, terms page 404), so the module could not run in any licence profile (A1: unknown terms stay disabled everywhere) and no unknown-terms source may be default at release. cti_lead and the architect add that an aggregator of 70-100 feeds without per-record provenance double-counts feeds V3LUM already ingests. ATT&CK, the alias index and ORKL cover the relationships meanwhile.
P297.title: MalwareIntel knowledge-graph API

final_conditions: Feeds are a team-curated data/cti_feeds.json validated in CI, one entry per feed with terms note, tier, health and last_ok: The Record, BleepingComputer, DFIR Report, Krebs, Help Net Security, Dark Reading, CyberScoop, Schneier, DarkFeed, Dark Web Informer, ICHI, DataBreaches.net and CERT.br.
CTIR Gov and CAIS/RNP join only after re-verification from the team network; The Hack (stale since 2022) and CISO Advisor (Cloudflare challenge) are excluded.

Licence (A1, legal floor): feed terms are 'unknown' until legal reviews them, so nothing runs yet in any profile. Legal's feed-reader decision (poll <= hourly; headline + link + date only; no full text; no redistribution) is recorded per kept feed with its class and evidence; a feed whose terms forbid business use or automated reading is dropped.

Fetching: one fetch per feed, never per entity, through the dataset manager, `v3lum watch` or a scan-start refresh (10 s budget), at most hourly, with conditional GET (ETag/Last-Modified). Anti-bot challenge pages are excluded, never bypassed (rule 1).

Parsing: the safe XML helper (DOCTYPE/entities rejected), feed size cap 2 MB, <= 200 items per feed. Items (title, link, date, feed id) are kept in a local SQLite with 180-day retention; no article content is stored or scraped.

Matching is offline (disclosure 'none'; no watched name leaves the machine): word boundaries, accent folding, exact match for CVE ids. Terms come from org_profile brands/domains, suppliers and case seeds (company, actor, malware, CVE).

Ambiguous names: brand aliases under 5 characters or on a common-word list (Claro, Oi, Vivo, Natura, Inter...) match only with a context term (company suffix, domain, 'operadora', 'banco') or a second token; a fixture where 'claro' is an adjective must not match.

Findings: matches are INFO/LOW context with links and never raise risk alone; a dark-web-news or DataBreaches.net item naming the own organisation is MEDIUM 'reported claim - verify', never 'breach confirmed', deduplicated against ransomware-victim trackers. The terminal shows the 5 most recent headlines (date, source, link).

Per-feed health (stale > 90 days, blocked, error) in doctor and coverage. Tiers are recorded per feed (CERT.br and The Record trusted; anonymous feeds unknown, labelled 'unverified source'); feed downloads carry no investigated value, so the module's disclosure is 'none' and its derived tier is 'n/a' for the TLP gate (A8 BR1); feed tiers drive the label and the A3 default only.

Merge gate (A16): offline tests with FakeHttp (unmatched requests fail, network guard active) over trimmed real fixtures without personal data (the captured feeds, with the truncated ICHI sample re-fetched), a provider-registry entry for every host, the registry contract test and the P327 lint.
P298.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. Offline matching over a local cache discloses nothing (redteam_lead). legal_dpo's floor makes the feed list terms-checked, so the class stays unknown and the module off until legal records the feed-reader decision (A1), and A3 keeps it opt-in. The architect's strict parsing, storage and matching rules and the common-word guard that cti_lead, osint_investigator and analyst_ux all asked for are the core. Severity: osint_investigator's MEDIUM for claims naming the own organisation, otherwise cti_lead's and the architect's INFO/LOW.
P298.title: CTI news / advisory RSS watcher (The Record, DarkFeed, Dark Web Informer, ICHI advisories)

final_conditions: BACKLOG unblock: a real stix.json capture (the only capture is a 15-byte 'Redirecting...' body) and Wiz reuse terms recorded by legal; then a daily local index of cloud incidents, actors and techniques, opt-in.
P299.rationale: Deferred mechanically (2 yes, 0 reject, 4 defer). Reuse terms are unreviewed, the only capture is a redirect body without STIX (architect), and value is low next to ATT&CK, CISA advisories (P374) and the alias index (P295).
P299.title: Wiz Cloud Threat Landscape (STIX/RSS)

final_conditions: Ship data/pivot_links/cti.json in the frozen P311 pack schema (label, template, entity_types, category, host, verified, checked_at, privacy, publishes=false, touches_target, login_required, antibot). The pack is offline data (disclosure 'none'): V3LUM never requests these URLs or any API behind them.

Rendering follows A2/P311: at TLP:AMBER and above every link is non-clickable text with 'opening sends <value> to <host>'; at RED third-party links are hidden from reports and listed only by `v3lum links` with the warning; links are never auto-opened and `links --open` at AMBER+ needs an interactive confirmation naming the host.

CI renders every template with a sample value per declared entity type and with hostile values (quotes, spaces, unicode, newlines): each result must be an https URL on the declared host, built only from whitelisted placeholders through the declared encoder (never str.format, never {raw} in URL position).

Every link host has a provider-registry entry with tier and rationale (A8); unknown-tier hosts get the 'unknown operator' badge and their templates take IOC_TYPES values only (A8 BR4): never PERSONAL_TYPES, CNPJ, company names, keywords, malware or actor names, or other free text (P311 lint).
Initial host tiers for the registry reviewer to confirm: trusted - MITRE ATT&CK and D3FEND (attack.mitre.org, d3fend.mitre.org), Malpedia (Fraunhofer FKIE).

Order: P311 groups links by analyst question with verified links first; inside a group the pack's file order is the curated analyst-value order (ATT&CK, Malpedia, D3FEND); the terminal shows at most 8 links per seed, the rest go to HTML and `v3lum links`.

Verified links carry checked_at; `v3lum doctor --links` (offline) lists unverified links and links not re-checked for more than 180 days. The pack ships in phase 1 with the other pivot packs (A16), whatever the state of the related automated modules.
ATT&CK: attack.mitre.org/techniques/{mitre_path}/ with a vetted {mitre_path} placeholder (T1059.001 -> T1059/001), unit-tested; groups and software pages by their G/S ids from P292.

Malpedia: malpedia.caad.fkie.fraunhofer.de/details/{slug}, with the slug (win.emotet, apt28, lazarus_group) taken from the P295 alias-index mapping, never from the raw family name. Manual browsing is unaffected by the API's CC BY-NC-SA licence and is the corporate-profile fallback for P296.
D3FEND: d3fend.mitre.org/offensive-technique/attack/{id}/ for mitre_technique entities (P294).
P300.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (analyst_ux voted P1, redteam_lead P3). The architect's two value transformations ({mitre_path}, alias-index slugs) prevent dead links. cti_lead, osint_investigator and legal_dpo confirm manual Malpedia browsing is fine under its licence, which makes this pack the fallback for P296.
P300.title: Pivot links: Malpedia and MITRE ATT&CK pages

final_conditions: Python @rule stays first-class. The approved packs (P027, P028, P084, P146, P171, P258, P291) ship now as @rule functions and are not blocked by the YAML engine.

Both kinds of rule share one metadata API: id, version, title, severity, criterion, references, ATT&CK ids, false-positive notes, positive and negative graph fixtures. There is one registry and one listing (`v3lum rules`), with per-rule precision.

YAML/JSON/TOML rules are optional data compiled into the same RuleInfo objects (one engine, one result type). They are loaded with a safe parser (JSON/TOML; PyYAML safe_load only as an optional extra; no eval/exec or object tags) and schema-validated at load, and validation errors fail CI.

The SpiderFoot correlation model is ported with MIT attribution (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md): collections with exact or regex filters (bounded, reviewed regexes) -> aggregation field -> analysis method -> headline. Analysis methods are limited to threshold | outlier | first_collection_only | match_all_to_first_collection | both_collections over vocab-keyed graph queries.

Rules run once after the BFS, because the pipelined engine has no pivot rounds. They only read the graph and emit correlations: they never schedule modules or pivots, change the opsec mode or widen the scope. Correlation adds < 2 s to a scan.

Every correlation carries evidence (finding ids + facts used), a one-line 'why', a recommendation and ATT&CK ids validated against the bundled ATT&CK data, with revoked ids mapped to their replacements (e.g. T1656 -> T1684.001).
Suppression rules only downgrade confidence, with a visible label, and never delete. Rules touching natural persons inherit the P258 caps.
Per-rule precision comes from P325: a rule with precision < 0.3 after >= 10 votes is demoted one severity level and flagged in doctor, never silently disabled.
User rule directories (~/.v3lum/rules) follow the plugin ownership/permission checks (AR12), are linted like modules and are listed by doctor.
P301.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (legal_dpo P1, analyst_ux P3). cti_lead, osint_investigator and analyst_ux insisted that the correlation packs must not wait for this L-effort engine. The architect's floor: YAML compiles into the existing RuleInfo, safe loader, schema validation, rules run once after the BFS and never schedule pivots. redteam_lead: rule files are data and cannot trigger collection. legal_dpo: SpiderFoot MIT notice, downgrade-only suppression, P258 caps. Demotion of imprecise rules is analyst_ux's, the doctor flag osint_investigator's.
P301.title: SpiderFoot-style YAML correlation rule engine

final_conditions: A pure function in core/scoring.py with documented constants. W_sev: CRITICAL 10 / HIGH 7 / MEDIUM 4 / LOW 2 / INFO 0. C_conf (P322): CONFIRMED 1.0 / PROBABLE 0.7 / POSSIBLE 0.4. R_src, the Admiralty prior from the provider registry: A 1.0, B 0.85, C 0.7, D 0.5, E 0.3, F 0.5. Per-finding weight = W_sev/10 x C_conf x R_src x decay x A_crit, combined by noisy-OR and capped at 100.

Decay follows the MISP polynomial base x (1 - (t/tau)^(1/delta)), with named constants tau: ip 30 d, url 30 d, domain 90 d, typosquat 180 d, breach 3 y, infostealer 1 y, hashes no decay; delta defaults to 1.0. t is computed from Finding.observed_last. Findings without a provider timestamp get no decay and the label 'age unknown'.
Severity ceiling: an entity or case level never exceeds the highest severity among its contributing findings and correlations. Weak signals escalate only through an explicit correlation rule.

Correlations never add on top of the findings they are built from: they take the max/uplift, not a second noisy-OR term. Contributions are deduplicated per (entity, tag family, upstream family). '+1 confidence level' applies only with >= 2 independent upstream families (P171).

Case score = seeds + correlations + the top-5 pivot entities, not every pivot. Pivot contributions are weighted by path confidence (AR07). Shared-infrastructure relations (co-hosted, same ASN, same NS/MX, CDN) cap the transferred contribution at LOW. Own assets and known-good/verified entities (BCB verified FI domains, gov.br) never inherit risk from neighbours.

A seed reads 'inconclusive' (never 'clean' or 'no findings') when fewer than 2 reputation-capable sources answered OK/EMPTY for it. The lowest level is renamed 'no findings', and the thresholds 80/55/30/8 stay.

A warninglist hit makes the finding POSSIBLE, with a label. Sources disabled by the licence profile contribute nothing. R_src is Beta-updated only by explicit feedback, after >= 5 votes (P325), with a floor of 0.3.
Asset criticality from org_profile gives A_crit: critical 1.0, high 0.95, medium 0.85, low 0.6. Entities without profile criticality use 1.0.

Output: the top-3 contributors with finding ids, path and confidence label, printed in plain words next to the score. Every report labels scores 'triage aid, not a conclusion'. The risk.score/level JSON fields stay backward compatible so stored cases still render.
For PERSONAL_TYPES entities the score is shown only with its top contributors. It is never exported to STIX/MISP as a score about a person and never drives an automated action (LGPD art. 20).

The model lands after the fields it needs (Finding.observed_last, Finding.source with its upstream family, the P322 labels). Golden-case tests: 30 pivots with one LOW each stay <= low (83.1 = critical today); one CONFIRMED CRITICAL outranks any number of LOWs; 2 HIGH findings plus their correlation stay HIGH; frozen-time tests per decay class.
P302.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1 (redteam_lead and the architect voted P2). analyst_ux measured the inflation: 30 single-LOW pivots score CRITICAL, and the draft formula ranks 10 LOW above 1 PROBABLE CRITICAL. Hence the severity ceiling, deduplication and top-5 pivots. cti_lead found double counting with correlations and 'clean' scores for unverified seeds, osint_investigator the guilt by association. The architect's floor: a pure function, golden tests, provenance and timestamps first, no decay without a timestamp, backward-compatible JSON. legal_dpo's floor: 'triage aid', no person scores exported, no automated action on them.
P302.title: Risk model (severity x confidence x Admiralty reliability x MISP decay x asset criticality, noisy-OR)

final_conditions: STIX 2.1 and MISP event JSON are hand-rolled, with no stix2/PyMISP runtime dependency; both serve only as dev test oracles. MISP galaxy data is used under its licence, with notice.

Deterministic ids. SCOs = uuid5(namespace 00abedb4-aa42-466c-9c01-fed23315a9b7, JCS of the id-contributing properties), with hash preference MD5 > SHA-1 > SHA-256 > SHA-512. Findings and notes use the deterministic Finding ids (AR09).
Global SDOs get stable ids, never case-scoped: vulnerability = uuid5 of the CVE id; attack-pattern = the official ATT&CK STIX id from P292; malware/threat-actor = the MISP galaxy uuid.

Markings: every SDO/SCO carries object_marking_refs from the case TLP (TLP 2.0 marking definitions, AMBER+STRICT supported). MISP events get tlp:* tags and distribution 0 (your organisation only) for AMBER, AMBER+STRICT and RED. Research-profile cases carry the licence banner.

Indicators are emitted only for CR27 consensus or analyst-confirmed findings; today a single 0.3-confidence finding becomes an indicator. They carry confidence 90/70/40 from P322, valid_until from the P302 decay tau and ATT&CK/kill-chain refs when known. POSSIBLE and warninglisted IOCs export as observables only (MISP to_ids=false) unless --include-weak.

Personal data is excluded by default: PERSONAL_TYPES SCOs (email-addr, user-account, phone, person names, CPF) and person identities need --include-personal, and CPF stays masked even then. report.description and notes never list seeds of those types; today bundle() writes every seed key there. Analyst notes and local evidence paths are never exported.
STIX pattern values are escaped for every type, so an e-mail containing a quote cannot break the pattern.

Export writes files. A REST push to the team's MISP/OpenCTI exists only as an explicit command with a dry-run summary ('1 event, 23 attributes, 4 to_ids') and confirmation, and only to configured internal instances with TLS verification on (ca_bundle). Pushed events are unpublished, distribution 0 (your organisation only) at every TLP, with no sharing group and no auto-sync.
Pushes never go to external sharing communities or to other organisations' instances.

Never pushed: RED cases and research-profile cases. Cases from LIGHT/ACTIVE engagements are excluded unless the analyst flags them exportable. AMBER+STRICT cases go only to the organisation's own instance with distribution 0.
Golden-file tests are validated against the stix2 oracle in dev and against the MISP JSON format, including personal-data stripping, markings on every object and quote-containing values.
P303.rationale: Approved 6-0. The chair raises the priority from the median P2 to P1 on the legal floor: today stix.py leaks every seed (CPF, person, phone) into report.description and emits no markings, and A2 requires markings on every export (legal_dpo and cti_lead voted P1 and list it as a must-have). cti_lead supplied indicator gating, stable SDO ids and decay; redteam_lead the organisation-only, unpublished push and engagement exclusion; osint_investigator and legal_dpo personal-data stripping; the architect's floor hand-rolled JSON, deterministic ids, escaping and an explicit draft-only push; analyst_ux weak IOCs as observables only.
P303.title: STIX 2.1 determinism + MISP event export

final_conditions: These templates live in the topic packs (data/pivot_links/<topic>.json) with verified != 'curl', in the frozen P311 schema plus the optional per-link max_tlp field that the phase-0 schema must include. The packs are offline data (disclosure 'none'): V3LUM never requests these URLs, not even from doctor, and never solves their challenges.

Rendering follows A2/P311: at TLP:AMBER and above every link is non-clickable text with 'opening sends <value> to <host>'; at RED third-party links are hidden from reports and listed only by `v3lum links` with the warning; links are never auto-opened and `links --open` at AMBER+ needs an interactive confirmation naming the host.

CI renders every template with a sample value per declared entity type and with hostile values (quotes, spaces, unicode, newlines): each result must be an https URL on the declared host, built only from whitelisted placeholders through the declared encoder (never str.format, never {raw} in URL position).
Every link host has a provider-registry entry with tier and rationale (A8); unknown-tier hosts (e.g. archive.today, hunter.how) get the 'unknown operator' badge and receive IOC values only.

Initial tiers (reviewer confirms): trusted - VirusTotal, Shodan, Censys, SecurityTrails, Cloudflare Radar, ICANN, Internet Archive, abuse.ch, AbuseIPDB, Talos, OTX, X-Force, Kaspersky (RU), Spamhaus, Hybrid Analysis, Joe Sandbox, MetaDefender, NVD, Exploit-DB, Meta; community - Netlas, Spur, CentralOps, DNSlytics, dotDB, TGStat, tellows, CVEdetails, Vulners, Ahmia, Arkham, Chainabuse.

Verification: verified takes 'curl', 'browser' (a dated one-time manual check by a team member) or false. Browser-verified links count as verified in the P311 ordering, so VirusTotal, AbuseIPDB, Shodan, OTX, Talos, abuse.ch and Wayback rank first; markers read '(browser)' or '(may show a challenge)'. The terminal shows at most 8 links per seed.

Rule 7: search/view/report pages only. VirusTotal uses /gui/file/{hash}, /gui/domain/{d}, /gui/ip-address/{ip} and /gui/url/<sha256 of the URL> (vetted placeholder); Wayback calendar or URL list, never /save; archive.ph capture lists, never /submit.

VirusTotal, Hybrid Analysis, Joe Sandbox, Filescan and MetaDefender templates are never upload or rescan pages; the lint rejects upload, submit, save and rescan paths. CentralOps Domain Dossier never carries the svc_scan option (it port-probes the target; unit test on the template string).

Pages that require a login (e.g. Shodan search) are excluded by the P311 lint; host and report pages that work without login stay. Ahmia stays a manual link only (its scripted search needs a per-session anti-bot token, rule 1).

Kaspersky OpenTIP: badge 'foreign provider (RU) - check the company vendor policy' and max_tlp=clear, so it is hidden by default and listed only by `v3lum links` (redteam_lead, legal_dpo, analyst_ux).

Personal-data templates (tellows for phone, TGStat for username, e-mail pages) are privacy=true: analyst-typed seeds only, opt-in per case, trusted/community hosts only (A8). Under the corporate profile VirusTotal stays manual-only (public API excluded, A1/A15).

Also routed here: the challenge-walled explorers of P216 (Etherscan, BscScan, Tronscan, Arkham, Chainabuse), Meta Ad Library (BR scam ads) and CVE reference pages (CVEdetails, Vulners, NVD, Exploit-DB search). `v3lum doctor --links` lists browser-only links due for re-check (> 90 days). Ships in phase 1 (A16).
P304.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (cti_lead, osint_investigator and analyst_ux voted P1). Every member stressed rule 7 (no submit, save, upload or rescan deep links) and never fetching or solving challenges; the architect added that doctor never touches them. analyst_ux's 'browser-verified' status lets the analysts' top tools rank first without breaking P311's verified-first ordering. redteam_lead's and legal_dpo's CentralOps and Kaspersky conditions are adopted, and osint_investigator's privacy rule and routed entries complete the pack.
P304.title: Pivot links not curl-verifiable (SPA or anti-bot: VirusTotal GUI, OTX, Shodan host, Censys, AbuseIPDB, Talos, X-Force, SecurityTrails web, archive.today, Wayback calendar...)

final_conditions: Sources (all trusted tier): GitHub code search API with the team's own token (no scopes, public data, 10 req/min, <= 1000 results per query), the Sourcegraph public stream API (keyless; optional token), GitLab blob search with a token. API only: github.com/search is never scraped.

Key-terms (legal floor): the tokens belong to company/team accounts on plans whose terms permit internal business use, recorded in the provider registry (key_plans) before the module runs under the corporate profile. Keyless Sourcegraph use is recorded with its ToS evidence; if business use is not allowed that source is skipped (reason_code 'licence').

Default scope: analyst-typed seed domains/brands and org_profile assets only, never every pivot; one exact quoted query per seed by default (Sourcegraph keyless, GitHub when a token exists), <= 3 queries per entity, 20 s budget. The full dork pack (github-dorks ideas, Apache-2.0, re-implemented with attribution) runs only with an explicit option or for org_profile own domains.

Secret-pattern dorks ('password', 'apikey', 'secret', private-key headers...) are combined only with exact org-owned identifiers (verified org_profile domains, internal hostnames, e-mail domains) or inside an --authorized engagement; other entities get plain mention searches (domain, hostname, IOC string). Internal hostnames go only to these trusted providers.

username and e-mail inputs are not searched by default; only on explicit selection, for org_profile addresses or handles in an incident case with a recorded purpose, never sweeps of employees' personal accounts (legal floor).

Secret handling (rule 1, A7): matched fragments pass the P312 secret scanner and are masked before cache and evidence, keeping rule id, repo, path, line, commit date and a salted hash for dedup. Raw search bodies are never cached (ttl=0) or written to evidence. Repositories are never cloned or walked, and secrets are never validated, tested or reused.

Provenance: hits in public IOC-list or blocklist repositories are tagged 'listed in public IOC repo' (context, never an independent malicious vote, P171); hits in repos not attributed to the org read 'third-party repo mentions our asset' without showing the secret.

Limits: tokens via `v3lum keys`, headers only, never in URLs or logs (AR01); GitHub 10/min as a P334 minute window; 403 secondary limits and 429 -> RATE_LIMITED (could not verify). The Sourcegraph text/event-stream is read with max_bytes 2 MB and a 30 s deadline ('matches' events, chunkMatches[].content).
Output: deduplicated per repo, top 10 as repo/path/line links; severity INFO unless a P312 rule matches (then HIGH with the secret masked).
Merge gate: the Sourcegraph part with its capture now; the GitHub and GitLab parts only with trimmed real fixtures captured with the team's tokens (api.github.com was blocked in research).
P305.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (redteam_lead voted P1). Leaked secrets and internal references in public code are a top external finding. redteam_lead's and cti_lead's rules (secret dorks only with org-owned identifiers or an authorised engagement, never test or reuse a secret, third-party repo wording) and legal_dpo's floor (business-compatible team keys, purpose-bound person inputs, location-only reporting) are adopted. The architect's floor keeps raw bodies out of the cache, budgets the 10/min quota and gates GitHub/GitLab on real fixtures; analyst_ux's 20 s default budget keeps it default-capable.
P305.title: Code search APIs (GitHub code search with token, Sourcegraph public, GitLab blob search)

final_conditions: Links only: the module builds search URLs for Google, Bing and DuckDuckGo (duckduckgo.com/?q=) and makes zero HTTP requests (unit test); search engines are never queried, scraped or rendered by V3LUM (rule 1), and Google Programmable Search is not used (it ends on 2027-01-01).

Dork packs are V3LUM-owned data files written from operator facts (sitedorks and msdorkdump are AGPL, PhoneInfoga GPL, dorks_hunter and Fast-Google-Dorks-Scan unlicensed: nothing copied, A6) and validated like pivot packs (P311 schema test, whitelisted placeholders, each query <= 32 words and < 30 site: operators).

Families: exposure dorks (docs, configs, panels, errors, filetype) for analyst-typed entities, names under a typed apex and org_profile assets, never for pivoted third-party domains; Bing ip:/url: operators; site-category dorks from a team-curated BR-focused site list (jusbrasil, escavador, reclameaqui, mercadolivre, olx, gov.br portals, BR forums).

BR fraud families (osint_investigator): site:reclameaqui.com.br, site:jusbrasil.com.br and gov.br dorks for CNPJ and company names; quoted non-CPF PIX keys and phones with golpe/fraude terms and wa.me/t.me forms. BR phone variants (+55 11 9xxxx-xxxx, (11) 9xxxx-xxxx, 119xxxxxxxx, with and without the 9) are generated offline by the phone normaliser from E.164 (unit test).

Legal floor (rules 3 and 4): no template ever contains a CPF, and no template combines a person identifier with document, password or leak terms (cpf, rg, senha, password, vazamento, dump, pastebin); a template lint test enforces it. Paste-site dorks are for domains and brands only.

Person, phone, e-mail, username and PIX-key dorks are privacy=true: analyst-typed seeds only, privacy-tagged, non-clickable at TLP:AMBER+ (A2). LinkedIn X-ray links only when the company is the own organisation in org_profile (A11 BR9).

Every dork link follows A2/P311 rendering: non-clickable text with 'opening sends <value> to <host>' at TLP:AMBER and above, hidden from reports at RED and listed only by `v3lum links`, never auto-opened. Hosts in the provider registry: Google, Bing and DuckDuckGo, trusted tier (A8).
Caps: the terminal shows at most 5 curated dorks per seed; reports show at most 20 grouped links per entity, the rest behind `v3lum links --all`.
The Ceos pasted-URL router (destino()) is ported as a pure function with tests: `v3lum add-url <url>` attaches a URL the analyst found manually to the right entity and module.
P306.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (osint_investigator voted P1). Every member agreed on links only and an own dork list (A6). legal_dpo's floor adds the CPF/leak-term template lint; osint_investigator's BR fraud families are kept, with PIX-key dorks limited to non-CPF keys (rule 4, P311). redteam_lead's no-third-party-pivot rule, the architect's 20-link cap and seed-only gates, and analyst_ux's 5-dork terminal view complete it.
P306.title: Search-engine dork generator (exposed docs/configs/panels, site-category dorks, Bing ip:/url:, phone/username/e-mail variants, LinkedIn X-ray links, pasted-URL router)

final_conditions: veto_lift (1): SerpApi is removed, together with any provider that scrapes search engines with CAPTCHA solving, IP/proxy rotation or browser emulation (rule 1 by proxy); no registry entry exists for serpapi.com and a unit test asserts that no request ever reaches it.

veto_lift (2): engines are limited to first-party APIs with their own index and business-compatible terms: Brave Search API (preferred; X-Subscription-Token header; class key-terms, business plan recorded in key_plans) and DuckDuckGo Instant Answer (context only, not web search; class open, with attribution).

veto_lift (2, continued): Marginalia only with a commercial key; its free keys are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, so the source is class 'license': off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared or a commercial key plan is recorded.

veto_lift (2, continued): Tavily and Exa only with a company-account key and terms recorded by legal; until then their class is 'unknown' and they run in no profile (hence this module's class 'unknown'). Never keyless x402 or any other autonomous payment: HTTP 402 or an x402 offer maps to NEEDS_KEY, and no payment code path exists (unit test).

Tiers: Brave and DuckDuckGo trusted; Marginalia, Tavily and Exa community. Per-provider sub-sources with separate statuses in coverage; keys in headers where supported, any key in a URL covered by the central redactor (AR01).

veto_lift (3): Brave results are never cached raw (ttl=0) and never stored as raw JSON: the case and evidence keep only URL + title of returned results (no snippets) unless a Brave storage-rights plan is recorded in the registry; the shell lets the analyst keep only selected results.

veto_lift (4): person_name and e-mail queries only for subjects the analyst entered in a case with a recorded purpose, never automatically from pivots. Queries are built only from typed entities or org_profile identifiers and never contain secrets, tokens or full URLs with query strings (victim identifiers).

veto_lift (5): a per-case query budget (default 10, setting web_search_case_budget) and a per-provider monthly budget (P334) with QUOTA status and a coverage line ('3/10 queries used'); the TLP gate applies (excluded at RED; providers flagged reuses_queries excluded at AMBER+).
Opt-in (default_enabled=False): runs only on -M web_search_api, --preset deep or when another approved module (P287, P289) calls its Brave source (P253 uses GDELT only); seed-only by default.
Merge gate: the captured no-key/422/402 responses now, plus a success fixture captured with each provider's key before that provider is enabled (architect).
P307.rationale: Vetoed by legal_dpo (SerpApi advertises solving CAPTCHAs, which breaks rule 1 by proxy; Marginalia free keys are non-commercial); veto_lift adopted, so the item is approved with every lift condition in final_conditions. The other five members approved it as the lawful way to automate a few dorks, and their conditions (Brave preferred, no autonomous payments, URL/title-only storage, budgets, TLP gate, seed-only) coincide with the lift. The architect's floor adds per-provider statuses, header keys, 402 -> needs_key and real success fixtures per provider. The class is 'unknown' while Tavily and Exa await legal review, so it stays opt-in. Median priority P3 (osint_investigator voted P2).
P307.title: Keyed/official web search APIs (SerpApi, Marginalia, DuckDuckGo Instant Answer)

final_conditions: Ship data/pivot_links/search.json in the frozen P311 pack schema (label, template, entity_types, category, host, verified, checked_at, privacy, publishes=false, touches_target, login_required, antibot). The pack is offline data (disclosure 'none'): V3LUM never requests these URLs or any API behind them.

Rendering follows A2/P311: at TLP:AMBER and above every link is non-clickable text with 'opening sends <value> to <host>'; at RED third-party links are hidden from reports and listed only by `v3lum links` with the warning; links are never auto-opened and `links --open` at AMBER+ needs an interactive confirmation naming the host.

CI renders every template with a sample value per declared entity type and with hostile values (quotes, spaces, unicode, newlines): each result must be an https URL on the declared host, built only from whitelisted placeholders through the declared encoder (never str.format, never {raw} in URL position).

Every link host has a provider-registry entry with tier and rationale (A8); unknown-tier hosts get the 'unknown operator' badge and their templates take IOC_TYPES values only (A8 BR4): never PERSONAL_TYPES, CNPJ, company names, keywords, malware or actor names, or other free text (P311 lint).
Initial host tiers for the registry reviewer to confirm: community - WikiLeaks (search.wikileaks.org); Lyzem pending review (unknown until recorded).

Order: P311 groups links by analyst question with verified links first; inside a group the pack's file order is the curated analyst-value order (Lyzem, then WikiLeaks); the terminal shows at most 8 links per seed, the rest go to HTML and `v3lum links`.

Verified links carry checked_at; `v3lum doctor --links` (offline) lists unverified links and links not re-checked for more than 180 days. The pack ships in phase 1 with the other pivot packs (A16), whatever the state of the related automated modules.

Legal floor (rule 4): WikiLeaks search links only for company names and keywords, never person names or usernames (a person search over leaked documents is people-search over leaked data); link only, nothing ingested or stored (rule 3); banner 'leaked documents: open manually and handle per policy'.

Lyzem (lyzem.com/search?q=, Telegram content search for BR fraud channels): person-name and username links are privacy=true, only for analyst-entered subjects with the case opt-in. A8 gate: until the reviewer records Lyzem as community tier, only IOC values (domain, url) are templated for it.
All links in this pack render only for analyst-typed seeds (analyst_ux) and carry the caution marker.
P308.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3 (osint_investigator voted P2). legal_dpo's floor keeps WikiLeaks to organisations, consistent with the chair's rule 4 reading in P221, and allows Lyzem person links only for entered subjects; analyst_ux limits the pack to typed seeds. A8 limits Lyzem to IOC values until its operator tier is recorded. The architect's standard pack schema applies.
P308.title: Pivot links: Telegram content search (Lyzem) and WikiLeaks search

final_conditions: BACKLOG unblock: ZoomEye may return to the unverified pack (P304) after a browser check shows its web UI working again; the Bing URL visual search stays out while the URL parameter is not honoured.
P309.rationale: Rejected unanimously (0-6), as the synthesizer proposed: ZoomEye web search returned 521 and Bing's URL-parameter visual search redirects to the Images home, so the templates cannot be verified and would only produce dead clicks.
P309.title: Broken pivot templates (ZoomEye search 521, Bing Visual Search by URL)

final_conditions: Not automated: no SERP scraping (Marple) and no Google CSE client (closed to new customers, discontinued 2027-01-01); grep.app may appear only as a manual unverified link (P304) because the analyst passes its Vercel checkpoint in a browser (A9).
P310.rationale: Rejected unanimously (0-6), as the synthesizer proposed: Marple scrapes search-engine result pages (anti-bot evasion, rule 1), grep.app sits behind a Vercel checkpoint, and the Google Custom Search JSON API is closed to new customers and ends on 2027-01-01. Official keyed search goes through P307.
P310.title: Search scrapers and dead search APIs (Marple, grep.app, Google CSE)

final_conditions: core/links.py loads data/pivot_links/*.json packs. The schema is frozen in phase 0, before G14 starts: label, template, entity_types, category, host (discloses_to), verified, checked_at, privacy, publishes (must be false), touches_target, login_required, antibot. The current loader format is migrated, with a test.

Templates are rendered by whitelist placeholder substitution ({q}, {qp}, {raw}, {domain}, {user}, {b64}, {e164}, {cnpj_fmt}...) via re.sub, never str.format. Each template is validated at load: https only; fixed scheme and a host equal to the declared host; the value only in path/query through the declared encoder; known placeholders and entity types only.

Per-type encoders, unit-tested: E.164 digits; BR national format (DDD + number, with and without the 9); wa.me digits; CNPJ formatted, digits-only and 8-digit root; IDN Unicode and punycode; base64 (FOFA, Pulsedive).

The CI lint applies rules 7 and 4 to links. It rejects templates that submit or publish the value (urlscan public scan, VirusTotal upload, archive.org/save, public recent-searches pages, any scan_trigger), people-search/'painel' and leaked-database sites, and pages that need a login.

TLP (A2): at AMBER and above, links render as non-clickable text with 'opening sends <value> to <host>'. At RED, third-party links are hidden from reports and shown only by `v3lum links`, with the warning. Links are never auto-opened, and `links --open` at AMBER and above needs an interactive confirmation.

privacy=true links (person, phone, e-mail) apply only to analyst-typed seeds, never to auto-discovered entities such as QSA partners, and stay hidden unless the analyst opts in for the case. No template accepts CPF: a CPF never appears in a link (team rule 4, AR24), and the lint rejects such templates.

Templates that carry PERSONAL_TYPES or CNPJ values must point to trusted or community hosts; the lint rejects unknown-tier hosts for them (A8 BR4). Links to unknown-tier hosts (IOC types only) carry an 'unknown operator' badge.

touches_target links (they open the target, or make a third party fetch it live) render defanged and non-clickable with a warning, and are hidden for hostile entities unless the analyst expands them. The investigated URL itself is never a clickable link. rel=noreferrer and the no-referrer meta stay.

Fallback: when a module is skipped or blocked (licence, needs_key, BLOCKED, egress_country, quota, hostile_host), the engine emits that source's manual link (Module.manual_link: a template or pack id) with the reason 'automation skipped: <reason>'.

Ranking: links are grouped by analyst question (reputation, history, passive DNS, code/paste, social), verified first and unverified with a badge. The terminal shows at most 8 per seed; the rest go to HTML and `v3lum links`.

Each case gets a standalone manual-pivot HTML page, self-contained with the P336 CSP. V3LUM never fetches the links itself. A test renders every bundled template with a fixture value per type and asserts a valid https URL.
P311.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. Manual links are the fallback whenever automation is blocked or not allowed (cti_lead, osint_investigator). legal_dpo's floor: rules 7 and 4 apply to links, a CI denylist, plain text with a disclosure warning at AMBER/RED, never auto-opened. The architect's floor: injection-safe whitelist substitution instead of str.format, validation at load, encoder tests. redteam_lead added touches_target handling and non-clickable target URLs, osint_investigator the encoders and the skip-reason fallback, analyst_ux the ranking and noted that no pack ships today.
P311.title: Pivot-link engine and page generator (Céos fontes_manuais port)

final_conditions: Shared engine (architect floor): a library used by js_endpoints, public_api_exposure, archive_mining, email_header_analyzer and P172, plus a module for text_blob, file and jwt inputs only. It never fetches URLs itself.

Bundle gitleaks.toml (MIT, attribution; 222 rules, RE2-only patterns converted so 221 compile in Python re). Pipeline: keyword prefilter -> regex -> Shannon entropy -> allowlist. Every compiled pattern passes a ReDoS harness in CI (adversarial strings, per-pattern time budget). Input cap 5 MB per scan, lines truncated at 10k chars; google-re2 used when installed.

Allowlist of documented example/test credentials and placeholders (AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE, sk_test_ keys, the jwt.io sample token, 'xxxx', 'changeme'...), plus one positive and one negative synthetic test vector per rule.

Masking: tokens/keys of >= 20 chars are stored as type + first 4/last 4 + SHA-256 (P145); shorter secrets as type + SHA-256 only; password-type values (config passwords, SMTP credentials) never show any character (rule 3). The location (file/URL, line) is kept.

Redaction applies to findings, attributes and res.raw before the HTTP cache, evidence, case DB, reports, events and --debug output; an end-to-end test asserts a fake token appears nowhere on disk or in events.

Found secrets never leave the machine: never validated against providers (trufflehog-style verification is forbidden; trufflehog is AGPL, ideas only), never pivoted, never sent as search values (GitHub, grep.app, IntelX, Postman). They are SECRET_TYPES; only the local SHA-256 is used for dedupe and sightings.

Severity from context without any validity test: the organisation's own credentials HIGH/CRITICAL with a notify recommendation; third-party credentials MEDIUM with an owner-notification recommendation; provider-specific rules MEDIUM/HIGH; generic/entropy-only matches an info count. The same secret in several places is one finding with N locations.

Phishing-kit exfiltration rules enabled (Telegram bot token, Discord webhook, SMTP credentials). The optional P141 helper may add 'appears N times in public breach corpora' to credential-type findings.
P312.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1 (analyst_ux voted P2). The architect's floor: a shared library plus a text/file module, ReDoS harness, input caps, redaction including res.raw with a test. legal_dpo: redaction covers evidence, cache and logs. cti_lead's stricter masking (nothing shown for passwords, limited characters for short values) is adopted because a first/last-4 hint of a password would be a masked password (team rule 3). redteam_lead: secrets never leave the machine. osint_investigator: kit exfiltration rules. analyst_ux: provider-specific vs generic severity and one finding per secret. Offline: tier n/a; bundled MIT rules: terms open.
P312.title: Secret detection rules (gitleaks ruleset; trufflehog detectors as reference)

final_conditions: BACKLOG unblock: bundle an exchange-rate or holiday table only if a report feature needs one.
P313.rationale: Rejected unanimously (0-6), as the synthesizer proposed: BCB SGS/PTAX and the BrasilAPI utilities (holidays, NCM, ISBN, FIPE, CPTEC) answer no investigative question (value 1).
P313.title: BCB SGS/PTAX and BrasilAPI misc utilities (holidays, NCM, ISBN, FIPE, CPTEC)

final_conditions: Offline module: disclosure 'none' (no network at all; ScopedHttp refuses any request), terms 'open', provider tier 'n/a'; allowed at TLP:RED.

Decode only ids taken from recognised platform URLs (x.com/twitter.com .../status/ID, discord.com/channels/... and webhook URLs, tiktok.com/@.../video/ID, linkedin.com/...activity-ID) or an explicit prefix (snowflake:ID); arbitrary long numbers in text blobs or keywords are never interpreted.

Epochs: X 1288834974657 (ids below ~2.9e13, pre-November 2010, are sequential and not decoded), Discord 1420070400000, TikTok video ids (top 32 bits = Unix seconds), LinkedIn activity ids (first 41 bits = ms). Instagram and Mastodon variants are excluded until validated with vectors. tiktok-timestamp (MIT, Bellingcat) is attributed if adapted.
Sanity window: a decoded time must fall between the platform's launch and now + 1 day, otherwise it is discarded.
Output: a 'created' attribute in UTC ISO with the epoch used, rendered 'created ~2024-05-02 13:11 UTC (decoded from the ID)'.
P314.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (cti_lead voted P3). Offline and disclosure-free (legal_dpo). The architect's and analyst_ux's rule that only platform URLs or an explicit prefix are decoded, with a sanity window, prevents confident dates from arbitrary numbers.
P314.title: Snowflake/ID -> timestamp decoders (X, Discord, TikTok, LinkedIn, Instagram)

final_conditions: Offline module (disclosure 'none', runs at TLP:RED): IEEE MA-L, MA-M, MA-S (and CID) CSVs from standards-oui.ieee.org through the dataset manager (monthly; sent with the V3LUM UA because IEEE may block generic library UAs), parsed into a compact prefix index with longest-prefix match (MA-S 36 bits > MA-M 28 > MA-L 24).
Locally administered (0x02 bit of the first octet), multicast and randomised MACs are flagged 'random/private MAC: vendor lookup not meaningful' and are never looked up or sent anywhere.

The online fallbacks (api.maclookup.app with a team-account key, api.macvendors.com keyless at 1 req/s and 1,000/day) live in a separate opt-in module (architect), used only for prefixes missing from the IEEE index; 404 = unknown OUI, 429 = RATE_LIMITED. Both providers need a recorded community tier before that module runs (A8).

Privacy (legal floor): the fallback sends only the registry prefix (6, 7 or 9 hex digits for MA-L/MA-M/MA-S), never the full MAC, which is a device identifier; a unit test asserts it on the request URL.
Fixtures: trimmed real IEEE CSV heads plus the maclookup.app and macvendors captures; tests for longest-prefix match and the locally-administered bit.
P315.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (cti_lead voted P3). legal_dpo, osint_investigator, redteam_lead and analyst_ux all require prefix-only fallback lookups; the architect's floor makes the IEEE path offline and TLP:RED-safe and moves the redundant online mirrors to an opt-in module.
P315.title: MAC OUI vendor lookup (IEEE registries offline + maclookup/macvendors fallback)

final_conditions: Offline module: disclosure 'none' (no network at all; ScopedHttp refuses any request), terms 'open', provider tier 'n/a'; allowed at TLP:RED. JWTs are SECRET_TYPES (A8): never sent to jwt.io or any online decoder, never replayed, forged or verified against the issuer.

Redaction (core rule, architect): JWT entity values are persisted only redacted (signature stripped, replaced by its length and hash; sensitive claim values masked) in the case DB, reports and evidence file names; the full token exists only in memory. JWTs are SECRET_TYPES (A8): never exported, so STIX/MISP carry only the finding and the token's SHA-256.

Structural checks for any token: alg=none (CRITICAL), missing exp, excessive lifetime, kid/jku/x5u pointing to external URLs, PII claims present (e.g. name, email). jku/x5u/kid URLs become url pivots with expand=False and are never fetched. Findings map to T1606/T1528 and CR22.

Known-default-secret check, not cracking (A7 BR8): only for HS256/384/512 tokens whose issuer or audience is an org_profile or in-scope asset, against a bundled list of <= 100 publicly documented default secrets (e.g. 'your-256-bit-secret'); no generated candidates or wordlists; skipped for third-party tokens and never applied to RS/ES tokens.
A matched secret is never printed, stored or exported: the finding reads 'signed with a publicly known default secret (list entry n)'.
Detection in text blobs uses ^eyJ[\w-]+\.eyJ[\w-]+\.[\w-]*$ through the P172 extractor. Tests use the research jwt_demo and jwt_none vectors plus a third-party token that must skip the secret check.
P316.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (cti_lead voted P3). redteam_lead, author of the A7 forbidden-action list, and legal_dpo's floor limit the default-secret check to own or in-scope tokens and never reveal a secret; the chair takes redteam_lead's 100-entry list over the architect's 10,000 so the check stays a misconfiguration test rather than JWT cracking (A7 BR8). The architect's core redaction rule keeps the full token out of every persisted output.
P316.title: JWT decode & weak-configuration analysis

final_conditions: Offline matching (disclosure 'none') of user agents from the team's own logs and alerts: an own UA regex table (browser, OS, device, bot) plus the teler-resources bad-crawler list (CC BY 4.0), downloaded at runtime by the dataset manager with attribution in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES and reports (legal floor; stricter than bundling).

PHPIDS-derived web-attack filters (LGPL-3.0, payload PCRE patterns) are not used for UA matching and are never bundled (A6); if P340 uses them, they are a separate runtime-downloaded data file with credit.
ReDoS safety (architect): every regex in the table passes a ReDoS fuzz test with a per-UA time budget, and UA input is truncated to 1 KB before matching.

Results: scanner and attack-tool UAs (sqlmap, nuclei, masscan...) are tagged scanner (benign_scanner for known research scanners), never malicious; UAs are trivially spoofed, so a UA alone never raises an IP's risk above LOW.
Fixtures: the teler captures plus synthetic UAs (browser, bot, scanner, a pathological ReDoS candidate).
P317.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3 (redteam_lead and analyst_ux voted P2). legal_dpo's floor keeps the LGPL PHPIDS data out and fetches teler at runtime with attribution; the architect's floor excludes payload regexes from UA matching and adds ReDoS tests; cti_lead's 'scanner, never malicious' wording keeps a spoofable signal weak.
P317.title: User-Agent parsing & bad-crawler/scanner UA matching (teler-resources)

final_conditions: PCI minimisation as a tested core guarantee: any card number in any input is truncated at parse time (BIN6 + last 4 for display, AR24; only the 6-8 digit BIN kept as the card_bin entity), Luhn is checked offline, and the full PAN exists only in memory: a test greps cache, evidence, logs and the case DB for it.

Only the BIN (6-8 digits) ever leaves the host, to lookup.binlist.net with header Accept-Version: 3. The registry records binlist.net's free-service terms with evidence (A1); if no business-compatible terms are found, its class becomes 'unknown' and the module stays off.
Rate: a provider bucket of 5 requests per hour per IP (hour-window quotas, P334) with quota status in coverage; 429 -> RATE_LIMITED, never 'unknown BIN'; cache 30 days.

The binlist/data ranges.csv seed is class 'unknown' (A1 initial class, no licence file): not part of this build's sources, never bundled, until legal reviews it; a miss in any seed is never 'unknown BIN'. FreeBINChecker is excluded (Cloudflare Turnstile, rule 1).
Output: scheme, type, brand, issuer and country of the BIN as card-fraud triage context (INFO). Card BINs of the own organisation (org_profile card_bins) are tagged own_asset.

Merge gate (A16): offline tests with FakeHttp (unmatched requests fail, network guard active) over trimmed real fixtures without personal data (the binlist captures plus a 429 sample), a provider-registry entry for every host, the registry contract test and the P327 lint.
P318.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. legal_dpo, cti_lead, osint_investigator and the architect make PAN truncation a tested guarantee and send only BINs. The binding A1 class for binlist/data ('unknown') keeps the offline seed out until legal reviews it, which is stricter than the members' research-profile use. The architect's hour-window bucket and the 30-day cache respect the 5/hour limit.
P318.title: Card BIN lookup (binlist.net)

final_conditions: Offline Luhn validation of IMEIs stays in core validators (already present) and runs always, with no module; IMEIs are PERSONAL_TYPES, privacy-tagged and masked in reports.

The module is only the online TAC -> model lookup (imeidb.xyz), split from the offline check, opt-in (default_enabled=False), requires_keys with a team-account token sent in a header, never in URLs, logs or cache keys (AR01); 401 -> NEEDS_KEY.

Legal floor: only the 8-digit TAC leaves the machine. If the API needs 15 digits it receives TAC + 000000 + the recomputed Luhn digit, never the real serial; if imeidb.xyz cannot answer from the TAC alone the online part is dropped.

A8 gate: imeidb.xyz must be recorded as community tier (operator, terms, track record) before the online part runs; until then it is unknown tier and receives nothing. The full IMEI is never sent to any service.
Merge gate: a real success fixture captured with the team's token (only the 401 exists); tacdb.osmocom.org is dead and not used.
P319.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. legal_dpo's, osint_investigator's, cti_lead's and the architect's TAC-only rule (zero serial plus a recomputed check digit) keeps the device identifier local. The architect splits the online part from the core validator and gates it on a real fixture. The provider's tier is unreviewed, so A8 keeps it opt-in and silent until a community tier is recorded.
P319.title: IMEI validation (Luhn) + TAC lookup

final_conditions: Needs the vin entity type (P333, may slip to P3), detected only through an explicit TYPE:value prefix or a 'VIN/chassi' label next to a 17-character value without I/O/Q; never any bare 17-character token (collisions with other ids).

Offline first: a bundled WMI table (NHTSA public-domain data, manufacturer and country, incl. Brazilian WMIs such as 9BW, 9BD, 93H). The position-9 check digit is evaluated only for North American WMIs; for other WMIs a failed check is a note, never 'invalid'.

Online step (opt-in, default_enabled=False): NHTSA vPIC decodevinvalues (vpic.nhtsa.dot.gov, batches of up to 50 VINs), US-centric and labelled as such; VINs are PERSONAL_TYPES, so it runs only when selected in a case with a recorded purpose until personal_data_review is recorded (A3/A8).
Forbidden: owner, plate or registration lookups for a VIN (the P327 lint rejects such hosts). VINs are masked (partly) in external exports.

Merge gate (A16): offline tests with FakeHttp (unmatched requests fail, network guard active) over trimmed real fixtures without personal data (the captured vPIC response plus a non-North-American VIN with a failing check digit), a provider-registry entry for every host, the registry contract test and the P327 lint.
P320.rationale: Approved 4-0-2 at median P3 (cti_lead and analyst_ux deferred: rare and US-centric). osint_investigator and the architect identified the trap that Brazilian chassis numbers need not satisfy the North American check digit; the architect's strict detection, legal_dpo's no-owner-lookup and masking rules, and the opt-in online step are adopted.
P320.title: Vehicle VIN decoder (NHTSA vPIC)

final_conditions: One classifier in core/http.py (extending block_reason) runs on every response before any parsing and BEFORE cache.put. Responses classified blocked, rate_limited, quota or error-in-200 are never written to the HTTP cache; today a 200 'Just a moment' page and an 'API count exceeded' body are cached and replayed. ScopedHttp offers evict(resp) and a cache_if hook for module-level detections.

Generic markers come from maigret COMMON_ERRORS and sherlock WAFHitMsgs (MIT, attributed): Cloudflare 'Just a moment'/challenge-platform, AWS WAF, PerimeterX, Incapsula, DDoS-Guard, Vercel checkpoint and captcha pages, plus final-URL checks (ISC blockme.html redirect).
Weak markers (captcha words) apply only on error statuses. A regression test proves that normal pages mentioning captcha are not marked blocked.

Login walls (a redirect or final URL to /login, /accounts/login or /signin, the LinkedIn authwall, Instagram/Facebook login interstitials) give BLOCKED reason_code 'login_wall'. Geo-block pages (CloudFront 'request could not be satisfied', Akamai reference pages) give BLOCKED 'geo_block' with an egress_country hint. Neither is ever EMPTY or ABSENT.

Per-source error-in-200 rules are declared data, shared with P331 specs: error_markers in the registry or the module, each a JSON path + value or a regex mapping to blocked | rate_limited | quota | error.

Initial error-in-200 rules: HackerTarget 'API count exceeded', Criminal IP {'status':403}, IPQS success:false, Etherscan status '0', CheckPhish errorMessage, hunter.how {'code':401}, Leak-Lookup error:true, ReceitaWS status ERROR, TCU SISTEMA_INDISPONIVEL.
DNSBL refusal codes (Spamhaus 127.255.255.x) map to BLOCKED, never to 'listed' or 'not listed'. Keyless sources map HTTP 403 to BLOCKED, not ERROR.
Classification never yields EMPTY. Each rule maps to a human-readable reason shown in coverage (e.g. 'HackerTarget: daily quota exhausted (API count exceeded)').
Detection only (rule 1): no retry with another UA, headers, cookies, proxy/IP or solver. The maigret/sherlock bypass helpers are not ported, and messages give no bypass hints.

A host that returned a challenge or geo-block is short-circuited for the rest of the run (in memory, reason_code 'circuit') and never cached across runs. Generic challenge markers give BLOCKED reason_code 'challenge' (A3 BR16, A9).
Each marker ships one trimmed real fixture (from the research samples) with a test.
P321.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1; a phase-0 item. cti_lead, osint_investigator and the architect verified that block pages and error-in-200 bodies are cached and replayed today, so classification must precede caching (architect floor: one classifier, declared markers, never EMPTY). legal_dpo's floor: detection never becomes circumvention, and MIT attribution. osint_investigator added login-wall and geo-block detection, analyst_ux human-readable reasons and the weak-marker regression. redteam_lead agreed it keeps WAF pages out of LIGHT/ACTIVE findings.
P321.title: Body-level error and bot-wall detection (error-in-200, WAF/challenge fingerprints)

final_conditions: Finding carries confidence_label (confirmed | probable | possible) and criterion (text). res.finding(..., confidence=) accepts a label or a float, backward compatible: >= 0.85 -> confirmed, >= 0.55 -> probable, else possible. Labels map to 1.0 / 0.7 / 0.4 for scoring (P302) and 90 / 70 / 40 for STIX (P303), documented in one table.
criterion is mandatory for severity >= low; the module contract test fails otherwise. Finding.to_dict gains confidence_label and criterion, and stored cases without them still render.
Analyst overrides are stored separately, keyed by the deterministic finding id (AR09). They always win and survive re-runs.

Automatic downgrades happen only through named suppression rules (warninglist, sinkhole, generic/role address, stale listing, version-inferred CVE, homonym), recorded with the rule id and reason in the criterion (e.g. 'POSSIBLE - on warninglist <name>').
Automatic upgrades are at most +1 level and only with >= 2 independent upstream families. No automatic change ever crosses an analyst decision.
Pivot edges use the same labels, which feed path confidence (AR07).
The terminal findings table shows the label for every finding and the criterion for HIGH/CRITICAL; HTML/MD always show both.
Lands in phase 0, before group implementation (API freeze). Tests: the float mapping, override precedence, and a warninglisted IOC showing 'POSSIBLE - on warninglist <name>'.
P322.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. cti_lead and analyst_ux found that 'confidence never decreases automatically' contradicts the suppression rules of P146, P171 and P302. The chair resolves it their way: the lock applies only across analyst decisions, and rule-driven downgrades are allowed with a recorded criterion. This matches the architect's floor (downgrades only via explicit suppression rules recorded with the rule id), which also requires a backward-compatible API frozen in phase 0. osint_investigator extended the labels to pivot edges. legal_dpo, redteam_lead and osint_investigator approved without conditions.
P322.title: Finding confidence model (CONFIRMED/PROBABLE/POSSIBLE with mandatory criterion)

final_conditions: The pattern DB serves text_blob/file extraction and typing suggestions only. Single-value detect() keeps today's precedence, so a typed username or phone is never re-typed, and the existing test_detect suite passes unchanged.

From lemmeknow/pywhat regex.json and the SpiderFoot offline extractors (MIT, attributed in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md), import only patterns with a validator or a distinctive prefix/checksum: cloud keys, JWT, crypto with checksum, analytics ids, IBAN, cards with Luhn, SRV names, odd headers.
Generic patterns (phone, date, generic ids) are disabled by default. A pattern without a validator cannot exceed confidence 0.5.
Each adopted pattern ships a confidence, a validator and positive + negative vectors. Patterns with no consuming module and no masking need are not emitted as entities.

Payment card numbers are truncated to BIN(6)+last4 at detection time; the full PAN is never stored, logged or rendered (PCI DSS). IBAN, CPF-like numbers and other national ids are masked in every output.

Secret types (cloud keys, tokens, JWTs, bot tokens, private keys) are SECRET_TYPES: kept as type + masked preview (first 4/last 4) + SHA-256 only, NO_AUTO_EXPAND, never validated, used or sent anywhere (rule 1), and reported once as 'sensitive data in pasted text'.
Financial and secret hits yield local-only findings: no pivots, never passed to modules with disclosure third_party or target (shares_input=True), masked in terminal, reports, evidence and case DB.
Detection-triggered SRV/DNS lookups obey the TLP gate (no public DoH under TLP:RED).
Every imported regex gets a ReDoS review and a pathological-input test. Test: a mixed incident text sends no card number or secret off the machine.
P323.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (legal_dpo voted P1). All members feared 142 unfiltered patterns would flood pastes and route secrets or card numbers to third parties. Patterns are therefore restricted to validated or distinctive ones (cti_lead, architect floor: no validator -> confidence <= 0.5, existing detection untouched). legal_dpo's floor: PAN truncation at detection, never testing secrets, the TLP gate on lookups. redteam_lead and the architect added NO_AUTO_EXPAND and local-only handling, osint_investigator and analyst_ux kept single-value detection unchanged.
P323.title: Identification regex DB for text blobs (lemmeknow/pywhat, SpiderFoot extractors)

final_conditions: Evidence is content-addressed (SHA-256 of the stored, already-sanitized bytes, P145) and write-once: 0600 files in a 0700 case directory. A re-collection writes a new version plus an append-only audit row, never an overwrite, and the version keeps a diff summary.

Each evidence record stores the request context: method; redacted URL (AR01); final URL and redirect chain; HTTP status; selected response headers (date, content-type, server); UA and egress profile; from_cache; fetched_at (the cache row time when served from cache, not now()); collected_at from rt.now(); dataset name and SHA-256 for dataset-derived results.
Filenames follow <module>__<type>__<hmac12>__<sha10>.json (the A4 keyed HMAC). No raw e-mail, phone, CPF, username or any other value appears in a path.

Per-case audit trail (schema migration): case purpose, legal-basis code, requester/ticket (AR16), analyst (OS user or config), opsec mode, authorization reference, scope SHA-256, engagement window, egress profile and its public IP when known (last `v3lum doctor --egress` check, with its time), TLP changes, overrides (egress, breach scope, show-personal) and the org profile hash.

Per-case JSONL request ledger for every LIGHT/ACTIVE request: UTC time, module, method, host, resolved IP, port, redacted path, status, bytes, egress profile, opsec. It is written even with --no-evidence. Ledger and audit are append-only and hash-chained, and the report summarises targets touched and request counts.
`v3lum cases verify <id>` recomputes every evidence and report hash and the ledger/audit hash chains offline, and prints a pass/fail summary.

Retention (A10): 'immutable' means append-only within the retention period. Purge deletes every version and keeps a value-free tombstone. The minimal engagement audit and ledger (no bodies, paths redacted) follow audit_retention_days, which defaults to retention_days; a longer period needs a written legal decision.

Evidence has a size cap per file and per case, with gzip. Scans get no extra prompts: identity comes from config/OS user and the reference from the existing gate. On re-collection the report header shows 'since last run: N new findings, M resolved'.
Tests: tamper detection (edited file, broken chain), cache-served evidence keeps fetched_at, no raw value in filenames, and purge removes all versions.
Merge order: this proposal's audit record and request ledger land before any LIGHT/ACTIVE module merges, and the AR20 safety suite checks them (A7 BR13, A16 BR6).
P324.rationale: Approved 6-0. The chair raises the priority from the median P2 to P1: A7 binds every LIGHT/ACTIVE run to an audit record and a request ledger, so this must land before any LIGHT/ACTIVE module merges, and legal_dpo, osint_investigator and redteam_lead voted P1 (legal floor, A7/A10). redteam_lead defined the ledger, osint_investigator the request context and pseudonymised filenames, cti_lead the cache fetched_at. legal_dpo's floor: purpose and legal basis in the audit, append-only only within retention, sanitizer before any version. The architect's floor: content addressing, migrations, delete removes files and rows, tamper tests. analyst_ux: no extra prompts, a one-command verify.
P324.title: Evidence store with re-collection versioning and audit trail (Céos port)

final_conditions: Fix app.App.ask_feedback now. Only explicit judgements are stored: findings the analyst lists are wrong; unlisted ones stay unrated (no row). An overall 'yes' stores only the case verdict and credits no finding, and an optional 'which were right?' step records explicit positive votes. Today 'no' + Enter marks all 30 reviewed findings correct.

Votes are idempotent per (case, deterministic finding id, analyst): a re-vote replaces the earlier one and never double-counts (today a repeated `cases feedback` increments module_stats again). This requires the AR09 deterministic ids.

Beta(alpha, beta) is kept per source (registry source id) and per correlation rule, stored via a migration. The prior comes from the source's Admiralty grade, and 'partly' counts 0.5. Weights change only after >= 5 votes, with a floor of 0.3, and votes older than 12 months weigh half.

The overall verdict takes one keypress. The optional per-item review is capped at 10 items ordered by score contribution, correlations included (per-rule votes), with an optional one-key reason for 'wrong' (homonym / outdated / benign infra / wrong type) stored for tuning.

Attention points and the limitations section ('could not verify: X, Y (reason)') are generated from coverage statuses (blocked, quota, needs_key, licence, tlp, policy, timeout, deadline) by a tested pure function and shown on the first screen. They are worded as suggestions, and the analyst's verdict prevails.
Feedback never deletes or hides findings. Per-rule statistics feed P301 precision and A3 demotion.
Feedback notes and per-finding votes are case data, purged with the case (A10). Only aggregated per-source/per-rule counters without entity values survive.
Tests cover the yes / partial / no paths, idempotent re-votes and the rule that fewer than 5 votes have no effect.
P325.rationale: Approved 6-0. The chair raises the priority from the median P2 to P1 because the current loop corrupts the reliability statistics that P302 (P1) consumes: 'no' + Enter reinforces every finding (analyst_ux) and 'yes' auto-credits all of them, saturating at 1.0 (cti_lead). The two members differed on whether 'yes' should credit displayed findings; the chair takes cti_lead's stricter verdict-only rule and offers analyst_ux's explicit 'which were right?' step. The architect's floor: deterministic ids, idempotent votes, Beta after >= 5 votes with a 0.3 floor. legal_dpo's floor: votes and notes purged with the case, the analyst's verdict prevails.
P325.title: Analyst verdict, attention points and feedback (Céos parecer port)

final_conditions: Host profiles are entries of the single provider registry (data/providers.json, AR11): per provider user_agent, accept, accept_language, timeout, retries, max_bytes, ttl, min_interval and concurrency, consumed by HttpClient. There is no second table. FakeHttp gains header matching, and every profile entry has a unit test (UA/Accept per host).

veto_lift (1): hosts of providers flagged sensitive (XposedOrNot, LeakCheck, Hudson Rock, HIBP and similar breach, infostealer or people-data providers) are no-store in the HTTP cache, or the cache stores only the P145-sanitized payload. A test proves that no masked password/login, computer_name or IP from the Hudson Rock fixture appears in cache rows.

veto_lift (2): the default UA (setting user_agent) becomes a neutral 'V3LUM/<version>' that identifies neither the organisation, the team nor the analyst (no company name or mailbox), replacing today's spoofed Chrome string. Identifying UAs with a role mailbox (setting contact_email) appear only in profiles of providers whose terms ask for them: SEC, Wikimedia, Nominatim, bgp.tools.
registro.br gets a non-browser UA and Accept application/rdap+json. A provider that requires a contact UA while contact_email is empty is SKIPPED with reason_code 'config'.
