veto_lift (2, continued): LIGHT/ACTIVE requests never carry the organisation's identity. They use the egress-profile UA (setting ua_light, a common browser UA by default) or, for ACTIVE, the scope file's ROE UA/header, which may carry an engagement token agreed with the scope owner but never the organisation's name, team, mailbox or analyst. The contact UA never goes to unknown-tier providers.

veto_lift (3): a block, challenge or 403 is never retried with a different UA or headers. No UA rotation and no browser spoofing to defeat bot controls; a browser UA is used only where a provider's public page needs one, never to pass a bot wall (rule 1).

veto_lift (4): the effective TTL = min(profile ttl, cache_max_age_days, retention_days). Defaults: DNS 1 h, RDAP 24 h, CNPJ 72 h, sanitized breach payloads 7 d, crypto 1 h, sanctions 24 h. Long-lived reference data (IBGE/DDD) goes to datasets, not to the HTTP cache.
Retries: one retry honouring Retry-After <= 15 s, otherwise RATE_LIMITED. Retries and waits are bounded by the run deadline (AR05). Per-provider byte caps also apply to target responses.
Negative caching is unchanged: 401/403/429/5xx and P321-classified bodies are never cached, and failures are short-circuited only in memory for the rest of the run.
cache_key includes Accept and a hash of credential-bearing headers and params, so keyed and keyless answers never mix. Per-host politeness is max(module, host profile) (P334).

Other profiles from the research: HIBP (any UA), SANS ISC (Accept application/json), KeyCDN ('keycdn-tools:<site>'), PhishTank ('phishtank/<app>'), and Accept-Language pt-BR for Brazilian hosts. Host profiles never override opsec, scope, TLP or egress decisions.
P326.rationale: Mechanical status: vetoed by legal_dpo (yes 5 / reject 1). veto_lift adopted: legal_dpo's four lift conditions (sensitive hosts no-store or sanitized only, a neutral default UA without organisation or mailbox with identifying UAs only where providers ask, no UA/header retry after a block, TTLs within retention) are conditions 2-7, so the proposal is approved at its median P1 in phase 0. Most live failures in the sweeps were UA/Accept problems (cti_lead, osint_investigator). redteam_lead, osint_investigator and analyst_ux independently objected to the team-mailbox UA for opsec reasons. The architect's floor: profiles live in the single provider registry, the contact UA never goes to targets, Retry-After <= 15 s, header-matching tests.
P326.title: Per-host HTTP profiles (UA, Accept, timeout, retries, TTL, negative caching)

final_conditions: One pure function, core/policy.py decide(module_cls, entity, options, profiles) -> Decision(allowed, status, reason_code, reason), used by Engine.select, App.run_single, the shell, extract --scan, batch, watch and doctor health checks. No gate exists anywhere else, and decide() and the engine use only the canonical A3 reason codes and their Status mapping.

decide() order, first failure wins: metadata validity, offline, licence (A1), TLP (A2), tier/--allow-unknown (A8), privacy (run_on, breach scope, purpose, PERSONAL_TYPES to unknown tier; A4/A8), own_asset (A11), opsec vs mode, ACTIVE authorization + scope / LIGHT seeds-only (A7), egress_country (A9), keys, packages, datasets, quota (P334), circuit.

Secure defaults: Module.terms='unknown', provider tier 'unknown', no implicit disclosure. @register (also for ~/.v3lum/plugins and P331 specs) refuses a module whose class body does not declare terms, opsec, disclosure and hosts, or whose hosts and feeds lack a provider-registry entry.

Runtime enforcement: ScopedHttp and Resolver know the module's opsec, disclosure and hosts. PASSIVE modules reach only declared hosts (exact or '*.' wildcard) and core DoH; redirects to undeclared hosts are not followed; target-derived hosts only for LIGHT/ACTIVE.

Disclosure 'none' modules get no network at all, and 'internal' modules reach only their configured internal hosts (A8 BR9). A violation ends SKIPPED reason_code 'policy', recorded in the case audit and shown by doctor.

LIGHT/ACTIVE modules use only the core HTTP client and the core socket connector. The lint fails direct socket, urllib, http.client or subprocess network use in modules. ctx.allowed_opsec = min(scan mode, module opsec).
A forbidden-capability lint runs in CI over modules, plugins, P331 specs and data files (username site lists, pivot packs).

The lint rejects sign-up, register, availability, check_username, validate, password-reset and login endpoints; CAPTCHA solvers; FlareSolverr, cloudscraper and undetected browsers; credential/password fields outside P145 schemas; CPF-lookup or 'painel' hosts; publishing endpoints (rule 7); state-changing methods toward targets.

Forbidden actions (A7 BR8-BR9), enforced in code and by the lint in every mode: exploitation or payload confirmation; credential brute force, spraying, default-login checks or any login attempt; use of leaked or found credentials and keys; JWT/hash cracking; DoS/stress; uploads, writes or deletes; takeover claims; OAST/interactsh callbacks. ACTIVE uses only GET/HEAD/OPTIONS unless allow-listed.
Modules flagged sensitive, or returning passwords, must declare a P145 sanitizer schema; otherwise registration fails.

Registry-wide CI lint: metadata enums, declared hosts present in the registry, vocab-only attribute/tag/relation names, and a fixture-backed test per module. Tests assert that requested hosts are a subset of declared hosts plus DoH (FakeHttp records hosts).
Table-driven tests over TLP x disclosure x licence x tier x opsec x scope x org_profile x run_on, including App.run_single refusals under TLP:RED, with an exhausted quota and without authorization.
Each policy rule has an id, quoted in failure messages and in docs/RULES.md (generated from the rule table, AR22). The policy file is versioned with the council decision ids.

Analyst output: every denial maps to a readable reason in coverage (e.g. 'skipped: noncommercial terms (licence profile corporate)'), and the terminal aggregates denials into one line per reason. `v3lum info <module>` explains which policy applies and why. Registration and CI checks fail the build, never the analyst's scan.
P327.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1; the keystone of phase 0. The architect showed two execution paths, one of which (`v3lum run`) skips TLP, quota and the active-mode confirmation, so the floor is one pure decide() on every path plus table-driven tests. legal_dpo's floor: fail-closed metadata at registration (plugins and specs too), runtime enforcement, all gates at one choke point, a forbidden-capability denylist. redteam_lead: a metadata lint cannot stop a PASSIVE module that fetches the target, hence host-layer enforcement and the core socket connector. osint_investigator extended the lint to data files, cti_lead to declared hosts, analyst_ux asked for readable aggregated reasons.
P327.title: Collection policy as code (Céos docs/07 rules) + TLP gate

final_conditions: Status gains QUOTA (budget, daily or monthly limit), distinct from RATE_LIMITED (transient 429). The existing 8 values stay stable, and _STATUS_RANK, coverage and the renderers are updated.

ModuleResult gains reason_code (the canonical A3 codes) and partial (bool). A per-source execution report (completed / partial / rate_limited / quota / failed + stop_reason) is kept in the case JSON and in the coverage table.

Coverage is computed per (seed, module) with status counts, not per module with the last reason. Summaries rank could-not-verify statuses (quota, rate_limited, blocked, error, needs_key, unavailable) above empty; today 'blocked on the seed, empty on a pivot' is summarised as empty.
Tri-state convention for existence checks: attribute presence = found | absent | unknown, with the evidence (marker, URL, checked_at). ABSENT only on documented positive evidence.

Meaningful 404s are declared per module in Module.absent_statuses (e.g. {404}), replacing ok404. They are documented per source (InternetDB, GreyNoise, CIRCL hashlookup, PoC-in-GitHub, Cymru NXDOMAIN, HIBP breachedaccount) and tested.

Keyless modules map HTTP 403 to BLOCKED ('could not verify'), not ERROR as Engine.run_module does today. DNS SERVFAIL/REFUSED/timeouts mean UNKNOWN. A run that overruns its deadline ends ERROR with reason_code 'timeout'.

No output says 'not found', 'not listed', 'no account', 'clean' or 'does not exist' for a source that did not answer. The first screen shows 'N of M applicable sources answered; K could not verify' with the list, and a seed below the coverage threshold reads 'inconclusive' (P302).

Fix the reference modules with dead-DoH tests: email_basics must not turn a DoH failure into mx_valid=False or 'domain does not accept mail', and dns_records may emit negative findings only after OK A/AAAA/CNAME answers.
One test per status mapping and per meaningful-404 declaration.
P328.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1; a phase-0 item implementing rule 5 uniformly. The architect's floor: QUOTA added while the 8 values stay stable, keyless 403 -> BLOCKED, declared absent_statuses, the execution report. cti_lead and analyst_ux made could-not-verify visible on the first screen with 'inconclusive' instead of 'clean'. osint_investigator asked for the per-entity matrix and no absence claims. cti_lead flagged the email_basics rule-5 bug in the reference module. legal_dpo and redteam_lead approved without conditions.
P328.title: Result status semantics: quota vs not-found vs blocked vs unknown (tri-state)

final_conditions: This is an infrastructure self-check, not a LIGHT module, and is not gated by --mode. It contacts only a fixed list of benign hosts (the configured DoH provider, pypi.org...), never investigated targets.

A shared helper, core/tls.py, is used by tls_inspect (P275), P084 and doctor, so the logic is not duplicated. It checks chains against certifi's Mozilla bundle only: when the system store verifies but the Mozilla-only check fails, the issuer is recorded as 'TLS-intercepted by <issuer>'. Verification is never disabled and the corporate proxy is never bypassed.

It runs in doctor, and at most once per 24 h per egress profile (result cached in the home dir). At scan start it runs only when cert-derived modules are selected, in parallel, never blocking the scan start, and never in --offline.

When interception is detected: case metadata records the issuer, cert-derived findings (tls_inspect, CT comparisons, JARM, P084 CR17-CR19) are marked inconclusive for that run, and one header line says so (not one line per finding).
The check runs per egress profile, because interception differs per route. When the LIGHT/ACTIVE route is intercepted, a warning says that target traffic passes the corporate inspection proxy.
Unit tests use recorded chains (the design_tls_inspect fixture) and injected SSL contexts.
P329.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. Corporate TLS inspection would otherwise make certificate findings describe the proxy (Ceos and the research sandbox hit it). redteam_lead and the architect reclassified it as an infrastructure check, since it never touches targets. It runs per egress profile (redteam_lead), at most daily and never blocking startup (osint_investigator, architect floor, analyst_ux), with shared core/tls.py code (architect floor). cti_lead: the benign host list and inconclusive cert findings. legal_dpo raised no issue.
P329.title: Global TLS-interception detection (corporate proxy/AV re-signing)

final_conditions: `v3lum data update` refreshes iana_tlds.txt (data.iana.org) and public_suffix_list.dat (publicsuffix.org) into ~/.v3lum/datasets, never into the installed package. The bundled copies stay as fallbacks. Both providers are registered as tier trusted, terms open (IANA public data; PSL MPL-2.0).

Downloads are validated before they replace the previous copy: PSL markers '===BEGIN ICANN DOMAINS===', the IANA '# Version' header, minimum entry counts (com and br present), and anti-bot/error pages rejected through P321. The replace is atomic, and the previous copy is kept on failure.

One machine-readable registry (bundled files, register_dataset licence/terms/attribution fields, adapted MIT/BSD/Apache code) generates data/NOTICE and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. Each entry: name, source URL, version/commit or etag, SHA-256, licence, attribution text, bundled or runtime.
CI fails when a bundled file has no NOTICE entry, or when a GPL/AGPL/CC BY-SA/NC dataset is bundled instead of downloaded at runtime (A6).
The PSL stays an unmodified MPL-2.0 file with its notice, and the IANA list is public data. Attributions (ATT&CK, CC BY sources, runtime-only GPL datasets) are generated from the registry.
P330.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (legal_dpo voted P1). osint_investigator asked for validation before replacing, because a challenge page replacing the PSL would silently break every domain pivot. legal_dpo's floor: a machine-checked inventory and a CI block on bundled copyleft/NC data, the PSL kept unmodified. The architect's floor: datasets written to the home dir, never the package, atomic replace with a bundled fallback, notices generated from metadata. IANA and the PSL are data sources: tier trusted, terms open.
P330.title: Bundled reference data refresh (IANA TLD list, PSL, NOTICE file)

final_conditions: Each spec compiles into a real Module subclass with the full contract: terms with evidence, provider and tier, disclosure, opsec passive, hosts, quotas/min_interval, run_on, error_markers, found/absent rules, absent_statuses and a health_check value. Policy, quotas and status semantics therefore apply unchanged, and a spec without these fails the P327 lint.

Specs are bundled in v3lum/data/specs. User specs load only from ~/.v3lum/specs, with the plugin ownership/permission checks (AR12). Specs are schema-validated at load, with no eval and only whitelisted placeholders taking type-validated, URL-encoded values.

The request URL host must be a literal declared host of the spec (https only). Templating the host from the entity is refused, so a passive spec can never contact the target. Only GET search lookups are allowed (no POST of the value to submission or publishing endpoints, rule 7), and the spec language cannot express logins, cookies or CAPTCHA handling.

Machinae's declarative pattern is re-implemented with MIT attribution: request {url template, params, method, headers, ignored_status_codes}, results [{key dotted.path, pretty_name, regex, match_all, format}], multi_match onlyif, paginated, multi_json (NDJSON).

Supported formats: JSON, NDJSON, CSV, RSS/XML and HTML-embedded JSON (__NEXT_DATA__, ld+json). A minimal dotted-path extractor is used (no JSONPath library), with bounded, reviewed regexes. Machinae's site list is not ported.
The P321 classifier runs first, and challenge-protected sites are link-only (A9).
A spec is enabled only with a trimmed real fixture and a parametrized test (spec + fixture -> expected attributes/status), plus an error-in-200 fixture.

Defaults follow A3/A8: specs for unknown-tier operators or with unknown terms ship default_enabled=False and stay disabled under corporate until reviewed. Unknown-tier specs never receive PERSONAL_TYPES, and community profile-site specs follow the A5 username rules.
Specs failing their health checks on 7 consecutive days are auto-disabled with a doctor notice. `v3lum info` shows spec sources like any module (terms, tier, hosts).
P331.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (osint_investigator P1; cti_lead and analyst_ux P3, wary of adding long-tail unknown operators). The engine is approved, while each spec still faces the A1/A3/A8 gates and the default-off rule for unknown tiers or terms (legal_dpo, cti_lead). The architect's floor: specs compile into real Module subclasses, schema validation, declared hosts, a fixture per spec. redteam_lead: a URL template is code, hence the literal-host rule. legal_dpo: a spec cannot express logins, cookies or POSTs to publishing endpoints. osint_investigator: formats, health-based auto-disable.
P331.title: Declarative JSON/CSV/RSS collector (Machinae-style specs)

final_conditions: veto_lift: the subfinder-style multi-key random rotation is dropped. One key per provider per installation, or per user where the provider licenses per-user keys. Quotas are counted per key and per egress (P334).

veto_lift (continued): several keys only where the provider's terms explicitly allow multiple keys for one organisation (e.g. paid seats), selected deterministically by owner/plan alias and logged by alias, never by value. Never to multiply free-tier limits or to use other people's keys.

One consolidated schema replaces the overlapping fields, frozen in phase 0 as contract v2. Declared by the module: terms, disclosure (none | internal | third_party | target), hosts, provider, sources, access_model, run_on, max_requests, expected_latency, requires_egress, max_rate, absent_statuses, error_markers, manual_link, health_check().

Derived from the provider registry, never declared by the module: trust_tier, upstream families, reliability (Admiralty grade), sensitive, publishes_queries, reuses_queries and fetches_target (A8 BR8).
max_rate is the LIGHT/ACTIVE request rate per target host in req/s, never above the A7 ceilings.

access_model takes one of free_noauth_unlimited | free_noauth_limited | free_auth_limited | free_auth_unlimited | commercial_only | internal | offline, and is shown in `modules`/`info` with a plain-words label (e.g. 'free, no key, limited').

max_tlp (A2) is derived by core/policy.py from disclosure, tier and the publishes/reuses flags, never hand-set, and enforced by the engine: none/internal -> red; target -> amber (red only on verified own assets not third_party_hosted); trusted -> amber+strict; community -> amber; unknown or reuses_queries -> green (unknown only with --allow-unknown); publishes_queries -> never.
shares_input becomes a derived alias of disclosure (disclosure in {third_party, target}).

health_check() returns a benign value from one central list (example.com, 8.8.8.8, EICAR, CVE-2021-44228, octocat), or an offline self-test for LIGHT/ACTIVE modules. doctor (P337) and the keys wizard (P379) use it, and its calls count against quotas.

describe(), `v3lum info` and doctor show every field. A registry-wide contract test validates all registered modules (enums, explicit declarations, registry entries). Existing modules and stored cases keep working.
P332.rationale: Mechanical status: vetoed by legal_dpo (yes 5 / reject 1). veto_lift adopted: random rotation across several keys exists to evade per-key quotas (rule 6, and rule 1 when the keys belong to others). Dropping it, with one key per provider unless the terms allow more, is condition 1. Everything else is approved as legal_dpo's lift allows, with max_tlp aligned to A2. cti_lead, osint_investigator, redteam_lead, the architect and analyst_ux all asked for the same drop. The chair raises the priority from the median P2 to P1 on the architect floor: the A16 phase-0 freeze needs this schema before ~300 modules are written (architect and cti_lead voted P1). One disclosure concept replaces shares_input + max_tlp (architect, analyst_ux); max_rate is redteam_lead's.
P332.title: Module metadata taxonomy (access model, health check, TLP limits) from SpiderFoot/IntelOwl/Cortex

final_conditions: A type is added only if an approved module or pivot pack in this build accepts or produces it. Each new type names its consumer/producer and gets a normalizer, validator, display, a STIX mapping (or an explicit 'no STIX object') and collision tests. md5/sha1/sha256 detection is unchanged and the existing detect suite passes.

First wave: email_headers (raw header blocks, .eml, .msg) for phishing triage; telegram_handle and telegram_invite (t.me/<name>, t.me/+<invite>); discord_invite; social_account (platform + handle from profile URLs and platform-context @handles, never blindly expanded into a multi-site sweep); pix_brcode detection (EMV '000201'...'6304' + CRC16) feeding P233.

Also first wave: the structural hashes imphash, tlsh (T1 + 70 hex), telfhash, gimphash, authentihash, icon_dhash and code_signing_cert, needed by P351. Second wave: pgp_fingerprint, fediverse and bsky handles, steam profile, port/service. eu_vat, vin, tiktok video id and snowflake id may slip to P3.

Detection comes only from an explicit TYPE:value prefix, a URL pattern (t.me/, discord.gg/, bsky.app/...) or an unambiguous structure (header block, T1+70-hex TLSH, a leading-@ @user@instance). Detection is offline: no WebFinger or other lookup. Never from bare hex or digit length (imphash = MD5 length, authentihash = SHA-256 length, snowflake/TikTok ids vs phone/CPF).

Personal-identifier types (telegram, fediverse, bsky and steam handles, social_account, invites, vin, email_headers) join PERSONAL_TYPES: not auto-expanded from text/file inputs, excluded from cross-case sightings by default, and masked where they carry personal data (VIN partly).
CPF stays never-expanded, and person names are typed and used only after analyst confirmation.
Secret-like types (telegram_bot_token and similar) are detect-only SECRET_TYPES: NO_AUTO_EXPAND, masked, never used or validated against any API, never shared or exported.
email_headers/.eml/.msg parsing is static and offline: it never fetches remote images, tracking pixels, CSS or links, and recipient lists are not pivoted.
image: EXIF GPS is location data, tagged privacy, and never auto-pivoted to map or reverse-geocoding services.
Invites: public preview metadata only, never joining, logging in or accepting. port/service entities never trigger probing on pivot. The similar_to relation is low confidence and never auto-expanded.
Vocab additions (same_m365_tenant, intercepted_by, quota status) go to core/vocab.py. Local fuzzy-hash computation (py-tlsh, telfhash) comes only via optional extras.

Phasing: the first-wave types consumed by P1 proposals (email_headers, telegram_handle, telegram_invite, discord_invite, social_account, pix_brcode; used by P172, P112 and P233) land in phase 1 with P172. The rest follows this proposal's P2.
P333.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (osint_investigator voted P1). The architect's floor and analyst_ux: add only consumed types, never guess hex/digit-length formats, keep detection unchanged. cti_lead put email_headers and structural hashes first, osint_investigator social_account and pix_brcode for Brazilian scams. legal_dpo's floor: new personal identifiers join the protected class, EXIF GPS is never auto-pivoted, invites are preview-only, secrets are never used. redteam_lead: static e-mail parsing (tracking pixels reveal the investigation), no probing on port pivots.
P333.title: New entity types and detector patterns suggested by the sweeps

final_conditions: Budgets are keyed by provider (the registry quota block: per egress_ip or per key; hour/day/month UTC windows plus a token bucket for rate), not by module. All endpoints of a provider share one counter, and only requests to that provider's hosts count (DoH is not charged).

Quota is reserved before sending, inside HttpClient/ScopedHttp, with an atomic SQLite update that holds across threads and processes, so 12 threads cannot overshoot a 50/day budget. Exhaustion raises QuotaExceeded -> Status.QUOTA with 'could not verify' wording.

Budgets come from the registry with evidence of the published limit and default to at most 80% of it. Keyless budgets are global per installation and egress, never multiplied by keys, proxies or Tor exits. An optional team-shared quota DB path (setting quota_db_path) serves analysts behind one NAT. Keyed plans get monthly counters.

A per-destination-host limiter is shared by all modules: interval = the max of every interval declared for that host by modules and profiles, and of the opsec floor, and the slot is always reserved (today HostLimiter.wait_turn returns early for min_interval 0).
Hard ceilings: LIGHT <= 1 req/s and <= 25 requests per target host per scan; ACTIVE <= 10 req/s and <= 2 concurrent connections per host, lowered by the scope file when it says so.
20% of each daily budget is reserved for seeds; pivots at depth >= 2 never consume it. Seeds are prioritised and low-value calls deferred.

Each exhausted source gets one report line (e.g. 'HackerTarget: 50/50 today, 12 lookups deferred'), and deferred lookups are listed per source. `v3lum cases resume <id>` re-runs only the deferred or could-not-verify (module, entity) pairs.
The provider's own quota signal (P321 error markers) wins when counters disagree: the counter is set to exhausted until the window resets.
Exhaustion never triggers a fallback to LIGHT/ACTIVE alternatives, another account or another egress. Health checks (P337) and key tests (P379) count against budgets.
Module.daily_quota stays as a fallback for providers without a registry quota. Quota state is shown in coverage and doctor. Tests use a fake clock, plus a 12-thread overshoot test.
P334.rationale: Approved 6-0. The chair raises the priority from the median P2 to P1 on the architect floor: it is in the A16 phase-0 list because per-module accounting is both inaccurate and racy, and free quotas shared per egress IP ran out during research (the architect, legal_dpo and redteam_lead voted P1). The architect's floor: buckets per provider, atomic reservation before sending, QuotaExceeded -> QUOTA. legal_dpo's floor: budgets from published limits at <= 80%, never multiplied, no fallback to another account or egress. redteam_lead: the shared per-host limiter and hard ceilings. analyst_ux: the seed reserve, deferral lines and resume. cti_lead and osint_investigator: a shared quota store.
P334.title: Per-source quotas and token buckets (daily/monthly budgets, shared-egress awareness)

final_conditions: Grouping happens only in the presentation layer (terminal, HTML, MD). Case JSON, STIX/MISP exports and evidence keep every entity, finding, source and link. Distinct IOCs are never merged: URL variants are grouped visually and exported separately.

Only findings stating the same fact about the same subject are grouped: the same breach across sources; URL variants of one resource (refanged, www/no-www, tracking-param variants); the same CVE from several sources. Distinct identity entities (username, social_account, person_name, email, phone) are never merged.

A grouped row shows the highest severity and confidence with its criterion, the count, and the sources and upstream families (e.g. 'seen by 3 sources: XON, HIBP, LeakCheck'). Every member keeps its evidence and feedback id.
Correlations are grouped by entity. Grouping keys (normalized URL, breach name) are deterministic, documented and tested. Score de-duplication stays in scoring (P302), not in the renderer.

Normalized URL key (Ceos rules): lowercase host without www./m., no trailing slash, tracking parameters (utm_*, fbclid, gclid, igshid, ref, si, hl, trk) dropped and the query sorted. A URL without a path never groups, because portals reuse the homepage for different records.
Union-find implementation. Test: the same breach from 3 sources renders as 1 row and exports as 3 findings.
P335.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (analyst_ux voted P1). Display-only grouping that keeps machine-readable outputs atomic is the architect's floor and cti_lead's condition for TIP ingestion. osint_investigator: never merge identities (homonyms), keep every source and evidence link. analyst_ux: row format and variant grouping. legal_dpo and redteam_lead raised no issue.
P335.title: Duplicate grouping for triage/report (union-find)

final_conditions: HTML carries a Content-Security-Policy meta: default-src 'none'; img-src data:; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; script-src limited to the hash of the bundled JS (no 'unsafe-inline' script). All assets are embedded, and no external images, fonts or resources of any kind load (Gravatar/XON logos never).
One safe_href() (http/https only) is used for every anchor in HTML and Markdown, including case and manual-pivot links; today only references are scheme-checked.

Entity-derived URLs (targets, IOCs, references pointing at investigated hosts) and entities tagged malicious/phishing/c2/suspicious are defanged and non-clickable. Only pivot templates and allow-listed reference hosts are clickable, with rel=noreferrer, and pivot links only at TLP:CLEAR/GREEN: at AMBER and above they render as non-clickable text with the disclosure warning (A2, P311).

The evidence manifest (file, SHA-256) is embedded. The report's own SHA-256 goes to a sidecar <report>.sha256 and to the case DB, because a file cannot contain its own hash; any hash shown in the footer states that it covers the content above it. `v3lum cases verify` checks both.

TLP 2.0 marking (label and colour) appears in the header and footer of every report, at the top of every section and in print CSS. Markdown and JSON carry the tlp field and banner, and file names carry the label (A2).

A licence banner lists every noncommercial/license or allow-listed source used. Required attributions are generated from source/dataset metadata for the sources actually used (MITRE ATT&CK, HIBP CC BY 4.0, OSM ODbL, DB-IP CC BY 4.0, WhatsMyName CC BY-SA 4.0, OffSeq...) and shown in a collapsed footer section.
A 'contains personal data (LGPD)' notice appears when PERSONAL_TYPES entities are present. CPF is masked, and report files are written 0600.
LIGHT/ACTIVE cases get an engagement block: authorization reference, scope SHA-256, window, egress profile/IP, targets touched and request counts (A7).
Tests assert no external loads, neutralized javascript:/data: links, phishing URL fixtures rendered defanged, and markings present on every section.
P336.rationale: Approved 6-0. The chair raises the priority from the median P2 to P1 on the legal floor: A2 requires the TLP marking on every page and section, CC BY sources require attribution, and reports hold personal data and must be 0600 (legal_dpo, osint_investigator and the architect voted P1). The architect's floor: a CSP with a script hash, http(s)-only hrefs, a sidecar hash, generated attributions. osint_investigator and redteam_lead: no click into a phishing kit from a report, and the engagement block. analyst_ux: notices in a collapsed footer. cti_lead: attributions from the sources actually used.
P336.title: Self-contained hashed report (no external resources)

final_conditions: `v3lum doctor` stays fast (< 15 s): environment, permissions, keys, proxy/egress routes, TLS interception (P329) and at most 3 reachability probes. Per-module health checks run only through `v3lum doctor --sources [names]`, never at scan time or at startup.

Each module's health_check() uses benign values from one central list (example.com, 8.8.8.8, EICAR, CVE-2021-44228, octocat). Username packs use the platform's official account as claimed and a random 20-char handle as unclaimed, sampling 25 sites per run in rotation.

LIGHT/ACTIVE health checks are offline self-tests (binary/dataset presence and pinned hashes, a local loopback fixture on 127.0.0.1), never network probes against any host. LIGHT self-tests never contact third-party sites.
Sources disabled by the licence profile or by TLP are not called, even with benign values.

Checks are quota-aware: they count in the quota book; providers with a daily budget <= 100, or below 20% remaining, are skipped unless --include-quota-sources; each source is checked at most once per day.

Concurrency is bounded (<= 4), with per-host politeness and a per-check timeout. Results (ok / blocked / quota / needs_key / dead, with their age) are cached 24 h and shown in coverage (e.g. 'last source check 2 d ago: 5 failing'). Scans never run health checks.
Results feed the A3 demotion state: repeated failures move a source out of the default set with a notice, and dead sources are flagged, never silently removed. They also feed the P331 auto-disable.
doctor also reports, on request, the egress_country verification (A9) and each egress profile's public IP, and lists loaded plugins. The doctor runner has offline tests with FakeHttp.
P337.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (osint_investigator voted P1). All members worried that ~300 health checks from a shared NAT would burn keyless quotas, hence explicit `--sources` checks that are quota-aware, cached and sampled (architect floor, redteam_lead, analyst_ux). legal_dpo's floor: active self-tests only against 127.0.0.1, licence-disabled sources never called. osint_investigator and cti_lead: benign values and the degraded flag in coverage. It is an explicit command and never runs during scans, hence default_enabled false.
P337.title: Source health check ('doctor') with per-source self-tests

final_conditions: A pure function and report section over existing vocab tags and correlation results: no new collectors, no network.

The posture is computed only for subjects with a recorded purpose: own-domain employees within the security programme, VIP protection with the person's knowledge (executives opted in via org_profile), or incident victims. Never for any other third party, not even with an analyst opt-in (legal floor).
Employees' personal social-media life is excluded unless the person opted in (VIP programme). The 'predictable posting routine' (pattern-of-life) signal is dropped.
Wording: 'suggested posture (weak/regular/good)' with the evidence list per checklist item, plus one summary line naming the 3 items that drove it; the analyst confirms. No sensitive-data inference.
'good' is never shown when any core source for the subject could not verify: the posture then reads 'inconclusive' and lists the unverified items.
Never used for HR or disciplinary decisions (LGPD art. 20, human review). Posture labels stay inside the case, follow its retention and are not exported.
P338.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3; it is implemented in this build only if cheap (A16). A weak/regular/good label per person is profiling, so legal_dpo's floor governs: a recorded purpose, never other third parties (the auditor removed an analyst opt-in for other subjects as looser than the floor), no HR use, labels kept inside the case. osint_investigator dropped the pattern-of-life signal. analyst_ux: 'inconclusive' instead of false reassurance. The architect: a pure function over existing data. It runs only for opted-in subjects, hence default_enabled false.
P338.title: Exposure posture checklist + suggested posture (weak/regular/good)

final_conditions: This lands after per-run deadlines are enforced (AR05). It is implemented inside the existing single thread pool as a priority order (offline -> keyless passive -> keyed passive -> slow/opt-in -> light/active) plus per-module and per-provider concurrency caps, with no extra pools. Stages are priorities, not barriers: the pipelined BFS and all engine tests stay green.
The per-entity passive-before-LIGHT/ACTIVE ordering that the hostile-host guard needs is delivered with P376. Lanes must never reorder it.

Username and profile packs run in their own bounded lane (concurrency cap, run budget), so hundreds of site checks never starve other modules. Per-provider lanes serialise calls to the same upstream for quota safety.

LIGHT/ACTIVE work gets its own caps inside the single pool (<= 2 connections per target host and a bounded share of the pool's slots), so it never takes the slots of fast passive modules and no extra pool is created (architect floor). Cancellation stops LIGHT/ACTIVE work within 2 s.
Keyed calls may be skipped when cheap sources already answered (setting skip_keyed_when_answered, default false).
When the fast stage completes (target <= 20 s), a provisional summary line (risk so far, findings so far, sources pending) is printed. The live feed shows markers per lane.
Licence, TLP and scope gates stay in core/policy.decide; no lane bypasses them.
A deterministic test with simulated slow modules shows that fast results are not blocked. A bench test checks that a default domain scan completes at p90 <= 60 s with recorded latencies.
P339.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (analyst_ux P1, architect P3). The architect's floor: only after deadlines are enforced, inside the existing pool as priorities, with the guard ordering owned by P376. cti_lead, osint_investigator and redteam_lead require passive-before-light per entity, so the guard sees TI tags. redteam_lead: separate LIGHT/ACTIVE concurrency and 2-s cancellation. analyst_ux: the provisional summary and the time budget. legal_dpo: no lane bypasses the gates.
P339.title: Staged collection pipeline with per-service lanes (Céos coleta port)

final_conditions: New input detection for Apache/Nginx/IIS access logs with a streaming parser: the file is never read whole, the line length cap is 8 KB, and size/line caps are reported when hit. 1M lines must parse in < 30 s offline, with progress shown.

Matching runs offline against the teler-resources web-attack patterns and bad-crawler lists (CC BY 4.0, attributed) and PHPIDS (LGPL-3.0), downloaded at runtime and never bundled (A6), compiled once. Patterns with catastrophic backtracking are excluded by a pathological-line test. One loader is shared with P317 user_agent_analysis.

Aggregation per client IP/path/UA happens before any pivot. Only IPs that matched attack signatures or bad-crawler lists become entities and may be enriched, capped at the top 20 by suspicious hits. Benign visitors' IPs are counted, not stored (customer IPs are personal data).

Private/internal IPs and hostnames from logs are never sent to third parties. URLs from logs lose their query strings before any external lookup (logs carry session and reset tokens). Request lines are stored with query-string values redacted and without cookies.
IPs from logs get passive enrichment only, never LIGHT/ACTIVE contact.
Log-derived cases default to TLP:AMBER. The log file is not copied into the case: evidence keeps the matched lines (redacted) and the file's SHA-256.
The first screen is a summary (e.g. '312 IPs, 14 matched rules, top 10 by hits, paths attacked').
P340.rationale: Approved with yes 5 / defer 1 at median P3; it is implemented only if cheap (A16). cti_lead deferred because mass-enriching customer IPs from logs discloses personal data and risks graph explosion. The conditions address exactly that: only signature-matched IPs leave the machine, capped at 20 (osint_investigator's cap, stricter than analyst_ux's 25 and the architect's 50), with legal_dpo's floor on redaction and evidence. The architect's floor: streaming, caps, ReDoS-safe runtime patterns. redteam_lead: passive only, private IPs and query strings never sent out. Auditor: terms set to 'open' from the dataset licences (runtime download plus attribution, A1/A6); provider_tier stays 'n/a' because matching is offline and no investigated value leaves the machine during it.
P340.title: Log-file input type (web access logs) with teler-resources matching

P341.rationale: Mechanical status: vetoed by legal_dpo (yes 0 / reject 5 / defer 1). The veto is not lifted, so the proposal is rejected. DeepL API Free may use submitted text to improve its service, and case reports carry investigated persons' data and incident context (an international transfer for the provider's own purposes; TLP alone does not make a report free of personal data). Even with the veto_lift adopted, only legal_dpo's vote would turn positive (yes = 1), still a rejection. cti_lead, osint_investigator, redteam_lead and analyst_ux rejected it, and the architect deferred. Backlog note: bundled pt-BR/en templates for V3LUM's own text (veto_lift item 5, analyst_ux). Machine translation of case text may be revisited only with a paid no-retention plan and DPA, entity placeholders, TLP:CLEAR/GREEN only and an explicit per-report flag.
P341.title: Optional report translation (DeepL API Free)

final_conditions: Reuse the TXT answer already fetched by email_security_posture/dns_records (DoH cache hit); at most one TXT query through ctx.dns when absent. DoH errors mean could not verify, never 'no SaaS'.

Map record prefixes to vendors with a bundled own-work table data/txt_verification_prefixes.json (atlassian-domain-verification, google-site-verification, MS=, docusign=, stripe-verification, zoom-domain-verification, notion-domain-verification, knowbe4-site-verification, adobe-idp-site-verification, openai-/anthropic-domain-verification, DirectFedAuthUrl...).

Output: the saas_vendors attribute (added to core/vocab.py in the same change), info only, with phishing-simulation/ASM hints (which IdP, helpdesk and e-signature brands attackers would imitate). Unknown prefixes are listed raw.

Tokens prove a past verification, not current use: worded 'verification record present'. Token values are never pivoted and not republished in bulk: reports show vendor names, raw values stay in evidence only.
Tests with the recorded gaps__saas_tenants fixture.
P342.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 with no member conditions beyond the synthesizer's. legal_dpo: public DNS answers, no personal data, values not republished in bulk. The architect: cached DoH answer, bundled map, saas_vendors in vocab.py. Data travels through the core DoH resolvers: tier trusted, terms open.
P342.title: SaaS footprint from DNS TXT verification tokens (vendor prefix map)

final_conditions: applies() is decided only from the shared IANA RDAP bootstrap helper of P003 (a TLD without an RDAP service, e.g. .ru via the bootstrap), never from another module's runtime result (the engine has no module ordering). The second .br path runs only on explicit analyst selection.

Order: a self-hosted who-dat instance (MIT) when the setting whodat_url is configured, then direct port-43 WHOIS to the registry server taken from the IANA root-zone page (cached 7 days). The public who-dat.as93.net instance is a separate module whois_fallback_public: unknown tier, default_enabled=False, excluded at AMBER and above.

Port 43 goes through a small core whois43 helper on the core socket connector: 10 s timeout, 64 KB cap, at most one referral hop; UNAVAILABLE when a proxy is configured or 43/tcp is blocked. Registry WHOIS terms are respected (per-query only, no bulk or marketing use).

Keep registrar, dates, nameservers, status, DNSSEC and meta.source/server. Personal contact fields are dropped at ingestion, before evidence (registro.br exposes tech-contact names/e-mails); unit test with the .br sample.
WHOIS/who-dat output never creates CNPJ pivots: the .br -> CNPJ pivot stays RDAP-only (publicIds, P003).
Tests with the recorded gaps__whois_fallback fixture and a referral case.
P343.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (architect voted P3). The architect's floor: applicability from the bootstrap helper, not module ordering; a bounded whois43 helper; the public who-dat instance as a separate input-sharing adapter off at AMBER and above (osint_investigator rates it unknown tier, so it is opt-in, A3 BR2). legal_dpo: personal fields dropped, registry terms, no CNPJ pivots. Default module tier trusted (IANA and registries), terms open.
P343.title: WHOIS fallback for TLDs without RDAP (who-dat RDAP/WHOIS-over-HTTPS + port-43 via IANA root db)

final_conditions: A library called by web_fingerprint (P072) and js_endpoints (P068) on JavaScript bodies they already hold, plus a module for file/text inputs. It never fetches the target; reading cached JS uses a cache-only flag in ctx.http.

jsrepository-v4.json (RetireJS, Apache-2.0, ~650 KB) is a weekly dataset with the NOTICE in data/NOTICE. Extractors: uri, filename, filecontent and hashes; 'func' extractors need a JS runtime and are skipped. Version regexes pass the same ReDoS harness as secret_scanner (P312).
OSV npm confirmation queries (library name and version only, never the target) are capped at 10 per entity and 20 per run.

One finding per library+version listing its advisories (CVE/GHSA). Severity = the highest advisory severity, capped at MEDIUM unless the CVE is in KEV or exploited (P291), and only for org_profile own assets or in-scope targets; third-party and hostile sites get info.
Confidence by extractor: uri/filename-only detections are labelled 'version inferred from file name' (<= 0.5, POSSIBLE); filecontent/hash detections rank higher.
Tests with the recorded gaps__retirejs fixture (jquery 1.12.4 -> 4 advisories) and a ReDoS case.
P344.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (cti_lead and osint_investigator voted P3). The architect's floor: an explicit hand-off over bodies already fetched, no requests of its own, the ReDoS harness, capped OSV queries. cti_lead and analyst_ux: ownership-scoped severity capped at MEDIUM unless KEV, one finding per library. redteam_lead: version-inferred confidence. Tier community (the RetireJS project dataset; OSV is trusted); terms open.
P344.title: Vulnerable front-end library detection (RetireJS repository, offline)

final_conditions: Implemented as a report exporter (-f takedown, and `v3lum takedown <case>`) over the case graph (architect floor): registrar and abuse contacts already produced by rdap (P003), ripestat (P031) and abusix_contacts (P041), plus the IANA registrar-ID registry as a weekly dataset. No network at report time and no new HTTP clients.

Generated automatically only when the case has a phishing/malicious finding >= HIGH backed by consensus (>= 2 independent families, P171) or analyst confirmation; never from a single-source hit. Otherwise only on request.

Contacts are ranked by authority with the reason, source and retrieval date: registrar abuse (RDAP via the IANA registrar id) > hosting abuse-c (RIR) > Abusix > CDN abuse portal (with origin hints when a CDN is in front). Compromised legitimate sites add the owner contact from security.txt (P065) when available.

.br domains and BR-hosted IPs add CERT.br guidance (notify the source network, cert@cert.br in Cc). Manual report links: Google Safe Browsing report_phish, Netcraft, and the platforms abused in BR scams (WhatsApp, Instagram/Meta, Telegram, Google Forms/Sites) when the case holds such entities.
V3LUM never sends e-mails or submits forms. Submitting a report shares the URL with the provider: the analyst decides per case and records the disclosure decision in the case audit.

Minimisation: the packet includes only what the takedown needs (hostile URL/host, timestamps, evidence SHA-256 hashes, screenshots of the hostile page); victims' e-mails, tokens and other personal data and internal case details are redacted. The packet carries the case TLP marking.
Each evidence item lists its SHA-256 with UTC and America/Sao_Paulo timestamps; a ready-to-copy message template in pt-BR and English cites the hashes.
Unit tests on a synthetic case graph (registrar + RIR + Abusix contacts, a .br case, a single-source hit that must not generate a packet).
P345.rationale: Approved 6-0. The tally median is P2 on a 3-3 split (cti_lead, osint_investigator and analyst_ux voted P1); the chair keeps P2 because it is an exporter over data the P1 modules already collect. The architect's floor makes it an offline report exporter. legal_dpo's floor: the packet is a third-party disclosure, so it is minimised, TLP-marked and the decision recorded. cti_lead: consensus or analyst confirmation and contact ranking. osint_investigator: CERT.br and BR platform paths, dual timestamps. analyst_ux: on-demand generation and templates. Tier trusted, terms open (IANA registry dataset).
P345.title: Takedown / abuse packet for hostile URLs and hosts (RDAP abuse, RIPEstat abuse-c, Abusix, IANA registrar ids, report forms)

final_conditions: Brand terms come only from org_profile brands, or from a company_name/keyword seed the analyst typed with explicit -M; never from arbitrary domain pivots.

Apple iTunes Search/Lookup (country=br, entity=software): Apple's Search API terms cover promotional use, so this source is 'license': off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared (legal records a metadata-only scope in licence_allow).

App metadata only (name, seller, bundle id, URL); artwork and previews are never downloaded or displayed. <= 20 calls/min (min_interval 3 s); a 403 is retried once with the same UA, then BLOCKED ('could not verify'), never with another UA (P326).

Android official apps are confirmed through the digital_asset_links client of P008 (package + signing-certificate SHA-256, no copy of the client) and, for analyst-provided APK files, the apk_triage certificate SHA-256. F-Droid is dropped from this build (multi-MB index parsed in RAM, low relevance for banking brands).
Koodous only with a company token (key 'koodous', terms recorded, real fixture), for APK hash/package lookups; keyless 401 gives NEEDS_KEY. Google Play only as manual pivot links, never scraped.

Official apps (seller name/URL/bundle prefix matching org_profile) form a known_good list. Look-alike = brand term in the app name AND seller/developer not matching org_profile AND absent from the official domain's Digital Asset Links, scored by name similarity and seller mismatch.
Look-alikes are a review list at LOW ('needs analyst review'), capped at 20 in the report, pivots expand=False, never 'malicious' without analyst review.
.apk links found on scam pages or in pasted messages are recorded as url entities only and never downloaded automatically.
Tests with the recorded gaps__app_store_search and Digital Asset Links fixtures: official app recognised, look-alike listed for review, 403 handling.
P346.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (architect voted P3). legal_dpo's floor: Apple's terms are promotional, so iTunes use is metadata-only under a recorded scope (terms license, a licence-gated default candidate per A3 BR4), Koodous with a company token, Google Play never scraped. The architect's floor: rate limits, the P008 client, F-Droid dropped. cti_lead, osint_investigator and analyst_ux: the look-alike definition, a capped review list and APK links never downloaded. The synthesizer's 'normal client UA' is replaced by the default UA (P326 forbids changing the UA after a 403). Tier community (Koodous; Apple and Google are trusted).
P346.title: Brand app discovery and look-alike apps (iTunes Search, F-Droid index, Koodous, Digital Asset Links cert check)

final_conditions: veto_lift (1): ships as the separate optional extra v3lum[capture]; nothing in v3lum/core imports playwright. Not merged or enabled before the AR20 safety suite passes.

veto_lift (2): refuses to start unless Chromium's sandbox is active (never --no-sandbox; abort when running as root without a usable sandbox) and a non-corporate egress proxy (P376 proxy_light) is configured; fail closed, never a fallback through the corporate IP.

veto_lift (3): every request goes through a route interceptor that aborts private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT, ULA and metadata destinations, intranet names (DNS rebinding) and non-http(s) schemes. DNS is resolved through the egress proxy.

veto_lift (4): downloads, permissions (geolocation, notifications, clipboard, camera, microphone), service workers, extensions and file:// are disabled, with a fresh ephemeral context and temporary profile per page, deleted afterwards. Hardening asserted by a launch-args test: WebRTC limited to proxied traffic (no non-proxied UDP), QUIC off, integrated Windows/Kerberos auth disabled.
veto_lift (5): hard budgets of 30 s, 25 MB HAR, one screenshot, <= 10 redirect hops and <= 150 requests per capture. No clicks, scrolling, typing, form submission or credentials.

veto_lift (6): runs only on explicit -M selection for analyst-typed seed URLs already tagged phishing/malicious (LIGHT, A7). URLs carrying a recipient identifier need an explicit per-capture override. No stealth or anti-detection plugins (rule 1); challenge pages (Turnstile/hCaptcha) end BLOCKED with no retry.

veto_lift (7): unit tests run against a fake driver interface, with a single @live test. veto_lift (8): reuse of public urlscan screenshots lives in urlscan_search (P066, passive) and works without playwright.

A benign-looking or cloaked capture reads 'inconclusive (possible cloaking/geofencing)', never evidence of benign. HAR and DOM are scrubbed of our cookies, auth headers and proxy credentials; victims' e-mails shown on pages are redacted in report text.

Evidence record: final URL, redirect chain, UTC and America/Sao_Paulo timestamps, SHA-256 of screenshot/DOM/HAR, the egress profile used, the case TLP; under case retention (A10) with access limited to the case. Screenshots are embedded in the self-contained HTML as JPEG data URIs (<= 1.5 MB) with a caption (source, egress, time).
P347.rationale: Vetoed by the architect (5-1 otherwise): a full browser engine against attacker pages executes hostile code on the analyst's workstation, and the draft lacked sandbox enforcement and private-address blocking. veto_lift adopted: all eight lift conditions are in this spec, and redteam_lead's hardening (WebRTC, QUIC, NTLM, DNS rebinding, request cap, no stealth plugins) is folded in. legal_dpo: retention, scrubbed HAR, redacted victims' data. cti_lead and osint_investigator: cloaking caveat and a court-usable evidence record. analyst_ux: embedded, captioned screenshots. LIGHT and explicit-only: default_enabled false. Target contact: tier n/a; Playwright Apache-2.0: terms open.
P347.title: Headless page capture for evidence (Playwright screenshot/DOM/HAR) with urlscan screenshot reuse

final_conditions: Read-only adapters cti_framework/misp_sightings and opencti_sightings (P1) and thehive_sightings (P2, A12): plain requests clients (no PyMISP/pycti dependency), each enabled only when URL and key are configured via `v3lum keys` (least-privilege read-only service accounts). MISP restSearch lands first; OpenCTI and TheHive land when synthetic fixtures for their documented versions exist.

disclosure 'internal' (allowed at TLP:RED) only for instances operated by the company or a contracted processor; community, sector-ISAC or shared instances and sharing groups are third_party providers with tier and terms. The SSRF guard lets these adapters reach only their configured internal hosts.

TLS verification is always on with the ca_bundle setting; no verify=False exists anywhere. Read-only in code: a per-platform method+path allow-list (MISP restSearch and sightings reads, OpenCTI queries without mutations, TheHive search) with a test that refuses add/edit/mutation calls; a startup check warns when a configured key has write permissions.

Values travel only in JSON bodies or GraphQL variables, never interpolated into query strings. <= 50 results per value; per-run request cap (<= 2 req/s per platform); TIP lookups time out after 5 s; a failure means could not verify (rule 5).

MISP: to_ids=false attributes are context only (no malicious tag); decay scores, false-positive sightings and warninglist hits returned by restSearch are honoured. OpenCTI: x_opencti_score, revoked and valid_until (expired -> historical, low).

Every hit carries event/case id, org, TLP/marking and date as references. Source markings are respected and never downgraded: Finding.tlp is stored per finding, the higher of platform and case TLP applies, and renderers omit findings above the report TLP.

Galaxy/actor tags become attributed_to pivots with expand=False, names kept unchanged for STIX/MISP round-trips. No write-back, sightings or sharing from V3LUM: export happens only through the explicit P303 command.

Covert red-team exercises: a case flag --covert (alias --no-internal), recorded in the case, skips internal lookups, because TIP and SIEM query logs would show the SOC the red team's own infrastructure.
Report: internal sightings first ('known internally: MISP event #N, TheHive case #M'); query order case DB (P375) -> MISP/OpenCTI -> TheHive. Synthetic fixtures per platform version.
P348.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1, consistent with A12. legal_dpo's floor limits 'internal' to company-operated or contracted instances; the architect's floor requires plain clients, injection-safe queries, the ca_bundle setting and per-finding TLP; redteam_lead adds code-enforced read-only allow-lists and the covert-exercise skip; cti_lead's to_ids/decay semantics and analyst_ux's 5 s fail-soft timeout are kept. The architect's 'drop runs FIRST' is honoured (results merge regardless of order; the report lists them first). Internal platform: tier 'n/a'.
P348.title: Internal TIP sightings (own MISP restSearch, OpenCTI GraphQL, TheHive/Cortex observables)

final_conditions: Module cti_framework/siem_search, default_enabled False, for the team's primary SIEM only in this build (A12), with a read-only token through `v3lum keys`, TLS verification on (ca_bundle) and disclosure 'internal'.

Only SOC-approved, versioned templates: OpenSearch/Elasticsearch JSON DSL term/terms queries on approved fields and index patterns (never query_string/Lucene syntax); Splunk only by dispatching SOC-approved saved searches with arguments, and only for values whose canonical form matches a strict charset (IP, domain, hash, e-mail); other types are refused.
Values enter templates only as parameters or escaped literals, tested with hostile values such as x" OR * | delete and a bare *.

Bounds: one query per entity, <= 20 queries per run, 30-day window by default, <= 1,000 results, 1 concurrent query, timeout 15 s by default and never above 30 s (A12); a failure means could not verify. Output: counts and first/last seen per entity only (no raw events), shown near the top ('seen in our logs: N events, first/last').
Results are also recorded as internal sightings (count, first/last seen, index pattern) and exported as sightings, never as raw events. Internal hostnames and usernames found are never auto-pivoted.

Workplace monitoring (LGPD): personal identifiers (username, e-mail, user_agent tied to a person) are searched only within a case with a recorded incident purpose, under the company's monitoring policy and privacy notice; queries are logged with analyst and case id; results follow case retention; never used for HR or performance purposes.
The covert-exercise flag of P348 also skips SIEM lookups. Synthetic fixtures for both backends.
P349.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2, per A12. The architect's floor (JSON DSL term queries only, strict-charset Splunk arguments) and redteam_lead's hostile-value tests make template injection impossible; legal_dpo's floor binds personal searches to a case purpose and the monitoring policy; cti_lead's sightings recording and analyst_ux's primary-SIEM scope and top-of-report line are kept. Internal platform: tier 'n/a'.
P349.title: Internal SIEM look-back (approved saved searches on OpenSearch/Elasticsearch or Splunk)

final_conditions: Offline module malware_hash/offline_hash_sets (disclosure none, TLP:RED-safe). This build: the MalwareBazaar v2 recent export (https://mb-api.abuse.ch/v2/files/exports/{AUTH_KEY}/recent.csv, last 48 h) with key 'abusech' through the dataset manager, refreshed at most hourly and indexed into SQLite; a hit reads 'known MalwareBazaar sample: <signature>, first seen <date>' (medium).

Licence: the MalwareBazaar export follows P156 ('license', abuse.ch terms s.4.1): off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared (a Spamhaus subscription or a written abuse.ch decision in licence_allow). The key-bearing URL passes AR01 redaction and is never logged, cached or shown.

Deferred inside this proposal: the VirusShare MD5 corpus (512 files, ~1.5 GB of text, stale since 2022) and the 1 GB CIRCL hashlookup Bloom filter, until the dataset manager offers a compact on-disk index (sorted 8-byte prefix file or mmap Bloom reader) behind an explicit size confirmation; neither is ever loaded into memory.

When added: VirusShare is a separate module (terms 'unknown' per A1 BR16, default_enabled False) worded 'present in the VirusShare corpus (historical; may include PUP/benign)', low, never malicious alone and never in CR27; the CIRCL Bloom (open data, 2023 snapshot) comes only from `v3lum data fetch hashlookup-bloom` with a 1 GB warning and is a prefilter, never a known_good verdict.

Downloads are verified (size, published hash when available) and stored under ~/.v3lum/datasets; the MalwareBazaar export is the one dataset registered for abusech (P156), never downloaded twice; dataset dates are shown in every finding and in coverage; misses mean nothing (no row).
P350.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (the architect voted P3). The architect's floor limits this build to the keyed MalwareBazaar recent export and defers the multi-GB corpora until compact on-disk indexes exist; legal_dpo's floor keeps the export under P156's licence gate and VirusShare (no licence) off until legal decides; cti_lead's, osint_investigator's and analyst_ux's wording keeps corpus membership from reading as a verdict. Chair-file terms follow the export ('license'); the module is a default candidate that is off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared (A3 BR4).
P350.title: Offline hash sets (VirusShare MD5 corpus, MalwareBazaar SHA-256 export with Auth-Key, CIRCL hashlookup Bloom prefilter)

final_conditions: Depends on the P333 structural hash entity types (imphash, tlsh, telfhash, gimphash, authentihash, icon_dhash, code_signing_cert) and the P267/P271/P368 attributes; the relation similar_to is added to core/vocab.py in the same change.

Remote pivots: MalwareBazaar get_imphash/get_tlsh/get_telfhash/get_gimphash/get_dhash_icon/get_issuerinfo/get_subjectinfo with key 'abusech', limit <= 50, query_status no_results -> EMPTY; YARAify (P175) supplies the structural values of known samples.

Licence: the MalwareBazaar pivots and the Code Signing Certificate Blocklist (CSCB, from the keyed export via the dataset manager; the legacy URL is 410) follow P156 ('license'): off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared; YARAify (CC0) and local similarity run freely.

Results are hypotheses: relation similar_to with confidence 0.3-0.6 and expand=False, never a finding above low on their own, labelled 'hypothesis' in reports. A certificate on the CSCB is a malicious-signer finding (high).

Generic-value stoplist: imphash/telfhash/gimphash values seen across > 10 unrelated MalwareBazaar signatures or > 500 samples (e.g. the .NET imphash f34d5f2d4577ed6d9ceec516c1f5a744) and common installer/packer stubs are shown as 'common, not distinctive' and never pivoted.

Output is grouped per structural hash ('N samples share this imphash; families X (8), Y (3)'), top 10 listed. Local TLSH/ssdeep distance between files of one case is a correlation rule over case attributes, not a per-entity module; TLSH comparison waits for a wheel-providing implementation.
P351.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. legal_dpo's floor puts the MalwareBazaar parts under P156's licence gate while YARAify and local similarity run; cti_lead's and redteam_lead's stoplist, the architect's correlation-rule split for cross-file similarity and analyst_ux's grouped output are consolidated. A default candidate that is off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared for the MalwareBazaar parts (A3 BR4).
P351.title: Structural / fuzzy hash pivots (imphash, TLSH, telfhash, gimphash, icon dHash, code-signing cert) via MalwareBazaar + local similarity

final_conditions: Explicit `v3lum data sync cves` only, never inside a scan: the CVEProject cvelistV5 daily baseline release zip is streamed to disk by the dataset manager and read member by member (zip-of-zip handled; caps on member count, 5 MB per member and total uncompressed; no extraction, member names never used as paths); declared hosts include the release-asset redirect host.

Records are indexed into SQLite (id, state, dates, CNA/ADP metrics, KEV/SSVC fields, compressed JSON), resumably; hourly deltas come from deltaLog.json with githubLink restricted to raw.githubusercontent.com/CVEProject/ and are applied only when dateUpdated is newer. Never a git clone.

cve_record (P183) reads the mirror first and falls back to cveawg/NVD only for misses, with the shared CVE 5 parser. The mirror exposes CISA ADP SSVC (exploitation, automatable, technical impact), the KEV flag and ADP CVSS.

Attribution per the CVE terms (MITRE copyright designation in the notices; CISA ADP content public domain). doctor shows disk usage and mirror age; the baseline size is verified from the team network.
P352.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. The architect's floor (explicit sync, streamed archive reading with caps, restricted delta links, SQLite index) and legal_dpo's attribution are the conditions; the other members' notes (NVD rate limits, TLP:RED offline lookups) are the reason it ships. Offline: tier 'n/a', terms 'open'.
P352.title: Offline CVE mirror (CVEProject cvelistV5 baseline + hourly deltas incl. CISA ADP Vulnrichment)

final_conditions: Offline module vulnerability_cve/msrc_patch_tuesday on the dataset manager: api.msrc.microsoft.com/cvrf/v3.0/updates lists the month documents; each document (~20 MB; max_bytes 64 MB per document) is streamed to disk, parsed one at a time and indexed into SQLite (CVE -> KBs, products, exploited/publicly disclosed, severity, fixed build, supersedence).

Refresh out of band by `v3lum data update` (never mid-scan) when CurrentReleaseDate changes in /updates (GET with If-Modified-Since; never HEAD, which returns 405); default window the last 24 months, older months on demand.

Threats Type 1 'Exploited:Yes' goes to the exploited attribute with source 'msrc' and raises severity like KEV, but kev stays CISA-only; Type 3 gives severity; Remediations Type 2 (KB, URL, FixedBuild, supersedence) become remediation attributes on the CVE card; product names come from the ProductTree.
Disclosure none at scan time. Tests use a trimmed fixture cut from the gap-fill sample.
P353.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (cti_lead voted P1). The architect's floor indexes the 20 MB month documents instead of holding them in memory; cti_lead keeps Microsoft's exploited flag separate from CISA KEV. Offline: tier 'n/a', terms 'open'.
P353.title: Microsoft Patch Tuesday data (MSRC CVRF v3: KBs, products, Exploited / Publicly Disclosed flags)

final_conditions: Generic CSAF 2.0 client on the dataset manager: provider-metadata.json -> distributions (changes.csv or ROLIE feeds) -> daily incremental sync by `v3lum data update` into a local index (CVE -> vendor advisory id, products, fixed versions, CVSS, exploitation notes, VEX status). Vendors in config with licence and attribution (start: Cisco, Siemens ProductCERT, Red Hat; perimeter vendors next).

Every document URL must stay on the provider's declared hosts (https only; URLs taken from data elsewhere are refused); <= 2,000 documents per provider per sync and 5 MB per document; .sha256/.sha512 checked when published.

Red Hat VEX is fetched only per CVE for in-scope CVEs: that part sends the CVE id and is a separate adapter with disclosure third_party under the CVE fan-out rule (P183). VEX not_affected lowers a version-based CVE match for that product (context, never a deletion).

Each advisory is stored with vendor id, canonical URL and licence/terms (Red Hat CC BY 4.0 to confirm; Cisco treats copies without the distribution URL as uncontrolled; Siemens under its website terms); reports show excerpts plus links, never full copies. Output feeds the CVE card's vendor-fix line.
P354.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3. The architect's floor pins document URLs to declared hosts, caps the sync and splits the per-CVE VEX fetch out as a third_party adapter; legal_dpo's floor keeps provenance and links instead of redistributing documents; cti_lead's VEX use and redteam_lead's perimeter-vendor order are included. Tier refers to the Red Hat VEX adapter (the index itself is offline).
P354.title: CSAF 2.0 vendor advisories (Cisco, Siemens, Red Hat; generic provider-metadata client)

final_conditions: Opt-in dataset security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/data/json (~93 MB, refreshed at most daily by `v3lum data update`), parsed with a streaming parser (ijson optional extra) into SQLite (package -> CVE -> release status/fixed version); never json.load'ed whole; no per-query network calls; default_enabled False.
Results are shown only when the asset is known to run a Debian-based system (fingerprint/banner or analyst input).

Backport check: when a banner exposes a Debian package revision (e.g. 'OpenSSH_8.4p1 Debian-5+deb11u3'), map it to the source package and release and compare it with the tracker's fixed_version using the dpkg version algorithm (own implementation of Debian Policy 5.6.12, test vectors with epochs).

Fixed -> the version-inferred CVE is suppressed through a named P322 suppression rule with reason 'fixed in distro package'; unfixed -> confidence raised. Without a visible distro revision nothing changes. A trimmed fixture is used in tests.
P355.rationale: Approved 5-1 at median P3. cti_lead rejected it as redundant with OSV's Debian records; redteam_lead's backport check (the main false-positive class in external assessments) is the part OSV cannot do without a package entity, so it is included. The architect's streaming parser and SQLite index and the opt-in default are kept. Offline: tier 'n/a', terms 'open'.
P355.title: Debian security tracker (distro fix status per CVE/package)

final_conditions: Module darkweb_ransomware/ransomfeed: the RSS rss-complete.php (iso-8859-1, ~520 KB, ~600 items) through the dataset manager at most hourly and the core safe XML helper, HTML stripped from descriptions, matched offline for watch and supplier screening; per-entity API search (api.ransomfeed.it /search/{name}, /gang/{group} for actor cards) only for analyst-typed or org_profile names.

Matching uses the shared victim-name normaliser (P196): an exact domain/website or CNPJ decides severity (critical for org_profile entities or listed suppliers); name-only = POSSIBLE, medium at most; dedupe through the shared ransomware correlation rule ('corroborated by N trackers': victim + group + date +/- 3 days).
Claims are actor statements ('claimed by'); descriptions are stored as excerpts of <= 300 chars; victims who are natural persons get no description text; claim and onion links are never visited.
Licence: CC BY 4.0 (site footer, verified 2026-11-26): attribution in reports and exports. Registry provider ransomfeed: tier community, terms open. Trimmed fixtures are cut from the gap-fill sample.
P356.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1. The second licence-clean tracker: cti_lead, osint_investigator and analyst_ux apply P196's matching and severity rules; the architect reuses the shared normaliser, XML helper and dedupe rule; legal_dpo adds the no-description rule for natural persons; redteam_lead keeps supplier matching offline.
P356.title: ransomfeed.it ransomware claims (RSS + REST API, CC BY 4.0)

final_conditions: Only inside `v3lum watch` (A14), never in scan: foreground, with --once, --max-runtime (default 8 h) and --max-alerts bounds. It polls https://t.me/s/{channel} public previews with the shared t.me parser of P112; no account, session, joining or bot token (rule 1).

Channel list = team-curated data/telegram_watch.json (public channel handles only, with a justification, owner and review date per channel, reviewed by the CTI lead and legal before use) plus deepdarkCTI Telegram entries marked ONLINE/VALID (GPL-3.0, runtime download, parser shared with P198); <= 50 channels per cycle; channels unreachable for 30 days are auto-paused.

Politeness: >= 10 s between requests, <= 3 pages (?before=) per channel per cycle and backoff on 429; the last-seen post id is persisted so only new posts are read; the generic 'Contact @name' page = could not read.

Rules only over org_profile brands, domains, CNPJ roots, the organisation's own card BINs and the supplier list, plus IOC types; never natural persons. Matching is local after IDNA->Unicode and accent folding; BIN prefixes match only inside a Luhn-valid PAN-like string or next to a 'BIN' keyword.

P145 scrubbing before alerts or cache: card numbers reduced to BIN6 + last 4, CPFs masked, credentials, combos and leaked records dropped, secrets redacted (type + hash); alerts keep post id, date, URL and a short excerpt only.

Text only: media, files, og:image and link previews are never fetched and links in posts are never visited; extracted URLs and wallets become hostile-tagged, passive-only pivots; hits only enqueue capped passive enrichment (<= 30 per hour, A14).

Alerts: a deduplicated digest (one line per new match with channel, date, matched rule and channel-list provenance, deepdarkCTI vs team list), first_seen by post id, mutes per channel and per rule; alerts follow retention_days and the case TLP (default AMBER).

Companion feed: Dark Web Informer RSS (headline + link only, safe XML helper); DarkFeed is login-gated and not used. Offline tests replay recorded pages with a fake clock (fixtures: channel page, generic page, a post with a PAN and a CPF).
P357.rationale: Approved 5-0-1 at median P2. osint_investigator deferred pending legal review and minimisation; legal_dpo approved with exactly those safeguards (org-only rules, curated reviewed list, P145 scrubbing, retention), which are adopted together with A14. The architect's bounds and shared parsers, redteam_lead's text-only rule and analyst_ux's BIN matching and digest complete the spec. GPL lists used at runtime are 'open' under the A1 definitions; tier is Telegram's (the only provider that receives requests).
P357.title: Telegram public-channel watch (t.me/s previews of curated channels: brand, BIN, domain, CNPJ mentions)

final_conditions: Offline module crypto/crypto_address_labels (disclosure none): GraphSense public TagPacks (MIT; tags from public sources, no PII by repository rule) fetched weekly as one repository archive through the safe-archive helper (in memory, no extraction) or as raw files; YAML parsed with yaml.safe_load only (PyYAML optional extra), never yaml.load.

Indexed into SQLite with source URL, category, confidence and pack date per tag. Exchange proof-of-reserves files (OKX signed-message list = high confidence, Binance PoR...) are imported manually by the analyst with provenance and date (the pages are JS/bot-protected: never automated past interstitials) and downgraded after 12 months.

A team-curated label file (data/crypto_labels.json) holds Brazilian exchanges and addresses confirmed in past cases, with provenance. Merged labels keep per-source provenance; conflicting labels are shown side by side (no silent override).

Exchange labels are stop-nodes (P213) and name the institution to which a court order can be sent; categories ransomware/ofac/scam raise severity; 'no label' never means 'unhosted' (TRON coverage is thin: ~31 exchange TRX addresses from 2022 snapshots).
P358.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. cti_lead's provenance and dating, osint_investigator's team label file, the architect's safe YAML path and analyst_ux's 'no label is not unhosted' wording are consolidated. Offline: tier 'n/a', terms 'open'.
P358.title: Crypto address attribution labels (GraphSense TagPacks + exchange proof-of-reserves lists)

final_conditions: Module company_org/org_code_footprint reuses the shared GitHub (P111), GitLab, Codeberg, npm, PyPI and Docker Hub clients (one budget per provider): company name/domain -> candidate orgs (GitHub search type:org, GitLab groups?top_level_only=true, Codeberg orgs, npm '@scope/' + maintainer:, the PyPI organisation page, Docker Hub /v2/orgs/{org}).

An org counts as confirmed only on a verified domain/blog match with org_profile or analyst confirmation (name collisions). Unconfirmed orgs are listed as candidates without expansion and yield no secret findings or member pivots.
In the default set it runs only for org_profile-confirmed orgs (the own organisation); suppliers and other companies only as explicit seeds with a recorded purpose (-M and --purpose).

Default preset: a fast inventory (API only, <= 15 s, Module.max_requests <= 10 per entity) with repo/member counts and the 5 most recent repos per confirmed org (repos <= 30, recent first; forks skipped unless the org committed to them). Public members: count only, usernames on demand as expand=False pivots; members' personal profiles are not enriched without a case reason.

Deep preset or -M only: secret scanning (secret_scanner rules, P312) of the current tree from the provider's archive download (codeload/GitLab/Codeberg tar.gz) streamed through the core safe-archive helper in memory: no git binary, no extraction to disk, nothing built or executed, repo skipped when the API size is > 50 MB, 1 MB per member, binaries skipped; its own time budget and a progress line.

Secrets: type, file, commit, line and a keyed fingerprint with at most the first 4 characters; full values never reach evidence, cache, case DB, reports or logs and are never tested, validated or used (rule 1; Codigo Penal art. 154-A); worded 'exposed in public history; validity not tested'; one grouped finding per repo, high only for org-confirmed repos.

Third-party secrets (suppliers, customers) go to a disclosure workflow, not into shared reports. History scanning is deferred until the hardened git helper of P115 exists. Commit e-mails follow P115's rules.

Only SaaS forges are declared hosts (api.github.com, codeload.github.com, gitlab.com, codeberg.org, registry.npmjs.org, pypi.org, hub.docker.com); self-hosted forges on org domains are target infrastructure (LIGHT/ACTIVE with scope). API only (no github.com HTML, AUP s.7); token per P111's machine-account rule; a PyPI challenge = BLOCKED.

Fixtures for the GitHub /orgs paths are captured from the team network before it enters the default set (the research proxy blocked them). Registry: GitHub, GitLab, npm, PyPI and Docker trusted; Codeberg community. Sources: GitHub REST 'key-terms' (as P111); GitLab, Codeberg, npm, PyPI and Docker Hub 'open'. personal_data_review covers its username inputs (A3 BR8).
P359.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 on a 3-3 tie (osint_investigator, redteam_lead and legal_dpo P1) that the chair leaves at P2: it depends on the P111 client and the safe-archive helper, and the architect's sequencing floor rated it P2. legal_dpo's floor (default only for confirmed own orgs, secrets kept to the first 4 characters and never used) is stricter than P145's first4/last4 and is adopted; the architect's archive streaming replaces clones; analyst_ux's fast-inventory/deep split and redteam_lead's fork and self-hosted-forge rules are kept.
P359.title: Organisation source-code footprint (GitHub/GitLab/Codeberg orgs, npm/PyPI/Docker Hub org packages -> secret scan)

final_conditions: Datasets (dataset manager only, never during a scan): BCB Olinda DominiosVerificados (~630 KB) downloaded daily in full and matched locally, because server-side $filter/$count are broken; the slow Sedes* sets (3-35 s) and the CVM registries refreshed by `v3lum data update` through one CVM loader shared with P244/P361.
Each copy is validated (row count close to the previous one) before replacing it; the dataset date goes into evidence and coverage.
OData comment-wrapped error bodies ('/*{...}*/') are ERROR, never an empty list (P321). Default-on by A3 decision (BCB authorised institutions and DominiosVerificados).

Matching uses the PSL registrable domain and exact host, or a subdomain of a verified domain; never substrings, lookalikes or string suffix matching. A match sets known_good plus an INFO finding with legal name, CNPJ root, segment and conglomerate.
