known_good annotates, never suppresses: it lowers domain-reputation weight only, never downgrades malicious findings from other sources (a flagged verified domain surfaces as 'possible compromise - verified institution domain, review URL'), and URL-level hits stay.
A URL on a verified domain whose query or fragment carries a redirect target on another host (open-redirect pattern) is not known_good and is tagged 'redirect via verified domain'.
Absence produces no finding: at most an INFO line 'no verified domain registered with BCB' (1,066 institutions have none), never a fraud signal.

Protected-brand feed for P012/P028: a lookalike of a verified institution domain is HIGH only when registered and active (resolves, MX, fresh certificate or live page), otherwise a MEDIUM watch item. A lookalike whose registro.br registrant CNPJ root equals the institution's is defensive and suppressed; conglomerate registrants may legitimately differ.

CNPJ-root or name queries answer in one line 'authorised by BCB/CVM: yes (<segment>) / not found as of <date>'. CVM natural-person registries (advisers, portfolio managers) are matched only in explicit due diligence, with CPF masked and never a lookup key (rule 4).

Tiers: BCB and CVM trusted (government). Attribution BCB/CVM in reports; CVM's ODbL share-alike applies only if a derived database is redistributed. Fixtures: trimmed real DominiosVerificados and Sedes rows plus a comment-wrapped error body. BACKLOG: authorised betting operators (.bet.br, SPA/MF) once a data source is verified.
P360.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1: bank and fintech impersonation dominates Brazilian phishing and this is the strongest official known-good list. The architect's floor: full daily download through the dataset manager, PSL matching, known_good that annotates and never suppresses. cti_lead and osint_investigator stop known_good at the domain (open redirects, compromised pages) and supply the defensive-registration and active-lookalike rules. legal_dpo's minimisation for natural-person registries and analyst_ux's one-line answer complete it.
P360.title: Authorised financial institutions and their verified domains (BCB Olinda + CVM registries)

final_conditions: Two steps (architect): step 1 ships the offline sector registries (CVM cadastros ';' ISO-8859-1, BCB Sedes*/DominiosVerificados through the loader shared with P360/P244) plus GLEIF and Wikidata through the clients shared with P220 and P224; step 2 adds the local RFB name index once the shared P238 importer exists.
Index: built only by `v3lum data import-rfb --names` (Empresas + Estabelecimentos only, ~6.8 GB compressed, streaming, resumable, disk-space check, shared downloader with P238), never during a scan.

SQLite FTS5 is detected at runtime (PRAGMA compile_options) with a normalised-token table as fallback; names are normalised by core/namematch.py (accents; LTDA, S.A., S/A, EIRELI, ME, EPP, SLU); active head offices rank first.

Rule 4 / legal floor: MEI names are stripped of 11-digit CPF sequences before indexing (tested); the index serves company-name search only, never person search (even for MEI/EI names), and a person_name input never queries it (test).

Output: ranked 'possible CNPJ' hypotheses with match evidence (similarity, normalised name, UF/city, situacao, head office, source, index snapshot date) as pivots with expand=False; non-interactive scans list at most 5 with the exact follow-up command.

The P236 chain starts automatically only on an exact unique match of the normalised razao social of an active head office; nome fantasia matches never auto-chain; every other case needs analyst confirmation (TTY selection or the printed command). The resolver never runs on a legal name that came from a CNPJ record.

Online fallbacks only when the local index is absent or returns nothing (tiers: RFB, CVM, BCB, GLEIF and Wikimedia all trusted): GLEIF fuzzycompletions/fulltext (CC0) and Wikidata P6204 items (identifying UA on Wikimedia hosts only), labelled 'large companies only'. Without the index the module says 'local name index not installed (v3lum data import-rfb --names, ~7 GB)'.

CNPJs derived from DOU/Querido Diario excerpts stay hypotheses. Hypotheses and domains derived from them never become LIGHT/ACTIVE seeds, org_profile entries or scope entries without analyst confirmation (redteam_lead).

Performance and tests: a query returns in < 500 ms (benchmark on a synthetic 200k-row index); fixtures: the 11 GLEIF/Wikidata/CVM/BCB captures plus a synthetic RFB slice with an MEI name carrying CPF digits.
P361.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (legal_dpo voted P1). It lets Brazilian chains start from 'Empresa X Ltda'. legal_dpo's floor (company search only, CPF digits stripped, confirmation before P236) and the architect's two-step delivery with shared clients and importer are adopted. On auto-chaining the strictest consistent rule wins: exact unique razao social of an active head office (cti_lead, analyst_ux), never nome fantasia. osint_investigator's person_name test and redteam_lead's no-scope-leak rule complete it.
P361.title: Company name -> CNPJ resolver (RFB light name index, CVM and BCB registries, GLEIF, Wikidata P6204)

final_conditions: Build gate (architect, osint_investigator, analyst_ux): the automated module is implemented only after the API parameters and trimmed fixtures (results, empty, geo-block) are captured from the team's own Brazilian network; until then it ships as the manual link to comunica.pje.jus.br (A9).

Legal floor (A1): the Comunica PJe API terms were not readable from the research egress, so terms='unknown' until legal records them (official communications under CNJ Resolucao 455/2022); until then it runs in no profile and default_enabled=False.

A9: requires_egress={'BR'}; automated only from the team's own Brazilian egress, never through a VPN/proxy chosen to defeat the geo-block. CloudFront 403 'block access from your country' = BLOCKED reason_code 'geo_block' (could not verify), never 'no communications'; no evasion or retries with other headers.

Queries: the formatted CNPJ and the razao social within a date window (default 5 years), for CNPJ seeds by default; person names only for due-diligence subjects the analyst entered with a recorded purpose; never used to screen employees or job candidates.
Stored per communication: court, date, communication type/class, CNJ number and an excerpt of at most 300 chars; never full texts, and party names beyond the excerpt are dropped.

Output: counts by litigation class (trabalhista, consumidor, execucao fiscal, criminal...) and court plus the 5 most recent communications. CNJ numbers become cnj_process pivots routed to P241 asynchronously, under P241's licence gate.
P362.rationale: Approved 4-0-2 at median P2 (redteam_lead voted P3; cti_lead and the architect deferred because the endpoint is unverified and geo-blocked). Their objection becomes the build gate: real BR-egress fixtures first, the manual link meanwhile, as osint_investigator and analyst_ux proposed. legal_dpo's floor adds A9 egress honesty, terms recorded before use (unknown until then, so not default), minimal storage and no employment screening.
P362.title: Court communications mentioning a company (CNJ DJEN / Comunica PJe) -> CNJ numbers -> DataJud

final_conditions: Offline (disclosure 'none', TLP:RED-safe). The tesseract binary is optional, found via a config path or PATH and never auto-installed; pytesseract (Apache-2.0) is the wrapper; rapidocr-onnxruntime is not used. A missing binary gives UNAVAILABLE reason_code 'package' with the exact install command.
Models: por and eng tessdata_fast (Apache-2.0, tesseract-ocr project on GitHub) through the dataset manager with SHA-256 pinning.

Parsing runs in the shared file-analysis sandbox core/sandbox.py: a python -I child process with a wall timeout, POSIX rlimits (memory <= 1 GiB, CPU, no file writes), input cap 100 MB and JSON output cap 1 MB; doctor reports the reduced isolation on Windows. Downloaded data is never executed. Images pass Pillow's pixel cap first (Leptonica parses hostile images).
pypdf text layer first; OCR only for image-only pages and at most 10 pages per document.

Because text is never auto-expanded, the module itself calls the shared P172 extractor, the P232 BR rules, the P233 boleto/PIX parsers and the P261 QR helpers, and emits their results as pivots (relation extracted_from), not a text_blob.

OCR-derived entities carry provenance ocr, confidence <= 0.6 and expand=False until the analyst confirms (0/O, l/1, rn/m misreads). They never trigger typosquat/lookalike findings, and OCR-derived boleto/PIX check-digit failures never trigger tampering findings, without a non-OCR confirmation.
The report shows the OCR snippet around each extracted IOC; the full OCR text is kept only in case evidence (it may hold personal data) and CPFs found are masked and never pivoted.
Fixtures: synthetic rendered-text images generated in tests (URL, PIX payload, boleto line, CPF to mask, a misread-prone domain).
P363.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (osint_investigator, legal_dpo and the architect voted P1): most Brazilian scam evidence arrives as screenshots. The architect's floor: optional external binary, pinned models, sandboxed OCR, and the module running the shared extractors itself. cti_lead's and analyst_ux's OCR-misread guards keep misreads from becoming lookalike or tampering findings, consistent with P233; legal_dpo confirmed offline Apache-2.0 components.
P363.title: Offline OCR of screenshots and scans (Tesseract por+eng; PDF text layer first)

final_conditions: Offline module: disclosure 'none' (no network at all; ScopedHttp refuses any request), terms 'open', provider tier 'n/a'; allowed at TLP:RED. FILE input only; APKs are parsed, never installed, emulated or executed.

Default path (architect): an own parser on the core safe archive helper: central-directory zip reading tolerant of malware zip tricks, a binary AXML manifest decoder, v1 (META-INF PKCS#7) and v2/v3 signing-block certificate SHA-256, and URL/IP/domain extraction from dex strings through the shared P172 extractor. androguard (Apache-2.0) is only an optional extra for deep analysis.

Parsing runs in the shared file-analysis sandbox core/sandbox.py: a python -I child process with a wall timeout, POSIX rlimits (memory <= 1 GiB, CPU, no file writes), input cap 100 MB and JSON output cap 1 MB; doctor reports the reduced isolation on Windows. Downloaded data is never executed. Entry-count, size and ratio caps apply.

Outputs: package and app label, permissions, exported components, signing-certificate SHA-256 (pivot, code_signing_cert type of P333), embedded URLs/domains/IPs. Embedded hosts pass P169 warninglists; SDK/analytics/CDN hosts (firebase, crashlytics, google-analytics, app-measurement) are noise; the rest are hostile pivots for passive modules only, never contacted by any automatic step.

Banker profile as data: accessibility service + overlay (SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW) + SMS + device admin, plus REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES/QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES, gives a MEDIUM heuristic finding 'consistent with Brazilian banking trojans' listing the triggering permissions in plain language; 'malicious' only with a hash, family or YARA-family hit.

Impersonation: app label or package matching an org_profile or BCB-protected brand (P360) AND a signing certificate different from the official one = HIGH. Reference certificates: org_profile app entries, a curated dated list of official BR bank app certificates in data/, P008 Digital Asset Links results already in the case, or an archived assetlinks.json (no request here).

A direct fetch of a brand's /.well-known/assetlinks.json happens only in --mode light for analyst-typed seed domains, through the P269 LIGHT fetcher (A7 BR5: org_profile domains that are not typed seeds get P008 data only). Without a reference certificate the finding reads 'protected brand used, official certificate unknown', with no impersonation verdict.
Fixtures: a minimal benign APK built in tests (v1 and v2 signed) plus malformed-zip variants (duplicate entries, bad central directory, bomb ratio).
P364.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1 (redteam_lead and analyst_ux voted P2): Brazilian banking malware arrives as APKs. The architect's floor replaces androguard's heavy dependency tree with an own sandboxed parser, keeping androguard optional. osint_investigator supplied the reference-certificate sources and the 'official certificate unknown' wording, redteam_lead the passive certificate comparison and never touching embedded C2, cti_lead the SDK-noise list and the suspicious-not-malicious profile, and analyst_ux the plain-language banker finding.
P364.title: Android APK static triage (androguard: permissions, components, signing cert, embedded IOCs)

final_conditions: Offline module: disclosure 'none' (no network at all; ScopedHttp refuses any request), terms 'open', provider tier 'n/a'; allowed at TLP:RED. Built on the single core safe archive helper shared with the dataset manager, P269 and P364: zipfile/tarfile (filter='data') listing by default; members are never executed.

Limits: total uncompressed <= 500 MB, ratio <= 100, members <= 10,000, nesting depth <= 3. Names with absolute paths, '..', drive letters, symlinks, hardlinks or devices are flagged and never extracted.
Extraction only with an explicit flag, into a fresh 0700 temp dir that is deleted after the run.
Encrypted members are listed and decrypted only with an analyst-supplied password; the conventional sample passwords ('infected', 'malware') only as an explicit option; never guessed or brute-forced.

Licences (A6): rarfile (ISC; header listing only, no unrar extraction), py7zr (LGPL-2.1+) and pycdlib (LGPL-2.1) only as unmodified optional extras imported dynamically. VHD/VHDX are reported, never mounted.

Rule 3 (legal floor): archives recognised as stealer-log or leak bundles (members such as Passwords.txt, Cookies, Autofill, wallet files) are listed only as names, sizes and counts, never extracted, parsed or printed beyond member names.

Findings: containers that defeat Mark-of-the-Web (ISO/IMG/VHD holding LNK/EXE/JS/HTA) are suspicious; executables, scripts and double extensions inside are flagged; small members are hashed in memory and emitted as hash pivots (at most 50 per archive) routed to P270 and hash lookups under the case TLP (no external lookups at RED).
Fixtures: synthetic zip/tar/ISO files plus path-traversal, symlink, bomb, encrypted and stealer-bundle-like samples generated in tests.
P365.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1 (osint_investigator and redteam_lead voted P2). The architect's floor: one hardened archive helper with tested limits, listing by default, no guessed passwords, LGPL extras only dynamically. legal_dpo's rule 3 floor keeps stealer bundles metadata-only. cti_lead's Mark-of-the-Web finding and TLP-bound member lookups are adopted.
P365.title: Archive and disk-image listing (ZIP/TAR/RAR/7z/ISO) with bomb and depth limits

final_conditions: Offline module: disclosure 'none' (no network at all; ScopedHttp refuses any request), terms 'open', provider tier 'n/a'; allowed at TLP:RED. Pure-Python static decoders only: no eval, exec or subprocess, no PowerShell or JS engine, no emulation; a unit test asserts it.
Techniques: UTF-16LE base64 of -EncodedCommand, FromBase64String, char-code joins and String.fromCharCode, unescape/%u, VBS Chr/ChrW, hex blobs and simple string concatenation.
Bounds: at most 5 layers, 1 MB output per layer and a 5 s total time budget; every pattern passes a ReDoS fuzz test.

Each layer is recorded in evidence with secrets redacted by the central redactor (AR01) and shown as defanged plain text with the technique ('layer 1: base64 UTF-16LE -EncodedCommand'), truncated in the terminal and complete in evidence.

Decoded text goes to the shared P172 extractor; IOCs are emitted as pivots (relation extracted_from, tag decoded) with the layer path as provenance. Schema, namespace and documentation URLs (schemas.microsoft.com, w3.org, go.microsoft.com) and common library CDNs are filtered through P169 first.

Decoded download cradles are hostile IOCs for passive modules only and are never contacted by any automatic step. The functions are reused by P367 (LNK, MSI, OneNote), P365 and pasted EDR command lines.
Fixtures: synthetic encoded samples for each technique, nested up to 5 layers, plus an oversized and a ReDoS-candidate input.
P366.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (cti_lead, legal_dpo and analyst_ux voted P1). The architect's floor bounds layers, output and time and ReDoS-tests the patterns; cti_lead's namespace-URL filtering and provenance, analyst_ux's readable layer view and redteam_lead's 'decoded cradles are never touched' complete the static-only design every member asked for.
P366.title: Script de-obfuscation (PowerShell -enc, JS/VBS/HTA string decoding) for IOC extraction

final_conditions: Offline module: disclosure 'none' (no network at all; ScopedHttp refuses any request), terms 'open', provider tier 'n/a'; allowed at TLP:RED. FILE input only.

Parsing runs in the shared file-analysis sandbox core/sandbox.py: a python -I child process with a wall timeout, POSIX rlimits (memory <= 1 GiB, CPU, no file writes), input cap 100 MB and JSON output cap 1 MB; doctor reports the reduced isolation on Windows. Downloaded data is never executed.

LNK through LnkParse3 (MIT) as an optional extra (it pulls PyYAML, allowed only inside that extra): target, arguments, working dir, icon location, timestamps, machine id, droid MAC and volume serial. Arguments go to the P366 decoder functions.

OneNote: embedded files found by an own scan for the FileDataStoreObject GUID header (pyOneNote 0.0.2 is not used). MSI: olefile streams and, when the optional pre-release pymsi (MIT) is installed, the CustomAction, Binary and Property tables; otherwise the status says 'MSI tables not parsed', never empty.

Embedded scripts (HTA, JS, VBS, PowerShell in CustomActions or OneNote) go to P366; embedded files are hashed in memory and emitted as hash pivots, never written to disk or made executable. A parser failure is ERROR, never EMPTY.
UNC and WebDAV targets in shortcuts become hostile pivots that are never touched (no SMB or WebDAV access), as in P269.

LNK machine id, droid MAC and volume serial are clustering attributes only (expand=False, never sent to any lookup) and are indexed in the P375 case-DB sightings so Grandoreiro/Mekotio-style campaigns link across cases.
Fixtures: synthetic LNK, OneNote and MSI samples built in tests (including a malformed one of each).
P367.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (legal_dpo voted P1). The architect's floor avoids the pre-release parsers (own OneNote scan, pymsi optional with an honest 'not parsed' status) inside the sandbox. cti_lead's cross-case clustering of LNK machine ids, redteam_lead's untouched UNC/WebDAV targets and legal_dpo's attributes-only rule for machine identifiers are adopted.
P367.title: Windows artefact triage: LNK shortcuts, MSI installers and OneNote files

final_conditions: Offline module: disclosure 'none' (no network at all; ScopedHttp refuses any request), terms 'open', provider tier 'n/a'; allowed at TLP:RED. FILE input only; samples are parsed, never executed. This module makes no network call.

Parsing runs in the shared file-analysis sandbox core/sandbox.py: a python -I child process with a wall timeout, POSIX rlimits (memory <= 1 GiB, CPU, no file writes), input cap 100 MB and JSON output cap 1 MB; doctor reports the reduced isolation on Windows. Downloaded data is never executed.
pyelftools (pure Python, public domain) only: architecture, interpreter, needed libraries, imported and exported symbols, section entropy and UPX markers (INFO hints).

The telfhash library is not used (its dependency set includes the dead nose package, capstone and two TLSH bindings); a telfhash value is taken from YARAify/MalwareBazaar results when those modules return it, and those lookups follow the abuse.ch licence decision (A1: MalwareBazaar class 'license').
Fixtures: a small benign ELF built in tests plus a truncated one.
P368.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3 (legal_dpo voted P2). The architect's floor drops the telfhash package and keeps pyelftools in the sandbox; cti_lead's and legal_dpo's licence condition on the MalwareBazaar telfhash pivot is enforced where those lookups happen. Scheduling (A16 BR1): P3 effort S, but pyelftools would be a new runtime dependency (optional extra), so it is not built in this build; BACKLOG.md keeps this spec.
P368.title: ELF basic triage (pyelftools + telfhash)

final_conditions: ACTIVE gate (A7): runs only with --mode active, a non-empty --authorized REF and a --scope FILE on every path (scan, run, shell, watch, batch; non-interactive runs refuse without both), on scope-file matches only after resolution and per redirect hop, never on pivots or on entities extracted from text/files; CDN/shared-hosting/SaaS IPs excluded unless listed.
The nuclei target list is written only from scope-file entries; nuclei opens its own sockets, so the proxy, argv and template rules below replace the core per-request scope check.

Binary (A7 BR10): external nuclei (MIT) from a config path or PATH, version and SHA-256 checked by doctor against a pinned range; never downloaded, installed or updated by V3LUM. Without it the module is UNAVAILABLE reason_code 'package' ('install nuclei vX.Y'); no internal template engine is re-implemented.

Templates: a pinned nuclei-templates release (SHA-256 in data/active.lock) through the dataset manager, refreshed only by `v3lum data update` with a diff summary. Allowed only when ALL tags are in {tech, panel, exposure, misconfig, ssl, dns, detect, discovery}, none is in A7's forbidden set, protocols are http, ssl or dns only, and the id is on the list reviewed by the red team lead and legal.

Consequence of A7 BR11: templates tagged cve, kev or takeover are excluded in this build (takeover is covered by P276; version-inferred CVEs by P291). Templates that confirm by exploiting (file read, command execution, SSRF, auth bypass, data extraction) are excluded whatever their tags.

Fixed argv, no shell: -ni -duc -dut -dr -or -lna (unless the scope lists private ranges) -rl 10 -c 2 -bs 5 -timeout 10 -retries 1 -jsonl -tlog <case trace>, -p set to the proxy_active profile, and the scope file's ROE header via -H (never the organisation's identity, P326). A unit test asserts the built argv.

Never passed: -pd/-pdu/-cup, -ut/-turl, -sa, -ev, -lfa, -tlsi, -dast, -code, -headless, -sresp/-srd, -sf; -ept code,headless,javascript,file,websocket,whois always set; the environment is scrubbed (no PDCP_API_KEY).
CI test over the pinned template set: it fails on any excluded tag, on {{interactsh-url}}, on methods other than GET/HEAD, and on payloads that read files, run commands or bypass auth (A7 BR8).

Ledger and kill switch: the -tlog trace is folded into the hash-chained P324 ledger; on cancel, end of window or deadline the process gets SIGTERM, then SIGKILL, so target traffic stops within 2 s. Template ids and versions are recorded in the audit trail; the banner shows REF, scope SHA-256, egress IP and start/end time for SOC deconfliction.

Output: JSONL size-capped, every value untrusted (AR13 escaping) and matched values passed through the P145 sanitizer. Info results collapse into one count ('12 technologies detected'); medium+ results are findings with template id, version, matched URL and evidence; tech/panel/version detections read 'exposure', never 'vulnerable'.

Results are tri-state (confirmed / not observed / could not test; blocked egress or proxy = could not test). Tests use a stub executable that emits recorded JSONL; merge only after the AR20 safety suite passes (A16).
P369.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (osint_investigator voted P3). redteam_lead's argument list (pinned binary and templates, no interactsh, no cloud upload, no TLS impersonation, caps, tracing), the architect's fixed argv, protocol exclusions and scope-derived targets, and legal_dpo's no-exploit-confirmation floor are merged. The binding A7 BR11 tag rule excludes cve/kev/takeover templates, which is stricter than cti_lead's and redteam_lead's reviewed KEV list; widening it needs an A7 amendment (needs_human). -c is 2 so per-host concurrency stays within A7's 2 connections.
P369.title: Template-based exposure checks (nuclei + filtered nuclei-templates allow-list)

final_conditions: ACTIVE gate (A7): runs only with --mode active, a non-empty --authorized REF and a --scope FILE on every path (scan, run, shell, watch, batch; non-interactive runs refuse without both), on scope-file matches only after resolution and per redirect hop, never on pivots or on entities extracted from text/files; CDN/shared-hosting/SaaS IPs excluded unless listed. Only apexes listed in the scope file.

A7 ceilings enforced by the core client and socket connector: <= 10 requests/probes per second and <= 2 concurrent connections per target host, the case ACTIVE budget, the kill switch (traffic stops within 2 s), proxy_active egress profile (A13), the hostile-host guard, and every request in the hash-chained P324 ledger; the report banner carries REF, scope SHA-256, window and egress.

Candidates: SecLists subdomains-top1million-5000 by default (MIT, pinned SHA-256 in data/active.lock, through the dataset manager); custom lists <= 5,000 entries (A7); permutations (alterx/dnsgen style, MIT ideas re-implemented) generated offline only from names already found under scoped apexes, <= 2,000 per parent and <= 10,000 per run.

Resolution through ctx.dns over the proxy_active profile's DoH (Cloudflare or Quad9; Google only with edns_client_subnet=0.0.0.0/0), never by querying the target's authoritative NS directly from the analyst host; its own provider bucket of <= 10 queries/s (legal_dpo, A7, stricter than 20); answers bypass the shared HTTP cache (no cache or a dedicated short cache).

Wildcards: >= 3 random labels per parent, comparing answer sets. Existence = an A/AAAA/CNAME answer that differs from the wildcard answer; NODATA or NXDOMAIN alone prove nothing (Cloudflare 'black lies'); SERVFAIL or a timeout = unknown (rule 5).

Found names become subdomain pivots with expand=False and provenance 'brute-force'; they join the ACTIVE scope only if they fall under a scoped apex AND resolve to scoped IPs; names on CDN/SaaS IPs get passive modules only.

Runtime: module timeout set explicitly (600 s) with ctx.cancelled() checks and progress events. Output summarised: count plus the top 20 by interest (dev, staging, admin, vpn...). Tri-state results; merge only after the AR20 safety suite passes (A16).
Tests with DoH fixtures (FakeHttp add_dns) covering a wildcard zone, a Cloudflare NODATA zone and a SERVFAIL.
P370.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3 (redteam_lead, legal_dpo and the architect voted P2). The A7 floor applies; where members' numbers differed the stricter value wins (legal_dpo's 10 qps, the 10,000-per-run permutation cap). redteam_lead's resolver rule (never direct to the target NS from the analyst host, no ECS) and scope-join rule, the architect's cache isolation and wildcard logic, and analyst_ux's summary are adopted. Scheduling (A16 BR1): P3 with effort M, so it is not built in this build; BACKLOG.md keeps this spec as the unblock target.
P370.title: Authorized DNS brute force and permutations (SecLists + alterx-style patterns, wildcard-aware)

final_conditions: Candidates only from org_profile (brands, domain labels) or the scope file of an --authorized client engagement: at most 5 candidates per vendor per run, one anonymous GET per vendor per candidate, no permutation guessing of tenant names (redteam_lead, architect).

Fixed URL builders (architect): Okta https://<name>.okta.com/.well-known/openid-configuration, Atlassian https://<name>.atlassian.net/_edge/tenant_info, Zendesk https://<name>.zendesk.com/hc with redirects not followed; any other path is unreachable by construction. Okta's /.well-known/okta-organization answers for any name and is never used.

Rule 2: a unit test asserts no request to login, authn, signup, password-reset, user-lookup or credential-type endpoints and that no username or e-mail is ever sent. Tenant login pages are never contacted in any mode.

Differential decisions from the exact markers in the fixtures: Okta 200 with issuer vs 403 errorCode E0000006; Atlassian cloudId JSON vs 404; Zendesk 200 vs 301 to help-center-closed. Any other status, a generic 403, 429 or a challenge = unknown (rule 5); bodies parsed raw (not via get_json, which maps 403 to AuthRequired); a challenge stops the check (rule 1).

A positive is a 'candidate tenant' until corroborated by DNS verification records (P342), IdP issuer metadata or org_profile; a homonym tenant is never attributed by name alone. Tenant hosts become identity-provider attributes and pivots for passive modules only.
The candidate name is disclosed only to the named vendors (trusted tier), under the TLP gate. Output: one tri-state row per vendor. Opt-in (default_enabled=False).

Merge gate (A16): offline tests with FakeHttp (unmatched requests fail, network guard active) over trimmed real fixtures without personal data (the captured positive/negative pairs for each vendor), a provider-registry entry for every host, the registry contract test and the P327 lint.
P371.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P3 (osint_investigator voted P3, redteam_lead P2). legal_dpo confirms it is organisation-level discovery, not account enumeration, under the rule 2 guard. The architect's construction-level URL builders and exact markers and redteam_lead's tighter candidate cap, no permutations and corroboration rule are adopted over osint_investigator's optional permutation sweep.
P371.title: Organisation SaaS tenant discovery (Okta, Atlassian, Zendesk; differential, tri-state)

final_conditions: Datasets: the BushidoUK Ransomware Tool Matrix and Vulnerability Matrix (CC BY 4.0, commercial use allowed with attribution) downloaded weekly from raw.githubusercontent.com through the dataset manager, pinned by commit/ETag, with the commit date recorded; matching is offline (disclosure 'none').

Parsing (architect): the Tool Matrix from its CSV files; the Vulnerability Matrix Markdown tables with a header check per table. An unexpected layout gives ERROR 'format changed' while the last good index stays in use; never a silently empty result.
Group names are joined through the P295 alias index; unresolved names are listed as unresolved (doctor), never guessed.

Tools are hunting leads tagged dual_use (new vocab tag, INFO), never malicious verdicts: AnyDesk, Atera, ScreenConnect and Rclone are legitimate too (and appear in Brazilian fake-bank-call scams). Optional joins to LOLRMM and ATT&CK software ids where names match exactly.

CVE cards read 'reported exploited by ransomware groups X, Y' with the per-row source links, combined with CISA KEV knownRansomwareCampaignUse to raise patch priority; a CVE row without a group link stays 'reported'.

Provider tier: community (an individual researcher's public repository with >= 2 years of track record; reviewer confirms). Reports carry the CC BY 4.0 attribution with source links. Fixtures: trimmed real CSV and Markdown files plus a changed-layout file.
P372.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. The architect's floor (pinned weekly download, loud failure on a changed layout, last good copy kept) and cti_lead's dual-use and 'reported exploited' wording are adopted; legal_dpo verified CC BY 4.0 and the leads-not-verdicts rule that every member endorsed.
P372.title: Ransomware group -> tools and exploited CVEs (BushidoUK Tool Matrix + Vulnerability Matrix, CC BY 4.0)

final_conditions: Sigma: the sigma_core.zip release asset (DRL 1.1) downloaded on release through the dataset manager and read in memory through the safe archive helper (member count and size caps, no extraction to disk). Rule YAML is parsed only with yaml.safe_load from the optional PyYAML extra; without it the index is UNAVAILABLE reason_code 'package'.

Licence (A6): no Sigma-derived index is bundled (DRL 1.1 is not on the A6 bundling list); the index is built locally from the runtime download. Only metadata is indexed (title, id, status, level, tags, logsource, path), keyed by attack.tXXXX and cve tags; rule bodies are reproduced only with DRL 1.1 author attribution.

Atomic Red Team: index.csv (MIT) read with the stdlib csv module (no YAML): per technique the test names, GUIDs and executors as links only. Nothing is ever executed or written to disk; a test asserts the module never spawns a process.
Ordering and data: stable/test Sigma rules first, experimental/deprecated marked; tactic names read from the data (v18+ renames such as 'stealth'), never hard-coded; release versions recorded.

Providers: SigmaHQ (community) and Red Canary Atomic Red Team (trusted); downloads only, no value sent. Output: technique, CVE and malware cards show 'N Sigma rules / N atomic tests' with links. Fixtures: a trimmed real sigma_core.zip slice and the Atomic index.csv head.
P373.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2. The architect's floor treats the zip as untrusted input and keeps YAML out of core; his dev-time bundled index is not adopted because A6 lists only MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, CC0 and CC BY 4.0 data for bundling, so the DRL 1.1 index is built locally at runtime. cti_lead's ordering and never-execute test, and legal_dpo's attribution conditions, complete it.
P373.title: Technique -> detections and tests (SigmaHQ rules index, Atomic Red Team index)

final_conditions: Merge gate (architect): real fixtures (the advisories RSS, one advisory page or JSON, one STIX 2.1 IOC file) captured from the team network first, since research got only Akamai 403s. If the team network is also refused by Akamai bot management, no automated module is built and the advisories ship as manual links (A9).
Rule 1 / rule 5: a 403 or challenge is BLOCKED ('could not verify'), never 'no advisory'; no browser-UA spoofing, header games or other evasion.

Ingestion: the advisories feed polled daily through the dataset manager (www.cisa.gov), XML through the safe XML helper; STIX/JSON IOC attachments validated with a schema check and parsed by the shared STIX/IOC ingestion code used by the other offline feeds (no second STIX parser); attachments are untrusted data, never executed.

Indicators are matched locally (disclosure 'none') and carry the advisory id and publication date; IP and domain IOCs older than 90 days become 'historical' context (infrastructure rotates; many are VPS, VPN or Tor nodes), while hashes keep their weight.

Legitimate tools and known-good hashes listed in advisories (PsExec, AnyDesk, Rclone; CIRCL hashlookup without KnownMalicious, P169 lists) are tagged dual_use, never malicious; public resolvers and cloud ranges are tagged by P169, not matched as malicious.

Advisories are indexed by actor/family through P295, ATT&CK ids through P292 and CVEs. Actor, family and CVE cards show advisory title, date, link and 'IOC file available'; matched IOCs are tagged 'CISA advisory'; the dataset date is shown. US government work (public domain), noted in reports.
P374.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (the architect voted P3). The architect's floor gates the merge on fixtures captured from the team network and reuses the shared STIX ingestion; legal_dpo adds no evasion and untrusted parsing, and A9 turns a persistent bot wall into manual links. cti_lead's IOC ageing and dual-use tagging and osint_investigator's warninglist pass keep advisory IOCs from over-scoring.
P374.title: CISA #StopRansomware and cybersecurity advisories (IOC files, TTPs, CVEs)

final_conditions: An index table (entity key, case id, case TLP, created, verdict) is written at save time via a migration. Lookups are offline (disclosure 'none', allowed at TLP:RED), and findings are never copied across cases.

The default index covers IOC_TYPES only. PERSONAL_TYPES (every e-mail, org-domain ones included, username, phone, person, CPF, pix_key, P333 handles) are indexed only as the keyed HMAC (A4), and only when the team enables it (setting sightings_personal, default false) with a recorded purpose. Equality lookups still work.

TLP (A2): a case sees sightings only from cases with TLP <= its own. Higher AMBER/AMBER+STRICT cases appear as 'seen in N restricted cases' with no ids, dates or verdicts. RED and LIGHT/ACTIVE engagement cases never surface in a lower-TLP case. CLEAR/GREEN exports and shareable reports omit cross-case references.
Noise entities (public resolvers, CDNs, big providers, warninglists, sinkholes) and own org assets are excluded from the 'recurrent' logic.
The rule recurrent_infrastructure fires when the same IOC (domain, IP, URL, hash or wallet) appears in >= 2 cases. It never applies to natural persons or to PERSONAL_TYPES.

When there is at least one prior case, one line appears on the entity and in the summary (e.g. 'seen in 3 previous cases, last 2026-11-20, verdict: malicious'), shown first among internal sightings (A12).
The retention purge (A10) removes a case's index rows immediately.
Explicit tests for TLP leakage (RED never surfaces; higher AMBER is counted only) and for noise exclusion.
P375.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (cti_lead, osint_investigator and analyst_ux voted P1). legal_dpo's floor keeps it from becoming a watchlist: IOC types by default, personal identifiers only as a keyed HMAC and only when enabled with a purpose, the recurrent rule never on persons. That is why osint_investigator's 'same PIX key/phone' recurrence is not adopted; pix_key can be a CPF or phone. The architect's floor: migration-backed index, TLP <= own case, explicit leakage tests. redteam_lead: RED and engagement cases never surface in exports. analyst_ux and cti_lead: noise and own-asset exclusion, the one-line display.
P375.title: Cross-case sightings from the V3LUM case database

final_conditions: Settings: proxy (the default route: third-party APIs and DoH), proxy_light and proxy_active. HttpClient and a core socket connector pick the session per request from module opsec and case tags; modules never choose proxies. Third-party API calls always stay on the default route.

Non-default profiles get their own requests.Session with trust_env=False (no environment proxies, NO_PROXY bypass or ~/.netrc credentials) and explicit proxies. Names are resolved through the profile (socks5h via optional PySocks, or DoH through that proxy), and a test asserts no local getaddrinfo for target hosts.

Fail closed: when a configured LIGHT/ACTIVE profile's proxy is down, the request is blocked and never sent through the default/corporate route. Tor is allowed for LIGHT reads only, never as proxy_active. The research VPN/proxy is a contracted provider, because it sees target URLs.
Raw-socket work (TLS handshake, JARM, port scan, AXFR, websocket) obtains sockets only from the core connector applying the profile. The lint fails direct socket use in modules.

Two-phase scheduling per entity in Engine: LIGHT/ACTIVE modules for an entity are submitted from _absorb only after its passive results (TI and archive lookups included) are absorbed and the guard has been evaluated.

Guard, on by default on every path including `v3lum run`: LIGHT/ACTIVE contact, redirect targets included, with an entity tagged malicious/phishing/c2/suspicious (in the case or in case-DB sightings), or listed by a consensus source, gives BLOCKED reason_code 'hostile_host' ('needs non-corporate egress').
The guard treats hostile-shaped entities the same way: org-brand lookalikes, domains <= 30 days old, lure-word domains, and URLs/domains extracted from text or e-mail inputs.
The guard yields only when proxy_light/proxy_active is configured or --egress-override "<reason>" is passed. The override is recorded in the case audit and the report banner.

The refusal message gives the reason, passive alternatives (urlscan search results, archived copies, sandbox reports), the config command for proxy_light and the override syntax. The refused contact becomes a manual pivot.

URLs with probable per-recipient tokens (an org_profile e-mail in plain, URL-encoded or base64 form, or opaque tokens of >= 16 chars in path/query) are never fetched automatically and need a per-URL confirmation (A7 BR15).

Each evidence file and ledger entry records the egress profile, and the public IP when known. `v3lum doctor --egress` shows each profile's public IP on request via a benign echo service. The report header shows the egress used, and `links --open` on a flagged host shows the contact warning.
Egress profiles serve opsec separation only, never quota evasion: P334 budgets are global regardless of egress. FakeHttp tests assert profile selection, fail-closed behaviour and refusals.
P376.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1; redteam_lead called it the most important opsec control of the build. All members require the guard to decide after the entity's passive results, which the pipelined engine does not do today, hence two-phase scheduling. redteam_lead: fail-closed sessions, trust_env=False, DNS through the profile, the socket factory. The architect's floor: the core picks profiles, the lint on sockets, no Tor for ACTIVE, IPs only on request. legal_dpo's floor: third-party APIs on the default route, a contracted VPN, never quota evasion, recorded overrides. osint_investigator: hostile-shaped heuristics, victim tokens, manual-pivot fallback. analyst_ux: the explanatory refusal and the override flag.
P376.title: Per-opsec egress profiles and hostile-host contact guard

final_conditions: Per-source terms live in the provider registry (providers.<id>.sources.<source>.terms: class, evidence_url, quote, checked_at, reviewer, free_plan_business_use). A CI test checks that every module and every feed of aggregator modules (P149, P071, P159) has an entry, and that Module.terms equals the most restrictive source class.

Module.terms defaults to 'unknown' (fail closed). shodan_internetdb is relabelled 'noncommercial' now, with its tests updated, because it is the template others copy. App.doctor stops calling internetdb.shodan.io under corporate.

Setting licence_profile = corporate (default) | research. Corporate allows open sources; key-terms only with free_plan_business_use=true or key_plans.<key>='business'; noncommercial/license only with an active licence_allow entry; unknown never (A1).

research is allowed only when a research_basis records a legal basis (provider grant or written permission). It is selected by config or --licence-profile research and recorded in case metadata. Every report then carries a banner listing the NC/license sources actually used, research cases are never pushed (P303), and unknown-terms sources stay disabled in every profile.

The licence_allow file (licence_allow_path, 0600) holds entries {source_id, basis, scope, legal_ref, approver, decided_at, review_by <= 12 months, evidence_url, quote}. Expired entries are inactive (doctor warns 30 days ahead). Active entries are shown in `v3lum info` and in the report coverage section.

Enforcement happens only in core/policy.py (P327), for scan, run, shell, watch and doctor. Blocked sources are SKIPPED with reason_code 'licence'. Aggregators receive ctx.allowed_sources and report their blocked feeds. A blocked source is never replaced by an automatic LIGHT/ACTIVE alternative, and its manual pivot link is emitted where the web UI allows manual use.

Initial classes (A1): abuse.ch MalwareBazaar/URLhaus/ThreatFox = 'license' (terms 2026-10-21 s.4.1) until a subscription or written decision; YARAify, Feodo Tracker and SSLBL = 'open' (CC0, s.3.4); Shodan InternetDB, VirusTotal public and Censys free = 'noncommercial'.

The terminal prints one line (e.g. '12 sources skipped by licence profile corporate - v3lum doctor --licences'). The HTML/MD appendix 'Coverage lost under licence profile' lists the sources per entity type.

`v3lum doctor --licences` runs offline from metadata. It prints per-entity-type coverage before and after; the unknown-terms review queue ranked by coverage impact, with reviewer and date stored; and attack-surface coverage lost (ports/services, CVEs, subdomains) with the licensed alternative.

doctor --licences also prints the budget list: HIBP Core, Google Web Risk, ransomware.live PRO, a Spamhaus/abuse.ch subscription, xonAPI+, a commercial Shodan/Censys/Netlas tier and the OpenSanctions business licence.

`doctor --licences --refresh` re-fetches terms pages last checked more than 30 days ago (meant to run monthly; doctor reminds when a check is overdue) and flags changed pages for re-review. It never enables or disables a source automatically.
P377.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1; a phase-0 item implementing A1. legal_dpo's floor: corporate default, research only with a recorded legal basis, key-terms only with a business plan, the abuse.ch split, the InternetDB relabel, monthly terms re-checks, allow-list entries with scope and a 12-month review. The architect's floor: per-source data plus one gate, a CI test per feed, the reference module fixed. cti_lead, osint_investigator, redteam_lead and analyst_ux made the loss visible and recoverable: the review queue, manual-link fallback, no LIGHT/ACTIVE substitution, a one-line terminal summary.
P377.title: Licence profile (corporate | research) enforced per source + `v3lum doctor --licences` coverage report

final_conditions: The profile is org_profile.toml (tomllib) or JSON at setting org_profile_path (default ~/.v3lum/org_profile.toml; a team-maintained read-only path is allowed). It is 0600 in a 0700 home and schema-validated with clear errors. PyYAML is only an optional extra, used with safe_load.

Entries: domains (verification seeded | confirmed | txt_verified | attested {by, date}); brands (accent-folded and IDN/homoglyph variants); cnpj_roots; card_bins (own card BIN prefixes, used by P357); asns; cidrs; app_ids (e.g. M365 tenant); favicon hashes; suppliers.
Also: executives (explicit opt-in only, informed under the VIP-protection programme); criticality per entry (critical|high|medium|low); a third_party_hosted flag.
Membership uses the PSL registrable domain plus a subdomain match, and ipaddress containment; never string suffix matching. Tests cover subdomains, IDN and IPv6.

Own-asset-only modules (run_on='own_assets_only': HIBP/XON domain search, stealer domain searches, IntelX phonebook, Hunter domain search) require a txt_verified entry (DNS TXT 'v3lum-verify=<token>') or an attested entry (name and date) and refuse anything else: SKIPPED with reason_code 'own_asset'. Without a profile they print one hint line.

Per-person breach/infostealer modules (run_on='own_assets', A4) treat an address as own only when its domain entry is txt_verified or attested; seeded or merely confirmed entries do not unlock them (legal floor, A11 BR4).
The profile is never exported or sent out: reports, STIX/MISP and case JSON carry only own_asset/third_party tags and the profile SHA-256 (case metadata). Watch and typosquat matching are local.

Commands: `v3lum org show|check|seed|verify`. `seed` proposes entries from passive sources (registro.br RDAP publicIds CNPJ, NIC.br ASN list, RIPEstat announced prefixes, M365 tenant domains, CT SAN affiliates, BCB/gov.br lists) as a normal passive scan through the policy gate, never LIGHT/ACTIVE. Every entry needs analyst confirmation, and nothing is auto-trusted.

The ACTIVE scope never defaults from the profile. `v3lum scope draft --from-org` writes a draft scope file that the analyst confirms and binds to the authorization reference (A7). third_party_hosted entries (CDN, cloud front doors, SaaS, detected by ASN/warninglists) are excluded from ACTIVE network probes unless the scope lists them.

Findings are tagged own_asset or third_party, and reports list 'your assets' findings first in their own section. own_asset tags drive the severity rules of P027, P028, P084, P146 and P291, and criticality feeds P302.
Profile changes are logged in the audit trail. 'LinkedIn X-ray' exists only as manual links or through an official API, never as automated search-engine scraping.
P378.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P1; several approved conditions (own-domain-only endpoints, scope files, brand watch, ownership-dependent severity) cannot be enforced without it. legal_dpo's floor: a sensitive inventory that is 0600 and never exported, verification before people-data modules unlock, executives only with notice, changes audited, no LinkedIn scraping. The architect's floor: TOML/JSON, schema validation, PSL/ipaddress membership, seeding through the policy gate. redteam_lead: the profile informs but never becomes the active scope (stricter than the draft, consistent with legal_dpo's mandatory --scope). osint_investigator, cti_lead and analyst_ux: brand variants, criticality, the team-shared file, a single hint line.
P378.title: Organisation profile (own domains, brands, CNPJ roots, ASNs/CIDRs, app ids) with auto-seeding and own-asset tagging

final_conditions: `v3lum keys setup` content is generated from REGISTRY (requires_keys/optional_keys, coverage gained per entity type) and from the provider registry (licence class, tier, free_plan_business_use), never from a hand-maintained list.

Keys are ranked by coverage gained under the active licence profile. Each step says what the key unlocks and the provider's terms in plain words. VirusTotal public and Censys free are not offered under corporate.

Under corporate, keys of noncommercial/license providers are shown as 'requires licence/legal decision'. A key alone never enables their modules; only an active licence_allow entry or recorded licence does (A1 BR4).
abuse.ch is presented per its 2026-10-21 terms: MalwareBazaar, URLhaus and ThreatFox are license-class (a subscription may be required, s.4.1); YARAify, Feodo Tracker and SSLBL are open (CC0, s.3.4).

The wizard offers the free Brazilian Portal da Transparencia API key (P237: CEIS/CNEP/CEPIM, contracts) next to OTX, GreyNoise community, AbuseIPDB, urlscan (search only), ransomware.live PRO and the GitHub token.
The wizard records each key's plan (business | free) in key_plans (A1). Every step can be skipped (Enter) and the wizard can be resumed.

Sign-up URLs are only shown or opened; there is no automated sign-up. Accounts are created by hand under the corporate identity by an employee authorised to accept the provider's terms, one account per provider unless its terms allow more; never multiple free accounts or shared personal accounts.

Keys are entered with hidden input (getpass), stored 0600, displayed masked, and never printed or logged. Key values are registered with the central redactor (AR01), so URLs that embed keys (abuse.ch v2 exports) never reach cache rows, the live feed, errors, evidence or reports. Unit test with a fake key in a query string and in a path.
One benign test call per key runs through the module's health_check (P337), counted in quotas, and reports ok / invalid / quota. `v3lum keys test` re-checks all keys non-interactively.
The first scan with no keys configured prints one hint line.
P379.rationale: Approved 6-0 at median P2 (cti_lead and analyst_ux voted P1); it is a release must-have (A16). legal_dpo's floor: the licence class decides what is offered, NC/license keys leave their modules disabled under corporate, abuse.ch per its current terms, accounts opened by authorised employees, one per provider. The architect's floor: generated from metadata, getpass/0600, tests via health_check, central redaction. osint_investigator added the Portal da Transparencia key, redteam_lead redaction across all sinks, analyst_ux skippable steps, `keys test` and the first-scan hint.
P379.title: First-run key setup wizard (`v3lum keys setup`): free keys ranked by coverage gained
